- [x] I have installed the latest stable version of RStudio, and confirmed that the issue still persists.
- [ ] If I am reporting an RStudio crash, I have included a [diagnostics report](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/troubleshooting/diagnostic-report.html). (Not a crash report.)
- [ ] I have included a minimal, self-contained set of instructions for consistently reproducing the issue. (The session-specific procedure and measurements are above; a shareable reduced input file is still missing.)

title: packageInfo() is empty for package directories whose project build type is not Package
description:
### Summary

`ProjectContext::packageInfo()` is only populated when the project's build type is `Package` (`updatePackageInfo()` in `SessionProjectContext.cpp`). But `ProjectContext::isPackageProject()` also returns `true` for projects of any other build type whose project directory contains a `DESCRIPTION` with `Type: Package`.

For those projects, callers that gate on `isPackageProject()` and then read `packageInfo().name()` get an empty string:

- `ParseStatus::resolveLookupContext()` in `SessionRParser.cpp` stores `""` as the package name, so the two source-index lookups in the parser (`RSourceIndex::getPackageInformation` and `hasFunctionInformation`) query package `""`.
- `SessionDiagnostics.cpp` calls `RSourceIndex::addGloballyInferredPackage("")` at session init.
- `SessionCodeSearch.cpp` guards against the empty name and skips native-symbol registration.

The practical effect is that functions defined in the package's `R/` directory are not recognized by diagnostics in such projects, where they would be if the build type were `Package`.

### Possible fixes

- Populate `packageInfo_` from the indexed `DESCRIPTION` (the one `isPackageProject()` consults) rather than only for the `Package` build type, or
- expose the indexed package info and have the parser and diagnostics read from it.

Noted by @gtritchie while reviewing #19057; split out since it is independent of the performance change there.

title: RStudio Desktop drops command-line flags when restarting itself in Playwright tests
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.05.0
    OS Version      : Windows 11, but applies to all platforms
    R Version       : N/A

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Launch RStudio Desktop from the command line with any flag.

    Windows (PowerShell):
    ```powershell
    & 'C:\Program Files\RStudio\rstudio.exe' --remote-debugging-port=9254
    ```

    macOS:
    ```
    /Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/RStudio --remote-debugging-port=9254
    ```

    Linux:
    ```
    /usr/bin/rstudio --remote-debugging-port=9254
    ```

2. Confirm the flag took effect. For `--remote-debugging-port=9254`, open a browser and visit `http://localhost:9254/json/version`.
    - The Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint responds.
3. Trigger an RStudio restart by invoking a command that restarts the IDE -- for example, install Posit Assistant, then invoke "Uninstall Posit Assistant" from the command palette and confirm.
4. After RStudio comes back up, check the same endpoint at `http://localhost:9254/json/version`.
    - The endpoint no longer responds. The flag was not carried over to the restarted process.

### Describe the problem in detail

When RStudio Desktop restarts itself, the new process is spawned with a freshly built `argv`, not by inheriting the original command-line flags. The relevant code is in `src/node/desktop/src/main/application-launch.ts`, where `launchRStudio()` constructs:

    const argv = app.isPackaged ? [] : [process.argv[1]];

This drops all flags from the original launch. Any flag passed at startup -- `--remote-debugging-port`, `--enable-logging`, `--user-data-dir`, etc. -- is lost across a restart.

This affects test infrastructure. The Playwright test suite at `e2e/rstudio` launches RStudio with `--remote-debugging-port=<N>` so Playwright can attach over CDP. Tests that exercise an IDE restart (e.g. the Uninstall Posit Assistant flow) lose their CDP endpoint mid-test. The fixture works around this by snapshotting RStudio process IDs, killing the non-CDP self-respawn, and launching a new CDP-enabled instance.

Other flags exist that a developer might pass at startup -- e.g. `--enable-logging`, `--user-data-dir` -- and these are similarly lost on restart.

There is no observable effect on users who launch RStudio by clicking the icon, because they don't pass flags to begin with.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Flags from the original launch would carry over to the restarted process, so that anything configured at first launch (debugging endpoint, log destination, user data dir) stays in effect across restarts.

Implementation note: Possibly forward CLI flags (anything starting with `-`) but continue to resolve positional arguments (working directory, project file) from the restart options as today.

title: E2E runs that select zero tests are reported as successful
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : N/A -- affects the Desktop and Server E2E engines alike
    RStudio Version : N/A
    OS Version      : N/A -- affects every per-OS engine
    R Version       : N/A

### Steps to reproduce the problem

In any per-OS E2E engine workflow -- for example `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-14-arm64.yml`:

1. Go to Actions and select the engine workflow.
2. Click "Run workflow".
3. Enter `tests/smoke/startup.test.ts` in the `test_selector` field.
4. Click the green "Run workflow" button.
5. Wait for the run to finish.
    - The run finishes with a green check and a `success` conclusion.
6. Open the `e2e-merge` job and expand its summary step.
    - The log reads `Overall: passed=0 failed=0 skipped=0 flaky=0 rate=0%`.
    - The sticky comment and job summary report the run as a pass.

### Describe the problem in detail

`e2e/rstudio/scripts/summarize-merged-report.mjs` totals the results, computes a pass rate, writes them as step outputs, logs them, and ends. It has no zero-test check and no non-zero exit, so a run where Playwright selected nothing looks identical to a run where everything passed. Playwright exits 0 when no tests match a selector, so nothing upstream catches it either.

This reaches every per-OS engine, since they all merge through the same summarizer.

The `test_selector` input makes it easy to hit by accident. `tests/smoke/startup.test.ts` is tagged `@smoke`, and `playwright.config.ts:80` grep-inverts `@smoke` unless `PW_RUN_SMOKE` is set -- which no engine workflow passes -- so that selector selects nothing at all.

This has already caused a real false pass. Run 30363343377 finished with a `success` conclusion while reporting `passed=0 failed=0 skipped=0 flaky=0 rate=0%`, and was taken as validation for an engine that had asserted nothing.

### Describe the behavior you expected

A run that selected no tests would ideally fail, or at least not report success. An opt-out along the lines of `PW_REQUIRE_TESTS` would keep deliberately empty runs possible where they're wanted.

title: Add Windows 11 ARM to the E2E rotations and enable its database stack
description:
### Problem Statement

The Windows 11 ARM engine (`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-11-arm64.yml`) landed dispatch-only, from #18542 and PR #18675. It's the only engine that isn't scheduled -- the other 21 all run on a fixed weekday and again in the Sunday sweep, so this one runs only when someone remembers to dispatch it by hand.

It also leaves `install-database-stack` unset, so the Connections pane specs skip. That was deliberate, since PostgreSQL and the ODBC drivers aren't verified on Windows-on-ARM, but it's worth closing now that the engine itself works.

One thing to weigh before scheduling it. The engine tests the x86_64 build under Windows' x64 emulation, since there's no arm64 RStudio build, and its first full-suite run passed 614 of 623. The six failures are genuine emulation problems, not engine defects -- the Viewer pane never appears for markdown, Quarto, and RMarkdown renders; two readr Import Dataset previews error; and the Build pane never prints "Test complete". All six pass on the x86_64 sibling against the same daily build. Putting this engine in a rotation means those six go red on a schedule until they're fixed or skipped with a reason.

### Proposed Behaviour

Three things, in rough priority order:

1. Add the engine to a weekday slate in `os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml`, so it runs on its own day like every other engine.
2. Include it in the Sunday macOS and Windows sweep, so it's covered weekly even if a weekday run is missed.
3. Set `install-database-stack` and whatever Windows-on-ARM setup the PostgreSQL and SQLite drivers need, so the Connections pane specs actually run. #18704 covers the related `odbc` problem on engines that leave the flag unset.

Registering an engine also touches the certification workflow's job list and cell map, the PR gate's path filter and caller, and the cache-seed and sentinel workflows.

title: Remove the dead post_pr_comment step from six e2e engine workflows
description:
### Problem Statement

Six e2e engine workflows each define a step named "Post E2E results to PR" that runs `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment`, gated on `inputs.post_pr_comment == true`:

- .github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025.yml
- .github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-26-arm64.yml
- .github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-14-arm64.yml
- .github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-15-x86_64.yml
- .github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-server-os-ubuntu-24.yml
- .github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-linux.yml

No caller ever passes `post_pr_comment: true`, so the step never runs. It used to: os-test-e2e-rstudio-pr.yml passed it to each engine until commit 2fecf2bd41 (#18115) switched to `defer_merge: true`, moving to one unified PR comment posted by that workflow's own merge job instead. The per-engine input and step were never cleaned up afterward, and the input's description ("Pass true only from PR-triggered callers") no longer matches any real caller.

### Proposed Behaviour

In each of the six files, remove the two `post_pr_comment` input declarations (under `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call`), the "Post E2E results to PR" step, and the comment referencing it. This should have no functional effect, since the step never runs today.

title: e2e Playwright tests use isVisible with a timeout option that Playwright ignores
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : N/A
    RStudio Version : N/A
    OS Version      : N/A
    R Version       : N/A

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Several files in e2e/rstudio check for an optional page element (a confirmation dialog, a login form, a step-specific field) with this pattern:

```
if (await someLocator.isVisible({ timeout: 5000 }).catch(() => false)) {
  ...
}
```

Search each of these files for "isVisible" to find the exact lines:

- e2e/rstudio/tests/projects/project_id.test.ts
- e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/posit-assistant-chat/shiny-app-r.test.ts
- e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/posit-assistant-chat/shiny-app-python.draft.ts (a .draft.ts file, not part of the run suite yet)
- e2e/rstudio/utils/project.ts
- e2e/rstudio/fixtures/server.fixture.ts

This was found and fixed in e2e/rstudio/utils/github-device-authorize.ts (a GitHub Copilot sign-in helper) while investigating a check for a two-factor authentication prompt placed right after a password submit.

### Describe the problem in detail

Playwright's documentation for `Locator.isVisible()` (https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-is-visible) states its `timeout` option is deprecated and ignored: "This option is ignored. `locator.isVisible()` does not wait for the element to become visible and returns immediately."

So every call site above checks the DOM at that exact instant and returns right away, no matter what timeout value is passed. Combined with the `.catch(() => false)` that follows each one, a check that runs a moment too early silently reads "not present," with nothing in the test output to distinguish that from the element genuinely never appearing.

This doesn't fail every run--it depends on how quickly the target element renders relative to when the check executes, so it would show up as an occasional flake rather than a consistent failure, most likely on checks that immediately follow an action that can trigger a page transition (a form submit, a click that navigates).

The same docs page also recommends `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` to avoid flakiness, but that's a hard assertion--it fails the test if the element never appears. Every check listed above is a genuinely optional probe (the element may or may not show up, and both outcomes are valid), so the fitting replacement is `locator.waitFor({ state: 'visible' })`, which does wait and poll, wrapped so its timeout becomes a plain `false` instead of a failed assertion.

### Describe the behavior you expected

The timeout parameter should genuinely wait for the element to appear. The fix applied in e2e/rstudio/utils/github-device-authorize.ts replaces each `isVisible({ timeout }).catch(() => false)` call with a small wrapper:

```
async function appears(locator: Locator, timeoutMs: number): Promise<boolean> {
  return locator
    .waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: timeoutMs })
    .then(() => true)
    .catch(() => false);
}
```

The same fix would apply to the other locations listed above.

One missing Linux platform blocks the whole dispatch, including engines that never needed that key. Nothing is failing today, as all ten keys are present as of 2026-08-05.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Resolving only the keys the selected engines need, so a missing platform fails just those engines. Every `emit` stays fatal.

See #18452, which added `resolute-amd64` to the existing set.

title: Backend fails to build against OpenSSL 4
description:
### System details

RStudio Edition: Desktop and Server (build-time issue)
RStudio Version: 2026.10 / main
OS Version: any; first seen on macOS with Homebrew's `openssl` formula
R Version: n/a

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Install OpenSSL 4.x (e.g. `brew install openssl`, which now resolves to `openssl@4` since Homebrew/homebrew-core#313581 on 2026-09-28).
2. Configure and build the RStudio backend against it.

### Describe the problem in detail

The build fails compiling `src/cpp/core/system/Crypto.cpp`. OpenSSL 4.0 changed `X509_get_subject_name()` to return a `const X509_NAME *`, and the self-signed certificate generator in `core::system::crypto` mutates the returned name in place:

```
error: no matching function for call to 'X509_NAME_add_entry_by_txt'
note: candidate function not viable: 1st argument ('const X509_NAME *') would lose const qualifier
```

This is the only OpenSSL 4 incompatibility in the backend; everything else (plus Boost's Asio SSL layer) compiles unchanged against 4.0.3.

A related wrinkle on macOS: the OpenSSL include directory is added with `include_directories(SYSTEM ...)`, but clang searches the driver-added `/usr/local/include` ahead of every `-isystem` directory. With an x86_64 Homebrew OpenSSL under `/usr/local`, builds silently compile against those headers while linking the arm64 OpenSSL, which is why the error above does not reproduce on every machine.

### Describe the behavior you expected

RStudio should build cleanly against OpenSSL 1.1, 3.x, and 4.x, and should compile against the headers of the OpenSSL it links.

title: Epic: Exploratory testing of RStudio with Phileas
description:
## Description

Phileas is an exploratory/monkey testing engine for Electron apps. A Route usually starts from a known state (a **Fix**), then takes a seeded series of random actions (**Hops**). Each Hop targets one of the controls on the page, such as a button, menu entry, field or tab, found by its accessibility role and name, so the engine doesn't need a list of what the app contains. Checks run after every Hop, and the Route stops at the first failure. Every Hop is journaled as it happens, so a crash still leaves a full record, and a seed replays the Route exactly on the same build.

It complements the scripted suite rather than replacing it. This epic covers turning the current trial into something the team runs, shares and acts on, and measuring whether it earns that place.

## Current state

- **Engine:** Phileas travels through an app, journals every Hop, replays from a seed, and runs six checks after every Hop: uncaught errors, console errors, app still responding, window not blank, no unexpected dialog, and errors in the app's own logs. Hops can click, type, press keys, select, focus and use the native menu.
- **RStudio adapter:** built and running against RStudio Desktop 2026.09.1 on macOS. Each Route gets its own home folder, profile and R package library, and a guard fails the run if the machine's R library changes. The adapter watches `rdesktop.log` and the session log, excludes risky commands, and stubs outbound links, native file dialogs, and new sessions.
- **Fixes:** three so far: an R script with code, a session with a data frame, model, and plot, and the R Markdown creation dialog.
- **Known findings:** a finding already filed is recorded, so later Routes carry on past it instead of stopping there.
- **Findings so far,** each an error logged with nothing wrong on screen:
  - rstudio/rstudio#18976: Closing a terminal logs "Unknown handle" errors in the session log (fixed by rstudio/rstudio#18983)
  - rstudio/rstudio#19003: Installing odbc from New Connection logs an empty-path error
  - rstudio/rstudio#19005: Refreshing an empty Find in Files pane logs a TypeError on resultsCount
  - Open Project with nothing chosen logs an error, a duplicate of the existing rstudio/rstudio#14985

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Journey | One run of the engine, defined by a seed and a number of Routes. |
| Route | One independent pass through the app, and one Playwright test with its own verdict, timeout, and trace. Routes know nothing of each other, so any one can be replayed alone. |
| Fix | The known opening of a Route: steps written in advance, the same every time. Optional, but most Routes begin with one. |
| Hop | One action on one control on the page (or a menu entry or key), drawn from the seed. Checks run after each. |
| Journal | One file per Route, one line per Hop, written as each Hop happens so it survives a crash. Records what was chosen, what else was available, and the check results. |

## 1. Investigation: Performance over time

The central open question is whether it keeps finding issues, or finds a handful up front and goes quiet.

See sub-issues #19043, #19044, #19045, #19046, and #19047.

## 2. How the team uses it

- [ ] Decide who runs it (QA, developers, CI) and for what: a background signal, a pre-release sweep, or probing one area through its Fix.
- [ ] Document how it sits beside the scripted suite and manual testing.

## 3. How often it runs

The engine is built not to gate merges, since an unlucky seed would block unrelated work.

- [ ] Choose a cadence: scheduled runs, occasional one-offs, PR-triggered informational runs, or a mix.
- [ ] Set the number of Routes per Journey and Hops per Route.

## 4. Reporting

Each Route ends passed, failed, or stranded (ran out of moves, which is reported separately and is neither). Output is a line-per-Hop journal of what was chosen and what else was available, plus a Playwright trace. `phileas show` prints a run readably.

- [ ] Build a per-Journey summary for triage.
- [ ] Decide where results go (CI artifacts, Slack, an issue queue) and whether trends over time are tracked.

## 5. Interpreting findings and filing bugs

A finding is a candidate. Someone reads the journal, reproduces it by hand, decides whether it is a bug, files it in rstudio/rstudio, and records it as a known finding pointing at the issue. That is how the four above were handled.

- [ ] Assign triage ownership, since nothing forces a run's results to be read.
- [ ] Make findings reproducible across machines and after a fix. A seed replays only on the same build and R setup; replaying from the journal is the proposed approach.
- [ ] Have each finding state the build it came from, since the test build differs from what users install.

## 6. More kinds of checks

- [ ] Build the two remaining universal checks: every visible control has an accessible name, and no navigation away.
- [ ] Add RStudio-specific checks, for example console history returning the last line after arbitrary actions, and at most one modal dialog at a time.
- [ ] Add accuracy checks against independent sources: a separate R process for Environment and data viewer values, files on disk for what the editor saves (e.g. visual editor saving `*text*` as `_text_`). Expected answers never come from RStudio's own code.
- [ ] Judge which kinds pay off, against real RStudio bugs.

## 7. Use of an LLM

Checks stay deterministic, since a check's verdict has to reproduce from the seed. A model fits around the checks, not inside them.

- [ ] Summarize a failed Route's journal into a draft bug report.
- [ ] Shorten a failing Route to the minimal steps that reproduce it.
- [ ] Read many journals for suspicious patterns no check asks about, as suggestions for a person to confirm.
- [ ] Decide where journals may be sent: a hosted model or only a local one.

## 8. Adapter development

The adapter grows run by run: early Journeys each turned up something to handle, such as a What's New screen masking the IDE or a log that rotates.

- [ ] Move the trial adapter into its permanent home (see section 14).
- [ ] Assign an owner to keep it current as RStudio changes.

## 9. Exclusions and stubs

Excluded today: Quit, New Session, the crash command, update checks, package updates, outbound help pages, Posit Assistant and Copilot, the ticking memory readout, and the Command Palette. Package installs are allowed, since they land in the Route's own library.

- [ ] Review which exclusions hide areas worth testing, such as Assistant.
- [ ] Derive exclusions from source where possible, so a new way out of the app fails a check instead of going unnoticed.
- [ ] Bring back the Command Palette, which needs exclusions to reach its copies of menu commands.

## 10. Limitations to work through

- [ ] **New session or new project in a new window:** RStudio starts a second copy of itself, which escapes the Route's sandbox, so it is stubbed and untested. A small RStudio change, passing `--user-data-dir` on to the child, would close the gap.
- [ ] **Other windows** such as plot zoom: a Route sees one window.
- [ ] **Frames:** Help, Viewer and the data viewer are iframes, not read yet.
- [ ] **Drawn surfaces:** the console, source editor and visual editor offer few controls. A Fix can type into them directly, and checks can read them.
- [ ] **Native dialogs** are beyond Playwright, so web dialogs are used. Findings on that path say so.
- [ ] **Menu commands run behind RStudio's own modal dialogs.** Needs a decision on whether that is intended.

## 11. Cross-platform

macOS only today. RStudio's shipped release is hardened against automation; on macOS the trial uses a local copy with two Electron settings switched back on.

- [ ] Find the equivalent way to launch a testable build on Windows and Linux, or build from source.
- [ ] Remove the engine's macOS assumptions (app bundle layout, finding signatures tied to the macOS temp folder).
- [ ] Run on all three platforms, and compare what each finds.

## 12. Fixes

A Fix is a short TypeScript function, one per file, that brings RStudio to a known starting point before the random part begins. Fixes are optional, but most Routes should begin with one; a Route without a Fix starts wherever RStudio starts and is pure randomness. A Fix runs fresh at the start of every Route and is never cached, which keeps Routes independent.

- [ ] Decide who writes Fixes. Area owners know which states are worth starting from.
- [ ] Add Fixes for high-value areas, such as Connections, Git, Build and Quarto.
- [ ] Review Fixes like other test code, and add a new Fix rather than edit one that recorded findings depend on, since editing it changes where every seed goes.

## 13. A shared resource

Today the known findings live in one JSON file that every run rewrites, which works for one person and will conflict for several.

- [ ] Have runs write new findings to a local pending file, and change the shared list only through a reviewed step.
- [ ] Store one file per finding, so separate findings never conflict.
- [ ] Record engine, adapter, RStudio, R and package versions in every journal.

## 14. Where it lives

The engine is its own package; only the adapter, Fixes and Journeys live with a consumer.

- [ ] Decide between a `phileas/` directory in rstudio/rstudio, beside the existing tests, and a separate Posit test repository pointed at RStudio builds.

## 15. Which products

- **RStudio Desktop:** the current target.
- [ ] Assess resuming the Positron trial, which found candidate bugs and has a partly built adapter.
- [ ] Assess RStudio Server and Workbench, which are browser-based rather than Electron.
- [ ] Inventory other Posit Electron apps.

title: Agree on the bar for continuing or stopping measurements
Separate findings in long-standing code from regressions in new code.
Track cost: machine time, adapter upkeep, and triage time per bug filed.
Record which areas yield findings and which yield nothing.
Run Journeys across successive daily builds and releases, and track new findings per 100 Routes.

title: Upgrade the Node.js that CI installs from the end-of-life Node 20 to Node 24
description:
### Problem Statement

Every workflow that runs npm or Playwright installs Node.js through `actions/setup-node`, and all 21 of those sites still pass `node-version: 20`.

Node.js 20's security support ended on 2026-04-30. The Node.js project hasn't shipped a patch for any CVE in that line since, so CI has been building and testing on an unpatched runtime for about four and a half months.

This is a separate axis from [#18587](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/18587) and [#18598](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/18598), which covered the Node runtime each *action* itself runs on (the `using: node20` line in an action's own `action.yml`). Both of those are done. It's also separate from [#18670](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/18670) and [#18671](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/18671), which covered the Node.js bundled inside the shipped product. This one is the Node.js that builds and runs our own test and build steps.

The repo already asks for something newer than 20. The root `package.json` declares:

```
"engines": {
  "node": ">=22.18.0"
}
```

and `RSTUDIO_NODE_VERSION` is `22.22.2` in both `cmake/globals.cmake` and `dependencies/tools/rstudio-tools.sh`. CI installs a Node two majors below that floor, which is what makes npm print `EBADENGINE` warnings during install.

The 21 sites, all in `.github/workflows/`:

- `os-cache-seed-e2e-deps.yml` -- 1
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-pr.yml` -- 1
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-autocomplete-scheduled-windows-server-2025.yml` -- 1
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-linux.yml` -- 2
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-14-arm64.yml` -- 2
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-15-x86_64.yml` -- 2
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-26-arm64.yml` -- 2
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-27-arm64.yml` -- 2
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-server-os-ubuntu-24.yml` -- 2
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-11-arm64.yml` -- 3
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025.yml` -- 3

There's no deadline forcing this the way the action-runtime removal forced #18598. The exposure just keeps accumulating.

### Proposed Behaviour

Move all 21 sites to a supported Node.js major.

Node 24 would be the target. It's an active LTS with security support through 2028-04-30, and it's the major GitHub's runners already default to for action runtimes since June, so both axes would line up on the same number.

Node 22 is the alternative worth considering. Security support runs to 2027-04-30, it's a smaller jump, and it would match `RSTUDIO_NODE_VERSION` exactly. The tradeoff is that it buys only about seven months before this comes back around.

Either way, it'd be good to settle whether the `setup-node` version and `RSTUDIO_NODE_VERSION` are meant to track each other. Right now they don't, and nothing in the repo says whether that's deliberate.

Two things to watch while verifying: a native module with no prebuilt binary for the new Node ABI on some runner, and real behavior differences between majors. Unlike the action-pin sweep, a clean deprecation-annotation check won't prove anything here -- this needs actual e2e passes across the OS engines.

### Problem

`VirtualConsole` renders two kinds of output:

- **Dynamic** output is a stream where later bytes may rewrite earlier ones: the console, Build / Compile Output text, chunk output. Control characters like `\r`, `\b`, and `\f` are interpreted as a terminal would, in every *ANSI Escape Codes* preference mode.
- **Static** output is a finished message rendered once: Markers pane rows, the error lists under Build / Compile Output / R Markdown render, and editor lint tooltips. These opt in with `setSgrOnly(true)` (added in #19033), and only newlines and color codes should survive; nothing in the message should be able to rewrite what came before it.

The static path gets this wrong when the preference is *Ignore ANSI escapes*: `\b` and `\f` are still interpreted, so the message rewrites or truncates itself.

| `ansi_console_mode` | `foo\bbar` | `warning: foo\fbar` |
|---|---|---|
| `on` / `strip` | `foobar` | `warning: foobar` |
| `off` | `fobar` | `bar` |

The preference should only decide how escape sequences are rendered. It should not decide whether a message is treated as static or dynamic.

### Example

Run this with an R file `foo.R` open in the editor:

```r
markers <- data.frame(
  type    = "warning",
  file    = normalizePath("foo.R"),
  line    = 1,
  column  = 1,
  message = c("expected foo\bbar", "line 1 is fine\fline 2 is not"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

rstudioapi::sourceMarkers("example", markers)
```

| Message | *Render* / *Remove ANSI escapes* | *Ignore ANSI escapes* |
|---|---|---|
| `expected foo\bbar` | `expected foobar` | `expected fobar` |
| `line 1 is fine\fline 2 is not` | `line 1 is fineline 2 is not` | `line 2 is not` |

The same rows appear as gutter lint tooltips in `foo.R` once it is re-linted. The second case is the bad one: half the message disappears with nothing to show that it did. Any marker producer can hit this, e.g. a `stop()` / `warning()` message that interpolates user data during a build or knit, or a `#pragma message("...")` in a file compiled with `Rcpp::sourceCpp()`.

### Cause

In static mode, `VirtualConsole.submit()` calls `AnsiCode.stripNonSgr()` for `on` / `strip`, which removes `[\007\b\f]` up front and then parses with `SGR_ONLY_PATTERN`. For `off` it instead reuses the dynamic path's `AnsiCode.strip()` (removes only BEL) and `CONTROL` pattern, so the surviving `\b` and `\f` run `backspace()` and `formfeed()` just as they would in the console.

### Fix

Make the static path strip control characters unconditionally, either by stripping `[\b\f]` in the `off` branch too or by merging the two helpers into one `strip(input, keepSgr)` so they cannot drift. Add the `off` cases above to `VirtualConsoleTests` (verified failing on the PR head with a scratch GWT test).

title: Open saved files automatically picks up changes made to them externally
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop and Server
    RStudio Version : 1.3.1093, 1.4.1653
    OS Version      : MacOS 11.3, Ubuntu 20.04 using Chrome on MacOS 11.3
    R Version       : 4.0.4

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Open a new R script file in RStudio.
2. Add `x = 1` to the file.
3. Save the file.
4. Change the contents to `x = 2` but don't save the file.
5. Use an external editor to edit the file, e.g. vi in a terminal.
    - Note that the file still says `x = 1` as expected.
6. Using the external editor, change the contents to `x = 3`.
8. Save and close the file in the external editor.
9. Switch to RStudio and click in the source pane.
    - A message pops up stating that the file changed.
10. Choose "Yes" to load the updated version.
    - The contents in the source pane switches from `x = 2` to `x = 3`.
11. Change the contents to `x = 4`.
12. Save the file.
5. Open the file again using an external editor.
    - The file says `x = 4` as expected.
6. Using the external editor, change the contents to `x = 5`.
8. Save and close the file in the external editor.
9. Switch to RStudio and click in the source pane.
    - No message pops up stating that the file changed.
    - The contents in the source pane switches from `x = 4` to `x = 5`.

### Describe the problem in detail

If a file is open and saved, then edited externally, the file in the IDE changes without warning.

### Describe the behavior you expected

RStudio should warn the user that the file has been updated and allow the user to not load the changes.  Compare this to what happens if the file has been edited but unsaved in the IDE, or similarly if the open file has been deleted under the seams.

title: Console on Right places the Console top-right after it was placed bottom-right
description:
### System details

RStudio Edition: Desktop and Server
RStudio Version: 2026.01.0 and later (any build with the generated pref accessors)
OS Version: any

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Global Options > Pane Layout, move the Console to the bottom-right quadrant and apply. This stores `panes.consoleRightOnTop = false`.
2. Choose View > Panes > Console on Right (or run the `layoutConsoleOnRight` command).

### Expected

The Console goes to the bottom-right quadrant, where it was last placed on the right.

### Observed

The Console goes to the top-right quadrant.

### Cause

`scripts/generate-prefs.R` emits boolean getters on preference objects as `return this && this.<prop> || <default>;`. When the default is `true`, a stored `false` is replaced by the default, so the stored value can never be read back. `PaneConfig.getConsoleRightOnTop()` is one such getter (`PaneManager` uses it to pick quadrant 2 or 3). The same generator bug also affects other true-default booleans on prefs/state objects, e.g. the Save Plot as Image dialog's "Use device pixel ratio" option never persisting as off.

The fix (emit `typeof this.<prop> === "boolean" ? this.<prop> : <default>`) is part of #18895.

title: Python interpreter discovery can hang the Global Options Python panel indefinitely
description:
### System details

RStudio Edition: Desktop and Server
RStudio Version: 2026.10.0 (main)
OS Version: all

### Steps to reproduce

1. Tools > Global Options > Python > Select...
2. Have a Python (or conda) executable on the PATH or in a scanned location that hangs or is very slow to start.

### Describe the problem in detail

The "Finding interpreters..." progress box stays up with no way to cancel. Interpreter discovery (`.rs.python.findPythonInterpreters`) runs every candidate interpreter and `conda env list` through `system2()` on the main R thread with no timeout, so one wedged process blocks the dialog and the `python_find_interpreters` RPC forever. The e2e suite hit this on the server-linux shard of run 34637770965: the RPC never returned within 60s, while the same test completes in a few seconds on a retry.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Each probe is bounded; an interpreter that does not answer is listed as invalid (or skipped, for conda) and the dialog opens with the rest.

```
RStudio Edition : Workbench 2026.09.0 (likely present for a while)

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Configure Workbench with several R versions whose combined display names are long -- for example, module-based R installations with long `rhome` paths and/or long admin-defined labels.

Long R version names "escape" the Global Options container. The native `<select>` sizes itself to its widest option, and nothing constrains the R version widget, so the closed control is clipped at the dialog edge and its label wraps onto several lines.

The "Default version of R" label stays on one line and the select ends before the pane edge, truncating the selected text with an ellipsis when it is too long.

### Testing

Requires manual verification against Workbench with several long R version names; the control only appears when multiple R versions are configured.

title: desktop can reclaim a running server session's source database
description:
### Problem

With no project open, RStudio Desktop and RStudio Server can use the same user data directory. Desktop defaults to advisory file locks, while Server defaults to link-based file locks. Source database recovery checks only the new session's lock type, so Desktop can treat a running Server session as orphaned and rename its `sources/session-<id>` directory.

The original Server session remains alive but attempts to create a document fail with `system error 2 (No such file or directory)` when writing `<document-id>-contents` beneath its original session directory. Existing unsaved documents also move with the directory.

### Reproduction

Reproduced on macOS with the local development build:

1. Start a Server-mode rsession without a project, using a temporary `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME`, and create a document.
2. Keep it running and start a Desktop-mode rsession with a different launcher token, using the same temporary data directory.
3. Observe that the original `sources/session-<server-id>` directory is renamed to the Desktop session's ID while the Server process is still alive.
4. Invoke `new_document` in the Server session. It fails with ENOENT.

The reproduction invokes the actual RPC with `.rs.invokeRpc("new_document", "r_source", "", list(tempName="Untitled"))`. Giving Desktop a separate `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` prevents the rename and the RPC succeeds.

### Related test isolation problem

The `rsession` C++ scope in the Unix and Windows `rstudio-tests` launchers initializes a real session without first assigning temporary RStudio data/configuration directories. The R test scope already assigns these directories. Consequently, C++ session tests can interact with an IDE running as the same user. Unscoped Server sessions can also select the same active session ID, and source database initialization currently logs lock contention and continues.

### Expected behavior

Source database recovery should recognize both lock types and leave live sessions alone. A session should refuse to reuse a source directory that another process owns. Both C++ and R session tests should use temporary RStudio state.

### QA

Verify concurrent Server/Desktop sessions sharing a temporary user data directory in both launch orders. Both should retain their source directories and continue creating documents. Also verify that abandoned directories can still be recovered, that a second process cannot reuse an actively owned session directory, and that the C++ test launcher uses isolated state even when real RStudio data/configuration variables are inherited.

title: Windows CI runs fewer unit test scopes than Linux/macOS
description:
## Summary

After #17824, the Windows CI `Tests` stage runs only the `core` scope.
Other platforms run substantially more, leaving Windows-specific
regressions in several areas uncovered by CI.

## Coverage gaps

`jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows` still invokes only `core`:

    bat 'cd package/win32/build/src/cpp && rstudio-tests.bat --scope core'

`rstudio-tests.bat` itself now accepts every scope the Unix runner does
(`core`, `rserver`, `rsession`, `r`), so what remains is a gap in what CI
asks for rather than in what the runner can do:

- `rsession` and `r` are supported by the batch script but not invoked by
  the Jenkinsfile. Running all scopes in CI was attempted and reverted
  (7f7d9be, see comment below) pending investigation of the failures.
- `rserver` has nothing to run on Windows: those tests are not built on
  the platform, so the scope prints a skip notice and passes.
- `shared_core` is not a separate scope. It runs as part of `core`, along
  with `server_core` where that is built.

For comparison:

- Linux (`jenkins/Jenkinsfile.linux`): four separate invocations --
  `core`, `rsession`, `rserver`, `r`
- macOS (`jenkins/Jenkinsfile.macos`) and PR build: bare `./rstudio-tests`,
  which runs all available scopes
- Windows (`jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows`): `core` only

## Runner interface (addressed)

When this issue was filed the two helper scripts used divergent argument
syntax: the bash `rstudio-tests` took `--scope <name>`, while
`rstudio-tests.bat` took bare positional tokens. That mismatch is what
silently disabled Windows tests between #14883 and #17824.

#18069 gave `rstudio-tests.bat` the same `--scope` / `--filter` interface as
the Unix runner, added the `r` scope, and made the script propagate
failures -- any failing suite now exits 1, where the positional wrapper
always exited 0.

#18384 takes the Windows runner one step further: `--scope` accepts more
than one scope per invocation, in any of three equivalent forms:

    rstudio-tests.bat --scope core,rsession
    rstudio-tests.bat --scope core rsession
    rstudio-tests.bat --scope core --scope rsession

Scopes always run in `core`, `rserver`, `rsession`, `r` order regardless of
the order requested, and an unrecognized name fails before any suite runs.
The Windows `Tests` stage can therefore cover several scopes in a single
`bat` step, rather than one step per scope as on Linux. The Unix
`rstudio-tests` still takes a single scope per invocation.

## Remaining work

1. Investigate and fix the failures that caused 7f7d9be, so the `rsession`
   and `r` scopes pass on the Windows agents.
2. Add those scopes to the Windows `Tests` stage once they are stable, as a
   single invocation -- e.g. `rstudio-tests.bat --scope core,rsession,r`.

title: console escape parsing follow-ups from #18917
description:
Follow-ups from the review of #18917 (console escape sequence parsing). None of these affect well-formed output; they are edge cases in how malformed or split escape sequences are handled, collected here so they don't get lost.

### `VirtualConsole`

1. **A held-back submit drops a pending new-range flag.** When a submit is entirely held back (a lone `ESC`, a partial CSI, or an unterminated string), the `forceNewRange_` read at the top of `submit()` is consumed but never restored, unlike `flushPartialAnsiCode()`, which preserves it. If an output group was just closed (`ESC g`) and the next submit is a split escape, the text that completes it is appended into the closed group's last range. Pre-existing in the old partial-code path. Fix: restore the flag at each hold site before returning.

2. **One-shot `VirtualConsole` users never flush a held-back sequence.** `ConsoleError`, `SourceMarkerItemCodec.renderMessage`, `TextEditingTargetLintSource`, `ChunkInlineOutput` and `ShellWidget.consolify()` submit once and never call `flushPartialAnsiCode()`, so text after a stray, unterminated `ESC ]` (or a partial CSI) at the end of their input is not shown, where the old code showed it minus the escape. Only reachable with malformed input, since a valid string terminates within the render. Fix: flush after the final submit, or find a mechanism that doesn't rely on every owner remembering to.

3. **Dead flush before `clear()` in `ChunkOutputStream.initializeOutput()`.** `clear()` is `formfeed()`, which empties the element, so the flush added when switching from text to another output type renders text that is erased on the next line. Remove it; the flush in `completeOutput()` is the one with an effect.

4. **Pre-prompt flush ordering and announcement.** `ShellWidget.consolePrompt()` calls `normalizePreviousOutput()` before `ensureStartingOnNewLine()`, where the flush now lives, so flushed text lands after the trailing-newline trim of the last group, and it goes through the nested `submit()` with `ariaLiveAnnounce = false`. Cosmetic; malformed input only.

5. **Quadratic rescans of a held-back string.** Each submit re-concatenates the held string and rescans it from its introducer for a terminator. Bounded by the 1 MB cap (`MAX_PARTIAL_STRING_LENGTH`), so at most on the order of 100 MB of string work in the worst case. Could remember the offset already scanned.

### `AnsiCode`

6. **A skipped sub-parameter token inside an extended-color sequence triggers a reset.** In `processSgrParameters()`, `ESC[38;4:3;1m` skips `4:3` while `extendedColor` is still 38, so the following `1` is taken as an unknown extended-color format and everything resets. Only reachable with a nonsense sequence (a sub-parameter can't legally sit between 38 and its `5`/`2` marker), and the reset is the safe outcome. Clearing the extended-color state when a token is skipped would keep the rest of the sequence effective.

title: Inspect the /upload streaming multipart driver for RFC accuracy
description:
Split out from #18727, per [this comment](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/18727#issuecomment-5717229753):

> Just because it can't have its implementation merged doesn't mean it shouldn't be touched. It if isn't going to be unified (sensible) it should be inspected for accuracy to the RFC.

The plan in #18727 for the **Duplicate implementation** item unifies only the two header-parsing
helpers in `SessionFiles.cpp` (`getBoundary`, `parseContentBuffer`) with `core/http/Util.cpp`, and
explicitly leaves the streaming driver `handleFileUploadRequestAsync`
(`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionFiles.cpp:1103`) alone, because it is a genuinely different
algorithm (chunk-at-a-time, payload written straight to a temp file) rather than a copy.

Not sharing the implementation is the right call, but it means the driver's own multipart handling
never gets reviewed against RFC 7578 / RFC 2046. This issue covers that review: read the driver
against the RFCs, fix what is actually wrong, and add regression tests.

### Things to check

Observations from reading the code -- these are starting points for the review, not a verified
defect list.

1. **Closing delimiter requires a trailing CRLF.** `:1266` searches for
   `"\r\n" + boundary + "--\r\n"`. RFC 2046 §5.1.1 makes the CRLF after the close-delimiter
   optional (an epilogue may follow, or nothing). A client that ends the body at `--boundary--`
   fails the `rfind` and gets "Invalid form data received - final end of form not found". This is
   the same class of terminator bug as the first item in #18727.

2. **Transport padding.** RFC 2046 allows linear whitespace between a boundary and its CRLF. Both
   delimiter searches (`:1241`, `:1266`) are exact string matches, so a padded boundary is missed.

3. **Quoted / parameterized boundary.** The driver gets its boundary from `getBoundary`
   (`:1085`), which takes everything after `boundary=` to the end of Content-Type. `boundary="X"`
   or `boundary=X; charset=utf-8` yields a garbage token. Already noted in the #18727 plan; the
   fix has to be carried into the driver's two call sites, which prepend `--` themselves.

4. **Fixed two-part shape and ordering.** The driver assumes the body is exactly a file part plus a
   `targetDirectory` part, in one of two orders, and decides which on the first chunk (`:1186`).
   RFC 7578 preserves ordering but does not promise a part count; extra or reordered parts should
   fail cleanly rather than mis-parse.

5. **Header parsing by substring search.** `parseContentBuffer` (`:1052`) matches
   `form-data; name="(.*)"` with a greedy regex, scans for `filename="` and stops at the first
   `"`, and locates the target directory value by searching the buffer for the literal
   `targetDirectory` (`:1069`) -- which can match inside a filename. RFC 7578 allows parameters in
   any order, arbitrary whitespace, case-insensitive names, and backslash escapes inside quoted
   strings.

6. **First-chunk assumption.** `:1187` asserts that upstream buffering guarantees all of the first
   part's headers are in the first chunk. Worth confirming against the actual upload handler
   buffering, and failing explicitly if not.

7. **Offset arithmetic.** `fileEndPos = pos - 1` at `:1252` and `:1279` underflows if `pos == 0`.

8. **Content-Transfer-Encoding.** RFC 7578 §4.7 says it must not be used, but it appears in the
   wild; the driver ignores the header entirely.

9. **`filename*` / percent-encoded filenames.** The separate filename-encoding item in #18727
   lands in the shared parser; check whether the driver's path picks it up or needs its own fix.

### Testing

There is currently no automated coverage of the `/upload` path -- no C++, no testthat, no
Playwright. Anything fixed here needs a test, which likely means factoring the delimiter/offset
logic far enough out of the async continuation to be driveable from a unit test, or adding an
end-to-end upload test. Manual verification through the Files pane should cover a plain file, a
zip (the unzip branch), and a filename containing a space and a quote.

### Out of scope

Unifying the driver with `core/http`'s multipart parser. That was considered in #18727 and
rejected; this issue is inspection and correction in place.

title: YAML autocompletion suggests incorrect 'category' (singular) instead of Quarto's 'categories' (plural); schema type should be array
description:
### System details
- **RStudio Edition**: Desktop
- **RStudio Version**:   `2025.09.1+401`
- **OS Version**:  Linux Mint
- **R Version**:  `4.3.3`
- **Quarto Version**: `1.7.33`

---
### Steps to reproduce the problem
1. **Create a new Quarto document**:
   - Open RStudio.
   - Go to `File → New File → Quarto Document` (any format, e.g., HTML).
2. **Trigger YAML autocompletion**:
   - In the YAML frontmatter, type `cat` and pause to let autocompletion suggest fields.
   - Observe the suggested field: `category:` (singular, string type).
3. **Verify incorrect behavior**:
   - Accept the suggestion (`category: "Test"`).
   - Render the document (e.g., "Render" button or `quarto render`).
   - **Result**: Quarto ignores `category:` (no error, but no effect).
4. **Manual correction**:
   - Replace `category: "Test"` with `categories: [Test]`.
   - Re-render. **Result**: Works correctly.

---
### Describe the problem in detail
RStudio’s YAML autocompletion suggests the **incorrect field** `category:` (singular, string) for Quarto documents (`.qmd`), but the [official Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/html.html#metadata) specifies that the correct field is `categories:` (plural, array).

**Root cause**:
The schema in RStudio’s internal YAML validator (`/opt/quarto/share/editor/tools/yaml/web-worker.js`, line ~16457) defines:
```json
{
  "name": "category",
  "schema": "string",
  "description": "The document category."
}

title: debugSource() throws a warning when getOption("keep.source") is FALSE
description:

> LINENO()
[1] NA
Warning message:
In structure(c(refs[[1]][1], refs[[1]][2], refs[[lastref]][3], refs[[lastref]][[4]],  :
  Calling 'structure(NULL, *)' is deprecated, as NULL cannot have attributes.
  Consider 'structure(list(), *)' instead.
> 
```

I think this is easily fixed in `.rs.makeSourceEquivFunction()`, right after `refs <- attr(content, "srcref")`, by adding something like:

```
    if (is.null(srcref))
        return(fun)
```

I'm not sure if this has any further implications for other functions in RStudio, but I'd imagine something similar could be added to those as well. Thank you!

title: Add "Copy Selection" keybinding entry in Modify Keyboard Shortcuts when Emacs keyboard shortcuts are selected.
description:
<!--

Thanks for taking the time to file a feature request! Please take the time to search for an existing feature request, to avoid creating duplicate requests. If you find an existing feature request, please give it a thumbs-up reaction, as we'll use these reactions to help prioritize the implementation of these features in the future.

If the feature has not yet been filed, then please describe the feature you'd like to see become a part of RStudio. See:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Writing-Good-Feature-Requests

for a guide on how to write good feature requests.

-->

### Problem Statement

When users choose to use emacs keybindings in Global Settings, there should be an option to modify a "Copy Selection" keybinding in the Modify Keyboard Shortcuts window.  Currently, there is no entry corresponding to "Copy Selection" in that window. This was mentioned a [few years ago](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/12957), but I don't think anything came of it.

Its absence can be verified by opening Modifying Keyboard Shortcuts, choosing a keybinding which currently has no specified inputs, and pressing "M-w". No conflict is raised.

More generally, it seems like because there is no "Copy Selection" keybinding, users who choose emacs keybindings are finding that `M-w` doesn't work, as reported in [2022](https://forum.posit.co/t/emacs-keybinding-meta-w-doesnt-save-or-copy-selection/149839) and [2023](https://forum.posit.co/t/emacs-keybindings-in-rstudio/169589) (and also reported in the issue linked above).

I observe that `M-w` works in RStudio Mac (2026.01.1 Build 403) but doesn't work in Rstudio Windows (2026.01.1 Build 403). I wonder if explicitly creating a "copy selection" entry would fix the "M-w not working" issue in Windows.

### Proposed Behaviour
> Describe the proposed behaviour which would solve the problem above.

When emacs keybindings are selected in Global Settings, an explicit keybinding entry corresponding to "Copy Selection" in the Modify Keyboard Shortcuts. 

### QA Notes

title: R diagnostics: warn about zero-padded '%s' format strings in sprintf()
description:
R's `sprintf()` passes format strings through to the C library, and the C standard leaves the `0` flag undefined for `%s` conversions. In practice, some C libraries zero-pad and others space-pad, so code like

```r
sprintf("%05s", "a")
```

produces `"0000a"` on some platforms and `"    a"` on others.

The R diagnostics engine should warn when a format string passed to `sprintf()` or `gettextf()` uses the `0` flag with `%s`, and suggest `formatC(x, width = n, flag = "0")` instead.

title: Git pane: list, open, create, and remove git worktrees
description:
Switching between git worktrees of the same repository is awkward in RStudio today. The Git pane's branch menu lists a branch that is checked out in another worktree as an ordinary entry, and selecting it fails with git's "already checked out at ..." error. Moving to that worktree means leaving the IDE, locating the directory, and opening its project by hand; creating or removing a worktree also means dropping to a terminal.

Proposed enhancement:

- The branch menu lists the repository's worktrees (from `git worktree list`), showing each one's branch and path, with the current worktree marked.
- Selecting a worktree opens it as an RStudio project in this window, or in a new session on Desktop and Workbench. If the worktree has no `.Rproj`, offer to create one.
- A branch that is checked out in another worktree is labelled as such, and selecting it opens that worktree instead of attempting a checkout.
- More > New Worktree... runs `git worktree add` for a new or existing branch, and New Branch can create its branch in a new worktree. More > Remove Worktree... runs `git worktree remove`.
- A project opened from a worktree is labelled with the primary checkout's name and the worktree directory (e.g. `rstudio [feature-x]`), so several worktrees of one project can be told apart in the window title and the Recent Projects list.

title: Tutorial pane should provide nagivation for tutorials by package
Load Vim key mappings from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vim/vimrc
description:
RStudio loads Vim key mappings from `~/.rstudio-vimrc` or `~/.vimrc` (#7350), but not from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vim/vimrc`, which Vim 9.1 supports. Users who keep their vim configuration under the XDG base directory get no mappings loaded.

RStudio should also check `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vim/vimrc` (or `~/.config/vim/vimrc` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset), after `~/.rstudio-vimrc` and `~/.vimrc`.

Implemented in #18689.

title: Use the bundled Posit Assistant when the administrator's selected.json names no version
description:
## Summary

#18998 reads administrator-installed Posit Assistant versions from `versions/` beside the bundled copy, chosen by the administrator's `selected.json`. When `selected.json` has no valid entry for the session's protocol, `selector::resolveSlot()` falls back to the newest verifying slot under `versions/`.

For the user's storage directory that fallback is right: RStudio writes those slots and repairs that selector itself. For the administrator's directory it means:

- Sessions can run a version the administrator never selected, for example after `selected.json` is deleted, damaged, or names a slot that was removed.
- There is no way back to the bundled copy short of deleting every slot newer than it. Removing the selection just hands sessions the newest slot instead.

## Proposed behavior

For the system storage directory only, the administrator tier contributes a candidate only when `selected.json` names a valid slot for the session's protocol. Otherwise it contributes nothing, and the bundled copy and the user's slot compete as they do today.

| Administrator's `selected.json` | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Missing | newest slot under `versions/` | bundled copy |
| Malformed | newest slot | bundled copy |
| Entry names a missing, failing, wrong-protocol or unusable slot | newest slot (logged) | bundled copy (logged) |
| Entry only for another protocol | newest slot for this protocol | bundled copy |
| Valid entry for this protocol | selected slot competes with the bundled copy | unchanged |

The user's storage directory is unchanged: it keeps the fallback and the repair.

With this change, removing the protocol's entry from `selected.json` is enough to return sessions to the bundled copy. rstudio/rstudio-pro will add a `rstudio-server upgrade posit-assistant select --bundled` command that does that.

## Changes

- `src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatSelector.hpp` / `.cpp`: add a resolution that returns only the recorded selection, or an empty path when it is missing or unusable, for example `selectedSlot(storageDir, protocol)`. `resolveSlot()` can use it for its first half. `SelectorRepair::Disabled` stays: `locatePositAssistantInstallation()` still uses it for the user directory when user installs are disabled (`ChatInstallation.cpp:272`). Its comment, which names the administrator's directory, needs updating.
- `src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatInstallation.cpp`, `rankedCandidates()` (lines 236-241): resolve the system storage directory with the selection-only variant, and update the comment ("a stale entry is resolved around and never rewritten"). `userInstallWouldBeSelected()` goes through `rankedCandidates()`, so it follows without its own change.
- `src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatInstallationTests.cpp`:
  - `ResolvesAroundAStaleAdminSelectorWithoutRewritingIt` and `ResolvesTheNewestAdminSlotWithoutCreatingASelector` should now expect the bundled copy (or nothing, without one), still without writing `selected.json`.
  - Add cases for a malformed administrator `selected.json` and for a selection of a slot serving another protocol.
- `src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatSelectorTests.cpp`: cover the selection-only variant: valid selection, missing file, malformed file, missing slot, unusable name, wrong protocol. The existing `ReadOnlyResolve*` tests still apply to `resolveSlot()`.
- `src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatSlots.hpp` and `ChatSelector.hpp`: in the header comments, note that rstudio-pro's upgrade CLI (`src/go/upgrade-cli/internal/assistant`) writes administrator slots and `selected.json` by these rules, so a change to slot names, the files a slot needs, `protocol.json`, the `selected.json` format, or how the administrator's selection is resolved needs a matching change there. The Go package already points back at these files. Requested in review of rstudio/rstudio-pro#13019.

Unchanged: a valid selection still competes with the bundled copy and the user's slot on protocol, then version, so a selection older than the bundled copy still does not run.

Right now, the global + project options are part of the Tools menu. However, by convention, macOS applications usually put their settings menu items within the primary application menu (the one matching the name of the application).

title: Posit Assistant backend log directory is unwritable in Workbench sessions
description:
Companion to https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/issues/2539.

### Problem

In Posit Workbench sessions, `positai.log` is never created. `SessionChat.cpp` launches the Posit Assistant backend with:

```cpp
args.push_back("--logger-type=file");
args.push_back("--log-dir=" + log::LogOptions::defaultLogDirectory().getAbsolutePath());
```

In a Pro build, `defaultLogDirectory()` always returns `RSTUDIO_DEFAULT_LOG_PATH` (`/var/log/rstudio/rstudio-server`, see `defaultLogPathImpl()` in `src/cpp/core/LogOptions.cpp`). That directory is owned by `rstudio-server` and the session user can't write to it. The backend's file logger fails silently, so no logs are written at all.

Open-source Server isn't affected only because the session runs as a non-root user, so the same call happens to return the user's XDG log directory.

### Proposed fix

Pass the directory rsession already uses for its own log:

```cpp
args.push_back("--log-dir=" + core::system::xdg::userLogDir().getAbsolutePath());
```

rsession initializes its log with `xdg::userLogDir()` (`SessionMain.cpp`), which is `~/.local/share/rstudio/log` by default, or under `XDG_DATA_HOME` if that's set. With this change, `positai.log` lands next to `rsession-<user>.log`, where the Workbench admin guide already points admins for session logs. It behaves the same way for Launcher/Kubernetes sessions, and the current support workflow of asking for `positai.log` keeps working.

### Alternative considered: `--logger-type=rstudio`

This would route backend logs to rsession over JSON-RPC (the `logger/log` notification handled by `handleLoggerLog`). It works mechanically today, but we aren't going with it for now:

- **Almost everything gets filtered out by default.** `handleLoggerLog` drops messages below `CHAT_BACKEND_MIN_LEVEL`, which defaults to `error`. Messages that pass that filter still have to clear rsession's own level, which defaults to `warn`. Getting useful detail means setting an environment variable in the session or raising rsession-wide logging. Both are awkward in Launcher sessions, and the second makes the rsession log noisy.
- **No per-section control.** Backend messages are logged with plain `ILOG`/`DLOG` and an `[ai]` text prefix, not a named log section. Admins can't raise the backend's level alone through `logging.conf`.
- **`--log-dir` still matters.** In `rstudio` mode the backend still keeps a file logger for its own connection and JSON-RPC client logging, so it needs a writable directory anyway.
- **It reverses an earlier choice.** #16754 deliberately switched the backend from rstudio logging to file logging.

Routing through rsession's logging could make sense later, once backend logs use a named section with a sensible default level. That's a separate change.

On the assistant side, posit-dev/assistant#2539 also covers checking that the log directory is writable and falling back if it isn't. That's worth doing regardless of what RStudio passes.

title: R diagnostics: give invalid characters a specific message instead of 'unexpected token'
description: A pasted smart quote, an unterminated raw string, or a lone `%` currently all produce a generic "unexpected token" diagnostic. A specific message (e.g. suggesting the straight quote) would make these much easier to fix.

title: R diagnostics: flag library() and require() calls for packages that are not installed
description: The editor offers to install missing packages via an info bar on save, but there is no inline diagnostic for `library(foo)` when `foo` is not installed. `character.only = TRUE` should be respected; `requireNamespace()` and `loadNamespace()` take strings (often variables) and the former is usually an availability check, so they should be excluded.

title: R diagnostics: flag 'if (x<-1)' where 'x < -1' was likely intended
description: `if (x<-1)` parses as an assignment of `1` to `x`. When `<-` is glued to both operands, the right-hand side is a numeric literal, and the expression is an `if` or `while` condition, the author almost certainly meant `x < -1`. `if (x <- foo())` is a legitimate idiom and should be left alone.

title: R diagnostics: flag a bare 'return' without parentheses
description: `if (x) return` evaluates to the `return` primitive rather than returning from the enclosing function, which is essentially never intended. The diagnostics system should warn, unless `return` is a variable in scope (grid has a formal named `return`).

title: R diagnostics: flag assignments to constants
description: `TRUE <- 1`, `1 <- x`, and `x -> NULL` all fail with "invalid (do_set) left-hand side to assignment" but are not reported by the diagnostics system. Strings remain valid targets (`"x" <- 1`).

title: R diagnostics: flag repeated formal arguments and named arguments matched more than once
description:
`function(x, x) {}` is a parse error in R, and `rnorm(n = 1, n = 2)` fails with "formal argument matched by multiple actual arguments". Neither is currently reported by the diagnostics system.

The second check should only fire on exact matches against a known formal; names absorbed by `...` (e.g. `c(a = 1, a = 2)`) are legal.
