title: rserver can't tell which session process a request outcome came from, so a predecessor's response can clear a new launch's pending entry
description:
### Summary

rserver avoids launching the same session twice by keeping a pending-launch entry per session context (`src/cpp/server/session/ServerSessionManager.cpp`), and it clears that entry when a request for the context succeeds or fails. It can't tell whether the outcome came from the process it just launched or from the one being replaced. A request answered by, or failing on, an exiting predecessor can therefore clear the new launch's entry, and the next request that finds the session unavailable launches it again.

Two guards cover parts of this:

- #18572: a request error keeps the entry while the launched process (by recorded pid) is alive.
- #18944: a `launching` flag keeps the entry, whatever the outcome, until the launch function returns.

Gaps that remain:

1. After the launch function returns, a *successful* response from the exiting predecessor still erases the entry; the #18572 guard only applies to errors.
2. `removePendingSessionLaunch(username, sessionId)`, the variant Workbench calls when forwarding launcher session RPCs, erases the entry unconditionally and ignores both guards.
3. (Minor) `endLaunching()` runs only if `sessionLaunchFunction_` returns normally. If it throws, the entry keeps `launching = true`, and relaunches for that context are suppressed until the one-minute pending window expires. A scope guard would fix this.

For server sessions on a local stream, #18944's session-side claim makes a duplicate exit early in startup, so the practical cost there is one wasted process launch. Sessions that don't listen on a local stream (such as Workbench launcher sessions) don't have that backstop.

### Possible fix

Only let an outcome from the launched process clear its entry, rather than adding a guard for each window. For example, compare the answering peer's pid (`SO_PEERCRED` / `getpeereid()` on the local stream) with the pid recorded for the pending launch, or stamp each launch with a generation that the session echoes back. Either would subsume both the #18572 guard and the `launching` flag.

Related: #18572, #18941, #18944.

title: Inactive source columns can hide commands for the active document
description:
With more than one source column open, a command refresh in an inactive column can hide or disable commands that belong to the active column's document.

### Steps

1. Open a second source column and open a saved `.R` file in it. Type into it so it has unsaved changes.
2. Click the main column and open a saved `.Rmd` file there. Publish is shown.
3. Run **File > Save All**.

Publish is now hidden, although the `.Rmd` in the main column is still the active document. It comes back when the main column's tab is clicked. This was reproduced in an e2e probe on the branch of #18950; nothing on this path is changed from main.

### Cause

`SourceColumn.manageCommands(forceSync, activeColumn)` runs for inactive columns too. Most calls pass `setCommand = active` to `SourceAppCommand.setVisible`/`setEnabled`, so an inactive column updates only its own toolbar button. Several don't: the one-argument `setVisible(x)` and `setEnabled(x)` expand to `setCommand = true` and write the shared command.

- `manageRSConnectCommands`: `setVisible(false)` on `rsconnectConfigure` and `rsconnectDeploy`
- `manageSynctexCommands`: `setVisible(false)` / `setEnabled(false)` on `synctexSearch`
- `manageRMarkdownCommands`: the same on `editRmdFormatOptions`
- `manageRunDocumentCommand`: `setVisible(active && ...)` on `runDocumentFromServerDotR`, `compileNotebook`, and `knitDocument`
- the `commandsToDisable` loop, for dynamic commands the column's previous editor supported (e.g. `renameSourceDoc`, `showActiveDocDirInFiles`)
- `activeEditor_.manageCommands()`, which the column calls for its own editor whether or not the column is active

Any refresh that runs in an inactive column alone hits this, for example:

- its per-document dirty-state handler (`SourceColumn.java`, `target.dirtyState().addValueChangeHandler`): Save All, or `rstudioapi::insertText(id = ...)` on a document in that column
- closing a tab in that column (`closeTabIndex`)
- the per-column `SynctexStatusChangedEvent` handler, where the inactive column's handler can run after the active one's (#18950 moved the `FileTypeChangedEvent` handler to `SourceColumnManager` for this reason)

Having inactive columns use only the `(setCommand = active, ...)` overloads, and skip `activeEditor_.manageCommands()`, would fix it at the source.

Raised in review of #18950.

title: Posit Assistant: GitHub Copilot provider unusable — isProviderAllowed("copilot") hardcoded to false, blocking the only Sign In entry point
description:
Summary
In the Posit Assistant "LLM Providers" panel, GitHub Copilot's only available action is Sign In (no "Configure" option, unlike other providers). Clicking Sign In always fails with:

Authentication Failed — Error: Provider "copilot" is not available on this platform

This is reproducible immediately after a full RStudio restart (fresh process, PATH re-read), so it's not a stale-session/PATH issue.

Environment
- RStudio Desktop 2026.07.1+147, Windows 11
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.73 (GitHub.Copilot via winget) — on PATH, working (copilot runs fine standalone)
- gh CLI 2.96.0 — authenticated (gh auth status OK)
- Node.js LTS v24.18.0 / npm 11.16.0 — on PATH
- @github/copilot@1.0.73 npm package — installed globally via npm install -g @github/copilot, confirmed present under %APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\@github\copilot

Root cause (found via inspection of bundled server)
Log file %LOCALAPPDATA%\RStudio\log\positai.log:

Failed to start device auth: Error: Provider "copilot" is not available on this platform
    at XI.startDeviceAuth (.../pai/bin/dist/server/main.js:2530:23650)

In C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\RStudio\pai\bin\dist\server\main.js (minified), the relevant logic is:

var DLr = new Set(["copilot"]);
function q6(t){ return !DLr.has(t) }          // q6("copilot") === false, always

isProviderAllowed(e){
  return q6(e)
    ? (this.catalogService ? this.catalogService.getProvider(e)?.enabled ?? false : Mu(e))
    : false;                                   // <-- "copilot" always returns false here
}

startDeviceAuth(e){
  let r = this.resolveProviderConfig(e);
  return r
    ? this.isProviderAllowed(e)
      ? ...
      : Promise.reject(new Error(`Provider "${e}" is not available on this platform`))
    : Promise.reject(new Error(`Unknown provider: ${e}`));
}

"copilot" is unconditionally present in the DLr blocklist Set, so isProviderAllowed("copilot") always returns false, and the OAuth device-auth Sign In flow can never succeed, on any OS/config.

The provider catalog entry confirms it's still marked experimental:
providerId: "copilot", authMethodId: "oauth", experimental: true,
setupInstructions: "Requires the GitHub Copilot CLI to be installed."

There also appears to be an intended alternate runtime path that spawns the CLI headlessly (copilot --headless --no-auto-update --log-level warning --port 0, via registerModelFetcher("copilot", ...) / registerClientFactory("copilot", ...)), relying on credentials the CLI/gh already has rather than Posit's own OAuth store — but nothing in the LLM Providers UI currently exercises this path independent of the blocked Sign In flow, and there is no "Configure" button for Copilot as there is for other providers.

Steps to reproduce
1. Install GitHub Copilot CLI (winget GitHub.Copilot) and @github/copilot npm package globally; authenticate gh auth login.
2. Fully restart RStudio.
3. Tools -> Global/Project Options (or AI panel) -> LLM Providers -> GitHub Copilot -> Sign In.
4. Observe: "Authentication Failed — Error: Provider 'copilot' is not available on this platform" every time.

Expected behavior
Either:
- The Sign In / device-auth flow should succeed and register Copilot credentials, or
- If Copilot is intended to work via the headless CLI spawn path only, the UI should expose a "Configure"/"Detect" action for it (as it does for other local/CLI-based providers) instead of an always-failing "Sign In" button.

Actual behavior
Copilot cannot be activated through any UI path in this build; the blocklist Set (DLr) unconditionally excludes "copilot" from isProviderAllowed, regardless of installed tooling or authentication state.

title: Read administrator Posit Assistant installs only from posit-assistant-path, and let it win
description:
### Current behavior

A session looks for an administrator-provided Posit Assistant in two ways, and neither is what administrators need:

- **An implicit default location.** `<systemConfigDir>/pai` (`/etc/rstudio/pai` on Linux, `C:/ProgramData/rstudio/pai` on Windows) is always searched. Since #18892 that means its `versions/` slots through `selected.json` and its legacy unversioned `bin/`, on Server and Desktop alike. Whatever is there competes by version (#18774) with the user's own copy and the bundled copy, even though no administrator ever configured it.
- **`posit-assistant-path` in `rsession.conf`** (#18687, shipped in 2026.09). It pins one *unversioned* installation directory. It cannot use the `versions/` + `selected.json` layout, so an administrator who configures it gives up side-by-side installs and choosing a version.

Relevant code, all in `src/cpp/session/modules/chat/` unless noted:

- `ChatInstallation.hpp`: `InstallSearchPaths` (`systemStorageDir`, `pinnedPath`), plus the doc comments on `InstallSearchPaths` and `locatePositAssistantInstallation(const InstallSearchPaths&)`.
- `ChatInstallation.cpp`: `positAssistantSearchPaths()`, `systemSlot()`, `legacySystemInstall()`, `rankedCandidates()`, `locatePositAssistantInstallation(const InstallSearchPaths&)`, `userInstallWouldBeSelected(const InstallSearchPaths&, ...)`.
- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp`: the "installation not found" messages, which name `<systemConfigDir>/pai/bin` or the pinned path.
- `src/cpp/session/session-options.json`: the `posit-assistant-path` description.
- `src/cpp/session/include/session/SessionModuleContext.hpp`: the comment on `isPositAssistantInstallationEnabledByAdmin()`.

### Expected behavior

An administrator-provided installation exists only when an administrator configures one with `posit-assistant-path`. When they do, it always runs.

#### When `posit-assistant-path` is unset

`<systemConfigDir>/pai` is not read at all: not its `versions/`, `selected.json`, or `bin/`. The only sources are:

1. the user's slots (`<userDataDir>/pai/versions` via `<userDataDir>/pai/selected.json`), skipped when user installation is disabled (`posit-assistant-installation-enabled=0` / `RSTUDIO_DISABLE_POSIT_ASSISTANT_INSTALLATION`);
2. the bundled copy (only Workbench ships one; open-source Server, Desktop and Desktop Pro do not).

They compete under the existing #18774 rules: a compatible protocol first, then the highest version, with ties going to the user's copy.

Desktop doesn't read `rsession.conf`, so on Desktop the option is never set, and there is no bundled copy there. Desktop therefore runs only the user's own copy. That needs no Desktop-specific code; it follows from the rules above.

#### When `posit-assistant-path` is set to a directory `P`

`P` supplies the administrator's candidates:

- **Slots:** `P/versions/<slot>`, resolved with `selector::resolveSlot(P, kProtocolVersion, SelectorRepair::Disabled)`. The slot named by `P/selected.json` is used when it verifies. Otherwise the newest verifying slot for this protocol is used, and `P/selected.json` is never written.
- **`P` itself as a single installation directory** (the directory containing `dist`, checked with `verifyInstallDir()`). This keeps 2026.09 configurations working. `P/bin` is not read.

If both exist, they compete with each other under the #18774 rules (compatible protocol, then version; ties go to the slot).

**If `P` contributes a candidate, the best one runs. Nothing else is considered.** It beats the user's copy and the bundled copy whatever their versions, which lets an administrator hold users on a version older than the bundled one. The user's copy is ignored (not removed) even when user installation is enabled; keep the existing once-per-session warning when one exists. If the administrator's copy declares a different protocol, it still runs, and the session reports the protocol mismatch as it does for any incompatible install. It does not fall back to another copy.

#### When `P` holds no valid installation

`P` holds no valid installation when it contributes no candidate: it doesn't exist, is empty, or contains neither a verifying slot for this build's protocol nor a directory that passes `verifyInstallDir()`. (An empty option value means the option is unset.)

- The bundled copy is **not** considered. A typo or an unmounted share must not quietly run whatever version shipped with Workbench.
- The user's slot is still used when user installation is enabled (as `UsesUserSlotWhenPinnedPathIsInvalid` asserts today): the user's own install is not a silent downgrade.
- Log a warning once per session naming `P`.
- Otherwise Posit Assistant is reported as not installed.

#### Update and reinstall offers

`userInstallWouldBeSelected()` returns false whenever `P` contributes a candidate (the user's install could never run). When `P` is invalid, it is true if user installation is enabled. When `P` is unset, the user's install competes against the bundled copy as today.

#### "Installation not found" messages (`SessionChat.cpp`)

These can no longer point at `<systemConfigDir>/pai/bin`:

- `P` set: name `P` as the expected location, in both the managed and the unmanaged message.
- `P` unset, installation managed: say installation is managed by the administrator and none has been configured. Don't name a path.
- `P` unset, installation enabled: tell the user to install it from the Posit Assistant pane. Drop the "or have an administrator install it at …" clause.

### Compatibility

This drops the default location that 2026.09 and earlier read. Both of these need a NEWS entry:

- Server administrators who populated `/etc/rstudio/pai/bin` must set `posit-assistant-path=/etc/rstudio/pai/bin`, which is the unversioned-directory form. Pointing it at `/etc/rstudio/pai` reads slots under `/etc/rstudio/pai/versions` instead.
- Desktop no longer reads an administrator-provided copy from `<systemConfigDir>/pai`. Users install their own.

### Implementation notes

- Replace `InstallSearchPaths::systemStorageDir` and `pinnedPath` with a single administrator directory (`P`, empty when unset). Don't keep the old fields alongside it. `systemSlot()` and `legacySystemInstall()` become the slot and unversioned lookups against `P`.
- `rankedCandidates()` / `locatePositAssistantInstallation()`: when `P` is set, return the best of `P`'s candidates, or fall through to the user slot alone. When it is unset, rank the user slot against the bundled copy. Update the "No valid AI installation found" debug listing to match.
- Remove anything left unused. For example, check whether `kLegacyInstallDirName` is still needed outside the test that asserts the user's legacy `pai/bin` is never read.
- Rewrite the doc comments on `InstallSearchPaths`, `locatePositAssistantInstallation()`, `rankedCandidates()`, and `isPositAssistantInstallationEnabledByAdmin()` (which says a disabled install uses "only an administrator-managed installation"; it can also be the bundled copy).
- `session-options.json`: rewrite the `posit-assistant-path` description. It is the directory holding the administrator-provided Posit Assistant, either versioned installs under `versions` selected by `selected.json`, or a single installation directory (the one containing `dist`). When it holds a valid installation, that installation is always used. Regenerate `SessionOptions.gen.hpp`.

### Tests

`ChatInstallationTests.cpp` has many tests that stage installations in `systemStorageDir` or `legacySystemDir()`, or set `pinnedPath`. Each needs rewriting against `P`, or deleting where it covers behavior that no longer exists (a default-location copy competing by version):

`FallsBackToSystemSlot`, `FallsBackToLegacySystemInstallation`, `FollowsTheSystemSelector`, `ResolvesAroundAStaleSystemSelectorWithoutRewritingIt`, `PrefersNewerSystemSlotOverStaleUserSlot`, `PrefersNewerLegacySystemOverStaleUserSlot`, `PrefersNewestInstallation`, `PrefersCompatibleProtocolOverHigherVersion`, `FallsBackToHighestVersionWhenNoneIsCompatible`, `TreatsMissingProtocolFileAsIncompatible`, `RanksVersionlessInstallationLowest`, `BreaksVersionTiesBySource`, `SkipsUserSlotsWhenInstallsAreManaged`, `PinnedInstallationWinsOverNewerUserSlot`, `UsesUserSlotWhenPinnedPathIsInvalid`, `SkipsReadOnlySourcesWhenSystemPathIsPinned`, `FindsPinnedInstallationWhenInstallsAreManaged`, `UserInstallWouldBeSelectedOverVersionlessReadOnlyInstall`, `UserInstallWouldNotBeSelectedBelowNewerSystemSlot`, `UserInstallWouldNotBeSelectedUnderValidPinnedPath`, `ChatInstallation.BundledPathSkipsIncompleteBinSubdirectory`, `ChatInstallationHeld.DoesNotRunUserSlotForReadOnlyCopies`, `ChatInstallationHeld.ReportsNothingForALegacyInstallWithoutProtocol`.

`ChatStaticFilesTests.cpp` sets `pinnedPath` to serve one installation (`ChatStaticFilesResolution::serve()` and `ServesFromTheHeldInstallationUntilItIsCleared`). Switch these to `P` as an unversioned directory.

Cases the suite must cover:

- `P` unset: copies at the default `<systemConfigDir>/pai` (slots and `bin/`) are never used, even when nothing else exists; the user slot and the bundled copy compete by version, with ties going to the user.
- A slot under `P` selected by `P/selected.json` resolves; a stale or unusable selection falls back to the newest verifying slot without rewriting `P/selected.json`.
- `P` itself as a 2026.09-style unversioned install resolves; `P/bin` is not read.
- `P` holding both a slot and an unversioned install: the higher compatible version wins, and on a tie the slot wins.
- A valid `P` beats a newer compatible bundled copy and a newer user slot, with user installation enabled or disabled.
- A valid `P` whose only candidate has a mismatched protocol still runs rather than falling back.
- `P` nonexistent, empty, or holding only slots for another protocol: bundled is not used; the user slot is used when enabled; nothing resolves when user installation is disabled.
- `userInstallWouldBeSelected()`: false under a valid `P` regardless of version; true when `P` is invalid and installation is enabled; false when installation is disabled; ranked against bundled when `P` is unset.

### Docs

- `NEWS.md`, 2026.10 section: add an entry for this change, including the two compatibility points above. Also revise the unreleased entries it contradicts. The #18658 entry says "An administrator can provide the same layout under the system configuration directory", and the #18774 entry lists "installed system-wide" among the competing copies and says a per-user copy "no longer shadows a newer bundled or system-wide copy".
- The Workbench administrator documentation is maintained separately and will be updated to match.

### Verification

Build, then run the chat unit tests, for example as #18892 did:

```
GTEST_FILTER='Chat*' ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession
```

title: Install Posit Assistant side-by-side in versioned directories
description:
### Problem

Posit Assistant installs to a single shared directory per source, which every session using that source runs from. Because there is one directory, updating it mutates something other sessions may be executing from.

For the user's own install (`<userDataDir>/pai/bin`), #18276 addressed the resulting corruption with cross-session file locks, but the coordination is a refusal: an update fails while another session is running the assistant, and the user is told to close their other RStudio instances.

The administrator's install (`<systemConfigDir>/pai/bin`) has the same problem with no coordination at all. RStudio never writes there, but that does not make the directory immutable -- the package manager replaces it, and it does so while sessions are running. An in-place replace does not merely risk corruption:

- Client assets are read from the installation on every request (`servedInstallationPath()` in `ChatStaticFiles.cpp`). Since #18832 the session pins the installation it serves, but the pin is a path, not bytes: content-hashed chunks are fetched from disk long after the pane loaded, and replacing the tree under the pinned path makes the loaded page ask for filenames that no longer exist.
- The Content-Security-Policy is rebuilt when the pinned installation changes or the backend starts (#18833). A third party replacing the directory in place triggers neither, so a new client is served under the old package's policy.
- The backend keeps the files it has already opened, but anything it imports later comes from the new tree.

So an administrator rolling out a new version has to get every user out of the assistant first, which means draining or restarting sessions across the deployment. That is the cost this issue exists to remove, and today it falls on the party least able to accept it.

The single directory has a second consequence. It maps a protocol version to exactly one package version, and RStudio's supported protocol is compiled in (`kProtocolVersion`, currently `11.0`). Two RStudio releases on different protocols sharing a home compete for the one install: the older sees the newer package as a protocol mismatch, computes its own protocol's package as an available install, and prompts to replace it -- after which the newer prompts to replace it back.

### Proposal

Install each package version into its own directory ("slot"), append-only: slots are created, never modified or deleted. Because no operation touches a directory another session could be executing from, the corruption #18276 coordinated against becomes unrepresentable, and no cross-session locking is needed at all.

```
<userDataDir>/pai/               <systemConfigDir>/pai/
├── versions/1.1.0/              ├── versions/1.1.0/    # slots and selector
├── versions/1.1.0-2/            ├── versions/1.0.4/    # both written by the
├── versions/1.0.4/              ├── selected.json      # administrator,
├── selected.json                │                      # never by RStudio
├── manifest-check.json          └── bin/               # legacy; still read
└── bin/                         # legacy; never read, written, or deleted
```

The storage root stays `pai/`; only the backend's working directory (today `pai/bin`) becomes the slot.

**Slots.** The first install of a version gets the plain name (`1.1.0`); a fresh slot for the same version appends an ordinal (`1.1.0-2`). Names carry no version or protocol identity -- `1.1.0-2` is valid semver that sorts *before* 1.1.0, and `SemanticVersion::parse` rejects it outright -- so both always come from `package.json` and `protocol.json` inside the slot. The one thing read from a name is the reinstall ordinal, and only to order slots whose `package.json` versions are equal (`slotOrdinal()` in `ChatSelector.cpp`; a name not derived from the version scores 0). A slot name must never be passed to the version parser or reported as a version.

**Selector.** `selected.json` holds `{"selected": {"11.0": "1.1.0-2", "10.0": "0.4.8"}}` -- slot names keyed by protocol, so RStudio releases on different protocols no longer compete. It is advisory: if the named slot is missing, fails verification, or declares a different protocol, resolution falls back to the newest verifying slot for the protocol, ties broken by the later reinstall ordinal, then by name as a last resort so the answer is stable. Written temp-then-rename; concurrent writers are last-writer-wins, and a dropped entry self-heals through the same fallback.

In the user's directory the fallback also **repairs** the entry. The administrator's directory carries the same `selected.json`, in the same format and with the same meaning, but RStudio never writes there: the administrator's tooling records the selection when it installs a version (a separate work item), and a system selector naming a missing or unverifying slot resolves through the fallback **without being rewritten**. `selector::resolveSlot()` as merged in #18666 always repairs, so it needs a read-only mode (or a sibling) for the system tier; today's best-effort write would fail and warn on every resolve against a read-only `/etc/rstudio`.

### Resolution

#18774 established the rule and it does not change here: the sources contribute candidates that race by what they declare -- protocol-compatible first, then highest version, ties in source order (user, system, bundled) -- and `posit-assistant-path` sits outside the race, used outright when it verifies and ending the read-only search when it does not. `userInstallWouldBeSelected()` keeps gating the update offer. What each source contributes is what changes:

1. **User** (`pai/versions`, the only writable source): the slot `selected.json` names for `kProtocolVersion`, or the fallback above. One candidate, so a manifest that serves a lower version for this protocol (`isVersionDowngrade`) still decides what runs. Skipped entirely when `userInstallEnabled` is false (#18691). Because the selector is keyed by protocol, this source never contributes an incompatible slot: after an RStudio upgrade to a new protocol the user tier reads as *not installed* and the update check takes the initial-install path (fetching immediately, since `shouldFetchManifest()` never throttles when nothing is installed). The protocol-mismatch messaging (`hasProtocolMismatch()`, `unsupportedProtocol`) stays reachable only through the read-only sources.
2. **System** (`<systemConfigDir>/pai/versions`): the slot the administrator's `selected.json` names, or the same fallback, resolved but not rewritten. This is how an administrator chooses which installed version a deployment runs -- including holding users on an older slot while a newer one sits beside it -- without RStudio writing to a directory it does not own.
3. **System legacy** (`<systemConfigDir>/pai/bin`): one unversioned candidate, as today. It is what deployments have today and RStudio does not own it. Until the admin's package adopts `versions/`, an in-place replace keeps breaking live sessions exactly as it does now -- that is the migration cost, and it is the package's to pay.
4. **Bundled**: a single directory beside the session binary, unchanged.

`posit-assistant-path` stays an unversioned single installation directory ("the directory containing the installation's `dist` directory", as the option documents it). An administrator who wants side-by-side uses `<systemConfigDir>/pai/versions`; teaching the option to accept a `versions/` root as well is deferred.

The user's legacy `pai/bin` is **never** read, written, or deleted. Older RStudio releases still mutate it, unaware of the versioned layout, so reading it would re-import the problem this issue removes, and copying it into a slot would record a manifest of whatever another release had left there. A versioned-aware release does a fresh install into `pai/versions/`. The user-visible consequence: on first launch of the versioned-aware release, a user with a working `pai/bin` is prompted to install (initial-install wording, ~18 MB download) once; the old copy keeps serving any older RStudio release that shares the home.

**The bundled copy stays a single directory.** Only the Workbench package produces one (`bundledPositAssistantInstallPath()` derives it from `resourcePath()`; nothing in this repository installs it), and replacing it means replacing the session binaries beside it, which takes that node's sessions down. Its lifecycle is the RStudio install's -- one RStudio version ships one bundled assistant -- so versioning it would imply an independence it does not have.

**Resolve once per session.** A session resolves the installation once, lazily on first need, and every consumer reads that one answer: the backend start (`startChatBackend()`), the agent start (`paiLanguageServerPath()` in `SessionAssistant.cpp`), the asset handler and its CSP (today's `staticfiles::setInstallationPath()` pin, which becomes a reader of the shared resolution rather than a second pin), and installed-version and protocol reporting (`getInstalledVersion()`, `getInstalledProtocolVersion()`, `chat_verify_installed`, `chat_get_backend_status`). The pinned path is re-validated with the cheap existence check on each read, as `servedInstallationPath()` does today, so a slot removed out of band falls back to a fresh resolution. It is cleared by exactly one thing: this session's own successful install, so the components it restarts come back on the new slot. An install elsewhere -- another session, an administrator -- takes effect at this session's next start. The update check compares the manifest against the pinned version, so a session still running an older slot after another session installed a newer one is offered the update, and accepting it skips the download (below) and just re-selects.

### Install

Download -> verify SHA-256 -> extract to a staging directory under `pai/versions/` -> check the extracted package's identity -> `allocateSlot()` (write the slot manifest, verify, rename into place) -> update the selector -> stop and restart the backend and agent. Staging and final slot are siblings so the rename is atomic. The manifest is written before verification because verification includes checking it.

The identity check compares the extracted `package.json` version and `protocol.json` protocol against the manifest entry that was downloaded. A mis-published package would otherwise publish under another protocol's selector entry -- changing what a different RStudio release resolves -- and report an update this session cannot run. A package without `protocol.json` fails this check and is refused; `writeProtocolVersionFileIfMissing()`, which backfilled RStudio's compiled-in protocol into `pai/bin`, is deleted rather than carried into the staging step.

If the target version already exists in a verifying slot that declares the same version and protocol, skip the download and just update the selector. Concurrent installs of the same version race on the rename: the loser adopts the now-existing target when it verifies *and* declares the same version and protocol (`SlotPolicy::AdoptExisting`), otherwise bumps the suffix and renames again -- a directory's name is never taken as evidence of what it holds. The `ai.prev` backup and every restore branch in `installPackage()` are deleted: a slot only reaches its final name after verification, so a torn install cannot exist under a final name. The Windows access-denied message ("close all other instances of RStudio and try again") goes with them; it described a directory swap losing to another session's open handles, which no longer happens.

Staging directories are unique per install (`.tmp-<host>-<pid>-<nonce>`) and are never cleared. Two sessions sharing an NFS home can compute the same pid-based name -- under container runtimes they routinely do, each session pod having its own PID namespace -- and clearing that name would delete another session's half-extracted tree. The victim would then record a manifest describing the damage, verify it against itself, and publish a truncated slot that keeps verifying for the rest of its life.

Because nothing on disk is mutated, the backend and agent are stopped **after** the install succeeds rather than before it. Stopping is only about picking up the new version, so a failed install leaves a working assistant running, and the reap-wait (`waitForOwnComponentsReaped()`) with its "a process is still shutting down" failure path in `performInstall()` goes away.

### Verification

Today's check (`verifyPositAiInstallation()`) only tests that three paths exist; a zero-byte `main.js` passes. Slot verification (`slots::verifySlot()`, merged) is: the expected paths exist and are non-empty, `package.json` parses with a `version`, `protocol.json` parses with a `protocol`, and every file in the slot's manifest exists with its recorded size. The manifest (relative path -> size, plus SHA-256s recorded for future use but not routinely checked) is written after extraction, when the tree is known to match the verified zip. A slot with no manifest does not verify: every published slot has one, so its absence means no install ran to completion there. The stat walk is milliseconds even on NFS homes. What escapes detection is correct-size garbage -- which is what Reinstall is for.

Unversioned sources (`posit-assistant-path`, the administrator's legacy directory, the bundled copy) carry no manifest and are not named for a version, so they get the paths-exist-and-are-non-empty check and nothing more. What they declare is reported downstream to the update check rather than gating them here. `verifyPositAiInstallation()` and the `package.json`/`protocol.json` readers in `ChatInstallation.cpp` are replaced by that check and the slot readers -- including at their callers in `bundledPositAssistantInstallPath()` and `servedInstallationPath()` -- so two definitions of "valid install" never coexist.

### Reinstall

When the manual check (`Check for Posit Assistant Updates`) finds installed and available versions equal, the result dialog offers Reinstall instead of only reporting nothing to do. The startup check is unchanged. It is the ordinary install path with two changes: the skip-if-verifies shortcut is bypassed, and it never adopts an existing slot -- `SlotPolicy::AlwaysFresh`, so on a rename collision it always bumps the suffix and the user provably gets fresh bits. The old slot is left in place (another session may be running from it) and stops being selected. This is the in-product recovery for corruption that passes verification, and it deletes nothing, so it needs no locking.

Surface: the update state keeps the manifest's download URL and SHA-256 for the current protocol even when no update is available, `chat_install_update` takes a reinstall flag that bypasses the "No update available" guard, and the presenter's `onNoUpdateAvailable` path becomes a dialog with a Reinstall button (en and fr strings; `_fr.properties` is hand-maintained). Managed mode refuses it the way it refuses install and update.

### Uninstall is removed

The `uninstallPositAssistant` command and the `chat_uninstall_posit_assistant` RPC go away, with their menu entry, `Commands.java` stub, en/fr strings, presenter handling, the `PaneManager` carve-out that keeps the command visible, the `uninstall-posit-ai.test.ts` Playwright test, and the "Removing Posit Assistant" section of `docs/user/rstudio/ide/guide/tools/posit-ai.qmd`. That section is **replaced, not just deleted**: the same PR documents how to remove every Posit Assistant installation by hand, with RStudio closed -- the user data `pai/` directory on each platform (`~/.local/share/rstudio/pai`, `~/Library/Application Support/rstudio/pai` where applicable, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\rstudio\pai`), noting that it holds `versions/`, `selected.json`, the legacy `bin/`, and the assistant's own storage, and that the administrator's copy under `<systemConfigDir>/pai` and the copy bundled with RStudio are not the user's to remove. Detectable corruption self-heals via the selector fallback, undetectable corruption is handled by Reinstall, and removing the assistant from disk has no in-product path until the manage-installs work below. #18662 did this once and #18679 reverted it; since then #18691 (managed-mode refusal), #18815 (bundled-vs-system refusal wording) and #18832 (unpinning the served installation) have all changed the handler, so this is a re-implementation against current `main`, with #18662 as the checklist of what to touch.

### Locking is removed

`ChatInstallLock.{hpp,cpp}` and its tests (~1,700 lines) are deleted, along with the `installLock()` accessor in `SessionChat.hpp`, the `MutationScope` call site in `performInstall()`, the in-use acquire/release around the backend start in `SessionChat.cpp` and the agent start in `SessionAssistant.cpp` (three call sites each), and the #18790 owner-id fix that lives inside the lock. Every mutation is create-only into a directory nothing can be using, so the rename is the only arbiter concurrent writers need. Two fixes from #18276 that are not about locking must survive, both in `SessionAssistant.cpp`: the `onError` handling that no longer clears agent tracking state on a stream error, and the `setenv` (replace, not append) helper launch environment.

### Deferred

- **Managing installs.** Slots accumulate (~18 MB each) and install reclaims nothing, so `.tmp-*` directories from interrupted installs, superseded slots and corrupt slots remain until a future effort covering retention, deletion of unused slots, and removing the assistant entirely. That work needs a per-slot "in use" signal (a slot can be running-but-unselected), which is where a successor to the #18276 lock machinery would return. Until then there is no in-product way to reclaim the disk.
- **System-tier retention.** An ordinary package upgrade removes the version it replaces, so side-by-side requires the administrator's tooling to keep N versions instead. Pruning them safely needs the same in-use signal, so that side has to decide retention explicitly rather than inherit the default of removing what it replaces. Read support here does not depend on it: a system directory holding one slot behaves like today's single install.
- **`posit-assistant-path` as a versions root.** The option keeps naming one unversioned installation. Accepting a directory holding `versions/` and `selected.json` would give a pinned shared-mount deployment side-by-side too; small once the system source exists, but not needed for the first release.
- **Slot blacklisting on runtime failure.** The strongest corruption detector is the backend repeatedly failing to launch from a slot, but a backend can die for reasons that are not corruption, and wrongly blacklisting a good slot is worse. Reinstall covers the need manually.

### Decisions and assumptions

- **Downgrade to a user-chosen version is out of scope.** The layout permits it and the selector is the hard part, so a picker can be added later without rework.
- **Lost-selection downgrade is accepted, not made durable.** `selectSlot()` is an unserialized read-modify-write, so two sessions recording different protocols at once can drop an entry, and the repair converges on the *newest* verifying slot, not on what the entry said. With `isVersionDowngrade` wired to slots, a lost entry can resolve *up* to a newer slot the same protocol already accepted. It needs two sessions on different protocols installing in the same instant, and the next update check re-selects the manifest's version with no download. Making it durable would mean serializing the selector write (locking, which this effort exists to remove) or recording intent inside the slot (retention policy, deferred).
- **After an RStudio protocol bump the user tier reads as not installed** (Resolution, source 1). The alternative -- surfacing the old slot as an incompatible candidate -- would keep the "update required" wording for one release at the cost of re-introducing the two-releases-compete loop the selector exists to end.
- **Existing users re-download once** (Resolution, legacy `pai/bin`).
- **Concurrent mixed-version access to the shared store is assumed safe.** Side-by-side installs mean sessions can run different assistant versions against the same `pai/` storage -- by user action today, and as an operational certainty once Workbench bundles the assistant (rstudio/rstudio-pro#12483), where a rolling cluster upgrade briefly runs different bundled versions against one NFS-shared home. Posit Assistant is expected to tolerate this.

### Implementation sequence

State today (2026-09-21): the slot machinery landed inert in #18666 (`ChatSlots`, `ChatSlotManifest`, `ChatSelector`; nothing calls them). The uninstall removal landed (#18662) and was reverted (#18679). The wiring PR #18673 was closed unmerged; its branch `feature/pai-versioned-installs-wire` is four commits on a 2026-08-28 base, and the resolver, static-file handler and CSP code it rewrote have since been rewritten again by #18691, #18815, #18832 and #18833. Treat the branch as a reference for shape (three self-contained source functions, the identity check, `e2e/rstudio/fixtures/pai-seed.ts`), not as something to rebase.

1. **Remove uninstall** -- re-implemented against `main` (see above), including the user-guide section on manual removal that replaces the command. No dependency on the new layout; every later PR gets smaller once it is gone. NEWS entry: this removes a shipped command and should point at the manual-removal documentation.
2. **Slot machinery** -- done in #18666. Two changes land with PR 3: the read-only resolve for the system tier (Selector, above), and removing the prerelease and build-metadata handling from `preferredOver()` in `ChatSelector.cpp` (`releasePortion()`, `hasPrerelease()`, and the four tests that pin them). Posit Assistant versions are plain `x.y.z` and every other parser site rejects a suffixed version, so the selector must not be the one place that accepts one. What remains is: parse version, compare, then ordinal, then name. A re-review of the merged code (2026-09-21) found three more small items to take at the same time, none a correctness bug:
   - **Retry the publish rename** in `allocateSlot()` (`ChatSlots.cpp:359`). On Windows, antivirus or the indexer briefly holds a handle inside a freshly extracted tree and `MoveFileEx` fails with access denied; today that returns the error and orphans the staging directory. A bounded retry when the target does not exist turns a spurious failure into a success. The old install path had the same exposure behind the "close all other instances" message this PR deletes.
   - **Cap the hostname in the staging name at 32, not 180** (`ChatSlots.cpp:136`). The nonce carries uniqueness; the long cap only risks pushing deep `dist/client/assets/` paths past `MAX_PATH` during extraction on Windows.
   - **Filter `verifiedSlots()` by `isUsableSlotName()`** (`ChatSlots.cpp:268`). It skips only dot-prefixed entries, while `resolveSlot()` rejects a selection that fails `isUsableSlotName()`, so a hand-made directory with a trailing space is recorded, rejected on the next read, and recorded again on every resolve.
   - **Add a test** that `resolveSlot()` still returns the fallback when the storage directory is unwritable. The read-only system tier depends on that best-effort claim and nothing exercises it. The lost-rename-race branch (`ChatSlots.cpp:372`) has no test either and needs an injection hook to get one; acceptable to leave.
3. **Wire it: resolver sources + install path rewrite.** The one behavior-changing PR. `rankedCandidates()` gains the two slot sources, each read through its own `selected.json`; `installPackage()`/`performInstall()` become download -> stage -> identity check -> publish -> select -> restart; the `ai.prev` backup, the stop-before-install reap-wait and `writeProtocolVersionFileIfMissing()` come out; the single per-session resolution replaces the per-call resolves and the separate static-file pin; the selector gains its read-only mode and loses its prerelease handling (PR 2, above). `verifyPositAiInstallation()` and the `package.json`/`protocol.json` readers are replaced, not left beside the slot equivalents. The e2e sandbox provisioning (`PW_SEED_PAI`, today copied to `data-home/pai` with `bin/`) is laid out as a slot with a manifest and a selector, the version-under-test report follows the selector, and the per-spec data home must not write into the shared seed (today `pai` is symlinked per spec, so an install test would publish a slot into the seed every other spec reads). NEWS entry.
4. **Delete the locking.** After PR 3, `ChatInstallLock` is vestigial. A separate PR keeps PR 3 reviewable, is independently revertible, and forces the explicit check that #18276's two non-locking fixes survive.
5. **Reinstall** -- the forced-install path plus the dialog change for the installed-equals-available case. NEWS entry.

PRs 1-4 are a unit from the user's perspective and must ship in the same release; PR 5 only has to make that release. rstudio/rstudio-pro#12483's bundled install rule is independent of this and already landed on the OSS side (#18690).

### Testing

Each PR updates the e2e Playwright tests it impacts as part of the same change (uninstall-command tests with the removal; sandbox provisioning and install/update assertions with the wiring; new coverage with Reinstall), alongside unit tests for the slot, selector and verification code:

```
GTEST_FILTER='Chat*:SessionAssistant*:PositAssistant*' ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession
```
