title: removeLogDestination leaves a destination in sections it shares with other destinations
description: With an empty section, `log::removeLogDestination()` walks `SectionedLogDestinations` by value (`for (auto secIter: ...)`, `src/cpp/shared_core/Logger.cpp:948`), so the `erase` only changes the copy. A destination that shares a section with other destinations stays registered there and keeps receiving that section's messages. A section it was alone in is removed correctly, via `sectionsToRemove`. Fix: loop by reference. Found reviewing #18900.

title: git --version is probed redundantly at startup, and s_gitVersion goes stale when the git path pref changes
description:
After #18751, `initGitBin()` (`SessionGit.cpp:3370`) and `isGitInstalled()` (`SessionGit.cpp:3180`) issue the byte-identical call:

```cpp
error = gitExec(gitArgs() << "--version", &result);
```

Both run back to back at startup (`git::initialize()` then `source_control::initialize()`), and `isGitInstalled()` re-spawns git again at every client init (`SessionClientInit.cpp:430`) and on every `vcsContext()` call. So a reconnect or reload pays for a process launch whose answer is already known.

Recording `s_gitInstalled` alongside `s_gitVersion` in `initGitBin()` and having `isGitInstalled()` return `vcsEnabled() && s_gitInstalled` would remove the redundant spawns. It also closes a latent staleness bug: `onUserSettingsChanged(kGitExePath)` updates `s_gitExePath` but never refreshes `s_gitVersion`, so changing the git executable in Global Options leaves the version from the old binary in place. Re-running `initGitBin()` from that handler would fix both.

Worth confirming that nothing depends on `isGitInstalled()` being a live probe (i.e. picking up a git installed part-way through a session) before caching.

Not done in #18751 to keep a startup-hang fix from carrying a behavior change. Raised by @kevinushey in review of that PR.

title: rserver session launch can hang before exec, stalling restarts for a minute
description:
### Symptom

On RStudio Server (Linux), relaunching a session (Restart R, resuming a suspended session, switching projects) occasionally never comes back. The client polls `get_events` ("Service currently unavailable"), and every RPC waits its full 30s before failing with "Unable to connect to service". This lasts until rserver's one-minute pending-launch window expires and it launches another session.

In the e2e suite this shows up on server-linux as flakes in `panes/editor/rmarkdown.test.ts` ("empty chunk does not define variables") and `panes/console/interpreter_version.test.ts` ("refreshes after restart ..."). Seen on PRs #18877, #18880, #18881, #18883, #18887, #18895 and #18897; on #18893 (run 35764949923) it failed both attempts.

### Root cause

rserver launches each rsession with `launchChildProcess()`, which forks. In the child, `runProcess()` calls `permanentlyDropPriv(runAsUser)` before `execve`. On Linux that overload calls `core::log::refreshAllLogDestinations()`, which takes the logger's write lock. Every log write holds that lock's read side while it formats and writes the message. So if any rserver thread is mid-write at the moment of the fork, the child inherits a reader with no thread left to release it, and waits forever. The child never execs and stays alive as a root-owned `rserver` process. Since #18573, rserver keeps waiting on a pending launch whose process is alive, so it waits on this one for a minute. rserver logs heavily at debug level, which is what the e2e server runs with.

The same child also looks the user up with `getUserFromUsername()`, which takes the user cache's mutex. rserver's request threads share that mutex too.

### Evidence

- The CI server log for run 35764949923 reports the launched process alive ("Keeping pending launch of live session process 7663") for the full minute. Every connect fails with ENOENT, and nothing is logged from that pid. Both hung launches were forked within a millisecond of another rserver thread writing a log line.
- Reproduced with that PR's `.deb` in an Ubuntu 24.04 container, forcing relaunches while other requests keep rserver logging: 1 launch in 60 hung. The hung child is still `rserver` (never exec'd). It is past `restorePriv()` but short of `initgroups()`, blocked in a futex. Its memory holds the logger's `ReaderWriterMutex` with `IsWriting = 1`, `ReaderCount = 1`, and `WriteMutex` owned by the child itself: `lockWrite()` is waiting on a reader that exists only in the parent.
- In a native Linux build, a harness that calls `launchChildProcess()` as rserver does (root, run-as user set) while six threads log at debug level: 299 of 300 children hung.

title: replace vendored sundown markdown renderer
description:
`core::markdown` renders Markdown with a copy of [sundown](https://github.com/vmg/sundown) vendored into `src/cpp/core/markdown/sundown/` in April 2012 (5838dc010b, upstream commit `07d0d98`). Upstream was deprecated a few months later (vmg/sundown@37728fb, "Let the world know that Sundown is deprecated") and has had no commits since. Our copy has only received build and typo fixes. We should replace it with a maintained, CommonMark-compliant renderer.

### Callers

- `rs_markdownToHTML` / `.rs.markdownToHTML` (`SessionModuleContext.cpp`, `ModuleTools.R`), used for:
  - custom help handler descriptions in completion popups (`SessionHelp.R`)
  - roxygen2 tag descriptions (`SessionRCompletions.R`)
- HTML preview of plain `.md` files (`SessionHTMLPreview.cpp`)
- Tutorial pane (`SessionTutorial.cpp`)
- R Presentations (`presentation/SlideRenderer.cpp`, `presentation/SlideRequestHandler.cpp`)

### Candidate replacement

[cmark-gfm](https://github.com/github/cmark-gfm) (BSD-2-Clause) seems like the best fit:

- Maintained, CommonMark plus the GFM extensions we already enable (tables, strikethrough, autolinks).
- Safe by default: raw HTML is omitted and unsafe link schemes (`javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:`, most `data:`) are filtered unless `CMARK_OPT_UNSAFE` is set, so callers rendering content they don't control get safe output without having to opt into sundown's `escape` / `safelink` options.
- It's the library behind the `commonmark` R package, which the `markdown` package switched to from sundown in v1.3.

[md4c](https://github.com/mity/md4c) is a lighter alternative, but its HTML renderer does no link scheme filtering, so we'd have to add that ourselves.

### Considerations

- Most callers are legacy features whose output should stay stable, R Presentations in particular. We'd want to diff rendered output for a representative set of `.Rpres` / `.md` documents before and after.
- `core::markdown::Extensions` and `HTMLOptions` expose sundown-specific behavior that needs a cmark equivalent or an explicit decision to drop it: superscript (on by default, no cmark-gfm equivalent), lax spacing and space-headers (CommonMark rules differ), smartypants (`CMARK_OPT_SMART`), hard wrap (`CMARK_OPT_HARDBREAKS`), TOC, and the skip-HTML/style/images/links options.
- RStudio's own pre/post-processing (MathJax protection via `ignoreMath`, `stripMetadata`, `htmlPreserve`) wraps the renderer and should carry over, but needs retesting against CommonMark's parsing rules.

title: separate desktop and server source recovery namespaces
description:
Desktop and Server should have separate source-document recovery namespaces when they run as the same user and share an RStudio data directory. Switching between the two is uncommon in normal use, but it must preserve unsaved work and must not disrupt a running session. Development builds and automated tests make this overlap more likely.

This is an architectural follow-up to #18744 and the immediate mitigation in #18745. It records the investigation and proposed direction; the namespace change has not been implemented.

The failure was reproduced on macOS with two no-project `rsession` processes sharing a temporary `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME`: a Desktop-mode session renamed a live Server-mode session's `sources/session-<id>` directory during orphan recovery. The Server process remained alive, but a subsequent actual `new_document` RPC failed with ENOENT when writing `<document-id>-contents`. Existing unsaved documents moved with the directory. Giving the processes separate data directories prevented the failure. See #18744 for reproduction steps. This establishes a failure mechanism consistent with the reported symptoms; it does not establish which competing process caused the original incident.

The underlying problem is that recovery treats a shared directory as a common ownership domain, while processes can interpret its locks differently. Desktop defaults to advisory locking and Server to link-based locking on Unix; configuration can override the choice. Windows uses advisory locking. Previously, orphan recovery only inspected the current process's selected lock type. #18745 checks both types, rejects known ownership conflicts, and isolates C++ session test data/configuration. Its targeted tests cover live coexistence, abandoned-document recovery, and competing sessions with the same ID. This is a compatibility mitigation: older binaries retain the original behavior, and the ownership check, directory rename, and lock acquisition remain separate operations rather than an atomic ownership transfer.

Code inspection at [4608e7c](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/tree/4608e7ceb59a14ecdf94cca4f3bf3dddf92e737d) found a contained starting point:

- With no project, [scopedScratchPath() uses the common user scratch directory](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/4608e7ceb59a14ecdf94cca4f3bf3dddf92e737d/src/cpp/session/SessionModuleContext.cpp#L1218-L1224). Source recovery consequently shares the `sources` root across modes.
- [The supervisor constructs the recovery paths](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/4608e7ceb59a14ecdf94cca4f3bf3dddf92e737d/src/cpp/session/SessionSourceDatabaseSupervisor.cpp#L53-L114): live `session-*` directories, persistent titled/untitled documents in `per/t` and `per/u`, and most-recent stores `mt` and `mu`. [Document properties use another direct `sources/prop` path](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/4608e7ceb59a14ecdf94cca4f3bf3dddf92e737d/src/cpp/session/SessionSourceDatabase.cpp#L102-L109). These should use a common namespace-aware root.
- Project scratch directories already [include a context ID](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/4608e7ceb59a14ecdf94cca4f3bf3dddf92e737d/src/cpp/session/projects/SessionProjectContext.cpp#L217-L226). Desktop and Server [store state separately, explicitly to avoid sharing source databases](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/4608e7ceb59a14ecdf94cca4f3bf3dddf92e737d/src/cpp/session/prefs/UserStateLayer.cpp#L38-L43), so normal project configurations already have some separation. Copied profiles and legacy context IDs still need consideration.
- Most document operations already obtain their directory through the source database API. A focused root change appears to require only a handful of production files; no frontend or document-format change is expected. Migration and regression coverage are the larger part of the work.

A possible layout is:

```text
sources/
  desktop/
    session-<id>/
    per/{t,u}/
    mt/
    mu/
    prop/
  server/
    session-<id>/
    per/{t,u}/
    mt/
    mu/
    prop/
```

The precise namespace key remains a design decision: an explicit mode component guarantees Desktop/Server separation, while a stable context/profile component could also distinguish independent installations. It must remain stable across restarts, and Server's existing multi-session subdirectories and intended recovery behavior must be preserved. A per-process namespace alone would prevent subsequent recovery from finding abandoned work.

Alternatives and scope:

- **Separate source recovery roots:** directly prevents cross-mode recovery from claiming the other mode's documents, independent of lock configuration. Same-mode concurrency still requires correct locking; tests still need isolated state.
- **Separate the entire Desktop/Server data directory:** provides broader isolation, but affects substantially more state and migration behavior. It is not necessary to move preferences or all runtime state to address this source database problem. Active-session storage can also [involve Server RPCs](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/4608e7ceb59a14ecdf94cca4f3bf3dddf92e737d/src/cpp/session/SessionActiveSessionsStorage.cpp#L39-L61), so it warrants a separate audit.
- **Use one default lock type:** reduces default mismatches but does not establish a shared protocol when users customize locking or run older versions. Intentionally shared stores need an agreed ownership protocol, including atomic claims and safe protocol transitions, rather than relying on matching process defaults.

Migration needs an explicit design. Legacy `sources/session-*` and persistent stores do not reliably identify which mode should inherit the documents. A blind move or recursive copy can interfere with a live older session or allow concurrent launches to import the same recovery state. Existing `sdb` and `source_database_v2` migrations also need review. The old orphan scanner only considers immediate `session-*` children of `sources`, so it would ignore the proposed mode subdirectories; that helps coexistence but is not a complete upgrade/downgrade strategy. We should prioritize preserving and making unsaved work recoverable when switching modes, with the treatment of legacy shared tabs documented explicitly.

Acceptance and regression coverage should include:

- Concurrent Desktop/Server launches in both orders, with no project, sharing a temporary data root: each retains its directory and can create/save documents regardless of supported lock configuration.
- Same-mode restart, normal exit restoration, crash recovery, and Server suspend/resume and multi-session behavior.
- Existing project isolation, including legacy or copied context state.
- Migration of titled and untitled unsaved documents, simultaneous first launches, interrupted migration, and coexistence with an older running binary. No live directory may be reclaimed, and legacy work must remain recoverable.
- Explicit behavior after a mode switch or downgrade, without silently deleting or making recovery data inaccessible.
- Preservation of `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` overrides and automated-test isolation; platform coverage including Windows.

Historical context: #6742 documented shared Desktop/Server source databases for projects and was closed after a fix; #10242 documented a separate Desktop/Server source database interaction affecting session restarts and was also closed. These show prior issues in this area, but the newly reproduced no-project failure is tracked in #18744.

title: Dependency install job reports success when package installation failed
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop and Server
    RStudio Version : 2026.10 (Blue Mistflower) development builds; the code involved is long-standing
    OS Version      : any (observed on Ubuntu 24)
    R Version       : any (observed with R 4.6.1)

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Use a Linux machine without the `libsodium` development headers, and with `plumber` installed but `sodium` not installed. (This state is reachable: `plumber` lists `sodium` in `Imports` but never imports it in its `NAMESPACE`, so `plumber` installs and loads without it -- for example when a prebuilt `plumber` tarball is unpacked and the `sodium` install fails.)
2. Choose **File > New File > Plumber API...**
3. RStudio prompts to install the missing `sodium` package. Click **Yes**.

### Describe the problem in detail

The "Plumber R APIs Dependencies" background job runs `utils::install.packages("sodium")`, which fails to compile:

```
<stdin>:1:10: fatal error: sodium.h: No such file or directory
ERROR: configuration failed for package 'sodium'
* removing '/home/user/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.6/sodium'

✔ Package 'sodium' successfully installed.
Warning message:
In utils::install.packages("sodium") :
  installation of package 'sodium' had non-zero exit status
```

Despite the failure, the job prints "✔ Package 'sodium' successfully installed." and finishes with the status **Succeeded**. RStudio then re-checks the dependencies, finds them still unsatisfied, and silently abandons the original action -- the New Plumber API dialog never opens, and nothing tells the user why.

The install script generated in `SessionDependencies.cpp` assumes "the script aborts on error, so if we get here we can presume everything installed successfully". But `install.packages()` reports a failed installation as a *warning*, not an error, so the script carries on to the success message.

This affects every feature that installs packages through the dependency manager, not just Plumber.

### Describe the behavior you expected

When a package fails to install, the job should not claim success: it should report which packages could not be installed and finish with the status **Failed**.

title: Interaction between RStudio and Alfred's clipboard management
description:
Noting [these previously](https://www.alfredforum.com/topic/21395-clipboard-history-merging-activates-in-rstudio/)-shared [forum posts](https://forum.posit.co/t/interaction-between-rstudio-and-alfreds-clipboard-management/36273/1) here, I wanted to confirm that the problem still exists and provide another workaround idea.

### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop 
    RStudio Version : 2026.01.0 Build 392 (49fbea7a, 2026-01-04) for macOS
    OS Version      : macOS Tahoe 26.2 (25C56)
    R Version       : 4.5.2 (2025-10-31)

Together with Alfred 4.8 (1312).

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Enable Alfred's `Clipboard History > Merging > Fast append` option
   - with or without the `Place merged … or `Play sound …` options
3. In RStudio, select some text and normal-copy it. Repeat a few times with different text snippets.
   - Text source doesn't seem to matter: console, Rmd or R file, `About RStudio` popup content, …
   - Keyboard shortcuts and menu options for both copy & cut both trigger the problem.
5. Check Alfred clipboard (or note the sound)

=> _Frequently_ `Fast append` was triggered, but not always.

#### Workaround

1. Open Finder > `/Applicatons` and Alfred > `Clipboard History > Advanced`.
2. Drag `RStudio.app` into the `Ignore Apps` list.

### Describe the problem in detail

Same as in the above-linked forum posts. Alfred admin Vero suggested: "This happens in a few apps that also have their own clipboard copy mechanism. When you select text in RStudio, do you notice it being copied to clipboard?"

No, only selecting text does not auto-copy it, not triggers the problem.

My guess is that something related to some kind of RStudio-internal delay in the copy/cut action is relevant here. In other apps, a true `Fast append` action always seem to trigger the sound quicker, than a normal-copy in RStudio where there's an audible delay.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Normal-copy should not append.

title: Tasks deferred from #12367
description:
The PR for rstudio/rstudio-pro#12367 was merged to open-source at the last minute. A few edge cases came up in final code review which needed to be deferred.

### Terminator omitted from payload

When `std::string_view multipart` is constructed in `parseMultipartForm()`, it omits the terminator from the view. This was unintentional, and the only reason it works at all is because `BoundaryParser` was designed to tolerate a missing terminator.

This isn't actually IMPORTANT, because no RFC-compliant client will ever produce input that this mistake would impact, but I still want it to reflect the intended implementation.

### Uploaded file names

Filenames can be percent-encoded. I don't think we actually handle that anywhere. (Maybe this should be split out into its own issue.)

### Hypothetically flaky test

The `ComplicatedFormParsingWorksRandomByteBoundaries` test might be flaky. This might have been fixed already but needs investigation.

After `headers_parsed`, `parseBytes` correctly re-passes the same parseIter, but this loop draws a fresh `rand() % 8192 + 1` count. The parser then does `begin += bufferPos_` (121 for this request); if the new count < 121, begin lands past end, copyRangeToBuffer's std::distance goes negative, neededCapacity wraps to ~2^64, and formBuffer_.reserve() throws std::length_error.

Repro case: `parse(begin, begin+424)` -> headers_parsed, then `parse(begin, begin+50)`.

### Missing test coverage

The old implementation and the current implementation both ensure that if two files get uploaded under the same form field name, the first one wins. There should be a test for this.

Nested multiparts could have one boundary be the prefix of another. The parser handles it fine, but there's no test to prove it.

### Duplicate implementation

`SessionFiles.cpp` contains a mostly copy-pasted copy of the old code. Refactoring it to be able to reuse the same implementation looked invasive, so it needs to be followed up on.

title: Identify and decommission redundant GitHub Actions test workflows
description:
### Describe the enhancement

The `.github/workflows/` directory has accumulated E2E test workflows that overlap with newer, consolidated ones. The clearest example: `os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml` is a single "scheduled rotation and run-all" workflow that drives every reusable per-OS E2E engine on its own cron. Several older standalone per-OS scheduled callers appear to do the same job for one OS each, so they may now be dead weight.

This is a tracking task to audit the workflows, decommission the ones that are genuinely redundant, and delete them once we've confirmed nothing depends on them.

### Candidates to investigate

Standalone per-OS scheduled callers that the unified rotation may have superseded:

- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-26-arm64-scheduled.yml`
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-ubuntu-24-scheduled.yml`
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025-scheduled.yml`
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-server-os-ubuntu-24-scheduled.yml`
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-autocomplete-scheduled-windows-server-2025.yml`

These are starting candidates. The audit may turn up others.

### Proposed process

1. Audit `.github/workflows/` on `main` and list every workflow, its triggers, and what calls it.
2. For each candidate, confirm that a current workflow already covers the same OS and test scope.
3. Disable the redundant workflow first (comment out or remove its `schedule`/triggers) and let it sit for one cycle to confirm nothing breaks.
4. Delete the file once decommissioning is confirmed clean.
5. Check for lingering references (other workflows' `uses:`, docs, README) and clean those up too.

title: Restart R silently skips its completion event when the session takes more than ~10s to answer
description:
## Summary

When a Restart R takes more than about 10 seconds to produce a session that answers a ping, RStudio stops waiting for it, logs `Error connecting with session.` to the browser console, and never fires `ConsoleRestartRCompletedEvent` -- even though the session does come back a moment later.

The same thing happens if the very first ping *fails*: since #17906, one failed ping ends the wait outright, so the retry that would have reached the new session is never sent.

## Symptoms

Anything hanging off `ConsoleRestartRCompletedEvent` is silently skipped for that restart:

- the console prompt is not nudged and the console does not take focus (`Shell.onRestartRCompleted`)
- the Console pane's interpreter version is not refreshed, so a restart into a different R keeps showing the old version (`ConsoleTabPanel` -> `ConsoleInterpreterVersion.adaptToR`)

The restart itself still completes -- `onCompleted` runs, the progress indicator is dismissed and `RestartStatusEvent.RESTART_COMPLETED` fires -- so the failure is quiet.

## Cause

`SessionOpener.sendPing` schedules a `RepeatingCommand` every 200ms with `maxRetries = 50`, and increments `retries_` on every tick, including ticks where a ping is already in flight and nothing is sent. The budget is therefore a flat ~10.2s of wall clock no matter how many pings were actually attempted. When it runs out the loop marks itself completed; the ping that eventually succeeds is then discarded by the `if (completed_) return;` guard in `onSuccess`, so the event never fires.

A ping can legitimately stay unanswered for far longer than 10s: on Server, rserver holds an RPC aimed at a session it is still relaunching (up to `rsession-proxy-max-wait-secs`, default 30s), and the new session still has to restore the workspace and search path.

The `onFailure` path is the second half of it. Before #17906 a failed ping was retried and a later success still fired the event; that commit correctly made `onCompleted` fire exactly once, but also made the first failure terminal, which leaves `maxRetries` effectively unused.

## Reproduction

Most visible in CI: the e2e test `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/console/interpreter_version.test.ts` (added in #18858) restarts R twice on RStudio Server, where each restart takes 9-11s -- straddling the 10.2s budget. It currently fails on essentially every linux-server run, e.g. https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/35259099463/job/105336330462, with the second restart's ping answered at 10.9s and its success discarded.

title: Uploaded filenames may be percent-encoded
description:
Split out from #18727.

`parseMultipartForm()` takes the `filename` parameter of a part's `Content-Disposition` header verbatim:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/main/src/cpp/core/http/Util.cpp#L459

Browsers do not send it verbatim. The WHATWG `multipart/form-data` encoding algorithm has them escape three bytes in both `name` and `filename` before putting them on the wire:

| byte | sent as |
|------|---------|
| U+000A LF | `%0A` |
| U+000D CR | `%0D` |
| U+0022 `"` | `%22` |

Nothing else is escaped — notably `%` itself is left alone, so the encoding is not reversible in general. A file named `say %22hi%22.txt` and a file named `say "hi".txt` arrive as the same bytes from a browser, and non-browser clients (curl, most HTTP libraries) escape nothing at all, so the same bytes can mean either thing depending on who sent them.

That ambiguity is why this was deferred rather than fixed inline. Deciding it means picking one of:

- decode only `%0A`/`%0D`/`%22`, matching browsers and mangling the rare literal-`%22` filename from a non-browser client
- leave filenames verbatim, so browser-uploaded files with a quote or newline in the name keep a visibly escaped name
- key off `User-Agent` or some other signal, which is worse than either

Whichever way it goes, `filename*` (RFC 8187 extended parameters, e.g. `filename*=UTF-8''%E2%82%AC.txt`) is a separate and unambiguous case that is also unhandled today: `HeaderParams` lowercases the key to `filename*`, which never matches the `filename` lookup, so a part carrying only `filename*` is treated as an ordinary form field rather than a file.

Worth noting for scoping: `Request::uploadedFile()` has no callers in this repo — the consumers are in rstudio-pro. The file upload path in `SessionFiles.cpp` parses `filename` with its own separate code (`parseContentBuffer`) and feeds the result to `destDir.completeChildPath()`, so any decoding added there needs to not introduce `/` or `..` into the name.

title: Console pane shows (unknown) for the R version while the session is starting
description:
### System details

Not specific to a platform or version; applies to both RStudio Desktop and RStudio Server.

### Describe the issue

The Console pane's interpreter label (the R logo and version next to the working directory) reads `(unknown)` while a session is starting, and only switches to the real version some seconds later.

The label is created with the `(unknown)` placeholder and then fills itself in from the `get_rversion_info` RPC. At startup that RPC is queued behind whatever R is busy with, so the placeholder is what users see for the first seconds of every session -- longest on RStudio Server, on slow workspace restores, and on projects with heavy startup code.

### Suggested improvement

The version is already on the client before the widget is built: `client_init` sends it as `r_versions_info.r_version` in session info, from the same `module_context::rVersion()` the RPC uses, and session info is set before the workbench is constructed.

The label can therefore be seeded from session info synchronously, with the RPC left in place to refresh it (so a restart into a different R version is still picked up). `(unknown)` then remains only as the fallback for the case where session info isn't available yet.

title: Data viewer: View() fails with "invalid multibyte string" on columns holding invalid UTF-8
description:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

```r
View(data.frame(x = c("ok", "caf\xe9")))
# Error in nchar(col, type = "width") : invalid multibyte string, element 2
```

The grid never loads -- the failure aborts the whole `.rs.describeCols()` call, not just the affected column.

Also reproducible with `mobilizr::nutrition`, whose `name` and `ingredients` columns carry latin1 bytes:

```r
View(mobilizr::nutrition)
```

### Cause

`colMaxChars()` in `.rs.describeCols()` computes a column-width hint with `nchar(col, type = "width")`, which throws on text that is invalid in the session encoding. The factor branch (`nchar(lvls, type = "width")`) has the same exposure. Neither the helper nor its call site is error-guarded.

### Regression

Introduced by the data viewer rewrite (#17382), which added the `col_max_chars` hint. Clean on 2026.04; broken from 2026.05 through current main.

### Fix

Pass `allowNA = TRUE` so unmeasurable elements come back `NA` rather than throwing, report no hint in that case (the client falls back to sampling the visible rows), and guard the call site so a failure computing a sizing hint can never take down the grid.

### System details

    RStudio Version : 2026.05 and later

title: Data viewer: View() fails when a summary generic is masked by a package attached before tools:rstudio
description:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

With a stats-teaching package attached ahead of `tools:rstudio` on the search path -- which is what an `.Rprofile` (or project startup) `library()` call leaves behind, since `tools:rstudio` is attached at position 2 during session init and later `library()` calls push it down:

```r
# .Rprofile
library(mobilizr)   # Depends: mosaic
```

then in the session:

```r
View(atus)   # from the mobilizr package
# Error in mean_(x = x, na.rm = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) :
#   formal argument "na.rm" matched by multiple actual arguments
```

Converting the integer columns to double makes it work:

```r
for (nm in names(atus)) if (is.integer(atus[[nm]])) atus[[nm]] <- as.numeric(atus[[nm]])
View(atus)   # fine
```

`View(cdc)` (same package, no integer columns) is unaffected.

### Cause

`.rs.describeCols()`'s column-width hint calls `range(col, na.rm = TRUE)` for integer columns:

```r
if (is.integer(col)) {
   rng <- suppressWarnings(range(col, na.rm = TRUE))
   ...
```

`mobilizr` exports a masking `range()` which forwards `...` into a call that already fixes `na.rm`:

```r
range <- function(x, ...) {
  if (any(is.na(mosaic::mean(x = x, na.rm = FALSE, ...)))) { ... }   # <- ... lands next to na.rm = FALSE
  mosaic::range(x = x, ..., na.rm = TRUE)
}
```

so `na.rm = TRUE` is spliced in beside the hard-coded `na.rm = FALSE` and argument matching fails. (`mosaic::mean` rewrites the call to `mean_` via `match.call()`, which is why the error names `mean_`.) The double branch calls `range(finiteCol)` with no `na.rm`, so it never duplicates -- hence integer-only.

`colMaxChars()` is not error-guarded, so this aborts the whole describe call and the grid never loads.

Note `mobilizr`'s `max`/`min`/`sd` guard with `if (is.formula(x))` and delegate to base for plain vectors; `range`, `mean`, `median`, `sum`, `prod`, `quantile` and `var` do not.

### Fix

Namespace-qualify the summary generics on the data viewer's `View()` path (including `.rs.digest()`, which is reached via the column fingerprint), and guard the width hint so a failure there degrades to client-side sampling instead of taking down the grid.

### System details

    RStudio Edition : Server (Posit Cloud)
    RStudio Version : 2026.07.1

title: terminal PATH accumulates duplicate git/svn bin dir entries across session restarts
description:
When a terminal is restored after a session restart with `terminal_track_environment` enabled (the default), its saved environment -- including `PATH` -- is reloaded and then `amendShellPaths()` appends the non-PATH git and svn bin dirs again (`src/cpp/session/SessionConsoleProcess.cpp`, `createTerminalProcOptions`). `core::system::addToPath` / `modifyPath` never check for an existing entry, so a terminal restored across N restarts ends up with N copies of each directory.

This only affects users whose git or svn is not already on the PATH (e.g. a `git_exe_path` pref pointing outside it). PATH bloat rather than wrong behavior.

Noted while addressing review on #18763, where the same pattern for the postback scripts dir was fixed by checking the existing PATH before prepending. `amendShellPaths` (and probably `addToPath` itself) should do the same.

title: Custom application keybindings not applied at session start when the session is slow to initialize
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop and Server
    RStudio Version : 2026.10.0 (main)
    OS Version      : all
    R Version       : any

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. As a fresh user, before the first session start, write `~/.config/rstudio/keybindings/rstudio_bindings.json` containing `{"installPackage": "F10"}`.
2. Make R slow to initialize, e.g. `~/.Rprofile` containing `Sys.sleep(6)`.
3. Start a session with no documents open. Open **Tools**: "Install Packages..." shows no shortcut; press `F10`: nothing happens. Open **Tools > Modify Keyboard Shortcuts**: the row for the command shows `F10`.
4. Open a new R script (or reload the page): the menu now shows `F10` and the key works.

### Describe the problem in detail

Custom **application** keyboard shortcuts saved in `keybindings/rstudio_bindings.json` are sometimes not applied when a session starts. The file is read correctly and the JSON reaches the client, but the shortcut never gets attached to the `AppCommand` or the keymap: the menu label shows the default shortcut, the command palette shows the default, and pressing the custom key does nothing. Opening any editor afterwards, or reloading the page, applies the binding immediately. The Modify Keyboard Shortcuts dialog shows the custom binding the whole time, because it reads the same underlying object -- the value is loaded, it just never gets applied to the command.

The cause is `ConfigFileBacked.execute()` (`src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/core/client/files/ConfigFileBacked.java`), which waits for the `read_config_json` RPC to settle by polling a 20 ms GWT `Timer`, and **silently drops the queued command if the read has not settled within ~100 polls**. `ApplicationCommandManager.loadBindings()` relies on this and is only re-triggered by `EditorLoadedEvent`. Whenever the session is still busy starting up when that event fires, `read_config_json` can take longer than the poll budget to settle on the client side -- rsession answers with an `asyncHandle` and completes the request later over the event stream when it is busy, and the renderer's main thread can be saturated with GWT startup work -- so the bindings load into the object but the queued command to apply them is never run.

The window for this race was opened by #18716, which moved `initializeWorkbench()` into the `AceEditor.load()` callback directly after `client_init`. The console's editor now attaches, and fires the one `EditorLoadedEvent` the manager listens for, while R may still be initializing. This reproduces reliably in our nightly end-to-end test runs across every distro we test, both for Workbench and open-source RStudio Server builds, and is easy to reproduce locally with the recipe above.

The same class of race was found and fixed for the sibling `EditorCommandManager` in #18793 / #18797 (`SessionInitEvent` fallback added). `ApplicationCommandManager` and the underlying `ConfigFileBacked` give-up were not addressed there, so this is the application-keybinding analog of that issue. It may also explain the intermittent reports in #13817 and #15679.

A fix (queue commands and flush them from the load callbacks instead of polling with a cap) is ready and will be submitted as a PR against this issue. A `SessionInitEvent`-style re-trigger for `ApplicationCommandManager`, mirroring #18797's fix for `EditorCommandManager`, is a possible follow-up but is not required by the fix -- the drop happens after any such trigger fires, so removing the drop is what matters.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Custom application keyboard shortcuts are applied at session start regardless of how long the session takes to initialize, not only after a subsequent editor open or page reload.

title: Remaining cmd.exe dependencies hang the session when the command prompt is disabled by Group Policy
description:
#18751 removed `cmd.exe` from the git and svn startup probes, which is what kept RStudio from starting at all under `DisableCMD` (#18735). The underlying mechanism is still present everywhere else: on Windows every `core::system::runCommand()` is `cmd.exe /S /C`, and a `cmd.exe` disabled by Group Policy prints its message and then blocks on console input that nothing ever writes.

## Remaining automatic path

`src/cpp/session/modules/clang/CompilationDatabase.cpp:354` and `:367` run `R CMD config CXX` and `<compiler> --version` through `runCommand()` with no `_WIN32` fork. For any package project with `src/` files, `initializeDefinitionIndex()` schedules indexing shortly after the file monitor comes up, and `updateForCurrentPackage()` evaluates `computeCompilerHash()` (line 565) *before* the `isCurrent` check (line 567), so the spawn happens even when the cached compilation database is fresh. The result is that client init succeeds and the IDE renders, then the session goes unresponsive on first idle. The same chain fires on any `.cpp` edit or save.

These two sites are not a mechanical conversion to `runProgram()`: `R CMD config CXX` can return a command with flags (e.g. `g++ -std=gnu++17`), so `compilerCommand + " --version"` would need command-line splitting.

## Remaining user-initiated paths

- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionSVN.cpp` `createConsoleProc()` still builds `svn() << args.args()` as a shell string for `ConsoleProcess::create(command, ...)`, so every async SVN operation (update, commit, checkout, history, show) spawns a hidden `cmd.exe` that never exits and leaves the progress dialog spinning.

  The NOTE above that call site justifies the shell-string form with "so that we can redirect standard output to a file", which is not accurate on Windows: `ChildProcess::run()` applies `options_.stdOutFile` via `STARTUPINFO` regardless of which `init()` overload was used, and `init(exe, args, options)` only emits `LOG_ERROR_MESSAGE("stdOutFile/stdErrFile options cannot be used with runProgram")` without clearing the field. Relaxing that guard on Win32 and using `ConsoleProcess::create(s_svnExePath, args.args(), ...)` -- as git's `createConsoleProc()` already does -- would close this one.
- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionWorkbench.cpp:343` (ssh-keygen)
- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionSVN.cpp` (patch, ~line 1207)
- `src/cpp/session/modules/clang/CodeCompletion.cpp:252` and `:304`
- `src/cpp/session/modules/build/SessionBuild.cpp:2447`

## Suggested approach

A core-level fail-fast would cover all of them at once. In `ChildProcess::run()` (`src/cpp/core/system/Win32ChildProcess.cpp`, which already returns `Error`), when `exe_` has resolved to `cmd.exe`, read `DisableCMD` from `HKCU`/`HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System` and return a descriptive `Error` instead of spawning. A value of 1 blocks `/C` scripts. `core::system::RegistryKey` already exists (used by `RToolsInfo.cpp`) and would need a DWORD getter. That also covers `resolveCommand()`'s own `.cmd` -> `cmd.exe` rewrite, so `runProgram()` callers benefit too.

Turning the hang into an actionable error is a smaller and more complete change than forking each call site, though the clang sites may still want a real `runProgram()` conversion so compiler detection keeps working under the policy.

Reported by @kevinushey in review of #18751.

title: e2e: cover whole-project quarto render with no preview
description:
Follow-up from #18768, where the "(No Preview)" render path gained an e2e test (`tests/panes/editor/quarto_render_no_preview.test.ts`) covering a successful and a failed single-file render.

The whole-project branch of that path is still untested. In `QuartoPreview::args()` (`src/cpp/session/modules/quarto/SessionQuartoPreview.cpp`), a directory target renders as `quarto render --to <format>` with no file argument. The Build pane only routes through this code for Quarto website and book projects (`BuildPresenter.startBuild()` calls `quartoServe()` for those; default-type projects use the Build pane's own runner instead), so covering it needs:

- a website project (`_quarto.yml` with `project: type: website` plus an `index.qmd`) created and opened via `createAndOpenProject()`
- `rmd_viewer_type` set to `none`
- the `buildAll` command
- assertions that the Background Jobs pane shows a `Render: <project dir>` job in the Succeeded state and that `_site/index.html` exists
- `closeProjectIfOpen()` on teardown

That is two session restarts per platform for a three-line branch, which is why it was left out of #18768. `quarto render --to all` on such a project was verified manually to succeed.

title: Chat pane serves a stale Content-Security-Policy after Posit Assistant is updated in-session
description:
## Summary

`loadCspDirectives()` (`src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatStaticFiles.cpp`) reads `dist/csp.json` from the Posit Assistant installation into a function-local `static const auto`, so the directives are read once and kept for the lifetime of the rsession process. The doc comment states this deliberately:

> Once loaded (or once a failure is encountered), the result is cached for the lifetime of the session. A missing or broken file will not be retried.

That holds even when the installation changes underneath it. Updating Posit Assistant from the chat pane does not restart the session: `chatUpdatePositAssistant` stops the backend via `stopChatBackendForInstallMutation("update")`, installs, and the frontend then restarts the backend and reloads the UI (`ChatPresenter.installUpdate()` -- "Update complete - restart backend and reload UI"). The new package's `dist/csp.json` is never read, so the newly installed client is served under the previous version's CSP.

## Why it matters

The CSP is emitted by the databot build and is expected to track the client it ships with. If a new Posit Assistant version needs a directive the old one did not -- another `connect-src` origin, an `img-src`, a worker or font source -- the browser blocks it, and the symptom is a chat pane that is subtly or completely broken until RStudio itself is restarted. The user did nothing wrong and has no reason to connect the breakage to the update they just accepted.

The reverse case is quieter but also wrong: a new version that tightens its CSP is served under the older, looser policy.

## Scope

This is pre-existing, from #17132. It is not caused by #18774/#18815/#18819, though it came up twice while reviewing #18819, because the resolver and the served installation were being reworked there. The directives were always frozen at first read; #18819 only changed which installation seeds them.

## Options

- Key the cache on the installation path, so a restart onto a different installation re-reads `dist/csp.json` and an unchanged one still costs nothing. Fits how the served installation is now pinned per backend start (`staticfiles::setInstallationPath()`).
- Invalidate it explicitly wherever the installation is mutated -- the update and uninstall paths in `SessionChat.cpp`. Fewer moving parts, but it is another thing for a future install path to remember.

The first keeps the invalidation next to the thing being cached, and needs no cooperation from callers.

Note that `rebuildCspHeaderCache()` already re-runs on every `setChatBackendPort()`, so the surrounding header string is rebuilt on each backend start. Only the `csp.json` directive map is stuck, which is why the staleness is easy to miss.

Related: #18819, #17132.

title: Posit Assistant static asset requests re-resolve the installation on every request
description:
## Summary

`handleAIChatRequest()` (`src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatStaticFiles.cpp`) calls `locatePositAssistantInstallation()` on every `/ai-chat/` static asset request. Loading the chat pane issues dozens of these. Since #18815 the resolver ranks every tier rather than returning the first hit, so each request now runs `verifyPositAiInstallation()` plus a `package.json` read and a `protocol.json` read for up to three tiers (user, system-wide, bundled), instead of roughly three stats on the user tier.

On a workstation this is microseconds. On RStudio Server with a network-mounted home directory, or a system tier on a mounted share, it is per-request latency multiplied by the number of assets in the chat UI.

## Why a plain session cache is not the fix

The resolver re-checks the filesystem on every call by design: an administrator updating the system-wide copy, or a user removing their own install out of band, is noticed without a session restart. A cache invalidated only by this session's own install/uninstall (the two places that already clear `s_positAssistantVersion` and `s_updateState`) would miss both.

## Options

- Resolve once per chat-backend start and serve assets from that installation for the backend's lifetime. The backend is already launched from a specific install (`startChatBackend()`), and the assets it serves should match the server it runs, so this is arguably more correct than re-resolving per asset.
- Keep per-request resolution but memoize on the tiers' directory mtimes, so an unchanged filesystem costs a few stats rather than JSON reads.

The first is simpler and ties the served assets to the running backend; the second preserves today's behaviour exactly.

Related: #18774, #18815 (where this was raised in review).

title: Posit Assistant discovery should pick the highest version, and prefer bundled/admin installs when user installs are disabled
description:
## Summary

`locatePositAssistantInstallation()` currently returns the first installation it finds in a fixed tier order rather than the best one. That produces two surprising outcomes:

1. A stale per-user install permanently shadows a newer bundled (or admin-managed) install. A user who installed Posit Assistant before bundling existed keeps getting the old version indefinitely, even after upgrading RStudio — and "Help > Diagnostics > Uninstall Posit Assistant" is the only way out.
2. When user-managed installs are disabled, the bundled install is only used if the admin also sets the assistant path option, so admins have to do extra configuration to get a working assistant.

## Current behavior

Search order in `src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatInstallation.cpp:96-161`:

1. Per-user install (`~/.local/share/rstudio/pai/bin`) — only when user installs are enabled (`src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatInstallation.cpp:100-107`)
2. System/admin install — from `posit-assistant-path`, else XDG config dir (`src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatInstallation.cpp:119-123`)
3. Bundled copy — skipped entirely when `posit-assistant-path` is set (`src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatInstallation.cpp:139-145`)

Tiers and flags are assembled in `positAssistantSearchPaths()` (`src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatInstallation.cpp:86-93`); the admin gate is `isPositAssistantInstallationEnabledByAdmin()` (`src/cpp/session/SessionModuleContext.cpp:1609-1613`).

## Requested behavior

**When user-managed installs are enabled (default)**: choose `max_version(bundled, admin-installed, per-user)` instead of unconditionally preferring the per-user install. This mirrors how out-of-band Positron upgrades are resolved on the Workbench side (`max_version(bundled, manually installed)`), and means a per-user install only wins while it is actually newer.

**When user-managed installs are disabled**: fall back to `admin-installed || bundled` rather than `admin-installed || nothing`. Today an admin locking down installs must also point the assistant path option at the bundled directory to get a usable assistant, which is easy to miss. Admins who genuinely want no assistant at all already have the separate assistant-enabled option for that.

## Notes

• Mostly a Workbench/Pro scenario, but the locating and loading code is here in the open-source codebase, so the fix belongs here.
• Requires a version comparison across install tiers; related to #16888 (assistant doesn't know its own version) and #18658 (side-by-side versioned install directories), which may make the comparison cheaper/cleaner.• Also related: #18443 (setting to disable user-managed installs) and #18687 (admin-configurable installation path), which introduced the tiers this issue refines.

## See Also

Two existing issues worth a look before implementing: #18658 (side-by-side versioned install dirs) and #16888 (assistant doesn't know its own version — a prerequisite for version comparison).

title: Plots in Windows are always heavily aliased
description:
Default plots in WIndows have terrible aliasing. This can be fixed by using `type = "cairo"` when saving with (e.g.) `ggsave`. However, the Plots pane in RStudio doesn't use this option. Often it is convenient to save plots directly from the editor but this leads to ugly plots, especially when using small points or thin lines.

```
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Width, y = Sepal.Length)) + 
    geom_point() +
    stat_smooth(method = "lm", col = "red") + 
    labs(title = "Normal") +
    ggsave("normal.png") +
    labs(title = "Cairo") +
    ggsave("cairo.png", type = "cairo")
```

![5f688f5b706e8f4397ee749afce6dd649f6cc2e9](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23621596/35862328-34fb6834-0b43-11e8-9362-d0801ad0d1d7.png)
(Notice, in particular, jagged red line when zoomed in on normal plot)


This could be solved by having an option for `cairo` rendering in RStudio or making `cairo` the default.

title: Move SessionHttpConnectionListener unit tests upstream from rstudio-pro
description:
`SessionHttpConnectionListenerTests.cpp` lives only in rstudio-pro, but every behavior it covers is in this repo. The tests should move here, along with the three test seams that make them possible.

### Why it belongs here

The code under test is entirely open source. `src/cpp/session/http/SessionHttpConnectionListenerImpl.hpp` already has `handleAccept`, `consecutiveErrorCount_`, `kMaxConsecutiveErrors = 100`, and the log-throttling ladder, and `src/cpp/session/include/session/SessionConstants.hpp` already defines `SESSION_EXIT_TOO_MANY_OPEN_FILES` and `SESSION_EXIT_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY`. There is no Workbench-specific behavior in any of it.

The tests landed in pro as a single 2-file commit that added the seams and the tests together, which looks incidental rather than deliberate — the author was working in pro at the time.

### What needs to move

**1. The test file.** `src/cpp/session/http/SessionHttpConnectionListenerTests.cpp`, three cases:

- `DetectsConsecutiveErrors` — 100 accept errors log on a throttle and return 0; the 101st exits `EXIT_FAILURE`
- `DetectsOOMCondition` — the 101st exits `SESSION_EXIT_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY`
- `DetectsFDExhaustion` — the 101st exits `SESSION_EXIT_TOO_MANY_OPEN_FILES`

The fixture subclasses `HttpConnectionListenerImpl<boost::asio::ip::tcp>` and stubs out the accept loop so `handleAccept` can be driven directly with synthetic error codes.

**2. Three seams in `SessionHttpConnectionListenerImpl.hpp`.** These are the reason the fixture can exist, and they'd be dead code in pro if the tests left, so they have to travel with the file. None of them change behavior:

- `acceptNextConnection()` (~line 229): currently `private` and non-virtual. Needs to be `protected virtual` so the fixture can stub it and stop the accept loop from running.
- `exitEarly(int)`: needs a `protected virtual` override point wrapping `session::exitEarly(status)`, so the fixture can capture the status instead of terminating the test process.
- The three `LOG_ERROR(error)` calls in `handleAccept` (~lines 288, 304, 306): replaced by a `private virtual logAcceptError(const core::Error&, const core::ErrorLocation&)` that defaults to `core::log::logError(...)`, so the fixture can capture the error instead of writing to the log.

**3. No build changes.** `src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt:443` already does `file(GLOB_RECURSE SESSION_TEST_FILES "*Tests.cpp")`, so dropping the file in `src/cpp/session/http/` wires it into the `rsession` scope automatically.

### One thing to carry over

Do not port the fixture's original error-code construction. It built codes as `error_code(<errno value>, boost::system::system_category())`, which is only coherent on POSIX — on Windows that category holds Win32/Winsock values, so `ENOMEM` (12) and `EMFILE` (24) arrive as `ERROR_INVALID_ACCESS` and `ERROR_BAD_LENGTH`, neither of which Boost maps to a generic condition. Both `errc` comparisons in `handleAccept` then miss and it exits `EXIT_FAILURE` instead of the specific code, failing two of the three tests.

This was just fixed in pro by feeding `handleAccept` the codes Boost.Asio actually reports per platform — `ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY` and `WSAEMFILE` on Windows, `ENOMEM` and `EMFILE` elsewhere. Take the fixed version. `handleAccept` itself needed no change; Boost does map the real Windows codes, so the production path was already correct there.

Worth noting this is the strongest argument for moving the tests: the bug was a Windows platform-mapping issue in open-source code, and it only surfaced because pro started running the `rsession` scope on Windows CI. Windows coverage for this logic in this repo is currently zero and stays zero while the tests live in pro.

### Reference

rstudio/rstudio-pro#12766 (the Windows fix) and rstudio/rstudio-pro@476bd53d1e (the original tests and seams).

title: Custom Editor keybindings are sometimes not applied to the Console at startup
description:
### System details

RStudio Edition: Desktop and Server
RStudio Version: 2026.10.0 (main)
OS Version: all

### Steps to reproduce

1. Tools > Modify Keyboard Shortcuts, rebind an Editor-scope command (e.g. Remove Word Left) to a new shortcut, Apply.
2. Reload the browser page (Server) or restart RStudio (Desktop) with no source document open.
3. Type some text in the Console and press the new shortcut.

### Describe the problem in detail

Some of the time the shortcut does nothing in the Console until a source document is opened. The e2e canary `console_editor_keybindings.test.ts` ("the saved rebinding is applied to the console at startup") flaked this way on desktop-linux in run 34637770965, and its trace shows the client reading `keybindings/addins.json` and `keybindings/rstudio_bindings.json` after the reload but never `keybindings/editor_bindings.json`.

`EditorCommandManager` only registers its `EditorLoadedEvent` handler inside the `AceEditor.load()` callback, and `ExternalJavaScriptLoader` drains its callbacks one per scheduler tick, so the Console's Ace editor can attach and fire `EditorLoadedEvent` before the handler exists. When that happens the editor bindings are never loaded for that session until another editor loads.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Saved Editor keybindings apply to the Console on every startup, whether or not a source document is open.

title: Open file paths printed in the Terminal pane with Ctrl+Click / Cmd+Click
description:
### Feature request

Allow Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click on macOS) on a file path printed in the Terminal pane to open that file in the same RStudio instance.

The canonical example is `git status` output:

```
Changes not staged for commit:
        modified:   R/utils.R
        modified:   DESCRIPTION

Untracked files:
        tests/testthat/test-new.R
```

but it should apply to any file path a shell command prints: `ls` listings, compiler and linter diagnostics such as `src/foo.cpp:12:5: error: ...`, test failure locations, and so on. When a path carries a `:line[:column]` suffix, the file should open at that position.

### Details

- Relative paths should resolve against the terminal's current working directory (the one shown in the Terminal toolbar), not the R session's working directory.
- Only tokens that name an existing file should be underlined on hover, so ordinary words in the output are not turned into links.
- A plain click should keep its current behavior (positioning / selecting); the modifier is what opens the file, matching VS Code and most terminal emulators.
- There should be a way to turn this off, alongside the existing "Clickable web links" option in Global Options > Terminal.

The Terminal pane already makes web URLs clickable through xterm.js's web-links addon, and `rstudio <file>` (#14226) can open files from the command line; this would make the paths already on screen clickable too.

title: Request: also provide the insert-citation tool in source mode (it is só useful!)
description:
Thank you for all the efforts in making RStudio! This feature request has loose relationships with #7276 .

**Question**: Is it planned to provide the insert-citation tool (from visual mode) in _source mode_? That would be a great step IMHO. More experienced Rmd users will most probably prefer to work in source mode, but then would miss out this much relevant tool.

RStudio's insert-citation tool, compared to currently available tools (packages) in R, provides a unique combination of features which are really interesting in a collaborative, heterogeneous environment:

- ability to read both from bibliography files _and_ from Zotero
- ability to read and write to _csl-json, csl-yaml and bib_
- ability to amend existing bibliography files _without touching_ existing content

BTW did you also have a look at the [`rbbt`](https://github.com/paleolimbot/rbbt) package? While it does not combine all these features, it too has a very performant approach to connecting with Zotero; it may be inspiring.

title: Add API method for showing OS notifications; integrate with jobs
description:
Today, if you're running some code in RStudio that might take a while, there's no good mechanism for getting notified when it's done. There are a variety of R packages that can help, but the only truly cross-platform solution [emits a simple beep](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/beepr/index.html), which isn't much help if you're away from your desk. 

RStudio's API could add a method that would show a simple text notification, to be optionally used at the end of a long task. With the appropriate backends, it could show:

- Desktop notifications on MacOS, using `NSUserNotification` or [UserNotifications](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications?language=objc)
- [Toast notifications](https://github.com/Microsoft/Windows-classic-samples/tree/master/Samples/DesktopToasts) on Windows
- [Freedesktop notifications](https://developer.gnome.org/notification-spec/) on Linux
- [Web Notifications API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/notification) on RStudio Server

You could call this API at the end of your R Script to show a custom notification on completion. Optionally, we'd also show you an auto-generated notification:

1. When the IDE does not have focus, and an R command that took more than N seconds has finished executing
2. When a background job (in the Jobs pane) that took more than N seconds has finished
3. When indicated beforehand (gesture TBD) that a notification should be shown after completing the background job or R command about to be executed

Other interesting resources:

- [Notifications from R](https://kbroman.wordpress.com/2014/09/03/notifications-from-r/); blog post discussing approaches in 2014 (beepr, gmailr, rpushbullet)
- [Send OS X notification when done](https://gist.github.com/hrbrmstr/6545433); gist by @hrbrmstr 
- [Snorenotify](https://github.com/KDE/snorenotify); multi-platform Qt notification system

title: Quit or close project soon after a session restart prompts to save the workspace with save_workspace set to never
description:
### Describe the bug

A quit, project close, or project switch issued shortly after a session restart prompts "Save workspace image to `<path>/.RData`?" even when `save_workspace` is set to `never`.

The client learns the session's save action two ways, and before this fix both started at "ask":

- `ApplicationQuit.saveAction_` was initialized to `SaveAction.saveAsk()` and only corrected when a `save_action_changed` client event arrived. The action was not part of `SessionInfo`, so there was nothing else to fall back on.
- On the session side, `s_lastSaveAction` starts at `r::session::kSaveActionAsk` (`SessionDirty.cpp`), and `onClientInit` published that placeholder as-is. Only the first `onDetectChanges` pass recomputed it and emitted the corrected value.

So a close issued before the new session's first event batch reached the client used "ask" and prompted. Every session emitted `save_action_changed {action: -1}` followed by `{action: 0}`, which is directly visible in CI event-stream payloads.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `save_workspace` to `never`.
2. Open a project (or restart the session).
3. Within roughly a second of the new session becoming interactive, close the project or quit.

The prompt appears in that window. Outside it, the corrected save action has arrived and the close proceeds without prompting.

### Expected behavior

With `save_workspace` set to `never`, no close or quit prompts to save the workspace image, regardless of when it is issued relative to a session restart.

### Impact

For an interactive user this is one dismissible prompt, and every path that reaches it is user-initiated (quit, restart/update RStudio, switch R version, new project, close project, switch projects) -- nothing background can trigger it.

Two secondary effects:

- Inside the same window, Restart R derives `saveChanges` from `SAVEASK != NOSAVE`, so a restart can write `.RData` even with `save_workspace` set to `never`. This one is silent rather than dismissible.
- Unattended automation cannot answer the modal, so the close never completes. This blocked `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/posit-assistant-chat/restart-under-agent.test.ts`, which timed out after 30s waiting on `window.rstudio.project.isActive() === false` while the prompt sat unanswered.

### How it was found

Six consecutive failures of the above test on the Windows shard of the Posit Assistant release gate. In the failing trace the new session's first `get_events` took 1940ms, of which only 6.7ms was server think-time -- the rest was connection establishment. The close was clicked 1.64s before that batch was delivered, so the client held no save action for the session at all.

### Not a regression

Both defaults are long-standing: `saveAction_ = SaveAction.saveAsk()` dates to 2011 (`4993b7e7e3d`) and `s_lastSaveAction = kSaveActionAsk` to 2013 (`57a301581a1`). Both are present unchanged on `rel-autumn-hawkbit`. What changed was the timing of the first event batch, not RStudio.

### System details

- RStudio Edition: Desktop
- RStudio Version: 2026.10.0-daily+39 (also affects earlier releases)
- OS Version: Windows Server 2025 (observed); platform-independent by inspection
- R Version: 4.6.1

title: Refreshing the presentation preview crashes on a profile that has never opened the Presentation pane
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.09.0+175
    OS Version      : macOS 26.6.2
    R Version       : 4.6.1

### Steps to reproduce the problem

This needs a profile where the Presentation pane has never been shown. A new user account works, as does pointing `RSTUDIO_CONFIG_ROOT` at an empty directory.

1. Start RStudio on that profile.
2. Press <kbd>Cmd+Shift+P</kbd> to open the Command Palette.
3. Type "Refresh the presentation preview".
    - The entry is listed and available.
4. Click "Refresh the presentation preview".
    - Nothing happens on screen. No error dialog appears, and nothing reaches the browser console.
    - The session log records a client exception.
5. Press <kbd>Cmd+Shift+P</kbd> to open the Command Palette again.
6. Type "Refresh the presentation preview".
    - The entry is now greyed out and can't be picked.

The log entry, from `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME/log/rsession-<user>.log`. It's one line in the file, wrapped here to make the frames readable:

```
ERROR CLIENT EXCEPTION: (TypeError) : Cannot read properties of null (reading 'postMessage');
|||org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/presentation2/Presentation2Pane.java#430::postRevealMessage
|||org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/presentation2/Presentation2Pane.java#301::refresh
|||org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/presentation2/Presentation2Tab_Shim__Impl.java#92::onSuccess2
|||org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/presentation2/Presentation2Tab_Shim__Impl.java#85::onSuccess
|||com/google/gwt/core/client/impl/OnSuccessExecutor.java#33::execute
|||com/google/gwt/core/client/impl/SchedulerImpl.java#167::runScheduledTasks
```

### Describe the problem in detail

On a profile whose Presentation pane has never been shown, the Command Palette offers "Refresh the presentation preview" as available, but picking it throws an uncaught client exception instead of doing anything. The failure is completely silent from the user's side: no dialog, no message in the browser console, and no visible change. The only record is the session log.

It happens once per session. The same failure leaves the command disabled afterwards, so a second attempt finds the entry greyed out and nothing further goes wrong. This affects a first-run profile in particular, since a profile that has shown the Presentation pane even once won't reproduce it.

### Describe the behavior you expected

The command wouldn't be offered until the Presentation pane can accept it, and picking it wouldn't throw. Failing that, a failure of this kind would ideally tell the user something rather than doing nothing at all.

title: Highlight unexpected character encodings: "c" and "с"

Hi Team,

> Symbols "c" and "с" look identical, but actually belong to different encodings.

Sure enough:

$ cat c.txt 
c с

00000000  63 20 d1 81 20 0a                                 |c .. .|
00000006

0000000   c     321 201      \n                                        
0000006

Can we please add a highlight for unexpected character encodings?

title: Ctrl + shift +m to insert "+" rather than "|>" or "%>%" when operating inside a chunk of ggplot code
description:
Problem:
When writing R in Rstudio, ctrl + shift + m is frequently and commonly used to insert the pipe operator.
Conceptually, I think of it as "and this thing goes into the next thing."
This is how I think of the layers of a ggplot as well. (The complex semantic model of the grammar of graphics means, of course, that they aren't really the same thing. But they sure act like it most of the time.)

But then I hit ctrl+shift+m  for 'the next thing', but it is the wrong next thing connector, a pipe instead of '+.'

Solution:
On an invocation of ctrl+shift+m, parse nearby lines to see if in a ggplot block, and if so, then insert '+' instead of the pipe.

title: Add "Remove Word Left" to the keybindings of the console as well
description:
At the moment (Rstudio version 2022.07.1 Build 554) the "Remove Word Left" and "Remove Word Right" only exist in the "Editor" scope, but they are very useful features for the console (I believe he scope is called "R") as well. Also since the user has the option in the editor, it is very normal that they use the same keybinding in the console as well.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/390889/204461628-81a59d84-4b50-40e1-a71d-8952de085ed3.png)

This situation can also get into a very annoying situation if the Remove Word Left is mapped to <kbd>Ctrl</kbd><kbd>w</kbd>, because in Rstudio server which is opened in browser, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd><kbd>w</kbd> means "close tab". So the user can get zapped when they want to delete a word, but instead they close the whole Rstudio. Adding this keybinding for the console scope in Rstudio would make the browser to pass it to the webpage rather than using it itself to execute an action.

The <kbd>Ctrl</kbd><kbd>w</kbd> is by default mapped to "kill from the cursor to the previous whitespace" in almost all terminals (even R console), and all software that use readline:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/390889/204463116-1e5ab441-6813-4ac3-a043-c611019bb5fc.png)

you can get the same info page by running `info readline "command line editing" "introduction"` in the terminal of any GNU system.

title: Add infinite console history
description: ### Problem Statement Sometimes I mess up and print a lot of stuff I don't really care about, which "fills" the console, making it impossible to see old stuff that happened before the mishap (or sometimes even relevant info that caused the mishap). I want to have the option to access this old console output even if afterwards there were thousands of lines of nonsense. What caused this mess of numbers? nobody knows... ### Proposed Behaviour One solution would be to just have (practically) infinite console history. I know this is possible, because the terminal emulator I am using ([Konsole](https://konsole.kde.org/)) has this option. The implementation apparently relies on saving older data to disk (basically as a log file) to not require infinite amounts of RAM. This should of course not be enabled by default to not have users wonder why RStudio creates gigabytes upon gigabytes of temporary files. All of this is likely just as useful for the terminal. Another linked request would be to have the finite history configurable, i.e if I am fine with RStudio using more RAM to have the normal history be longer.

title: RStudio Desktop fails to startup when Command Prompt is disabled by Group Policy
description:
> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> We've fixed this specific issue so RStudio should now start when command-prompt is disabled, but more remains to be done before RStudio will actually be usable in such a configuration. #18758 at a minimum


### System details
RStudio Edition: Desktop (open source)
RStudio Version: 2026.08.2+200 "Yellow Yarrow" (Electron 42.7.1, Chrome 148)
OS: Windows 11, Intune-managed corporate device, standard (non-admin) account
R Version: 4.6.1 (x64, UCRT), C:\Program Files\R\R-4.6.1

### Symptom
RStudio launches, briefly shows the splash screen, then exits. No error dialog, no crash, nothing in the Windows event log. Occasionally it reaches "Initializing R — the R session is initializing" and stays there indefinitely. Last working session was 19 August 2026.

### What the debug log shows
With log-level=debug, R is detected and validated correctly, rsession is launched, and the front end makes exactly one request:
    18:50:45.432  Launching rsession: rsession-utf8.exe --config-file none
                  --program-mode desktop --www-port 23192
                  --launcher-token a1b0a639 --show-help-home 1
    18:50:45.489  Setting base URL: http://127.0.0.1:23192
    18:50:45.506  GET http://127.0.0.1:23192/ [mainFrame]
    18:50:45.569  GET file:///.../.webpack/renderer/splash/index.html
    18:50:45.680  GET file:///.../.webpack/renderer/splash/index.js
                  (no further entries)

The front end never retries and logs no failure. On other runs the only entry is:

    ERROR Failed to load http://127.0.0.1:<port>: ERR_CONNECTION_RESET (-101)

### rsession is healthy
rsession starts, binds, and takes its lock normally:

    18:50:45.988  Initializing HTTP connection listener
                  [address=127.0.0.1; port=23192; secret=<redacted>]
    18:50:45.989  Setting SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE socket option on connection
    18:50:46.303  (PID 26252): Acquired lock: .../sources/session-a1b0a639/lock_file

While a session was live I requested the same URL from an unrelated browser on the same machine. It returned HTTP 403 with an empty body in 7 ms — the correct response to an unauthenticated request. So the loopback path works, the port is reachable, and rsession answers immediately. The failure is in the authenticated exchange between the front end and the session.

### Ruled out
- R itself: Rterm.exe is queried three times per launch, returns 4.6.1 in
  ~140 ms, status 0 every time
- RStudio install integrity: verified complete, 4581 files, all renderer   bundles present
- RStudio state: full reset per the official procedure (renamed %APPDATA%\RStudio and %LOCALAPPDATA%\RStudio), repeatedly
- R startup files: no .Rprofile, .Renviron is one line, .RData is 18 KB;
  load_workspace disabled
- Package library: 42 packages, all built under 4.6.0/4.6.1, no 00LOCK dirs
- Renderer/GPU: renderer process is present (--type=renderer); software rendering and --no-sandbox make no difference
- Security software: Windows Defender protection history empty, no Exploit Protection program entries, FortiClient quit, Bitdefender not installed
- Proxy: no proxy configured
- Version: same behavior on 2026.08.0+187 and 2026.08.2+200
- Reboots, reinstalls of both R and RStudio

### Notes
