title: Remove dead recommendedRStudioVersion warning-bar code from SessionChat.cpp
description:
The `recommendedRStudioVersion` handling in `SessionChat.cpp` is dead code and can be removed. The corresponding field is being dropped from the Posit Assistant manifest, so nothing will populate it.

## Background

The code reads an optional `recommendedRStudioVersion` object from the Posit Assistant manifest and, when the running RStudio is older than the recommended version, enqueues a warning bar linking to a download page. It was added in #16907 (Jan 2026) for Posit AI beta testers and has not been modified since.

It cannot fire for released builds. The check is gated on the version string containing `-daily` or `-hourly`:

```cpp
bool isPrereleaseBuild = versionStr.find("-daily")  != std::string::npos ||
                         versionStr.find("-hourly") != std::string::npos;
bool forceCheck = !core::system::getenv("RSTUDIO_FORCE_DEV_UPDATE_CHECK").empty();
...
else if (!isPrereleaseBuild && !forceCheck)
   DLOG("  Skipping version warning (release build)");
```

It is additionally startup-only (`wasStartup`, so never on a pane-open or Retry check) and skipped when Posit Assistant is not installed. The banner text also references an arrangement that no longer matches how the product is described.

## Scope

All of it lives in `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp`:

| Lines | What |
| --- | --- |
| 4042-4085 | `getRecommendedRStudioVersion()` |
| 4087-4103 | `showRStudioVersionWarning()` |
| 4591-4593 | locals `showVersionWarning`, `recommendedVersion`, `downloadPageUrl` |
| 4623-4624 | the firing block in `finish()` |
| 4763-4800 | the `if (wasStartup)` computation block |

The `RSTUDIO_FORCE_DEV_UPDATE_CHECK` environment variable goes away with it; this is its only use in the tree.

**Keep** `client_events::kShowWarningBar` and the surrounding warning-bar plumbing — `showTestManifestWarning()` still uses it.

No tests reference any of this.

## Ordering

Independent of the manifest change. `getRecommendedRStudioVersion` already returns an error when the key is absent and the caller skips silently, which is the documented "expected for older manifests" path, so either side can land first.

title: getSubprocesses() on Windows reports unrelated processes as children after pid reuse
description:
### Summary

On Windows, `getSubprocesses()` (`src/cpp/core/system/Win32System.cpp:1085`) walks a Toolhelp snapshot and treats any process whose `th32ParentProcessID` equals the requested pid as a child:

```cpp
if (pe32.th32ParentProcessID == pid)
{
   // Found a child process
   ...
}
```

Windows never clears `th32ParentProcessID` when a parent exits, and it recycles pids. So any orphan whose long-dead parent's pid has since been reassigned is reported as a child of whatever process holds that pid now.

### Evidence

Found while investigating a `Win32ProcessTest` failure on the Windows daily build at 98adde4bfd8.

`vctip.exe` — the MSVC telemetry process, which the build itself orphans — sits on the machine with `ParentProcessId = 8000`, a pid that is dead and free for reuse:

```
ProcessId       : 2216
ParentProcessId : 8000
parent 8000 is DEAD -- pid free for reuse
```

A test that creates a `ping.exe` and asks for its children gets handed `vctip.exe` whenever that new process draws pid 8000. Over 400 iterations that happened 3 times (~0.75%):

```
unexpected children: vctip.exe(2216)
[  FAILED  ] Win32ProcessTest.EmptySubprocListWhenNoChildProcesses
```

Nothing about this is specific to the tests — it is the API answering the question wrongly.

### Impact

Callers use this to decide whether a process has a live child. `session::console_process` uses it to suppress console input capture while a subprocess is running, so a false positive suppresses capture for a terminal that has no child. It fails safe (nothing gets killed that shouldn't) and is rare, so this is low severity, but the answer is wrong and the flakiness it causes in CI is real.

### Suggested fix

Cross-check creation times: a real child cannot have been created before its parent. Fetch the candidate's and the parent's creation time via `GetProcessTimes` (or `PROCESSENTRY32`'s pid plus an `OpenProcess`/`GetProcessTimes` pair) and drop any candidate created earlier than the process it supposedly belongs to. That rules out stale parent references generally, since the reused pid is by definition younger than the orphan pointing at it.

### Related

The test-side half of this — the suite orphaning its own `ping.exe` grandchildren, which was the dominant cause of the daily-build failure — is addressed separately. That change removes the orphans the tests create but cannot remove the machine's.

title: Select and view specific columns in the data viewer
description:
The addition of the summary panel in the new version of RStudio is great. Pinned columns are helpful but is there a chance at any stage that we might be able to make this even better by being able to manually select/deselect columns to view in the data viewer? Something like the functionality that the dataviewR package and Stata (natively) provides. This would be an amazing functionality boost, rather than having to type my way there at the moment - e.g. `dat  |> select(x1, x2, x3) |> View()`. Adding an individual column select/deselect ability(via radio buttons or similar) to the column listing in the summary panel would do this, but given I don't know anything about programming, I don't know how easy or not it would be to implement.
Thanks for the new update.

title: Reduce the disk space used by RStudio installations
description:
# Reduce the disk space used by RStudio installations

RStudio installations include Copilot Language Server binaries for other platforms, JavaScript source maps, and uncompressed GWT symbol maps. macOS application bundles can also use transparent filesystem compression to reduce their installed footprint.

Reduce installed size by excluding unused platform binaries and JavaScript source maps, compressing GWT symbol maps while retaining runtime support for reading them, and transparently compressing the macOS application bundle while preserving valid code signatures.

Implementation and validation: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/18721

title: Optimize RStudio Desktop startup time
description:
# Optimize RStudio Desktop startup time

RStudio Desktop startup performs shell PATH discovery, R detection, session initialization, and client loading with opportunities to overlap work and avoid repeated processing.

Measure startup across the desktop, session, and client processes and reduce time to a usable workbench by caching shell PATH information, detecting R asynchronously, serving static assets during R initialization, precompressing GWT assets, and deferring client resources until they are needed.

Implemented and validated in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/18716 (already merged). This issue records the associated change for release-note traceability.

title: Diagnostics report spurious "unexpected end of document" when a file ends with a semicolon
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.10.0 (dev)
    OS Version      : macOS
    R Version       : 4.6.1

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Save an R script whose final statement ends with a semicolon:

```r
x <- 1;
```

### Describe the problem in detail

The diagnostics system reports "unexpected end of document" at the end of the file, even though this is valid R code. Any script ending in `statement;` (with or without a trailing newline) triggers the false positive; a semicolon followed by another statement is handled fine.

Found via differential testing of the diagnostics parser against R's parser while investigating #18717.

### Describe the behavior you expected

No diagnostic, matching `parse()`.

title: LaTeX math is invisible in Quarto Visual Editor and math preview fails in Source Editor in RStudio 2026.08.0+187
description:
### System details

RStudio Edition : Desktop R
Studio Version : 2026.08.0+187 OS 
Version : macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon, arm64) 
R Version : R 4.6.1 (2026-06-24) 
Quarto Version : 1.9.38

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Steps to reproduce the problem
Open RStudio 2026.08.0+187.
Create a new Quarto .qmd document.
Enter the following:

```
---
format: html
---

This is inline math: $\mu = 5$.

$$
\bar{X} \sim N\left(\mu,\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)
$$
```

Switch to Visual mode.
Observe that the mathematical expressions are blank/invisible.
Switch to Source mode and place the cursor over a mathematical expression. The rendered math preview popup does not appear.

### Describe the problem in detail

After updating RStudio Desktop from 2026.07.1+147 to 2026.08.0+187, LaTeX mathematical expressions in Quarto .qmd files stopped displaying in the editor.

In Visual mode, both inline and display equations are blank/invisible. In Source mode, the usual rendered-math preview popup also fails to appear.

The problem occurs in a newly created minimal .qmd file, so it does not appear to depend on the contents or configuration of an existing Quarto project.

I downgraded RStudio to 2026.07.1+147, without changing R or Quarto. The problem immediately disappeared: equations display normally in Visual mode and the math preview works normally in Source mode.

Thus:

- RStudio 2026.08.0+187: problem occurs
- RStudio 2026.07.1+147: problem does not occur
- R 4.6.1 in both cases
- Quarto 1.9.38 in both cases
- Same computer and .qmd test file

This appears to be a regression introduced in RStudio 2026.08.0.

One possibly relevant observation: I had previously experienced a separate issue in Visual mode in which the editor would jump unexpectedly when opening a new file and executing R code. That behavior appears to be fixed in 2026.08.0. I had a workable workaround for that earlier issue, whereas the failure to display mathematical expressions makes Visual mode difficult to use for documents containing substantial LaTeX math.

### Describe the behavior you expected

LaTeX mathematical expressions should be rendered in Quarto Visual mode, and the rendered-math preview should appear in Source mode as it did in RStudio 2026.07.1+147.

title: RStudio Server: rsession deadlocks at startup in __cxa_guard_acquire, session never becomes usable
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Server (open source)
    RStudio Version : 2025.09.2+418
    OS Version      : Ubuntu 24.04 (noble), running in a Kubernetes container
    R Version       : 4.5.2

Sessions run with `--auth-none=1`, one user per container.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

We have no deterministic reproducer — that is the main difficulty. It happens
sporadically when opening RStudio, on multiple independent workspaces.

Symptoms:

1. Open RStudio in the browser.
2. Spinner for 1–2 minutes.
3. Either "R is taking longer to start than usual" (Reload / Safe Mode / Terminate R),
   or a blank screen.
4. Reload and Terminate R do not help — the replacement session often deadlocks
   immediately as well. Safe Mode usually works.

### Describe the problem in detail

The rsession main thread is blocked in `__cxa_guard_acquire` — the C++ ABI's
thread-safe initialiser for a function-local `static` — reached from
`Rf_ReplIteration` / `R_ReadConsole`. From `eu-stack` on a core dump
(`kill -QUIT`; frames #2–#6 are unresolved because the shipped `rsession` is
stripped):

```
#0  0x00007e06b451828d syscall
#1  0x00007e06b47d55d0 __cxa_guard_acquire
#2  0x00005b474333f846
#3  0x00005b4743333c55
#4  0x00005b4743335bd8
#5  0x00005b47432973e2
#6  0x00005b4743df95bc
#7  0x00007e06b527230a Rf_ReplIteration
#8  0x00007e06b52727a8 R_ReplConsole
#9  0x00007e06b5272860 run_Rmainloop
...
#14 0x00007e06b441b28b __libc_start_main
```

Frame #2 is inside the `rsession` executable itself, not a loaded library.

**No other thread holds the guard.** All nine remaining threads are parked idle,
so this looks like an *orphaned* initialisation guard rather than contention:

| TID | top frame |
| --- | --- |
| 532 | `__select` |
| 468 | `clock_nanosleep` → `clic_thread_func` |
| 490 | `pthread_cond_wait` → `background_thread_entry` (jemalloc) |
| 458 | `__sigtimedwait` → `sigwait` |
| 545, 531, 460 | `pthread_cond_timedwait` |
| 459 | `pthread_cond_wait` |
| 461 | `epoll_wait` |

The main thread's `wchan` stays at `futex_wait_queue` and its CPU time does not
advance at all (0 ticks over 6s, measured from `/proc/PID/task/PID/stat`).

Downstream consequences, which we believe are effects rather than causes:

- The browser's `POST /rpc/client_init` stays **pending indefinitely**. We
  confirmed rserver did deliver it to rsession — rserver opens a fresh unix socket
  to the session for the request and both socket queues are drained — so rsession
  received it and never replied.
- `ERROR r error 5 (R symbol not found) [symbol: .rs.explorer.getCache]` and the
  same for `.rs.isReadingUserInput`, `.rs.renv.context`, `.rs.listInstalledPackages`,
  logged 1–2 seconds after session start. Presumably `tools:rstudio` is never
  established because init never completed.
- `ERROR The previous R session terminated abnormally` on subsequent starts, after
  a user presses Terminate R.
- rserver accumulates `CLOSE-WAIT` sockets on 8787 from abandoned attempts.

### What we ruled out

Each of the following was removed or emptied and the hang still occurred:

- server-data-dir and the server sqlite DB
- `~/.local/share/rstudio/sessions/active`, including `suspended-session-data`
- `Rprofile.site` and `~/.Rprofile` (both truncated to zero bytes)
- `.RData` (absent on an affected workspace)

Also excluded: memory pressure (`memory.events` `oom_kill 0`, ~1 GB of a 5 GB
limit), disk and inode exhaustion, and the container's storage backend (a
persistent volume and node-local disk measure the same for small-file and fsync
latency). It reproduced on a workspace whose home directory contained 29 MB, so
it is not accumulated state.

OpenBLAS (pthread build), libgomp, Intel TBB (via RcppParallel), Arrow and
jemalloc are all loaded in the process, but all of their threads are parked idle
and the blocking static is in `rsession`.

### Recovery, in case it helps others

`SIGKILL` the rsession process; rserver spawns a replacement by itself. Note
`SIGTERM` is caught and triggers a *suspend* instead, and a resumed session does
not re-run `Rprofile.site`. Killing alone is often not enough — the replacement
can deadlock immediately — but additionally clearing
`~/.local/share/rstudio/sessions/active` has recovered it each time we have tried.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Session initialisation either completes or fails with a diagnosable error, rather
than blocking indefinitely on a static-initialisation guard that no thread holds.

### What would help us give you more

`rsession` is stripped and the container lacks `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`, so we can only
get core-file backtraces and cannot resolve frames #2–#6. If you can tell us which
static initialisation sits on the `R_ReadConsole` path — or point at a debug build
or symbol file — we can pin it down. We can also test a patched or daily build:
one of our workspaces currently reproduces this on nearly every session start.

Also happy to attach the core dump (~900 MB) through whatever channel you prefer.

### Related

- Forum thread for this report: https://forum.posit.co/t/rstudio-ide-fails-to-start-with-r-is-taking-longer-than-usual-on-rstudio-server-linux/217690
- An earlier, apparently independent report of the same symptom on v2025.09:
  https://forum.posit.co/t/r-is-taking-longer-to-start-than-usual-on-rstudio-server-linux/210398
  (no diagnosis, auto-closed)
- #15276 shares the "previous R session terminated abnormally" symptom but has a
  different cause (a crash unserialising `suspended-session-data`); we verified
  removing that data does not prevent this hanng.
- We do not see this problem in other environments, where we are running RStudio Server 2024.12.0 Build 467 on ubuntu 20.04 on a kubernetes container

### Checklist

- [x] I have read the guide for submitting good bug reports
- [ ] **I have not been able to confirm this on the latest version.** We are on
      2025.09.2+418; the latest is 2026.08.2. I checked the release notes from
      2025.09 through 2026.08.2 and found nothing describing this, but I cannot
      claim it still reproduces on current. Testing an upgrade is next for us.
- [x] Core dump captured and thread backtraces included above
- [ ] No minimal reproducible instructions — the failure is intermittent and we
      have not isolated a trigger

title: Add connections troubleshooting FAQ to data-connections page
description:
## Problem Statement

The "Troubleshooting Connections" support article on support.posit.co (article 115011264307) is being retired as the support site shuts down. The article served as the primary user-facing entry point for database connection problems in RStudio's Connections Pane. Without it, users searching for connection troubleshooting have no single page to land on.

Most of the underlying content exists on solutions.posit.co but is scattered across multiple pages. The IDE User Guide's `data-connections.qmd` page has no troubleshooting content and lists only 3 of 5 connection discovery methods.

## Proposed Changes

1. Expand the "New connection interface" section to cover all 5 connection discovery methods (ODBC drivers, system DSNs, user-level DSNs, admin snippets, R package connection contracts)
2. Add a "Troubleshooting" section with 7 FAQ items migrated from the support article:
   - Connection not appearing in the pane (Connections Contract)
   - ODBC setup overview
   - What is a DSN
   - Package choice (odbc vs RODBC, JDBC)
   - Oracle connections
   - Encoding/catalog first-character issue
   - Apple silicon driver notes

Each answer is brief and links to the detailed page on solutions.posit.co or docs.posit.co rather than duplicating content.

Related to PPDS-601.

| `actions/setup-node` | v4.4.0 | v5.0.0 | 15 |
| `actions/download-artifact` | v4.3.0 | v7.0.0 | 14 |
| `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` | v2.9.4 | v3.0.0 | 6 |
| `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` | v4.3.1 | v6.0.0 | 6 |

Six of those references float on a major tag rather than a SHA and want pinning at the same time: `actions/checkout@v4` in `os-build-dependencies-windows.yml` and `os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml`; `actions/upload-artifact@v4`, `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4` and `r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2` in `os-build-dependencies-windows.yml`; and `actions/stale@v3` in `os-stale.yml`. That last one is on the Node 12 runtime and is eight majors behind, so it reads as a migration rather than a bump and would be easier to review on its own.

Nothing is broken today. GitHub has run node20-targeting actions on Node 24 since 2026-06-16, so these already work. Node 20 leaves the runner on 2026-09-16, and what goes with it is the `ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION` fallback, so an action that turned out to be incompatible would have no remedy short of bumping it. That is the reason to finish before mid-September.

### Proposed Behaviour

Bump each site to the first major of that action that runs on Node 24, keeping the SHA pin and trailing version comment the repo already uses.

The first node24 major rather than the latest, deliberately: the later majors are ESM rewrites, and `download-artifact@v8` turns a download digest mismatch from a warning into a run-failing error.

Splitting the work per action would keep any failure attributable to one change. `.github/actions/os-e2e-deps/action.yml` is worth doing early, since its six cache calls fan out to eight caller workflows.

Two caveats carry over from the sample:

- `actions/cache/save` cannot be exercised from a branch, because every save is gated on the `main` ref plus a cache miss. Each save reads `cache-primary-key` from its paired restore, and a break there would be silent rather than red, so it would be good to see one main-scoped save succeed on v5.0.0 before the other 20 move.
- The six remaining `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` sites cannot be exercised at all, because nothing sets the `post_pr_comment` input they are gated on. #18595 covers removing those steps, which may make six of these bumps unnecessary.

This change is scoped entirely to .github/workflows/*.yml and .github/actions/*/action.yml — GitHub Actions CI configuration only. No source code, build scripts, or RStudio's runtime behavior is touched. The blast radius, if anything were wrong, is limited to CI runs on this and future branches, not the product itself.

title: Handle callback snapshot failures safely in AsyncClient
description:
### Summary

AsyncClient copies boost::function callbacks out of socketMutex_ before invoking them. Several callback snapshot sites use LOCK_MUTEX / END_LOCK_MUTEX, whose unexpected-exception path logs the exception and continues execution.

If a callback copy throws, execution can therefore continue with only some local state initialized. In deliverChunks(), for example, handlersDisabled_ is copied before fixedBufferHandler_. If the handler copy fails, the local handler remains empty and the decoded chunk is appended to response_ as though no streaming handler were installed. The streaming consumer can then complete without receiving that piece. Similar snapshot behavior in closeAndRespond() and handleWrite() can lose completion or connection notifications.

The realistic trigger is allocation failure while copying boost::function, so this is a very low-probability exception-safety issue rather than a normal operational failure.

### Suggested change

Use an explicit lock guard for fallible callback snapshots and handle copy failure as an error. The operation should close or disable the client and take an error path, rather than treating the failed copy as an absent callback. A small helper returning ready, disabled, or failed could keep the behavior consistent across invocation sites.

A fault-injection test using a callable with a throwing copy constructor would help cover this path.

### Context

Follow-up from #18541.

Relevant code: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/2bed86b67fd559a8015f265f93132b4b220828ff/src/cpp/core/include/core/http/AsyncClient.hpp#L1460-L1467

title: Sidebar visibility and Pane Layout changes propagate to other open RStudio windows
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.06.0+242 through 2026.08.2
    OS Version      : macOS
    R Version       : any

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Sidebar:

1. Open two RStudio Desktop windows (two separate sessions/projects).
2. In window A, toggle the sidebar with the toolbar button (or Command Palette).
3. Look at window B.

Pane layout:

1. Open two RStudio Desktop windows.
2. In window A, open Tools > Global Options > Pane Layout and rearrange the quadrants (e.g. move Console from lower-left to upper-right), then click OK.
3. Look at window B.

### Describe the problem in detail

The change applies to every open window, not just the one where it was made. Showing or hiding the sidebar in one window shows or hides it in the others, and rearranging the pane quadrants in one window re-lays out the others live, while the user is working in them.

This is disruptive because the two windows are otherwise independent sessions, and the layout shifts underneath the user without any action on their part.

This did not happen before 2026.06.0+242. It reproduces in every release from 2026.06.0+242 up to and including 2026.08.2.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Previously, Sidebar visibility and pane layout changes only applied to the window where the change was made. Other already-open windows kept their current layout, but new sessions would use the new layout.

So it's "barely" a bug in some sense.

### Notes

`panes` (including `sidebar_visible` and `sidebar_location`) is a user-level preference in `rstudio-prefs.json`, so a write from one session propagates to the others via the `user_prefs_changed` client event. The frontend then applies it live: `PaneManager.java:438` re-runs the layout on any `panes` value change, and `GlobalToolbar.java:271` updates the sidebar toggle button. Whatever landed between 2026.05.1+225 and 2026.06.0+242 appears to have made that cross-session propagation actually reach other open windows.

title: CI: FetchContent git clones have no retry backoff, so a brief DNS blip fails the build
description:
### Problem

A momentary DNS failure on a CI runner fails the whole C++ configure step, because CMake's `FetchContent` git-clone retries fire back-to-back with no backoff.

Seen on the macOS 15 x86_64 cache seed ([run 30305581198](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30305581198)):

```
2026-07-27T21:18:04.4129040Z Cloning into 'zlib-src'...
2026-07-27T21:18:04.4714110Z fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/madler/zlib/': Could not resolve host: github.com
2026-07-27T21:18:04.5721460Z Cloning into 'zlib-src'...
2026-07-27T21:18:04.6439010Z fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/madler/zlib/': Could not resolve host: github.com
2026-07-27T21:18:04.6465780Z Cloning into 'zlib-src'...
2026-07-27T21:18:04.6486180Z fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/madler/zlib/': Could not resolve host: github.com
2026-07-27T21:18:04.6508470Z Had to git clone more than once: 3 times.
CMake Error at zlib-subbuild/zlib-populate-prefix/tmp/zlib-populate-gitclone.cmake:55 (message):
  Failed to clone repository: 'https://github.com/madler/zlib'
```

All three attempts start and fail inside ~236 ms. Three retries against an outage that lasts even a second are three retries against the same failure, so the retry loop buys nothing for exactly the class of fault it exists to absorb.

### Scope

This is not zlib-specific. `src/cpp/ext/CMakeLists.txt` declares 12 dependencies through the same `dependency()` helper, which always uses a git clone:

```cmake
FetchContent_Declare("${_NAME}"
   GIT_REPOSITORY "${${_PREFIX}_REPOSITORY}"
   GIT_TAG        "${${_PREFIX}_REVISION}"
   GIT_SHALLOW    ON
   ...)
```

zlib is simply the first one fetched (`fetch(zlib ZLIB)` at line 421, deliberately ordered ahead of libgit2), so it is the one that reports the failure. Any of the 12 is equally exposed, and any CI job that configures the C++ build can hit this -- PR builds included, not just the cache seeds.

### Notes toward a fix

The retry loop lives in CMake's *generated* `*-gitclone.cmake`, and CMake exposes no knob for the retry count or cadence, so the fix probably has to sit outside it. Some options, none obviously best:

- Retry the cmake configure step at the CI level.
- Cache or pre-warm the `_deps` source trees so a clone isn't needed on every cold build.
- Switch `FetchContent_Declare` to `URL` tarballs with a hash (and possibly a mirror), which downloads through a different code path than `GIT_REPOSITORY`.
- Prefer a system copy where one is reliably available (`RSTUDIO_USE_SYSTEM_<DEP>` already exists as a knob).

### Context

Found while investigating #18373. That issue's underlying cause -- a wrong GWT cache path that made the seed re-run every two hours -- is fixed in #18375; this flake is the unrelated reason that particular run went red, and is filed separately because it affects every platform and every dependency, not just the macOS seed.

title: E2E dependency install fails compiling the R odbc package on engines without the database stack enabled
description:
### System details

    Workflow        : Test: E2E Playwright RStudio (Scheduled Rotation and Run-All, Open Source)
    Affected step   : Install e2e test dependencies (.github/actions/os-e2e-deps)
    Affected engines: ubuntu-22-arm64, fedora-43-arm64, fedora-44-arm64

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Run the scheduled E2E rotation for an engine whose `.github/e2e-linux/<os>.json` does not set `install_database_stack: true` and whose distro/arch has no Posit Package Manager binary for the R `odbc` package, for example `ubuntu-22-arm64`.
    - The "Install e2e test dependencies" step fails while compiling `odbc` from source.
    - The log shows `fatal error: sql.h: No such file or directory` followed by `ERROR: configuration failed for package 'odbc'`.
2. See the failed run at https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/33310537121, jobs "Ubuntu 22 (arm64)", "Fedora 43 (arm64)", and "Fedora 44 (arm64)".

### Describe the problem in detail

`odbc` is listed in `e2e/rstudio/required-packages.txt`, which every E2E engine installs unconditionally. Compiling `odbc` from source needs the unixODBC headers (`unixodbc-dev` on Debian/Ubuntu, `unixODBC-devel` on Fedora/RHEL/Rocky), but those headers are only installed by the `os-e2e-deps` action when an engine's config sets `install_database_stack: true` (used to provision the fuller Connections pane test stack). An engine that leaves that flag unset and lands on a distro/arch where PPM has no `odbc` binary hits this failure. It doesn't affect every engine without the flag: several others (e.g. `rocky-9-arm64`, `ubuntu-26-arm64`) also leave it unset but currently get a PPM binary for `odbc`, so they aren't affected today.

### Describe the behavior you expected

The dependency-install step should succeed regardless of whether `install_database_stack` is set, since `odbc` is now a hard requirement for every engine, not just the ones testing Connections.

title: e2e flaky test: AsyncConnectionImpl.ContinueParsingResumesOnTheConnectionsStrand
description:
`AsyncConnectionImpl.ContinueParsingResumesOnTheConnectionsStrand`
(`src/cpp/core/http/AsyncConnectionImplTests.cpp:353`) fails intermittently in
`rstudio-core-tests`.

## Symptom

```
../src/cpp/core/http/AsyncConnectionImplTests.cpp:400: Failure
Expected equality of these values:
  handlerCalls
    Which is: 0
  1
```

## Frequency

Measured on macOS arm64 on 2026-08-24, at 00141138ba (the test file is
unmodified on the branch I measured from):

- `--gtest_filter='AsyncConnectionImpl.*'` -- 9 failures in 15 runs
- `--gtest_filter='AsyncConnectionImpl.ContinueParsingResumesOnTheConnectionsStrand'` -- 0 failures in 11 runs
- full `rstudio-core-tests` -- reproduced, less often

The test in isolation always passed, so the failure depends on the sibling
tests in the suite running first -- most likely the timing shift they
introduce rather than shared state.

## Likely cause

The baseline assertion at line 400 drains the io_context with a single
non-blocking `poll()`:

```cpp
pConnection->startReading();
ioc.restart();
ioc.poll();
ASSERT_EQ(handlerCalls, 1);
```

`startReading()` issues an `async_read`, but the request bytes written to
`peer` at line 392 still have to traverse the loopback socket before that read
can complete. `poll()` runs only the handlers that are ready at that instant,
so when delivery has not landed yet it runs nothing and `handlerCalls` stays
0. Nothing in the test waits for the read to become ready.

A bounded wait -- `ioc.run_for(...)`, or polling until `handlerCalls == 1`
with a deadline -- would make the baseline deterministic. Plain `run()` is not
enough on its own, since the connection stays readable.

Found while reviewing #18630, which does not touch this code: `AsyncConnectionImpl`
runs several hundred tests before the suite that PR modifies.

title: e2e: DOI citation tests fail when the service degrades after the reachability probe
description:
Three DOI citation tests failed together on a windows shard of PR #18417's CI run ([job](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30597217542/job/91056404631)):

- `citations.test.ts:88` inserts an authorless DOI citation into a markdown visual editor
- `citations.test.ts:123` inserts a DOI citation into a Quarto visual editor
- `citations.test.ts:161` deletes a staged citation

All three timed out waiting for the citation UI (`expect(locator).toBeVisible()` after 30s) during the live DOI lookup.

## Analysis

These tests are already guarded by `skipUnlessReachable(CITATION_SERVICE_HOSTS.doi)`, and the guard passed -- but the same runner's network then degraded mid-run (its Playwright report upload also failed with `fetch failed` three times at the end of the job). So the reachability probe has a pass-then-degrade gap: one successful probe at test start does not mean the DOI resolution a few seconds later will complete.

The citation *search* tests already treat a service-error status line in the dialog as a skip rather than a failure (#18267, added because NCBI rate-limits shared CI egress IPs). The DOI *insert* path has no equivalent: when the lookup fails or hangs, the test just times out and fails the shard.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the #18267 pattern on the DOI insert path: poll for either the inserted-citation UI or the dialog's lookup-error/no-result status, and `test.skip` on the error status (service problem, not a product regression). Optionally re-probe reachability on timeout and skip retroactively when the probe now fails, which would also have covered this run.

title: Data Viewer: avoid re-coercing every column on each global search
description:
From the #17806 performance audit (low-risk fixes landed in PR #18418).

### Problem

The global search in `.rs.applyTransform` (`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionDataViewer.R`) runs, per applied keystroke:

```r
matches <- lapply(searchColumns, function(column) {
   grepl(pattern, column, perl = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
})
matches <- Reduce(`|`, matches)
x <- x[matches, , drop = FALSE]
```

- `grepl` on a non-character column implicitly `as.character()`s the **entire** column, so every numeric/Date/POSIXct/factor column of the whole frame is re-formatted to strings on every search request.
- `perl = TRUE` + `ignore.case = TRUE` on UTF-8 input takes the slow PCRE path.
- All `ncol` logical vectors of length `nrow` are materialized before `Reduce` runs (transiently ~`nrow * ncol * 4` bytes), then the row subset copies the whole frame again.
- The transform is preceded by an unconditional `.rs.toDataFrame` copy of the input.
- The C++ superset optimization only helps when *extending* the search string; backspacing recomputes from the full frame.

### Proposal

- Cache a character projection of the frame per (cache key, pre-search transform state), built once and reused across keystrokes; invalidate from `onDetectChanges`.
- Or restructure the scan to short-circuit per row/column (stop coercing a column's remainder once a row already matched) and avoid materializing all logical vectors.
- Consider extending the working-copy reuse to narrowing edits (backspace) where a cached superset result exists.

title: e2e: terminal directory-listing test flaked on macOS after the DOM-renderer fallback
description:
`terminal.test.ts` "a file created in the terminal appears in a directory listing" failed both attempts on a macOS shard of PR #18417's CI run ([job](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30593746705/job/91045993265)): the poll for `ztestfile.txt` appearing at least twice in `rstudioapi::terminalBuffer()` (echoed `touch` + `ls` output) never reached 2 within its 15s budget.

## Analysis

Two candidate explanations, in order of interest:

1. **Timing correlation with the DOM-renderer fallback (#18405).** That change merged to main ~4 hours before this failure, and PR CI runs the merge ref, so this was one of its first excursions on a macOS runner. GH Actions macOS runners have no GPU acceleration -- exactly the environment where a WebGL context loss (and now the new fallback path) is most likely. The buffer read is server-side (pty), so a pure renderer change should not affect it, but the keystrokes are typed into xterm's textarea via `page.keyboard` -- focus/hit-testing during a renderer teardown/swap could plausibly swallow keystrokes. Worth checking whether the fallback's log line fired on that runner, and whether this test stays flaky on macOS post-#18405.

2. **The pre-existing keystroke-vs-shell race family.** #18328 hardened `openTerminal` to gate on a non-empty terminal buffer before returning, but the individual `type()`/`Enter` calls still race the shell's readiness to accept input (observed dropping keystrokes on macOS CI before that fix). If the `cd`/`touch` line was partially swallowed, `ls` lists nothing and the grep stays at 1 hit (the echoed command).

## Suggested fix

Gate each command on its own echo appearing in `terminalBuffer()` before typing the next (the same measurable-condition pattern the suite uses elsewhere), which de-flakes the test under either explanation. If occurrences cluster on macOS after #18405, treat it as a signal that the fallback affects input handling, not just rendering.

title: e2e: Consolidate the rig R installation steps into a shared composite action
description:
### Problem Statement

Eight workflow files install R with rig, and each carries its own copy of the same few shell lines:

- `.github/workflows/os-cache-seed-e2e-deps.yml`
- `.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-linux.yml`
- `.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-autocomplete-scheduled-windows-server-2025.yml`
- `.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-14-arm64.yml`
- `.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-15-x86_64.yml`
- `.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-26-arm64.yml`
- `.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025.yml`
- `.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-server-os-ubuntu-24.yml`

The copies have drifted. The three macOS ones query rig for the name it actually used, because rig names macOS installs by arch and major.minor (`4.5-arm64`) rather than the requested patch version. The Linux and Windows ones pass the version string straight to `rig default`, which works on those platforms.

That drift costs us. #18569 is the case where a Linux-shaped block was copied onto a macOS runner, and the seed's macOS job never worked once. #18322 is the same shape from the other direction: a guard existed on the macOS 15 engine but not the macOS 26 one, and had to be applied separately.

There's already a `.github/actions/os-install-rig-unix` composite action, but it installs rig itself, not R.

### Proposed Behaviour

A shared composite action that takes an R version, installs it, resolves the name rig actually registered for that platform, and selects it as the default. Callers pass a version and nothing else, so the platform quirk lives in one place and can't be mis-copied again.

Two plausible shapes: extend `os-install-rig-unix` to cover R as well, with a Windows sibling for the PowerShell form, or add a separate action beside it. Either is fine.

Worth noting the cost up front: this touches eight files, and each one needs a real workflow run to confirm, so it's larger than it looks.

### QA Notes

title: e2e: serve install.packages tests from a local file:// mini-repo
description:
### Motivation

CRAN outages surface as e2e flakes whenever `install.packages` runs on the test path. Most package needs are handled off the hot path (os-e2e-deps / globalSetup preinstall from PPM into a cached library, with skip-if-present `ensurePackages` safety nets in tests), and the worst offender -- the `s4_unloaded_package` spec's remove + network-reinstall cycle -- was made network-free via stash/restore helpers in #18510 after a CRAN stall blew its `afterAll` budget ([failing run](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31462849387/job/93693141740)).

Two tests in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/console/console_command_effects.test.ts` still depend on the network **every run**, because they deliberately exercise `install.packages` itself:

- "install.packages() reports not-available for a non-existent package" fetches the CRAN index from `cran.r-project.org` each run;
- "install.packages() installs a real CRAN package that library() can load" uninstalls `praise` and reinstalls it from the network each run -- the same flake class that hit the s4 spec.

### Proposal: local `file://` mini-repo

R natively accepts `file://` repository URLs, so no HTTP server or port management is needed -- a CRAN-like repo is a static tree with a `src/contrib/PACKAGES` index. Verified end-to-end locally: a generated pure-R package + `R CMD build` + `tools::write_PACKAGES()` supports both `install.packages(pkg, repos = "file://...")` and the "not available" warning path with zero network, on a stock R install (pure-R packages need no Rtools on Windows).

Sketch:

- globalSetup (alongside `fixtures/r-libs-setup.ts`) generates one or two trivial pure-R fixture packages, builds and indexes them into a cached mini-repo, and exposes the `file://` URL to tests (env var + `localRepoUrl()` helper).
- Convert the two `console_command_effects` tests to the local repo: the not-available test queries the local index; the real-install test uninstalls/reinstalls a generated fixture package instead of `praise`. Same product behavior exercised (real `install.packages`, real `library()` load), fully hermetic.
- `ensurePackages` safety nets stay on PPM/CRAN: they install real packages (dplyr, rmarkdown, ...) that the preinstall already keeps off the hot path.

### Caveats

- A `file://` install skips the libcurl download path, so it exercises everything after the download, not the download itself. If we ever want the HTTP path under test, a localhost static server works but adds lifecycle management, and non-HTTPS downloads can trigger RStudio's secure-download warning (`RSTUDIO_DISABLE_SECURE_DOWNLOAD_WARNING` escape hatch).
- Other network flake sources (NCBI citation lookups, Copilot/PAI downloads, Quarto) are out of scope.

title: Normalize de-chunked localhost proxy responses before rewriting them
description:
### Summary

AsyncClient consumes HTTP chunk framing before returning a buffered response. handleLocalhostResponse() removes Transfer-Encoding and sets Content-Length in its ordinary response branch, but responses handled by an earlier branch bypass that normalization.

In particular, a response containing Location or Refresh is copied and written immediately. If the upstream response used final Transfer-Encoding: chunked, the copied response contains a decoded body that is still labeled as chunked. The Spark UI rewriting path can similarly retain Transfer-Encoding while setBody() adds Content-Length.

For an upstream chunked redirect, the downstream protocol mismatch is deterministic: the client receives decoded bytes under a Transfer-Encoding: chunked header and attempts to decode them again.

### Suggested change

Normalize a buffered response once, before the redirect, Spark UI, and ordinary-response branches:

- When parseTransferEncoding(response.headers()).chunkedIsFinal is true, remove Transfer-Encoding.
- Set Content-Length to the decoded body size.
- Use that normalized response for all subsequent header and body rewrites.

This would also allow removal of the lower chunked-only response branch.

Add coverage for a chunked localhost response containing Location or Refresh, and ideally for the Spark UI rewrite path as well.

### Context

Follow-up from #18541.

Relevant code: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/2bed86b67fd559a8015f265f93132b4b220828ff/src/cpp/server/session/ServerSessionProxy.cpp#L429-L482

title: Add a setting to disable user-managed Posit Assistant installs
description:
### Problem

There is no way for an administrator to take Posit Assistant installation away from
users. Every session with Posit Assistant selected schedules a manifest fetch from
`https://cdn.posit.co/posit-ai/manifest.json` one second after deferred init
(`onDeferredInit` in `SessionChat.cpp`), the user can trigger a check at any time from
the Help menu, and the assistant itself can request one over `ui/checkForUpdates`. In
centrally managed and air-gapped deployments that outbound traffic is unwanted.

It also leaves an administrator's install unable to stay authoritative. Installs always
land in the per-user XDG data directory, and that tier is searched ahead of the
administrator's, so a user who accepts a single update prompt permanently shadows the
copy named by `posit-assistant-path` (#18688), the copy in the XDG system config
directory, or the copy bundled with Workbench — with no signal to either party. This is
deliberate: the answer is this setting, not a reordering of the search.

### Proposed change

An administrator setting that turns off user-managed installation of Posit Assistant.
Default: allowed, today's behavior. When disabled, the session:

- uses only the administrator-controlled installation — `posit-assistant-path`, the XDG
  system config directory, or the copy bundled with Workbench;
- ignores any user-level copy, including one left over from before the setting changed
  or hand-copied into place to get around it (ignored, never cleaned up);
- performs no manifest fetches at all;
- refuses the install, update, and uninstall RPCs;
- hides "Check for Posit Assistant Updates" and "Uninstall Posit Assistant".

#### Two surfaces in this repo

1. **`rsession.conf`** — `posit-assistant-installation-enabled`, default `1`, in the
   `pai` group of `src/cpp/session/session-options.json` next to
   `posit-assistant-enabled`.

   **Not an `allow-*` option.** `generate-options.R` emits `value || allowOverlay()`
   for every bool in the `allow` group, and open-source builds define `allowOverlay()`
   as unconditionally `true` — so an `allow-posit-assistant-installation` would have
   been force-allowed everywhere except Workbench. This has to work in open-source
   RStudio Server. That is the same reason `posit-assistant-enabled` lives in the `pai`
   group rather than beside `allow-posit-assistant`. (An earlier revision of this issue
   specified the `allow` group; it was wrong.)
2. **Environment variable** — `RSTUDIO_DISABLE_POSIT_ASSISTANT_INSTALLATION`
   (non-empty = disabled), mirroring `RSTUDIO_DISABLE_POSIT_ASSISTANT`. **Desktop
   only**, and not by a code gate: `rserver` builds each session's environment from
   scratch rather than passing its own down, so the variable does not reach a server
   session. Documented as Desktop for that reason. It can only ever restrict, never
   permit, so there is no bypass concern in letting the session read it unconditionally.

A third surface, `/etc/rstudio/profiles` key `assistant-installation-enabled` with
per-user/group scoping, is the Workbench admin surface and lands in rstudio-pro
(rstudio/rstudio-pro#12534): it is translated to
`--posit-assistant-installation-enabled 0|1` at session launch and so needs nothing
further here. The name is deliberately editor-neutral so Positron can consume the same
key later.

#### One helper, not a hand-synced pair

`isPositAssistantInstallationEnabledByAdmin()` in `SessionModuleContext`, beside
`isPositAssistantEnabledByAdmin()`:

```cpp
return options().positAssistantInstallationEnabled() &&
       core::system::getenv("RSTUDIO_DISABLE_POSIT_ASSISTANT_INSTALLATION").empty();
```

Every gate below and `client_init` call this one helper. The existing Posit Assistant
gate hand-syncs its logic between `SessionClientInit.cpp` and
`SessionModuleContext.cpp`; the new flag must not repeat that.

#### Effect on the search order

```
1. XDG user data dir                          <- SKIPPED when installs are disabled
2. posit-assistant-path set -> use it; if invalid, warn and stop
   not set                  -> XDG system config dir, then bundled
```

The `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` tier that sat ahead of these is removed outright;
see part (a) item 3.

The gate lives inside `locatePositAssistantInstallation()`, so both consumers — the
chat backend and the NES agent — honor it through the one resolution point, and the
rule ("skip user-writable tiers when installs are disabled") carries over unchanged to
the versioned store in #18658.

With the Workbench bundle in place, disabled mode always finds something: the
administrator's pinned install if present, else the shipped copy. Air-gapped sites work
with zero manifest traffic.

### Part (a): session-side enforcement

Complete and correct on its own — the UI degrades to error dialogs from the gated RPCs
until (b).

1. **The option, the env var, and the helper**, as above.
2. **Resolution skips the user tier**, as above. A user-level copy that is present but
   skipped is logged once per session, since it silently changes which version runs and
   may be a downgrade.
3. **`RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` is removed entirely** — the tier-1 branch and its logging
   in `ChatInstallation.cpp`, the search-order comment in `ChatInstallation.hpp`, and
   the now-dead env-path refusal branch in `chat_uninstall_posit_assistant` (the
   read-only-install refusal below it already covers every remaining case), plus the
   stale references in `SessionAssistant.cpp` and `SessionAssistantTests.cpp`. The
   variable is a development-only override: it is undocumented, unused by the e2e
   suite, and a plain environment variable any user can set in `.Renviron`, which would
   make this setting decorative. Removing it both closes that bypass and drops a tier
   from an already complex resolution scheme. Developers testing a local build install
   it into the XDG user data directory or point `posit-assistant-path` at it.
4. **`chat_install_update` refuses**, with a `client_info` message the UI renders.
   Today it gates only on `isPositAssistantWanted()`, which the user controls.
5. **`chat_uninstall_posit_assistant` refuses** likewise, and the gate sits *ahead* of
   the on-disk checks: in managed mode a leftover user copy may well exist, and it is
   ignored rather than removed.
6. **No manifest traffic — gate `shouldFetchManifest()`, not the call sites.** Every
   fetch funnels through `startUpdateCheck()`, whose three callers are `onDeferredInit`,
   `chatCheckForUpdates`, and `chatInstallUpdate`, and which already has the branch this
   needs:

   ```cpp
   if (!shouldFetchManifest(force)) { resolveWithoutManifestFetch(); return; }
   ```

   Making `shouldFetchManifest()` return false in managed mode covers all three call
   sites and any future one, and routes them through the existing local-state path so
   the client still learns installed/not-installed without touching `cdn.posit.co`. The
   managed gate must take precedence over `force`, which `chatInstallUpdate` passes as
   `true`. (There are no periodic checks to suppress — checks are startup plus
   user- and assistant-initiated, with throttle state persisted in `manifest-check.json`.)

   **`resolveWithoutManifestFetch()` needs widening.** Its comment says it is reached
   only when a compatible version is installed, which is why it reapplies only
   *persisted* blocks. Managed mode reaches it with whatever the administrator provides
   — possibly nothing, possibly a protocol-mismatched copy — so it must recompute the
   mismatch locally and normalize a missing install to `"0.0.0"`. On the throttled path
   the mismatch is false by construction, so nothing changes there.
7. **The assistant-initiated `ui/checkForUpdates` is suppressed separately**, since it
   fetches nothing: `handleCheckForUpdates` is a thin trigger that fires client event
   210 to run the frontend command flow. Gate it, and stop advertising the capability so
   the assistant hides its own update entry — capability negotiation already exists, so
   no assistant-side change is needed. Note that `rstudioCapabilities()` in
   `ChatConstants.cpp` returns a reference to a function-local static and so cannot vary
   by mode as written; the filtering belongs in a small pure function beside it
   (`negotiatedCapabilities(bool)`) rather than inline in `SessionChat.cpp`, so the rule
   is testable.
8. **The update-check result carries the managed state.** This is the contract part (b)
   builds on, so (a) fixes it: add a boolean (`installationManaged`) to the
   `chat_check_for_updates` result alongside `manifestUnavailable`, `unsupportedProtocol`,
   and the other discriminators. `chat_check_for_updates` itself keeps **succeeding** in
   managed mode rather than refusing — the prefs pane and the chat pane both need a
   resolvable answer. `chat_get_update_status` needs no change, and
   `chat_set_update_check_override` is already restricted to `--automation-agent`
   sessions.
9. **`sessionInfo["posit_assistant_installation_enabled"]`** set from the helper in
   `SessionClientInit.cpp`, next to `posit_assistant_enabled`.
10. **The "installation not found" error must not name the user directory** in managed
    mode. `startChatBackend()` tells the user to install to the XDG user data directory,
    which is the one location managed mode ignores and refuses.

### Part (b): client reactions (GWT)

1. `SessionInfo` accessor, exposed as `PaiUtil.isPositAssistantInstallationEnabled()`.
   The JSNI accessor must read an **absent** field as *allowed*: a session that predates
   the setting sends no such field, and defaulting it to false would report managed mode
   and remove an ability the session actually permits.
2. `PaneManager.manageChatCommands()`: hide `checkForPositAssistantUpdates` **and**
   `uninstallPositAssistant`. The current code deliberately never hides uninstall so a
   leftover copy can be removed; managed mode is the carve-out, since the leftover copy
   is inert anyway.
3. Chat pane (`ChatPresenter`'s init-time `checkForUpdates()`): when managed and no
   valid administrator or bundled install exists, show "Posit Assistant is managed by
   your administrator and is not currently installed" with no install button. When
   managed and installed, behave normally — no update prompt can appear, since there is
   no manifest state.
4. `promptToInstallUpdate()`'s client-side guard extends to the new flag.
5. `AssistantPreferencesPane`: hide the install button and the
   `positAssistantUpdateCheckIntervalHours` control, replacing the latter with an
   administrator notice ("Posit Assistant updates are controlled by your
   administrator") using the same `InfoBar` treatment `PackagesPreferencesPane` uses
   for CRAN repositories modified outside package preferences.
   `checkPositAssistantInstallation()` reports the managed state, and the
   `performPositAssistantInstall()`/`doInstall()` path becomes unreachable — except via
   `onCheckFailed`, which offers an install with no version info, so
   `showInstallUpdatePrompt()` needs the guard too.
6. `PositAiInstallManager.dispatchUpdateCheck()` is already a static, unit-testable
   dispatcher — add the managed-mode outcome there, keyed off the flag (a) added to the
   result. Read it with the file's existing convention for fields an older rsession may
   omit (absent defaults to false) rather than adding it to the required-discriminator
   set, so a mixed-version pairing degrades instead of reporting a malformed response.
   Rank it **below** the blocking outcomes — an administrator copy with a mismatched
   protocol has a more specific message — and **above** the install and update ones,
   which managed mode can never act on. Tests go in the existing
   `src/gwt/test/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/chat/PositAiInstallManagerTests.java`,
   run by `ant unittest`.
7. `installUpdate()`'s `onError` must surface the backend's `client_info` string, as the
   uninstall path already does; otherwise the managed refusal shows as a generic
   execution error.

### Behavior summary

| Configuration | User install/update/uninstall | Effective install |
|---|---|---|
| Default | allowed | user copy, else admin path/system dir, else bundled |
| `rsession.conf` (or profiles) disabled | blocked; user copy ignored; no manifest traffic | admin path/system dir, else bundled |
| Env var set (Desktop) | same as above | same as above |

### Docs and tests

- `session-options.json` -> `Rscript scripts/generate-options.R` -> regenerated
  `SessionOptions.gen.hpp`. The `rsession_conf.qmd` half is a no-op in this repo
  (`outputDocFile` is `/dev/null`; the qmd lives in the docs repo).
- `environment-variables.qmd`: the new variable next to
  `RSTUDIO_DISABLE_POSIT_ASSISTANT`, scoped to Desktop.
- `NEWS.md` in both repos. The unreleased 2026.09 entry for #18597 advertises
  `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH`; reword it to keep only the system-wide-installation half.
  **The rstudio-pro entry needs the same edit.**
- Tests: `ChatInstallationTests.cpp` (resolution skips the user tier when disabled, and
  still finds the pinned, system, and bundled tiers), `ChatConstantsTests.cpp`
  (capability negotiation), `SessionModuleContextTests.cpp` (the environment-variable
  half of the gate), GWT dispatcher tests for the managed-mode outcome and both
  precedence directions.
- **Removing `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` costs the tests their injection seam.**
  `ChatInstallationTests.cpp` uses it both to neutralize ambient state and to point
  `locatePositAssistantInstallation()` at temp directories; it is the only such seam
  the function has. Replace it with a parameterized overload following the
  `bundledPositAssistantInstallPath(resourcePath)` precedent from #18690 — an
  `InstallSearchPaths` struct built by `positAssistantSearchPaths()` — rather than
  driving `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME`/XDG, which keeps the ambient-state hedging that makes the
  current tests awkward.

### Manual verification

The option is honored in open-source builds, so this can be exercised with
`npm run rserver-dev`. Delete `~/.local/share/rstudio/pai/manifest-check.json` before
each run, or the throttle will skip the check and the two cases look alike.

With a user-level install present and `posit-assistant-installation-enabled=1`, expect
the user install to be used and `manifest-check.json` to be rewritten. With `=0`, expect
"Ignoring user-level AI installation at …: Posit Assistant installation is managed by
the administrator", no rewrite of `manifest-check.json`, and no `cdn.posit.co` reference
in the session log.

**No unit test can catch a reintroduced `allowOverlay()` term** — `session::options()`
is a process-global populated by program-options parsing, so a pure
`composition(option, env)` helper would still be handed `true`. That A/B is the guard.

### Notes

- **Existing installs change behavior.** Anyone with both a user-level and an
  administrator-level install switches to the administrator copy the first time the
  setting is enabled, potentially a downgrade. Log it.
- **An administrator-managed install must ship its own `protocol.json`**, and so must a
  Workbench bundle. A sideloaded, system-level, or bundled copy never goes through
  RStudio's install path, and `writeProtocolVersionFileIfMissing()` only ever runs
  against the user-data install, so nothing backfills one into a read-only location. A
  missing protocol counts as a mismatch, which is the correct outcome: a package with
  no bundled `protocol.json` predates every supported Posit Assistant version, so
  reporting it as incompatible is right rather than something to work around. In managed
  mode this is fatal rather than noisy — there is no manifest, so no update can be
  offered that would fix it.
- `posit-assistant-test-manifest` is moot in managed mode; the pre-release warning
  banner should not fire.
- **Known limitation: an administrator install with no `package.json` dead-ends in
  managed mode.** `verifyPositAiInstallation()` does not require `package.json`, so such
  a directory resolves and `startChatBackend()` would succeed, but `getInstalledVersion()`
  returns `""`, which `resolveWithoutManifestFetch()` normalizes to `"0.0.0"`. That sets
  `isInitialInstall`, so the pane reports "managed by your administrator and is not
  currently installed" and never starts the backend — no chat, despite a working
  installation. Unmanaged mode escapes this by offering an install; managed mode has no
  way out. Left as-is: it takes a malformed package (rstudio/rstudio-pro#12483 has the
  packaging step assert `package.json` is present), and fixing it means giving the
  update-check result a way to say "installed, version unknown", which `"0.0.0"` currently
  doubles as. Revisit if the versioned store in #18658 reworks that result shape anyway.
- A bundled install currently over-locks: the lock skip at `startChatBackend` exempts
  only the XDG system path, so with a bundle present every session running the
  assistant holds the in-use lock. This setting is the pairing that makes that
  harmless, since per-user install and update are refused outright.

### Resolved questions

- **The surviving bypass.** Removing `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` closes the direct
  override. `RSTUDIO_CONFIG_DIR` / `XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` can still redefine where "the
  system install" resolves, and both are plain environment variables — **out of scope**:
  policy comes from `rsession.conf` or profiles, which users cannot edit, and a user who
  can redefine the system config dir can already redefine much more.
- **Refusal wording**: "Posit Assistant installation is managed by your administrator
  and cannot be changed from RStudio.", matching the style of the existing uninstall
  refusals, delivered via `client_info`.
- **Managed-but-nothing-installed copy**: one message. The session cannot reliably tell
  "the administrator has not installed it yet" from "`posit-assistant-path` is set but
  invalid".

### Related

- Builds on #18688 (`posit-assistant-path`) and #18690 (bundled lookup), both merged.
  #18690 did the structural work this layers on: splitting
  `systemPositAssistantInstallPath()`'s callers into "where would an administrator
  install" and "is this install read-only", and finalizing the search order.
- #18658 (versioned side-by-side installs) is a **follow-up**, not a prerequisite. This
  work targets the current single unversioned `pai/bin` layout. Both the bundled tier
  and this gate live in the one resolution function and express rules that carry over
  to a store/selector layout unchanged.
- rstudio/rstudio-pro#12483 bundles Posit Assistant with Workbench, adding the tier
  disabled mode falls back to.
- rstudio/rstudio-pro#12534 adds the Workbench profiles key
  `assistant-installation-enabled`, which depends only on the `rsession.conf` option
  landing here.

title: Allow administrators to configure the Posit Assistant installation path
description:
### Current behavior

An administrator who wants Posit Assistant available to every user of an RStudio Server node has exactly one supported location for it: `pai/bin` under the XDG system configuration directory -- `/etc/rstudio/pai/bin` on Linux and macOS, `C:/ProgramData/rstudio/pai/bin` on Windows.

Sites that keep shared software somewhere else -- `/opt`, a read-only NFS mount, or a versioned deployment tree -- have no supported way to point RStudio at it. `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` can do it, but it is a per-process environment variable meant for development and testing, not a deployment mechanism.

### Proposal

Add a `posit-assistant-path` session option (set in `rsession.conf`) that names the directory holding the administrator-managed installation.

When the option is set it *replaces* the XDG system configuration location in the search order rather than adding another location to it, so the order becomes:

1. `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH`, for development and testing
2. The per-user installation under the XDG data directory
3. `posit-assistant-path` when set, otherwise `<XDG system config dir>/pai/bin`

If the option is set but the directory does not hold a valid installation, RStudio logs a warning and reports Posit Assistant as not installed. It does not fall back to `/etc/rstudio/pai/bin`, since that would hide the misconfiguration.

An installation found through this option is treated the same as one under `/etc/rstudio`: RStudio reads it but never writes to it, and refuses to uninstall it.

title: New project fails to open in sandboxed iframe (RStudio IDE)
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Server
    RStudio Version : 2022.07.2+576 "Spotted Wakerobin" Release (e7373ef832b49b2a9b88162cfe7eac5f22c40b34, 2022-09-06) for Ubuntu Bionic
    OS Version      : Ubuntu 20.04.5 LTS
    R Version       : 4.2.1 (2022-06-23) -- "Funny-Looking Kid"

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Load RStudio into an iframe with the sandbox attribute present.
2. Create a new project `File > New Project > New Directory > New Project > Create Project`.

I have attached a minimal working demo of the issue with a docker-compose file.
[rstudio_sandbox_issue.tar.gz](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/files/9909278/rstudio_sandbox_issue.tar.gz)

### Describe the problem in detail

#### Issue

Given R Studio is rendered in a sandboxed iframe, when I create and new project then it hangs on a toast saying "Switching to project path/to/project...". An error appears in the javascript console, akin to:
```
Unsafe attempt to initiate navigation for frame with URL 'http://localhost/rstudio/' from frame with URL 'http://localhost/rstudio/'. The frame attempting navigation is sandboxed, and is therefore disallowed from navigating its ancestors.
```

The issue only arises when the sandbox attribute is present. However, removing the sandbox attribute is not an option for us.

This is the same issue as previously raised on the [community forum](https://community.rstudio.com/t/rstudio-being-used-in-an-iframe-cannot-open-new-project-due-to-the-use-of-sandbox-element/146233).

#### Other observations

The project does load successfully if the top level navigation is manually refreshed. 

The javascript that triggers the refresh is calling `$wnd.location.replace(X)`. Setting a breakpoint where the error is thrown and instead manually invoking `$wnd.location.reload()` performs the refresh without issue, and the new project loads as expected.

### Describe the behavior you expected

When I create a new project in R studio that is rendered in a sandboxed iframe, the new project loads.

- [x] I have read the guide for [submitting good bug reports](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Writing-Good-Bug-Reports).
- [x] I have installed the latest version of RStudio, and confirmed that the issue still persists.
- [] If I am reporting an RStudio crash, I have included a [diagnostics report](https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/200321257-Running-a-Diagnostics-Report).
- [x] I have done my best to include a minimal, self-contained set of instructions for consistently reproducing the issue.

title: Update Posit AI references in the RStudio User Guide
description:
### Problem Statement

The Posit AI subscription service is being renamed to Posit AI Pass. The RStudio User Guide still refers to the service as "Posit AI".

Published page: https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/tools/posit-ai.html

### Proposed Behaviour

description:
### System details

OS Version : macOS 26.5.2 (Build 25F84), 
Apple Silicon / ARM64 R Version : 4.6.0 (2026-04-24) 
Quarto Version : 1.9.38

### Steps to reproduce the problem

I have attached recreate_bug.qmd in recreate_bug.zip, a small self-contained file that reliably reproduces the problem on my system.

1. Open recreate_bug.qmd in Visual mode.
2. Without making any edits, execute an R code chunk.
3. The editor jumps to the top of the document and then returns to the location of the chunk.
4. Execute another chunk without editing the document; the same behavior occurs.
5. Make any edit inside any R chunk. Even typing and deleting a single character is sufficient.
6. Execute a chunk again. The jumping no longer occurs.
7. Close the .qmd file and reopen it in Visual mode.
8. Without making an edit, execute a chunk. The jumping occurs again.

### Describe the problem in detail

When the document is first opened in Visual mode, executing an R chunk causes the editor to scroll rapidly to the top of the document and then return to the chunk. This happens each time I execute a chunk.

However, as soon as I make any edit inside any code chunk, the problem stops. Subsequent chunks execute without changing the scroll position. If I close and reopen the document, the problem returns until I edit a chunk again.

I initially noticed that adding or changing a chunk option stopped the jumping, but I subsequently determined that the option itself was irrelevant: simply typing and deleting a character inside any chunk has the same effect.

I have also tried the following without resolving the issue:

- Restarting RStudio and rebooting the computer.
- Pausing OneDrive syncing.
- Removing the _site and _freeze directories.
- Resetting RStudio's local state by moving ~/.local/share/rstudio and allowing RStudio to create a fresh state directory.

The behavior persisted after all of these.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Executing an R code chunk in the Visual Editor should not cause the document to scroll away from the chunk being executed. The scroll position should remain stable regardless of whether the document or a code chunk has been edited since the file was opened.

title: Posit Assistant persistence failure after automatic conversation compaction with Ollama
description:
# Posit Assistant persistence failure after automatic conversation compaction with Ollama

## Environment

* RStudio Desktop 2026.08.1+195
* Windows
* Posit Assistant
* Local Ollama provider
* Model: `qwen3-neuro-coder-96k:latest`
* Ollama model context is correctly configured and verified independently

## Problem

Posit Assistant consistently fails to save a conversation after automatic context compaction.

The UI reports:

> That conversation could not save its previous turn. Try again after repairing it.

This reproduces in newly created conversations, so it is not limited to a single corrupted conversation.

## Reproduction

1. Start a new Posit Assistant conversation using a local Ollama model.
2. Use the Assistant normally until the conversation becomes large.
3. Posit Assistant automatically triggers context compaction.
4. The turn then fails to persist and the conversation becomes unusable for further turns.

## Relevant log output

The failure is preceded by:

```text
2026-08-20T23:49:41.494Z [rstudio:INFO] Auto-compact triggered: 71886 tokens >= 68304 (30000 below limit)
```

Approximately 49 seconds later:

```text
2026-08-20T23:50:30.400Z [rstudio:WARN] Failed to save conversation b2220fa5-ca06-484e-9e14-49554355b53c {
  "name": "Error",
  "message": "Conversation node 161732ab-297b-4c7a-9c54-124129ce96d2 has a missing compaction link"
}
```

Posit then attempts persistence repair, which also fails:

```text
S8.performPersistenceRepair
S8.repairPersistence
yre.repairIfNeeded
```

and ultimately reports:

```text
ConversationLifecycleError: persistenceError
```

## Additional observations

The Ollama connection itself is working. RStudio successfully discovers the Ollama models, and Qwen completes generation.

The failure occurs specifically when Posit Assistant performs automatic conversation compaction and subsequently attempts to persist the conversation.

Resetting the Posit Assistant state temporarily clears an already-corrupted conversation, but the same failure reproduces in a fresh conversation once automatic compaction occurs.

This therefore appears to be a reproducible Posit Assistant conversation-compaction/persistence bug rather than an Ollama inference or model-context configuration problem.

## Logs

Relevant log:

```text
C:\Users\lcb77\AppData\Local\RStudio\log\positai.log
```

I can provide the complete relevant log section if needed.

[positai.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31285046/positai.log)

title: Add a near-success status to E2E run reporting, distinct from red and green
description:
### Problem Statement

A single failed test turns the whole E2E run red, with no indication of how close to green it was. A fleet that's one flaky test away from a clean run looks the same as a fleet that's actually broken.

### Proposed Behaviour

Option 1 (preferred): Have the run report a third status, distinct from both red (failure) and green (success), when only a small number of tests failed -- a "near-success" state, so a nearly-clean run is visually distinguishable from both a genuinely broken one and a fully clean one, without collapsing back into looking green.

Option 2: Keep the job strictly red or green, but have the run summary additionally report the pass rate, e.g. "20/21 engines passed, 1 test failed on ubuntu-26-arm64," so there's at least a written signal of how close it was even though the status itself doesn't change. The engines' e2e-merge job already computes this number (it prints passed=N rate=N%), so it exists without new plumbing.

Related: #18428 (E2E runs that select zero tests are reported as successful) is the opposite failure of the same reporting layer -- a run that's green when it shouldn't be.

### Testing

This can be tested by intentionally failing a small number of tests in an otherwise-clean run and checking that the run reports the near-success state rather than a flat failure, while a run with more failures still reports red. No new automated test is needed since this only changes how a run's result is reported, not the tests themselves.

### Describe the problem in detail

Clicking Install for Posit Assistant on Ubuntu 26.04 for ARM64 does not produce a working assistant. The pane's iframe is created but stays empty, and reopening the pane offers the install again, so the state does not persist.

This came out of the E2E suite while qualifying new Ubuntu 26 and ARM64 engines, so the observations below are from CI rather than a hand-run session. The install was attempted four times in a single job and never completed once; each attempt waited 60 seconds for the assistant iframe's contents before giving up. It happened the same way on a daily-build install and on a build from source, in separate runs, so it is not a one-off.

Run with the failures, both build paths: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30927465235

The x86_64 build of the same daily works. On Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64 the install is clicked once, completes, and later visits to the pane do not offer it again:
