title: Data Viewer: cache the sort/filter working copy for unbound View(<expression>) tabs
description:
From the #17806 performance audit (low-risk fixes landed in PR #18418).

### Problem

The working-copy cache in `applyViewTransform` (`src/cpp/session/modules/data/DataViewer.cpp`) is only consulted when `s_cachedFrames` has an entry for the cache key -- and entries are only created when the viewed object is bound in a named environment (`envName != kNoBoundEnv` in `rs_viewData`). Anything that isn't a bare symbol gets `kNoBoundEnv`:

- `View(head(df, 1000))`, `View(df %>% filter(...))` and other expression views,
- import-preview tabs (`.rs.viewDataFrame`).

For those tabs every 500-row page fetch with an active sort/filter/search re-runs the entire `.rs.applyTransform` (full-frame filter copies + full re-sort) from scratch -- and then writes a working copy via `.rs.assignWorkingData` that can never be read, because the exact-match check requires the missing `s_cachedFrames` entry. Scrolling a sorted expression view of a large frame re-sorts it on every page.

### Proposal

Create `s_cachedFrames` entries for unbound viewers too, so the exact-match/superset reuse applies. Their content is a snapshot (there is no live binding to change), so they can skip `onDetectChanges` handling entirely -- making them strictly simpler than the bound case. PR #18418's retention fix (only dropping working data when the object changed) then benefits these tabs automatically.

title: Data Viewer: make horizontal column-window updates incremental
description:
From the #17806 performance audit (low-risk fixes landed in PR #18418). This is the main remaining cause of horizontal-scroll jank and multi-second stalls on wide frames.

### Problem

Two levels of full rebuild on horizontal scroll:

1. **Every one-column shift of the rendered window** (`syncColumnWindow` from the scroll rAF -- potentially every frame during a trackpad gesture) calls `rebuildHeaderWindow`, which does `innerHTML = ""` on both theads and recreates every windowed `<th>` (each with pin icon, listeners, composed title), and then `renderVisibleRows(true)` takes the full-rebuild branch, discarding and recreating every rendered row and cell (~2,000 `<td>`s). The *row* window has an incremental enter/leave patch path; the column window has none.

2. **When the viewport leaves the fetched window**, `applyColumnWindowUpdate` runs as one synchronous main-thread task: `remapRowCache` allocates a new array per cached row and copies every cell (up to 20,000 rows x ~200 columns), then `autoSizeColumns`, a full header + body rebuild, custom-scrollbar updates, and it kicks off another 500-row x 200-column fetch -- and can chain into the next slide via `maybeSlideForScroll`. Nothing paints until it finishes.

### Proposal

- Mirror the row path: patch only the columns entering/leaving the window, reusing header and cell nodes.
- Make `remapRowCache` lazy (remap a block when it is next rendered) or in-place, and split `applyColumnWindowUpdate` across frames (rAF / `scheduler.yield`).
- Reduce `autoSizeColumns` re-runs on slides (it currently runs twice per slide: synchronously and again in the fetch callback).

title: Data Viewer: fetch only the rendered columns in row data requests
description:
From the #17806 performance audit (the low-risk fixes from that audit landed in PR #18418); this is the largest remaining win for open time, vertical-scroll stalls, and renderer memory.

### Problem

`fetchRows` requests `colsRequestList()` -- every column of the fetched window (up to `data_viewer_max_columns`, default 200) -- even though column virtualization renders only the ~10 columns intersecting the viewport (plus pinned). Consequences, per 500-row block:

- Up to 100,000 formatted cells per response: ~200 separate `.rs.formatDataColumn` evaluations on the R main thread server-side (`getData` in `src/cpp/session/modules/data/DataViewer.cpp`), and a multi-MB JSON parse client-side, all before anything paints.
- With `ROW_CACHE_LIMIT = 20000`, the row cache can retain ~4M cell strings (20,000 rows x 200 columns), producing GC pauses that read as random freezes.
- After any column-window slide, every cached block's column signature (`blockColsSig`) mismatches, so subsequent vertical scrolling refetches all 200 columns for every block again.

### Proposal

Request only the rendered column window (+ pinned columns + a horizontal buffer) in `show=data` fetches, and patch cached blocks per-column as the window slides instead of invalidating them wholesale. Pinned columns must always be included (cf. #17835). The `columns_requested` contract already supports arbitrary column lists, so this is client-side scoping plus cache bookkeeping.

title: "weird" issue-- XQuartz running when a .R file containing {weird} code is opened in RStudio
description:
I'm not sure where to put this, or even if it's really an issue. But I've been having an unexpected behavior on my Mac in the past few days and I think I've traced it back to the `weird` package and RStudio's code diagnostics engine. (Major caveat here: I used Claude to help me debug this, so it could be a hallucination! But the behavior seems consistent with the idea.)  Initially, I started writing this on @robjhyndman's https://github.com/robjhyndman/weird/ package, but the more I think about it I think it's a bug/unexpected behavior from RStudio. 

I have a `.R` file with some code I've been tinkering on. I don't have Source on save checked at the top. In that `.R` file is some code that uses `weird`. I'm not actually calling `library(weird)`, just using the `::` to get a function or two I need. For example, 

```
weird::hampel_anomalies(LakeHuron, bandwidth = 2)
```

As a minimal reproducible example, put just this line in a .R file. As soon as this file is opened in RStudio, XQuartz pops open on my computer. If I quit XQuartz while I am in a Project, my R session will be aborted. (This doesn't happen if I don't have an active Project open.) 


### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop 
    RStudio Version : 2026.07.1+147 (2026.07.1+147)
    OS Version      :  Mac OS Sequoia 15.6
    R Version       : 4.4.1

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Create a .R file that contains the line

```
weird::hampel_anomalies(LakeHuron, bandwidth = 2)
```

(or, any other code that calls something from `weird`). Save it. (Or don't, I think it happens just by writing the code and not executing it.) 

Open this file. 

### Describe the problem in detail

When you open the file, XQuartz pops open. If you have an active RStudio Project and then quit XQuartz, the R session experiences a fatal error and terminates. If you don't have an active RStudio Project, XQuartz still opens when you open the file, but when you quit XQuartz the fatal error doesn't happen. If I open the file in the standard R GUI, XQuartz does not open. 

Here's what Claude had to say about it:

"RStudio parses R scripts in the background for diagnostics/autocomplete (checking function calls, arguments, etc.). When it sees a library(weird) call in your script — even completely unexecuted — its diagnostics engine will silently call getNamespace("weird") to resolve what functions are available, so it can check your code against them. That single call cascades: weird imports from aplpack, which imports tcltk, and loading tcltk's namespace on your system launches XQuartz — all without a single line of your script actually running."

### Describe the behavior you expected

I would expect XQuartz not to open, or at least not to open until I had run some code that might trigger it.

title: Windows 11: Console corrupts UTF-8 input after pressing Enter until Sys.setlocale() is called
description:
### System

- RStudio: 2026.06.0+242 (Blue Plumbago)
- R: 4.6.1 (2026-06-24) UCRT
- Windows 11 Build 26200
- Locale: Turkish_Türkiye.utf8
- UTF-8: TRUE
- Code page: 65001

### Problem

Immediately after starting RStudio, typing Turkish characters directly into the Console works while typing, but after pressing Enter the echoed text becomes corrupted.

Example:

"Çalışma"

After calling:

Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", Sys.getlocale("LC_CTYPE"))

the problem immediately disappears, although `Sys.getlocale()` reports exactly the same value before and after the call.

### What works

- RGui works correctly.
- Source editor works correctly.
- Running code from the source editor (Ctrl+Enter) works correctly.
- `print()` output is correct.
- `charToRaw()` confirms the string is valid UTF-8.

### What does not work

Only interactive Console input is affected.

### Reproduction

1. Start RStudio.
2. In the Console type:

"Çalışma"

3. Press Enter.

The Console corrupts the echoed UTF-8 text.

Then run:

Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", Sys.getlocale("LC_CTYPE"))

Repeat the same command and the problem disappears immediately.

### Additional symptom

Another symptom is that immediately after starting RStudio, the Console behaves incorrectly before calling `Sys.setlocale()`.

For example:

```r
list.files()
```

returns

```r
character(0)
```

even though there are files in the current working directory.

After executing:

```r
Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", Sys.getlocale("LC_CTYPE"))
```

(or my `fix_tr()` helper which calls `Sys.setlocale()`),

the same command:

```r
list.files()
```

immediately returns the correct list of files.

So calling `Sys.setlocale()` appears to refresh more than just UTF-8 handling in the Console.

### Additional information

- Clearing all RStudio cache/state directories did not permanently fix the issue.
- The issue also occurs with a fresh Windows user profile.

title: Background Jobs: Option to inherit attached packages from the current R session
description:
### Problem

When running selected code as a Background Job, the **Copy environment** option copies objects from the Global Environment, but it does not preserve the packages that are currently attached with `library()`.

This makes it difficult to use Background Jobs for exploratory workflows. A common workflow is to organize a script with package imports at the top, followed by hundreds or thousands of lines of analysis. When I select code from the middle or end of the script and run it as a Background Job, the new R session does not have the required packages attached unless I also rerun all of the `library()` calls.

### Proposed behavior

It would be helpful if Background Jobs provided an option to inherit the attached package state from the current R session, similar in spirit to how "Copy environment" copies objects.

Possible implementations could include:

* Copy the current search path (attached packages) into the Background Job before executing the selected code.
* Add a separate checkbox such as **Copy attached packages** or **Restore attached packages**.
* Alternatively, automatically replay the `library()`/`require()` calls corresponding to the currently attached user packages.

### Motivation

The current behavior works well for standalone scripts, but it interrupts interactive analysis workflows where users frequently execute small sections of large scripts.

The proposed feature would make Background Jobs much more useful for long-running analyses by allowing selected code to execute in an environment that more closely matches the current interactive session, without requiring users to duplicate or source package-loading code.

title: Update Packages dialog may install older binary when source update is shown
description:
## Summary

The **Update Packages** dialog can report that a newer *source* version of a package is available, but when the user proceeds with the update, `install.packages()` is called without specifying `type`, so R may install an older *binary* version instead.

## Details

The R backend handler (in `SessionPackages.R`) calls `available.packages()` without an explicit `type` argument. On macOS and Windows, this defaults to `getOption("pkgType")`, which is typically `"both"`. This means the "available" version shown in the dialog may come from a source package that is newer than the latest binary.

However, the frontend (`Packages.java`) constructs the `install.packages()` command without passing a `type` argument:

```java
command.append("install.packages(");
// ... package names and lib path ...
command.append(")");
```

When `install.packages()` runs with its default `type`, it may prefer the binary version, which could be older than the source version displayed in the dialog.

## Relevant code

- **Backend** (available packages check): `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionPackages.R`, around line 206
- **Frontend** (install command generation): `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/packages/Packages.java`, around line 471

## Expected behavior

If the dialog shows a source version as the available update, `install.packages()` should be called with `type = "source"` for that package (or the dialog should only show versions that match what `install.packages()` will actually install by default).

### Problem Statement

Databricks is now encouraging users away from Workspace wide endpoints in favour of Unity Catalog models.

Posit Assistant's Databricks support (the experimental native `databricks` provider) only discovers and lists classic workspace Model Serving endpoints via `GET /api/2.0/serving-endpoints`. It has no way to discover or select a Unity Catalog AI Gateway route (a `catalog.schema.model`-style alias reachable at `POST {workspace}/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions`), even though that route works fine for real inference with the same PAT.

### Proposed Behaviour

Extend the native `databricks` provider so that:

- Model discovery also queries Unity Catalog AI Gateway routes accessible to the authenticated principal (e.g. via the appropriate UC/AI Gateway listing API), in addition to classic serving endpoints, so UC routes appear in the model picker like any other Databricks model.

- Alternatively, allow input to specify the model via `catalog.schema.model`. The example curl command for theses UC endpoints is:

```sh
curl https://adb-123.azuredatabricks.net/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DATABRICKS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{
    "model": "catalog.schema.model",
    "max_tokens": 1024,
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"},
      {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hello! How can I assist you today?"},
      {"role": "user", "content": "What is Databricks?"}
    ]
  }'
```

title: Posit Assistant cookie paths miss external proxy prefixes when www-root-path or a session prefix is configured
description:
### Summary

The Posit Assistant chat WebSocket depends on two cookies whose `Path` is derived from the server's own view of its URL. When RStudio Server sits behind a path-prefixing reverse proxy it was never told about (e.g. Open OnDemand's `/rnode/<host>/<port>/` routes) **and** a root path or session prefix is also in play, those cookie `Path`s can never contain the external prefix, so the browser omits the cookies on the WebSocket upgrade and the connection fails even when the URL routes correctly.

posit-dev/assistant#2166 fixed the client side of this: the chat client now resolves the WebSocket URL relative to its own page URL, so unknown proxy prefixes survive. That fix is complete for deployments using the default `www-root-path` (`/`) — which covers the motivating Open OnDemand report, posit-dev/assistant-feedback#95 — because in that case:

- the `port-token` cookie `Path` is taken from the **client-reported** `baseURL` in `client_init`, which carries the external prefix (`src/cpp/session/SessionClientInit.cpp`, the `path == kRequestDefaultRootPath` branch), and
- the `posit-assistant-auth` cookie `Path` collapses to `/` (`src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatStaticFiles.cpp`).

### Remaining problem

With a **configured** `www-root-path` (or a Workbench `/s/<id>/` session prefix) plus an additional unknown external prefix:

- `port-token`: the else-branch in `SessionClientInit.cpp` derives the cookie `Path` from `request().proxiedUri()`, i.e. the server-known path only (e.g. `/rstudio/`). The upgrade request to `wss://host/<prefix>/rstudio/p/<token>/ai-chat/ws` doesn't match, the browser omits the cookie, and rserver cannot descramble `/p/<token>/` (`ServerSessionProxy.cpp` falls back to the default token and 404s).
- `posit-assistant-auth`: `ChatStaticFiles.cpp` derives the cookie `Path` from `proxiedUri()` with `/ai-chat` stripped (e.g. `/rstudio/`), so the same omission occurs and the assistant backend closes the socket as unauthenticated.

This is a pre-existing limitation, not a regression from the client fix — before it, these configurations failed earlier (the WebSocket URL never routed at all).

### Reproduction sketch

1. Run `rserver --www-root-path=/rstudio` behind a prefix-stripping reverse proxy that serves it at `/proxy/rstudio/` (the proxy prefix `/proxy` not reflected in `www-root-path`).
2. Open the Posit Assistant pane (with the client fix from posit-dev/assistant#2166).
3. The WebSocket upgrade reaches the server at the right path but is rejected: the port-token and assistant-auth cookies are not sent because their `Path` (`/rstudio/`) does not prefix the browser-visible path (`/proxy/rstudio/...`).

### Fix direction

Derive both cookie `Path`s from the browser-visible base rather than the server-known path — the default-root-path branch in `SessionClientInit.cpp` already does this via the client-reported `baseURL`. Note the else-branch's comment says the server-derived path is used deliberately ("more securely using internal assumptions instead of using the URL from the JSON input"), so a fix needs to weigh that trust decision, or scope the cookies more broadly some other way.

The Workbench `/s/<id>/` variant is the same shared code path; it should be validated on Workbench after a fix, with a pro follow-up only if session-URL-specific behavior surfaces there.

title: Copilot->Posit code-assistant switch persists "posit" before install, leaving it uninstalled if cancelled/declined
description:
### Summary

Follow-up to #18350. That fix blocks the Global Options **OK/Apply** button while a Posit Assistant install/update check is in flight, so the fresh-profile / None -> Posit and Posit chat-provider paths can no longer persist a selected-but-uninstalled provider.

However, switching the **code assistant** from **GitHub Copilot** to **Posit AI** takes a different path that bypasses that guard. `disableCopilot()` eagerly persists `assistant = "posit"` the moment the selection changes -- independent of OK/Cancel and before the install check resolves. Two user actions then leave the exact state #18350 describes: provider selected, addon never installed, completions silently unavailable ("Posit AI: No completions available.").

This affects only the **Copilot -> Posit** code-assistant transition; it requires `copilot_enabled` to be true at the time of the switch. None -> Posit and the Posit chat provider are already handled by the #18350 fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a build where GitHub Copilot is available, set **Tools -> Global Options -> Assistant -> Use code assistant** to **GitHub Copilot** (so `copilot_enabled` is true).
2. Reopen Global Options and switch **Use code assistant** to **Posit AI Next Edit Suggestions**.
3. Before the install/update check resolves and the "Install/Update Posit Assistant" prompt appears, do either:
   - **(a)** click **OK** (which, after #18350, is blocked with a "Checking for Updates" warning) and then click **Cancel**; or
   - **(b)** wait for the install prompt and **decline** it (Cancel/No).
4. Reopen Global Options, or type in an R file.

**Expected:** the assistant reverts to the previous selection (Copilot), or the addon is installed before "posit" is persisted.
**Actual:** `assistant` is persisted as `"posit"` with the addon never installed; completions show "Posit AI: No completions available."

### Root cause

In `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/prefs/views/AssistantPreferencesPane.java`, when the code-assistant selector changes to Posit the change handler calls `disableCopilot(ASSISTANT_POSIT)`, which eagerly writes the pref:

```java
private void disableCopilot(String newAssistant)
{
   // Eagerly disable Copilot so the agent stops immediately
   if (prefs_.copilotEnabled().getValue())
   {
      prefs_.copilotEnabled().setGlobalValue(false);
      prefs_.assistant().setGlobalValue(newAssistant);   // <-- persists "posit"
      prefs_.writeUserPrefs((completed) -> {});           // <-- independent of OK/Cancel
   }
}
```

`writeUserPrefs` sends `setUserPrefs` immediately, so `assistant = "posit"` is committed as soon as the user picks Posit -- before the install check and regardless of how the dialog is later dismissed. Two concrete outcomes:

1. **Cancel after a blocked OK.** The #18350 guard blocks **OK** (via `validate()`), but **Cancel** is not gated. The dialog closes with `assistant = "posit"` already persisted and nothing installed.
2. **Declining the install prompt is a no-op revert.** `checkPositAssistantInstallation` captures `previousAssistantValue = prefs_.assistant().getGlobalValue()` *after* `disableCopilot` already set it to `"posit"`. On decline, `revertPositAiPreference` computes `revertTo == "posit" == selAssistant_.getValue()` and early-returns without reverting, so it stays `"posit"`.

(Method/line references are relative to the #18350 fix branch: `disableCopilot` ~L1031, its `ASSISTANT_POSIT` call ~L497, the `previousAssistantValue` capture ~L1080, and the revert early-return ~L1344.)

### Suggested fix

Some combination of:

- Capture the pre-switch assistant value **before** `disableCopilot()` mutates the pref, and thread it through so the revert restores the prior selection. Note: a correct revert to Copilot must also restore `copilot_enabled = true` (which `disableCopilot` set to false), so `revertPositAiPreference` (or its caller) needs to handle re-enabling Copilot, not just the `assistant` pref.
- And/or defer the eager `assistant` write in `disableCopilot` until the install check resolves (or until `onApply`), so the Copilot -> Posit transition also respects the OK / `validate()` gate instead of committing immediately.

Cover the fix with a test -- ideally the same `@ai` E2E scenario proposed for #18350, but starting from Copilot rather than None.

### Notes

- Found during code review of the #18350 fix.
- The eager write in `disableCopilot` predates #18350; this is a coverage gap of that fix rather than a regression it introduced.

title: Windows 32-bit build fails: ambiguous Message::setHeader call in FixedBufferProxyTests.cpp (C2668)
description:
## Summary

The `main` Windows hourly build fails while compiling the 32-bit session components:

```
src\cpp\core\http\FixedBufferProxyTests.cpp(393): error C2668: 'rstudio::core::http::Message::setHeader': ambiguous call to overloaded function
src\cpp\core\http\FixedBufferProxyTests.cpp(811): error C2668: 'rstudio::core::http::Message::setHeader': ambiguous call to overloaded function
ERROR: 32-bit session components build failed
```

## Root cause

`FixedBufferProxyTests.cpp` (added in #18541, "Stream localhost proxy responses") calls:

```cpp
pResponse->setHeader("Content-Length", body.size());
```

`Message::setHeader` has overloads taking `(const std::string&, int)` and `(const std::string&, uintmax_t)`. In the 32-bit build, `body.size()` is a 32-bit `size_t`, which matches neither overload exactly, so MSVC cannot choose and emits C2668. The 64-bit build is unaffected because `size_t` and `uintmax_t` are the same width there.

## Fix

Disambiguate at both call sites, e.g.:

```cpp
pResponse->setHeader("Content-Length", static_cast<uintmax_t>(body.size()));
```

(Alternatively, narrow the `setHeader` overload set so 32-bit `size_t` resolves unambiguously.)

## Notes

PR builds don't build the 32-bit session components (to save time), so this class of failure can only surface in the full Windows pipeline

title: Don't show What's New again after installing a patch release
description:
### Current behavior

RStudio Desktop's "What's New" window shows again after a patch release is installed, not just on the first run of a new release.

The seen-state is keyed by release name **and** patch level, and the check requires the stored patch to be greater than or equal to the running patch (`src/node/desktop/src/main/whats-new-state.ts`):

```ts
hasSeenRelease(releaseName: string, patch: number): boolean {
  const entry = this.findEntry(releaseName);
  return entry !== undefined && entry.patch >= patch;
}
```

The patch value is `buildInfo().RSTUDIO_VERSION_PATCH` — the third component of the version (`src/node/desktop/src/main/session-launcher.ts`). The release ("flower") name comes from `version/RELEASE`, which only changes on a minor branch update, so 2026.08.0 and 2026.08.1 both report the same release name.

So a user who installs 2026.08.0 and dismisses What's New will see it again after installing 2026.08.1, because `hasSeenRelease("Autumn Hawkbit", 1)` evaluates `0 >= 1` → false.

This is deliberate today and covered by a test (`test/unit/main/whats-new-state.test.ts`, "shows again for a higher patch of the same release").

### Requested behavior

Only show What's New once per release, not once per patch. After a user has seen What's New for a release, installing a patch of that same release should not show it again.

### Notes

The What's New content is keyed by release slug only — `resolveWhatsNewContentPath(slug)` resolves `assets/whats-new/<slug>/index.html` with no patch dimension. Unless a patch branch updates that page, the re-display shows the same content the user already dismissed.

If a patch ever does need to announce something, that would need a separate mechanism; per-patch content is not modeled today.

title: HTTP proxying of unchunked responses buffers entire response to memory
description:
### Problem Statement

> Describe the problem for which you are creating this issue.

When the http proxies in rstudio-server receive a response that is not using chunked transfer-encoding, the entire response is buffered to memory before being forwarded. This has at least two clear downsides, inefficient use of/unbounded use of memory, and high time to first byte (at least, of the response body) from the client's perspective.

### Proposed Behaviour

> Describe the proposed behaviour which would solve the problem above.

All proxied responses are forwarded in a manner that avoids full response buffering and begins forwarding response data while the upstream response is still in progress.

ℹ️ The initial implementation will not cover the session proxy, only the localhost proxy.

### QA Notes

> Once you have opened a PR, add additional information for QA on how to validate the change, paying special attention to the level of risk, adjacent areas that could be affected by the change, and any important contextual information not present in the original description.

Existing regression / e2e testing should be sufficient to verify core functionality is not disrupted. To verify the new behavior functions correctly, it is necessary to generate a large unchunked http response from a process running on localhost. One way to do this is to run [this shiny app](https://github.com/mbaynton/shiny-big-download) from inside RStudio. You can verify accuracy of the downloaded data via sha comparison, and can verify rss of `rsession` does not spike to greater than the download after transferring a large file.

title: Move Rmd option "evaluate chunks in directory:" to project settings or Rmd yml and change autocompletion
description:
I love Rmarkdown. I use it in all my projects and it is one of the first things I teach as well. However, one major caveat is, as is so often, the confusion about working directories and filepaths, which becomes especially prominent when I push for my students to use RStudio projects. I then have to explain how working directories work differently in Rmarkdown.
It get's even more confusing when the behavior of code chunks changes based on
```
editor_options: 
  chunk_output_type: console
```
, which is not immediately obvious (see: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2595).

The `here` package tries to alleviate this confusing by building filepaths for us https://here.r-lib.org/articles/rmarkdown.html
However, when typing a filepath inside of a string in the `here` function, RStudio's autocompletion still assumes that the working directory is the directory of the Rmd file, which throws a lot of people off.
Someone previously addressed this in an issue in `here`, but didn't seem to follow up on it (https://github.com/r-lib/here/issues/35)

There is the option in RStudio to set the working directory of Rmarkdown documents globally:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17450586/110929891-c3b0b380-8328-11eb-8a7f-204baeeb0dcc.png)
but there are two major drawbacks to this:
- The autocompletion doesn't respect this option
- It is part of a users global configuration and thus not reproducible

What I would love to see is this option as part of either the yml frontmatter to make it a shareable property of the document, like `chunk_output_type: console`, or at least as part of the project specific RStudio configuration to make it reproducible within the project. Of course it would then be great if the autocompletion could recognize this option.
These two changes would make Rmarkdown documents inside of RStudio projects work more seamlessly. And even if it doesn't fully remove the need for the here package it would make working with it more streamlined.

Here is a loose list of previous discussions on this topic:
- https://github.com/ropensci/targets/issues/230
- https://github.com/r-lib/here/issues/14
- https://community.rstudio.com/t/setting-working-directory-in-rmarkdown/70849
- https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/working-directory.html
- https://github.com/ropensci/ezknitr

title: Posit Assistant package download drops the failure reason, ignores the download status, and passes an ineffective timeout
description:
## Summary

`downloadPackage()` (`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp:4346`) downloads the Posit Assistant package with an in-process `download.file()` call. Three problems in that one function make a failed install hard to diagnose:

1. The reason for the failure is discarded, because `download.file()` puts it in a warning rather than in the error.
2. The return status is ignored, so some methods report failure only as a warning and slip past the check entirely.
3. The `timeout = 60` argument is not a `download.file()` parameter and has no effect.

This is the install/update counterpart of the manifest fix in #18578, which only covered the manifest fetch.

## 1. The failure reason is dropped

`download.file()` reports *what* went wrong in a warning; the error it raises says only that the URL could not be opened. Verified locally with `https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:9` and `download.file.method = "libcurl"`:

```
ERROR:    cannot open URL 'https://cdn.posit.co/posit-ai/manifest.json'
WARNINGS: URL 'https://cdn.posit.co/posit-ai/manifest.json': status was 'Couldn't connect to server'
```

`downloadPackage()` returns that error unchanged, and the caller builds the user-visible message from it (`SessionChat.cpp:5898`):

```cpp
s_updateState.installMessage = "Download failed: " + error.getMessage();
```

So a user behind a corporate proxy sees `Download failed: cannot open URL 'https://...'` -- no proxy/DNS/TLS detail -- and the same text goes to the log at `SessionChat.cpp:4372`.

The manifest path does not have this problem: it runs the download in a child process and its stderr captures both the warning and the error (`.rs.chat.manifestDownloadCommand`, `SessionChat.R`), which #18578 then routed to the log and dialog.

Fix: wrap the call in an R helper that collects warnings with `withCallingHandlers()` and folds their text into the returned error, so the cause reaches the install dialog and the log.

## 2. The download status is ignored

Not every method raises an error on failure -- `method = "curl"` returns a non-zero status and only warns. `downloadPackage()` never inspects the return value, so those failures fall through to the size check at `SessionChat.cpp:4376`:

```cpp
if (!destPath.exists() || destPath.getSize() == 0)
```

An empty file is caught there. A truncated-but-non-empty file is not: it reaches the SHA-256 verification and fails with (`SessionChat.cpp:5936`)

> Package integrity check failed (SHA-256 mismatch). The download may be corrupted or tampered with.

which points the user at a security problem when the actual cause is a dropped connection.

The manifest command already guards against exactly this, and `src/cpp/tests/testthat/test-chat.R:51` documents why. `downloadPackage()` should check the status the same way.

## 3. `timeout = 60` has no effect

`SessionChat.cpp:4367`:

```cpp
downloadFunc.addParam("timeout", 60);  // 60 second timeout for larger package
```

`download.file()` has no `timeout` argument:

```
function (url, destfile, method, quiet = FALSE, mode = "w", cacheOK = TRUE,
    extra = getOption("download.file.extra"), headers = NULL,
    ...)
```

The argument lands in `...` and is silently dropped; the transfer timeout is `options(timeout = )`, as the manifest command's documentation already notes (`SessionChat.R`, `.rs.chat.manifestDownloadCommand`). R's default is 60, so today's behavior happens to match the comment's intent, but a user or admin who sets `options(timeout = )` in a profile silently overrides it in either direction -- a short value can abort the package download early, and the code gives no indication that the 60 it names is not in force.

Fix: set `options(timeout = )` around the download (as the manifest command does) instead of passing a parameter that does nothing.

## Notes

- Single call site: `performInstall` at `SessionChat.cpp:5892`.
- Items 1 and 2 are testable through an R helper in `src/cpp/tests/testthat/test-chat.R`, alongside the existing `manifestDownloadCommand` tests that cover the same two behaviors for the manifest fetch.

title: On Windows, terminal bash shells don't save bash history when RStudio session closes
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.08.0+185
    OS Version      : Windows
    R Version       : n/a (not R-dependent)

> [!NOTE]
> This is not unique to RStudio; also a problem in Windows Terminal: https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/11697
>
> and VSCode: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/151105
>
> The "fix" is probably to write up and test instructions on how to configure bash on Windows so it saves history incrementally instead of only at shutdown. I posted an initial stab at this in https://forum.posit.co/t/terminal-history/214897.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Set the Terminal shell to Git Bash (Tools > Global Options > Terminal).
2. Before starting RStudio, delete the existing history file so the test starts clean.
3. Start RStudio and open a Terminal tab.
4. Run a couple of commands, e.g. `echo one` and `echo two`.
5. Close RStudio.
6. Inspect the history file: `echo one` and `echo two` are not there.

For contrast, repeat steps 2-4, but type `exit` in the terminal instead of closing
RStudio. Open a new terminal and run `history` -- the commands are present.

### Describe the problem in detail

Bash appends its in-memory history to `$HISTFILE` when it exits normally. RStudio's
Windows terminal never gives it the chance, because the shell is hard-killed on
shutdown.

`rCleanup()` calls `terminateAllChildren()` (`src/cpp/session/SessionMain.cpp:1561`),
which reaches `ChildProcess::terminate()` via `ProcessSupervisor::terminateAll()`.
That is an unconditional `TerminateProcess(hProcess, 15)`
(`src/cpp/core/system/Win32ChildProcess.cpp:337`) against the shell itself -- no
signal, no request to exit, no wait. The pseudoconsole teardown in
`ConPty::teardownLocked()` (`src/cpp/core/system/Win32ConPty.cpp:530`) runs later,
by which point the shell is already gone.

This is not specific to the ConPTY backend. `ChildProcess::terminate()` is unchanged
from the winpty implementation, which stored the shell's process handle in the same
field, so the same hard kill applied there.

No pseudoconsole teardown mechanism offers a graceful path either. Measured against
Git Bash running under a real pseudoconsole:

| teardown mechanism | shell exit | history saved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TerminateProcess` (what shutdown does today) | immediate, code 15 | no |
| `ClosePseudoConsole` | immediate, `STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT` | no |
| close the stdin pipe (EOF) | immediate, `STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT` | no |
| write `0x03`, then `exit\r` | 172 ms, code 0 | **yes** |

Closing the pseudoconsole does reach the shell -- conhost delivers `CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT`
-- but msys bash exits from cygwin's console-control handler instead of raising
`SIGHUP`, so its history flush never runs. Writing an exit command into the pty is
the only mechanism that takes bash's normal exit path. The same sequence also exits
`cmd.exe` (157 ms) and PowerShell (188 ms) cleanly, and the leading `0x03` keeps it
safe when the user has left a half-typed command line, a running foreground command,
or a stopped job.

The result is that any shell state normally persisted on exit is lost. Bash history
is the visible symptom, but the same applies to anything else a shell writes in its
exit path.

Posix is unaffected: closing the pty master raises `SIGHUP`, and bash saves history
on any terminating signal (confirmed: history is written on `SIGHUP`, lost on
`SIGKILL`).

Worth noting: the terminal pane's scrollback *is* preserved across a restart (it is
saved separately by `saveConsoleProcessesAtShutdown()` in
`src/cpp/session/SessionConsoleProcessTable.cpp:178`), so previous output reappears
even though the shell's own history did not survive. The two are unrelated
mechanisms, which can make the missing history easy to overlook.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Terminal shells should have an opportunity to shut down cleanly when RStudio exits,
so that shell-managed state -- bash history in particular -- is preserved, matching
what happens when the user types `exit`.

Posit Assistant: report the download configuration when the manifest fetch fails
description:
## Summary

When the Posit Assistant manifest download fails behind a corporate proxy, the failure text now reaches the session log and the Connection Error dialog (#18570 / #18578), e.g.:

```
Manifest download failed: cannot open URL 'https://cdn.posit.co/posit-ai/manifest.json'
Warning: URL 'https://cdn.posit.co/posit-ai/manifest.json': status was 'SSL connect error'
```

What is still missing is the configuration that produced it. The download options and proxy environment are not reported anywhere, and they are not inferable from the failure text:

- `SSL connect error` says TLS interception, but not whether the session is on the `libcurl` method that macOS forces (`.rs.initSecureDownload`, `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionPackages.R`), which ignores the Keychain, or already on `method = "curl"` with a `--cacert` in `download.file.extra` that isn't working.
- `Couldn't connect to server` with `https_proxy` set means the proxy URL is wrong or wants authentication; the same string with `https_proxy` unset means no proxy is configured at all.

Those are different fixes, and today triage has to ask the user to run `getOption("download.file.method")` and a few `Sys.getenv()` calls to tell them apart.

## Proposed change

Report a compact snapshot of the download configuration when a manifest fetch fails:

- The resolved `download.file.method` and `download.file.extra`.
- Whether `https_proxy` / `http_proxy` / `no_proxy` / `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` are set (checking both the lower- and upper-case spellings, and naming the one found, so the case in play is visible).

Redaction, not verbatim echo. This text is written to the log and shown in a dialog with a "Copy error" button (`generateManifestUnavailableHTML`, `src/gwt/.../chat/ChatPane.java`), so it is designed to be pasted into support tickets and forum posts:

- Proxy URLs routinely embed `user:password` -- reduce them to `host:port`.
- `download.file.extra` and `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` name internal paths -- report the flags in play without their values, and set/unset for the path.

Placement follows the existing message flow in `onUpdateCheckComplete` (`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp`):

- Always append it to the `Failed to download manifest` log line. A fetch failure with a compatible installation already present is deliberately silent to the user, so for that case the log is the only place it appears -- which is where triage looks anyway.
- It reaches `errorMessage` (and therefore the dialog and the chat pane) only in the branch that blocks Posit Assistant, which is already the only branch that sets `errorMessage`.

Collected in an R helper so the formatting and redaction are unit-testable in `src/cpp/tests/testthat/test-chat.R`, alongside the existing `.rs.chat.manifestDownloadCommand` tests.

## Out of scope

- **Remediation guidance in the UI.** An earlier draft of this issue proposed hint text naming the env vars and options to set and where to put them (`~/.Renviron`, `~/.Rprofile`). Dropped deliberately: guidance strings in a dialog are localized, go stale, and invite "I set that and it still fails," while the diagnostics above are inert facts that support and administrators already know how to act on.
- **Auto-detecting the macOS system proxy or trusting Keychain CAs.** A bigger change that would have to apply to all of RStudio's download paths, not just Posit Assistant.
- **The package download path.** `downloadPackage()` has its own defects (the failure reason is dropped, the download status is ignored, an ineffective `timeout` argument) -- tracked separately in #18610.

title: NES language server ignores RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH and system-wide installs
description:
### Summary

`paiLanguageServerPath()` hardcodes the Posit Assistant install location instead of resolving it the way the rest of the assistant code does. As a result the NES language server ignores both `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` and the system-wide install location, while the chat backend honors both.

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/main/src/cpp/session/modules/SessionAssistant.cpp#L453-L471

```cpp
FilePath paiLanguageServerPath()
{
   FilePath languageServerDir = xdg::userDataDir().completePath("pai/bin/dist/nes");
   ...
}
```

Everything else resolves the install through `locatePositAssistantInstallation()` (`src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatInstallation.cpp:48`), which checks three locations in order:

1. `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH`
2. `<XDG_DATA>/pai/bin`
3. `<XDG_SYSTEM_CONFIG>/pai/bin` (e.g. `/etc/rstudio/pai/bin`)

`paiLanguageServerPath()` only ever looks at (2).

### Impact

Two cases where completions silently diverge from chat:

- **`RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` set to a dev build.** Chat runs the dev build; NES runs whatever happens to be in `<XDG_DATA>/pai/bin/dist/nes`, or nothing at all. Mixing a dev chat backend with a stale language server is a confusing state to debug, since nothing reports the mismatch.
- **System-wide install only** (`/etc/rstudio/pai/bin`, no per-user install). Chat works; completions never start. `paiLanguageServerPath()` returns an empty path and logs at debug level only, so the failure is invisible unless assistant logging is turned up.

Note that the adjacent `copilotLanguageServerPath()` does provide an override (`RSTUDIO_COPILOT_JS_FOLDER`, `SessionAssistant.cpp:474`), so the escape hatch exists for Copilot but not for Posit Assistant.

### Suggested fix

Derive the NES directory from `locatePositAssistantInstallation()` and append `dist/nes`, so both halves of the assistant resolve to the same installation.

### Reproduction

1. Install Posit Assistant normally so `<XDG_DATA>/pai/bin` exists.
2. Set `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` to a different valid install (containing `dist/client/index.html` and `dist/server/main.js`) and start a session.
3. The chat pane loads from the override path; the NES language server still loads from `<XDG_DATA>/pai/bin/dist/nes`.

title: Upgrade GitHub Actions from the retiring Node 20 runtime to Node 24
description:
### Problem Statement

GitHub is retiring the Node.js 20 runtime that a lot of our workflow actions run on. Jobs using those actions already print a deprecation warning on every run, and once the runtime is actually removed, those steps will start failing outright.

The actions currently pinned to Node 20 versions, with their occurrence counts across `.github/`:

- `actions/upload-artifact` (v4.6.2, 42 uses) -- latest is v7.0.1 (Node 24)
- `actions/checkout` (v4.4.0, 25 uses) -- latest is v7.0.1 (Node 24)
- `actions/cache/save` and `actions/cache/restore` (v4.3.0, 21 uses each, 42 total) -- latest is v6.1.0 (Node 24)
- `actions/setup-node` (v4.4.0, 16 uses) -- latest is v7.0.0 (Node 24)
- `actions/download-artifact` (v4.3.0, 15 uses) -- latest is v8.0.1 (Node 24)
- `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` (v2.9.4, 7 uses) -- latest is v3.0.5 (Node 24)
- `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` (v4.3.1, 8 uses) -- latest is v6.2.3 (Node 24)
- `actions/stale` (floating `@v3`, 1 use in `.github/workflows/os-stale.yml`) -- this one is on the even older Node 12 runtime, latest is v11.0.0 (Node 24)

`actions/setup-python`, `mozilla-actions/sccache-action`, and `1password/load-secrets-action` are already on Node 24 and don't need touching.

Two smaller things worth folding in while we're here:

- A few references use a floating major tag instead of the SHA pin the rest of the repo uses: `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/upload-artifact@v4` in `.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml`, and `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4` and `r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2` in `.github/workflows/os-build-dependencies-windows.yml`.
- `r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2`'s runtime couldn't be confirmed (the API fetch of its `action.yaml` failed), so that one needs a separate check before assuming it's fine.

Some of these are big major-version jumps (`upload-artifact` v4 to v7, `download-artifact` v4 to v8, `cache` v4 to v6) and likely carry behavior changes worth reading through, not just a version bump. It'd probably go smoother done as a few PRs per action family rather than one big sweep.

### Proposed Behaviour

Bump each of the actions above to a current Node 24 major version, pinned by SHA the way the rest of the workflows already do it, and update the two floating-tag references to match. End state: no action in `.github/workflows/` still runs on Node 20 or Node 12, and no deprecation warnings show up in the run logs.

### QA Notes

title: Assistant agent stderr is logged verbatim, dumping bundled language server JavaScript into rsession logs
description:
### Problem

`onStderr` in `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionAssistant.cpp` logs the agent's stderr buffer verbatim:

```cpp
LOG_ERROR_MESSAGE(stdErr);
```
(`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionAssistant.cpp:1187`)

When the bundled language server throws during startup, Node.js prints the offending source line before the stack trace. That source is minified, so a single "line" is the whole bundle chunk. Each crash writes roughly 19 KB of minified JavaScript into `rsession-$USER.log`, with the actual error message buried at the end after the newlines have been collapsed to `|||`.

Observed while diagnosing a Copilot language server startup failure: six restart attempts produced a 226 KB log whose 24 lines were almost entirely the contents of `copilot-language-server-js/main.js`. Finding the real error (`ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` on `watcher.node`) required slicing the tail off a 19,027-character line.

### The same text also reaches the user

Immediately below, the buffer is accumulated into the startup error:

```cpp
s_agentStartupError += stdErr;
```
(`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionAssistant.cpp:1197`)

`s_agentStartupError` is surfaced in two user-facing places:

- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionAssistant.cpp:285` — `"The AI assistant agent failed to launch: " + s_agentStartupError`
- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionAssistant.cpp:2725` — `resultJson["output"] = s_agentStartupError`

so a startup crash puts tens of kilobytes of minified JavaScript into a status message and into the diagnostics report. Because `+=` appends on every stderr callback, the accumulated string grows with each chunk the agent emits.

### Suggested direction

Cap what gets logged and what gets accumulated — for example, truncate each stderr chunk to a sane number of characters (keeping the tail, where Node.js puts the error and stack trace, rather than the head), and bound the total size of `s_agentStartupError`. The full text is still available on the agent's stderr for anyone who needs it.

### Note

Not a regression, and not tied to any particular agent failure — any startup crash in a bundled JS agent produces this.

title: Chat pane can hold two Posit Assistant iframes for up to ~15s after R session restart
description:
### Describe the problem in detail

After an R session restart with the Posit Assistant chat pane open, the workbench DOM can contain **two** `iframe[title="Posit Assistant"]` elements at once for an extended window: the stale pre-restart frame (whose chat client keeps retrying its websocket against the dead session's proxy path, logging repeated handshake 500s) and the hidden replacement frame.

This is a consequence of the double-buffered resume swap in `ChatPane.loadUrlFromSuspended` (`src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/chat/ChatPane.java:333-430`):

1. On resume, a second hidden `RStudioThemedFrame` is created with the same title and added to `mainPanel_` alongside the existing `frame_`.
2. The old frame is only removed after the new frame's `onload` fires **plus** `FRAME_SWAP_DELAY_MS` (350ms).
3. If the new frame's document stalls -- e.g. the restarted session's chat backend/proxy is not serving `ai-chat/index.html` yet -- both frames stay attached until `FRAME_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` (15000ms) reclaims the pending frame.

So the duplicate window is bounded, but the bound is 15 seconds. During it, any lookup of the chat iframe by title (accessibility tooling, automation) is ambiguous, and the stale frame's websocket retry loop spams the console with `Error during WebSocket handshake: Unexpected response code: 500`.

### Observed in CI

`chat-pane-persistence.test.ts:92 › chat pane content survives R session restart` failed on an unrelated PR (#18578) with a strict-mode violation -- the locator resolved to both frames:

```
1) <iframe class="gwt-Frame" title="Posit Assistant" src="ai-chat/index.html?wsUrl=%2Fp%2F1e5689ee%2Fai-chat&_t=...&resume">
2) <iframe class="gwt-Frame" title="Posit Assistant" src="ai-chat/index.html?wsUrl=%2F130a5f0e%2Fai-chat&_t=...&resume">
```

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/32071332224/job/95525008596 (initial attempt and retry #1 both failed; the test's `toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })` races the 15s swap window exactly).

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Open the Posit Assistant chat pane.
2. Restart the R session (Session > Restart R) while delaying the new session's chat backend startup (slow machine or breakpoint).
3. Inspect the DOM during the resume swap: two iframes titled "Posit Assistant" are attached until the swap or the 15s load timeout completes.

### Describe the behavior you expected

At most one iframe exposed as "Posit Assistant" at any time -- e.g. blank or drop the pending frame's title until it is swapped in, or remove the old frame as soon as the pending frame starts loading. Independently, the e2e locator could be hardened (scope to the visible frame) so the suite does not race the swap window.

title: Playwright acceptUpdateDialog can silently skip the Posit Assistant install check
description:
### System details

    Repo Location   : e2e/rstudio (Playwright suite)
    Test Mode       : Desktop (test:desktop)
    Node Version    : v24.18.0
    Playwright      : 1.61.1
    OS Version      : macOS 26.5.2

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. In `e2e/rstudio`, run `npm run test:desktop -- tests/panes/editor/code_suggestions.test.ts -g "Posit AI"`.
2. Repeat several times back to back on the same machine.
    - Occasionally, most or all "Posit AI" tests in the file fail on a ghost-text or NES-suggestion visibility timeout.
3. Check the sandbox's assistant data directory (`data-home/pai` under the failed run's sandbox root).
    - It contains only `manifest-check.json`, no `bin` subdirectory -- the addon was never installed.

### Describe the problem in detail

`acceptUpdateDialog()` in `actions/assistant_options.actions.ts` checks whether the "Update Posit Assistant" dialog is visible with a single `isVisible()` snapshot, right after a fixed one-second sleep:

```
const updateBtn = this.page.locator('#rstudio_dlg_yes');
if (!(await updateBtn.isVisible())) {
  return;
}
```

The dialog only appears once an async RPC (`chat_check_for_updates`) resolves, and that RPC has no fixed latency. When it takes longer than the one-second window, this check reads as "no update needed" even though the dialog is about to appear, and the function returns without installing the addon. The test then proceeds as if the assistant were ready, and later steps that expect real completions (ghost text, NES suggestions) fail on a 30-second visibility timeout that gives no hint the real cause was a skipped install.

### Describe the behavior you expected

It would be cool if `acceptUpdateDialog()` waited for the dialog with a real timeout instead of an instant snapshot, and if `setupAssistantOptions()` verified the addon actually ended up installed before returning, failing loudly with a clear message if not, instead of letting the test proceed toward an unrelated-looking timeout.

See issue #18350.

title: E2E required-packages install fails on R 4.1 because it never falls back to source
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.08.1+195 (also seen on 2026.09 dailies)
    OS Version      : macOS 14 arm64 (GitHub macos-14 runner)
    R Version       : 4.1.3

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Any e2e engine can be dispatched with an arbitrary `r_version`, so this is reachable from every one of them. The certification workflow is the only caller that reaches it automatically, because it binds each environment to its own R version instead of passing `release`:

1. Dispatch "Test: E2E Playwright RStudio (Certification, Open Source)".
2. Set `cells` to `macos14`.
3. Leave every other input at its default.
4. Wait for the `macOS 14 arm64 (R 4.1.3) / e2e-desktop-macos14` job to reach "Install e2e test dependencies".
    - The step fails, before RStudio is exercised at all.
    - The log reports which packages could not be installed:

      ```
      [os-e2e-deps] installing required-packages: devtools, remotes, reticulate, shinytest2, styler
      Error: [os-e2e-deps] failed to install required-packages: devtools, reticulate, shinytest2
      ```

    - R names the reason just above that line:

      ```
      packages 'devtools', 'reticulate', 'shinytest2' are not available as a binary package for this version of R
      ```

5. Confirm that `remotes` and `styler` did install, so the failure is per package rather than the whole set.

The same failure is reachable without the certification workflow at all:

1. Dispatch "Test: E2E Playwright RStudio (Desktop, macOS 14 ARM64)" on its own.
2. Set `r_version` to `4.1.3`, replacing the `release` default.
    - The same step fails the same way.

### Describe the problem in detail

The required-packages install in `.github/actions/os-e2e-deps/action.yml` passes `type = "binary"` on any platform whose `.Platform$pkgType` is not `"source"`, and a binary-only install does not fall back to source on its own. Posit Package Manager's R 4.1 index carries no build for `devtools`, `reticulate` or `shinytest2`, so those three stay missing and the step's completeness check stops the job. The install is a deliberate hard gate, so the cell dies at provisioning and none of the suite runs.

R 4.1 is the cliff, not any particular OS. Checking PPM's indexes for those three packages:

| Platform | R 4.1 | R 4.2 |
|---|---|---|
| macOS arm64 | none of the 3 | all 3 |
| macOS x86_64 | none of the 3 | all 3 |
| Windows | none of the 3 | all 3 |

So Windows Server 2025 and macOS 15 x86_64 fail the same way if dispatched at R 4.1. Linux is unaffected, since those engines already install from source. The `macos14` certification cell is simply the only one pinned below R 4.2, which is why it surfaced there first.

Two copies of the same pattern, binary-only with no fallback, also sit in the test suite's own provisioning at `e2e/rstudio/fixtures/r-libs-setup.ts` and `e2e/rstudio/actions/console_pane.actions.ts`. Those matter for local runs, where macOS and Windows packages resolve from CRAN, which publishes no arm64 binaries below R 4.2 at all, so the per-test self-heal path cannot heal either.

### Describe the behavior you expected

A package with no binary for the running R would ideally be built from source, so the cached library ends up complete and the run carries on into the suite. An R version with full binary coverage would keep installing binaries and compile nothing.

See PR #18582.

title: Posit Assistant manifest download failures surface a generic errno instead of the captured cause
description:
### Describe the problem in detail

When the Posit Assistant manifest download fails, the specific cause is captured and then thrown away. Both the log line and the user-facing Connection Error dialog show a generic string instead.

`manifestFromDownloadResult` folds the child process's stderr into the error (`src/cpp/session/modules/chat/ChatIntegrity.cpp:286-291`):

```cpp
std::string detail = boost::algorithm::trim_copy(result.stdErr);
std::string suffix = detail.empty() ? std::string() : (": " + detail);

if (result.exitStatus != EXIT_SUCCESS)
   return systemError(boost::system::errc::io_error,
                      "Manifest download failed" + suffix, ERROR_LOCATION);
```

That `systemError` overload stores the text as a **`description` property**, not as the error's message (`src/cpp/shared_core/Error.cpp:542-549`). For an error built from an `error_code`, `Message` is just `in_ec.message()` (`src/cpp/shared_core/Error.cpp:199-202`).

Both consumers read `getMessage()`:

- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp:4599` — `WLOG("Failed to download manifest: {}", fetchError.getMessage());`
- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp:4622` — `errorMessage = fetchError.getMessage();`, which is what reaches the dialog via `s_updateState.errorMessage`

So the detail reaches neither the log nor the UI. On Linux/macOS the dialog reads "Input/output error". On Windows `boost::system::system_category()` is the Win32 category, where code 5 is `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`, so the message is likely "Access is denied" — actively misleading for what is usually a DNS, proxy, or TLS failure. (Not yet confirmed on a Windows build.)

The discarded detail is exactly what makes these reports diagnosable. Running the child command by hand shows R already puts the real cause on stderr, under the default `warn = 0`, because it flushes deferred warnings after a top-level error:

```
Error in download.file(...) : cannot open URL '...'
In addition: Warning message:
In download.file(...) :
  URL '...': status was 'Couldn't resolve host name'
```

The warning is the only part that distinguishes DNS failure from a proxy 407, TLS interception, or an HTTP status rejection (`... HTTP status was '403 Forbidden'`). The error line alone is identical for all of them. `AsyncRProcess` already captures this; nothing on the R side needs to change.

### Suggested fix

Use `core::errorDescription()` (`src/cpp/shared_core/Error.cpp:635-641`), which returns the `description` property and falls back to the message, at both sites in `SessionChat.cpp` — one line each.

### Note: this is a regression

Before the async manifest fetch landed in #17896, the download error came from `r::exec::RFunction::call()`, and `rCodeExecutionError` puts the R error text into `Message` (`src/cpp/r/RErrorCategory.cpp:87`). A user on 2026.04.0 hitting this sees:

```
Error in .rs.downloadFile(url = "https://cdn.posit.co/posit-ai/manifest.json", ... cannot open URL 'https://cdn.posit.co/posit-ai/manifest.json'
```

Still short of the warning text, but it at least identifies the operation and the URL. On a current build the same failure surfaces less information than it did before.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Break outbound access to `https://cdn.posit.co/posit-ai/manifest.json` (disconnect the network, or point at a proxy that refuses `CONNECT`).
2. Start RStudio with Posit Assistant selected, or run **Help > Check for Posit Assistant updates**.
3. Observe the Connection Error dialog, and the `Failed to download manifest` line in the session log.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Both the dialog and the log name the actual failure — e.g. `Manifest download failed: ... status was 'Couldn't resolve host name'` — rather than a generic errno string.

Live LaTeX/math preview in the editor does not render at all, in either "Inline" or "In a popup" mode (Tools > Global Options > R Markdown > Show equation and image previews), and in both Source and Visual editor modes.

This appears immediately after upgrading to 2026.08.0, which per the release notes shipped PR #8715 switching the editor's live preview renderer from MathJax 2.7 to MathJax 4. Final document rendering (quarto render, which still uses the old bundled MathJax 2.7 via mathjax: "local") works correctly, isolating the problem to the new in-editor MathJax 4 preview path introduced in #8715.

Create a new .qmd file with format: html and one line of inline math, e.g. $x^2 + y^2 = z^2$.
Set Tools > Global Options > R Markdown > "Show equation and image previews" to "Inline" (or "In a popup").
Place the cursor inside the math span in Source mode, or open the file in Visual mode.
Expected behavior A rendered preview of the equation appears inline or in a popup.

Actual behavior No preview appears in either mode, in either editor. Rendering the document with Quarto/Pandoc produces correct math output, confirming the LaTeX source itself is valid.

title: Run E2E tests with daily build of Posit Assistant
description:
### Problem Statement

Before promoting a daily build of Posit Assistant to be the released version that users will get, I've been running my own local e2e test of the `@ai` tests, on my Mac, by creating `e2e/rstudio/.prefs.local.json` containing:

```json
{
  "posit_assistant_test_manifest" : true
}
```
Then installing the latest daily build and running:

```bash
PW_RSTUDIO_PREFS_OVERRIDE=.prefs.local.json npm run test:desktop -- --grep @ai
```

### Proposed Behaviour

An automated run that does something similar on a regular schedule, on Mac/Windows/Linux (desktop) and perhaps Linux server.

Perhaps every Sunday evening, with the aim being to release a new Posit Assistant build on Mondays.

Would want to time it such that Sunday evening's Posit Assistant build has already completed, so the build we're testing is the one we'd release on Monday.

The Posit Assistant for RStudio build runs at 04:00 UTC = 11pm EST / midnight EDT.
