title: E2E engines warn that a run does not exercise Posit AI when it does
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : N/A
    RStudio Version : N/A
    OS Version      : N/A
    R Version       : N/A

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Dispatch any E2E engine with `POSIT_EMAIL`/`POSIT_PASSWORD` available but no
   OP service account token.
2. Read the job log for the `Check for OP service account token` step.
3. Read the `[auth-setup]` lines a few seconds later.

### Describe the problem in detail

The step emits a warning that states something untrue:

    ::warning::No OP service account token in this job. AI-gated tests will skip, so this run does NOT exercise Posit AI.

The OP token is one of two credential paths. `auth.setup.ts` also signs in via
OAuth device flow from `POSIT_EMAIL`/`POSIT_PASSWORD`, and when it does the same
log shows:

    [auth-setup] Posit AI sign-in complete; credentials are in place

[Run 32041592441](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/32041592441)
emitted both: it validated a pre-release Posit Assistant build
while warning that it had exercised no Posit AI. The step cannot know the answer
at the point it asserts one -- `auth.setup.ts` has not run yet.

Warnings surface in the Actions run summary, so this is visible without opening
the log. It is worst on the Posit Assistant release gate
(`os-test-e2e-rstudio-posit-assistant.yml`), whose only output is a
promote / don't-promote call: a prominent "does NOT exercise Posit AI" above a
run that did invites the wrong decision.

Present in all six engines -- the five `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-*` files and
`os-test-e2e-rstudio-server-os-ubuntu-24.yml`.

### Describe the behavior you expected

The warning would claim only what the step knows: that this one credential
source is absent. Either narrow the wording, or check both paths before
warning. A run with neither credential source should still warn.

### Testing

This can be tested by dispatching an engine with `POSIT_EMAIL`/`POSIT_PASSWORD`
but no OP token: the warning should no longer claim Posit AI went untested,
while `[auth-setup] Posit AI sign-in complete` still appears. Check one bash
engine and the Windows one, since that copy is PowerShell. With neither
credential source available, the warning should still fire.

title: Posit Assistant: check for updates periodically while RStudio is running
description:
### Current behavior

RStudio only checks for a new Posit Assistant version at startup, or when the user explicitly asks. Nothing re-checks while RStudio and the assistant keep running.

The entry points that can begin a manifest check are:

- `onDeferredInit` (`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp:4103`) — one check per rsession, kicked 1s after startup at idle via `startUpdateCheck(isStartup=true, force=false)`.
- `ChatPresenter.initializeChat()` → `checkForUpdates()` (`src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/chat/ChatPresenter.java:1103`) — the first time the chat pane initializes in a session, and again when the chat provider changes to Posit.
- User-initiated, all forcing a fetch: Help > Check for Posit Assistant Updates, the assistant's own gear-menu "Check for updates…" (`ui/checkForUpdates`), the Retry button after a manifest failure, the Assistant preferences pane, and the install flow.

`posit_assistant_update_check_interval_hours` (default 2) only throttles those checks — `shouldFetchManifest()` at `SessionChat.cpp:4767` compares the persisted `manifest-check.json` timestamp against the interval — it never schedules one. So an RStudio session left open for days keeps running whatever version it resolved at startup, even after the interval has elapsed many times over, and the user only learns about a new release by restarting RStudio or asking by hand.

### Requested behavior

While RStudio is running with Posit Assistant as the chat provider, check for updates automatically on a repeating schedule that honors `posit_assistant_update_check_interval_hours`:

- **interval > 0** — re-check about every N hours for the life of the session. The existing throttle still applies, so a check that another session already performed within the window resolves without a fetch.
- **interval == 0** — no automatic checks while running at all. The startup check still happens, as it does today, along with any user-initiated check.

Note the second meaning this gives to `0`: today it means "never throttle, fetch on every check", and the schema documents it as "Set to 0 to check every time". Under this request it additionally means "no periodic checks". Those two are compatible in the implementation (zero throttle window, no timer), but the pref title/description would need to say both. Alternatively `0` could keep only its throttle meaning and periodic checks get their own off switch — worth deciding before implementing.

### Notes for implementation

- When a periodic check finds an update, the existing non-blocking in-pane notification is the natural place to surface it: `showUpdateAvailableWithVersions()` (`ChatPane.java:694`) already offers Update / Dismiss without disturbing a running conversation. A mid-session check must not interrupt an in-flight conversation or restart the backend on its own.
- The check machinery is already single-flight and re-entrant (`startUpdateCheck` joins an in-flight check and queues completions), so a timer-driven caller can share the existing path.
- The throttle record lives in `~/.local/share/rstudio/pai/manifest-check.json` and is shared by every session for that user, so per-session timers across many concurrent sessions collapse to roughly one real fetch per interval.
- The timer has to react to the pref changing mid-session (interval edited in Global Options, including to and from `0`) rather than only reading it once at startup.
- Suspend/resume already gets a fresh check for free, because the new rsession runs `onDeferredInit` again — but only subject to the throttle, so it is not a substitute for a periodic check.

title: rserver can double-launch a session during restart, leaking an orphaned rsession
description:
### Symptom

An R session restart (or any session relaunch: project switch, suspend/resume) can leave behind an **orphaned rsession process** that runs forever. rserver launches two replacement sessions ~1s apart; both fully initialize and bind the same session stream socket; the proxy connects to whichever bound last, and the loser is never contacted again -- and never told to exit.

The orphan is invisible but fully alive: it holds the project's source-database lock (so the visible replacement reports "The previous R session terminated abnormally" and the client shows the modal **R Session Error** dialog), holds the Posit Assistant install in-use lock (so `chat_start_backend` in the visible session fails forever with a spurious "A Posit Assistant update is in progress" -- see #18571), auto-resumes its chat backend via the suspend/resume state, and keeps reacting to shared user-prefs changes (starting/stopping assistant agents) for as long as it lives.

Observed on the e2e server shard in [run 31839732347](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31839732347/job/94897988955?pr=18568): the orphan (pid 9716) was launched at 21:29:58, replaced at 21:29:59, and was still alive and spawning assistant agents at 21:43 -- 13 minutes later. Likely also a contributor to the #18394 wedge family.

### Root cause

From the rserver debug log of that run:

```
21:29:57.929  POST /rpc/suspend_for_restart  -> 200            (old session acks and begins forced suspend)
21:29:58.161  get_events    -> error: system error 2 (No such file or directory)   (old session's socket gone)
21:29:58.163  /rpc/ping connect fails -> recovery -> "Launching session for user: ..."
21:29:58.165  Launched session process ... pid: 9716
21:29:58.200  -- rpc error: other error for: /rpc/get_environment_state ... error: asio.misc error 2 (End of file)
21:29:59.171  "Launching RStudio session for: ..."             (second launch!)
21:29:59.172  Launched session process ... pid: 9722
21:30:02.346  RStudio session() started and connection made in 3.175s              (to 9722; 9716 orphaned)
```

The double launch happens because the pending-launch dedupe in `SessionManager::launchSession` was defeated:

1. `/rpc/ping`'s connect fails, the retry profile's recovery launches pid 9716, and a `pendingLaunches_` entry is recorded (`ServerSessionManager.cpp`).
2. `/rpc/get_environment_state` -- accepted by the *old* session just before it stopped its listener -- dies with EOF as the old session exits. Its error handler `handleRpcError` (`ServerSessionProxy.cpp:649`; `handleContentError` at :562 has the same call) **unconditionally calls `sessionManager().removePendingLaunch(context)`**, erasing the 37 ms-old pending entry for 9716 -- a live, booting process.
3. `/rpc/ping` keeps retrying its connect every 25 ms (failing while 9716 boots -- session startup takes ~3 s); its per-request launch throttle allows another recovery pass after 1 s, which now finds no pending launch and spawns 9722.
4. Both sessions initialize. 9716 binds the stream socket first (and wins the project source-database lock, and resumes the chat backend); 9722 re-binds the same socket path over it. The proxy connects to 9722. 9716 is unreachable (its listener holds an unlinked inode), is never sent a request or a quit, and leaks.

An in-flight RPC dying with EOF at the restart boundary is near-deterministic (the exiting session resets established connections when its listener stops), so this race window is hit by exactly the workload the e2e suite runs: session restarts with active background traffic.

### Fix

`removePendingLaunch` on the request-error paths must not erase a pending launch whose recorded process is still alive: the failure of some request for the context says nothing about the health of a separately launched, still-booting session. Guard the `success == false` removal with `pid != -1 && core::system::isProcessRunning(pid)`. If the launched process never becomes reachable, the existing safety nets still clear the entry: the SIGCHLD process tracker removes it when the pid dies (#18208), and the one-minute relaunch window in `launchSession` expires it otherwise. Custom session launchers (job launcher) never record a pid, so their behavior is unchanged.

Follow-ups (not this fix):
- The success path (`handleProxyResponse`) has a much narrower variant of the same race (a last-gasp response from the exiting predecessor between listener-stop and process-exit would also clear a fresh pending launch); in practice the exiting session resets in-flight connections, so errors -- not successes -- are what land in the window.
- An rsession could self-detect having been supplanted (periodically stat its stream-socket path and exit when the inode no longer matches its listener), which would clean up any orphan regardless of cause.

#18571 covers making the assistant install-lock owner id per-process so that even an orphaned predecessor cannot permanently block its replacement's chat backend.

title: reduce background filesystem operations for installed-package scans on remote library paths
description:
## Summary

Follow-up to #18059, which reduces background filesystem operations for projects that live on remote/network filesystems. That PR is intentionally scoped to **project-path** operations (the recursive project file monitor, `check_for_external_edit`), because its resolver keys on whether the *project directory* lives on a remote mount.

The Packages pane and installed-package machinery also perform repeated directory scans and per-package stats/reads, but these operate on `.libPaths()` -- **not** the project directory. The user/system library is frequently on a different filesystem than the project (e.g. a fast local disk even when the project is on NFS, or vice-versa). So these cannot be gated on the project's remoteness; they need their own remote detection against the library path(s).

## Proposal

Add library-path remote detection (reuse `core::system::isRemotePath()` against the entries of `module_context::getLibPaths()`, cached like the project detection in #18059 since `statfs()` on a hung mount can block) and use it to suppress the most expensive **startup / background** library scans -- while leaving explicit, user-initiated actions (opening/refreshing the Packages pane, "Check for Updates") alone.

## Candidate operations

- **`.rs.listInstalledPackages()`** (`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionPackages.R`, ~L1415-1505) -- highest impact. `list.files()` over every lib path, then a `file.exists(.../Meta)` stat plus a DESCRIPTION read per package. Fires at deferred init and after every install/remove and libPaths change.
- **Package-provided-extension indexing** (`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionPackageProvidedExtension.cpp`, ~L131-164) -- walks every package directory under `getLibPaths()` looking for `inst/rstudio/*` resources, at startup and after package commands.

## Explicitly out of scope (leave as-is)

- **Check for Updates** (`SessionPackages.R`, ~L167-236) -- purely on-demand (user clicked the button); the user has asked for fresh data, so don't suppress.
- **Async package info indexing** (`SessionAsyncPackageInformation.cpp`) and **PPM vulnerability fetch** (`SessionPPM.cpp`) -- mostly run in a spawned R process / over HTTP, so low session-thread filesystem impact.

## Notes / open questions

- Suppressing the deferred-init package-state refresh means the Packages pane may show stale/empty state until the user explicitly refreshes -- this is the same tradeoff as the project-scoped feature and should be documented for the user.
- Consider whether this should reuse the same global preference / per-project override UX from #18059, or get its own control, given the filesystem being detected is different (library vs project).

Addresses #10417.

title: spurious "Error Listing Objects" dialog when session restart outlives the restart grace period
description:
### Symptom

After an R session restart on RStudio Server / Workbench, a modal error dialog can appear:

> **Error Listing Objects**
> jsonrpc error 1 (Unable to connect to service)

Nothing is actually wrong -- the session comes back up normally -- but the modal blocks the UI until dismissed. Observed as an e2e failure on server-linux in `project_trust_dialog.test.ts` (PR #18528, run 31631625005-1), where the stray dialog both blocked console clicks and was misdetected as the project trust dialog.

### Root cause

`EnvironmentPresenter` refreshes the environment view on `RestartStatusEvent.RESTART_COMPLETED`. On Server that event fires when the `suspend_for_restart` RPC returns -- i.e. while the old session is still exiting -- so the refresh's `get_environment_state` RPC is dispatched into the restart window. rserver's session proxy buffers it (retrying for up to `rsession-proxy-max-wait-secs`, default 30s) and, if the relaunch is slow, fails it with jsonrpc `ConnectionError` (1, "Unable to connect to service").

`refreshView()`'s `onError` already tries to suppress restart noise, but:

- it only exempts `ServerError.TRANSMISSION` (6), not `CONNECTION` (1), and
- the `isRestartInProgress()` guard is cleared 500ms after `RESTART_COMPLETED` (see the bug #3651 comment in `WorkbenchContext`), while the proxied RPC can fail up to 30s later.

Trace timings from the failing run: `suspend_for_restart` returned in 5ms; the `get_environment_state` issued 4ms later was held for 30.02s before failing -- long after the 500ms grace window.

### Fix

Suppress the modal for `ServerError.CONNECTION` errors in the environment refresh as well. The refresh is a background operation; when the session is unreachable, the reconnect UI already communicates the state, and the environment view is refreshed again on the next deferred-init.

title: windows: environment variables set by rstudio are invisible to Sys.getenv and other CRT readers
description:
On Windows, an rsession process carries up to three distinct environment-variable stores, and RStudio's own environment writes are only visible in some of them. This issue collects the results of an audit of all global environment mutation in `src/cpp`, prompted by the `EnvironmentScope` bug fixed in #18523 (raw `::getenv` reading a different store than `core::system::setenv` writes).

## The three stores

1. **Win32 process environment block** -- what `core::system::setenv/getenv` use (`SetEnvironmentVariableW` / `GetEnvironmentVariableW`), and what child processes inherit at `CreateProcess` time.
2. **Our C runtime's environment** (`ucrtbase.dll`) -- what raw `::getenv` reads, including any third-party library linked into rsession. Snapshotted from the OS block and never refreshed by `SetEnvironmentVariable`.
3. **R's view** -- `Sys.getenv` is `_wgetenv` and `Sys.setenv` is `_wputenv`, against *R's* C runtime. For UCRT R (>= 4.2) that is the same `ucrtbase.dll` we use; for msvcrt R (<= 4.1) it is an entirely separate third store, loaded with `R.dll` (`REmbeddedWin32.cpp`).

Synchronization is asymmetric:

- `_wputenv` (i.e. `Sys.setenv`) propagates CRT -> OS block, so the R -> RStudio direction always works.
- `SetEnvironmentVariableW` (i.e. `core::system::setenv`, before the fix PR) updates the OS block only; no CRT ever notices.
- The UCRT initializes each CRT environment (narrow and wide independently) **lazily on first use, from the OS block**. R's wide environment materializes during R startup, so variables rsession stages *before* `r::session::run` are visible to `Sys.getenv` -- by timing, not by design. Variables set *after* R initializes are invisible to `Sys.getenv`, while remaining visible to R's child processes (which inherit the OS block). The *narrow* environment (used by R's C-level `getenv`, e.g. the Renviron machinery) materializes at process start for UCRT R, so it misses **all** of rsession's staging.
- Windows cannot represent "set but empty": both `SetEnvironmentVariableW` and `_putenv` treat an empty value as deletion.

## Audit findings

### Real defects

1. **Untrusted-directory `R_ENVIRON_USER=""` suppression is a no-op on Windows** (`SessionMain.cpp`, trust overrides). Two independent causes: the empty value deletes the variable instead of setting it empty (so R falls through to processing `~/.Renviron` -- see `process_user_Renviron` in R's `Renviron.c`), and for UCRT R the write never reaches R's C-level `getenv` snapshot anyway. Untrusted projects' user-level `.Renviron` files are still processed. *(Needs confirmation on a Windows machine.)*

2. **Secret scrubbing does not scrub the CRT copy.** `SessionOptions::read` and `socket_rpc::initialize` read secrets (`MONITOR_SHARED_SECRET`, the session RPC secret, launcher/user metadata vars, RSA keys are the same pattern in reverse) and immediately `core::system::unsetenv` them. On Windows that removes them from the Win32 block only; the CRT snapshot -- taken when the spawn environment still contained the secrets -- retains them for the process lifetime, readable by any in-process `::getenv` (e.g. third-party libraries).

3. **Global writes made after R initializes are invisible to `Sys.getenv`** while remaining visible to child processes, an inconsistency that is very confusing to debug. Live examples: `.rs.addRToolsToPath()` / `.rs.restorePreviousPath()` (`SessionBuild.cpp`, Windows-only, called from R -- child toolchains see the updated `PATH`, `Sys.getenv("PATH")` does not); the ssh-agent import (`SessionGit.cpp`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`/`SSH_AGENT_PID` invisible to R-side consumers such as gert/credentials); `BROWSER` (`SessionWorkbench.cpp`); `addToSystemPath` (e.g. tinytex); the standalone-port republish (`SessionHttpMethods.cpp`); environment-variable restore on resume/restart (`RSessionState.cpp`, timing-dependent).

4. **Pre-R staging works only by timing accident.** Everything staged in `rsessionMain` (`RSTUDIO=1`, `RSTUDIO_SESSION_PID`, `RSTUDIO_CONSOLE_WIDTH`, user identity, ports, `RS_RPOSTBACK_PATH`, the `syncConsoleColorEnv` cli/crayon variables, `R_HOME`/`R_DOC_DIR`/`R_LIBS_USER` in `r::session::run`) reaches `Sys.getenv` only because R happens to touch its wide environment after staging. Nothing guarantees this (any early wide-env use in a linked library would break it), and R's C-level narrow readers miss all of it for UCRT R regardless (finding 1 is the concrete instance).

### Correct as-is (for the record)

- All `Options*`/child-environment overload call sites (explicit child envs, no store involved).
- `r::util::setenv` call sites (`RSTUDIO_CONSOLE_WIDTH` runtime updates, partner vars, git askpass) -- bridged through `Sys.setenv`, which reaches every store.
- Server-only paths (`SessionClientInit.cpp` port token / URLs / referer) -- no Windows server.
- POSIX-only sites (`REnvironmentPosix.cpp`, `SessionPath.cpp`, `ODBCSYSINI`, `LANG`, `USER`, `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`) -- one store on POSIX.
- Raw `::getenv` remnants under `EnvironmentLock` (`PosixParentProcessMonitor` -- POSIX; `SessionConsoleProcess`'s `::getenv("ENV")` -- deliberate set-vs-empty distinction).
- `_RSTUDIO_LEVEL` job-object loop guard (`Win32System.cpp`) -- consumed via `core::system::getenv` and child inheritance.

## Fixes (PR to follow)

- [ ] `core::system::setenv`/`unsetenv` on Windows write through **both** the Win32 block and our CRT (`_wputenv_s`). This turns the pre-init timing accident into a guarantee for UCRT R, makes post-init writes visible to `Sys.getenv` (UCRT R), scrubs secrets from the CRT copy, and keeps raw `::getenv` readers consistent. (msvcrt builds of R still have a separate CRT that only the `r::util::setenv` / `Sys.setenv` bridge can reach.)
- [ ] Untrusted-directory suppression sets `R_ENVIRON_USER=NUL` on Windows (a set-but-empty value cannot be represented; the null device parses as an empty Renviron file, silently).
- [ ] Regression tests: core-level (raw `::getenv` observes `core::system::setenv`/`unsetenv` on Windows) and rsession-level (`Sys.getenv` observes a post-init `core::system::setenv`, in the live-R gtest harness).
- [ ] Update the stale `r::util::setenv` comments ("R links to a static copy of libc") to describe the actual mechanism.

Follow-ups, not in the PR:

- [ ] Migrate `SessionConsoleProcess`'s raw `::getenv("ENV")` to the two-argument `core::system::getenv` once #18523 merges.
- [ ] Consider a lint (in the spirit of the ASCII linter) banning raw CRT environment calls outside the `core/system` wrappers and test files.
- [ ] Verify on Windows: untrusted-project `.Renviron` suppression before/after the fix, and `Sys.getenv("SSH_AUTH_SOCK")` after using the git ssh-agent path.

## Verification notes

Behavior was derived from the UCRT sources (lazy per-width environment initialization from the OS block), the R sources (`sysutils.c` `do_getenv`/`do_setenv` via `_wgetenv`/`_wputenv`; `Renviron.c` `process_user_Renviron`; `sys-win32.c`), and cli/crayon detection code (both read `RSTUDIO`, `RSTUDIO_CONSOLE_COLOR`, and the hyperlink variables in-process via `Sys.getenv`). The Windows-specific claims are exercised by the new tests on Windows CI; the two items marked for manual verification need a Windows machine.

title: Breakpoints do not fire inside S7 methods on R versions before 4.3.0
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Server
    RStudio Version : 2026.08.0+187
    OS Version      : Debian 13 (arm64)
    R Version       : 4.2.3

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Using an R version before 4.3.0 (4.2.3 here) with the S7 package installed:

1. Create a new R script with this content:

```
library(S7)

s7mean <- new_class("s7mean")

method(mean, s7mean) <- function(x, ...) {
  message("inside the S7 method")
  42
}

obj <- s7mean()
```

2. Save the file as `s7-breakpoint.R`.
3. Click in the editor gutter to the left of the `message("inside the S7 method")` line to set a breakpoint.
    - A red dot appears in the gutter, so the breakpoint looks like it was accepted.
4. Source the file with <kbd>Ctrl-Shift-S</kbd>.
    - The red dot stays solid rather than turning hollow, again suggesting an active breakpoint.
5. In the Console, run `mean(obj)`.
    - The method body runs: the Console prints "inside the S7 method" and returns `42`.
    - The debugger never stops. The Console stays at the `>` prompt instead of `Browse[1]>`, and the Console Tab Debug toolbar never appears.
    - No error or warning is shown.

### Describe the problem in detail

On R versions before 4.3.0, a breakpoint set inside an S7 method body never fires. This happens consistently. The gutter marker looks like a normal active breakpoint the whole time and nothing reports a failure, so nothing signals that the breakpoint was never really attached. Execution just runs straight through it.

The same steps work correctly on R 4.3.3 and R 4.6.1, so this tracks the R version rather than the platform. It reproduced on Debian 13 (arm64) on R 4.2.3 while passing on Ubuntu 22.04 (x86_64, R 4.3.3) and Rocky 10 (arm64, R 4.6.1).

This also shows up in the automated suite. The test `'breakpoints fire in S7 methods for S3 generics (#16490)'` in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/debugger/debugger_extras.test.ts` failed on two separate certification runs (2026-08-11 and 2026-08-12) with:

    Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed
    Locator:  locator('[role="toolbar"][aria-label="Console Tab Debug"]')
    Expected: visible
    Received: hidden
    Timeout:  20000ms

    at DebuggerActions.waitForDebugMode (e2e/rstudio/actions/debugger.actions.ts:115)

One possible lead: S7's own package documentation notes that before R 4.3.0 the `@` operator only works with S4 objects, and recommends `prop()` instead. `SessionBreakpoints.R` uses `@` on S7 class and generic objects in `.rs.setBreakpointImpl` and `.rs.getUntracedFunctionS7Method`, and both callers wrap those in a `tryCatch` that falls back silently. That hasn't been confirmed under a live R before 4.3.0, so it's a starting point rather than a diagnosis.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Setting a breakpoint inside an S7 method would stop execution when the method is called, the same way it does on R 4.3.0 and later. Failing that, it would ideally be clear that the breakpoint isn't active, rather than showing a normal breakpoint marker that does nothing.

See issue #16490.

title: e2e Windows shard consumes the full job timeout when every RStudio launch fails instead of failing fast
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : built from source at commit 07b27665d27822f1c7a36c609fe00ae81c549f1b
                      (first occurrence) and 6453ef9272bdbc8fff1f8045f873238e3827cec9
                      (second occurrence)
    OS Version      : Windows Server 2025 (GitHub Actions windows-2025 hosted runner)
    R Version       : 4.5.3

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Seen twice on the Windows desktop e2e engine
(`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025.yml`), shard 4 of 4, in CI
rather than through interactive use. The two runs were built from different
commits, so this isn't a single bad build:

- https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31500379312/job/93818357157
- https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31535746560/job/93932162083

1. Run the Windows desktop e2e engine.
    - The sandbox warmup launch and the first several test launches all succeed,
      each reaching `window.rstudio.ready === true` in roughly 4.4 seconds.
2. Partway through the shard a launch stops connecting, and every launch after
   it fails the same way for the remainder of the job.
    - RStudio processes keep being spawned throughout, with new PIDs each time.
      End-of-job cleanup terminates orphaned `rstudio` (PID 8996) and
      `rsession-utf8` (PID 8372) processes.
3. `launchRStudio` retries once (2 attempts, `e2e/rstudio/fixtures/desktop.fixture.ts:344-360`),
   then throws, failing that test's launch.
4. The next test's launch fails identically, and so on until the job ends.
    - 138 `[launch] attempt` failures across roughly 110 minutes, in both runs.
    - No test result is ever recorded: zero passes, zero failures.
5. The no-output watchdog in `e2e/rstudio/scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs` never
   fires.
    - Its idle timer resets on any child output (`resetTimer()` is called from
      both the stdout and stderr handlers, lines 102-103), and each failed retry
      writes a `console.warn`, so a run making no progress still looks alive.
6. The job runs until GitHub's `timeout-minutes: 120` cutoff and is recorded as
   cancelled. Both occurrences ran almost exactly 2 hours.
    - This also holds the workflow's concurrency group. In the first occurrence a
      newer push to the same PR sat queued behind it for about an hour, and an
      explicit `gh run cancel` did not take effect either -- the job only ended
      at the timeout.

The transition, from the second run. Note that healthy launches take 3 seconds
from cleanup to process start, while the one that first fails takes 18:

```
21:30:36  Cleaning up any RStudio on port 9867...
21:30:39  Starting RStudio with CDP on port 9867...
21:30:39  RStudio process started (PID: 7316)
21:30:45  [launch-timing] + 4399ms window.rstudio.ready === true
21:30:54  Cleaning up any RStudio on port 9867...
21:30:57  Starting RStudio with CDP on port 9867...
21:30:57  RStudio process started (PID: 1504)
21:31:03  [launch-timing] + 4395ms window.rstudio.ready === true
21:31:19  Cleaning up any RStudio on port 9867...
21:31:22  Starting RStudio with CDP on port 9867...
21:31:22  RStudio process started (PID: 3816)
21:31:29  [launch-timing] + 4657ms window.rstudio.ready === true
21:32:26  Cleaning up any RStudio on port 9867...
21:32:44  Starting RStudio with CDP on port 9867...
21:32:44  RStudio process started (PID: 9380)
21:33:16  [launch] attempt 1/2 failed: Failed to connect to CDP at http://127.0.0.1:9867 within 30000ms: browserType.connectOverCDP: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.
21:33:16  Cleaning up any RStudio on port 9867...
```

The first failure reports `Timeout 5000ms exceeded`. Every one after it reports
`ECONNREFUSED`, and continues doing so for the rest of the job:

```
21:33:33  RStudio process started (PID: 1160)
21:34:02  RStudio process started (PID: 4708)
21:34:32  [launch] attempt 1/2 failed: Failed to connect to CDP at http://127.0.0.1:9867 within 30000ms: browserType.connectOverCDP: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9867
21:34:49  RStudio process started (PID: 7944)
21:35:38  RStudio process started (PID: 1376)
21:36:08  [launch] attempt 1/2 failed: Failed to connect to CDP at http://127.0.0.1:9867 within 30000ms: browserType.connectOverCDP: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9867
```

and, nearly two hours later, still the same, until the job is cut off:

```
23:22:04  [launch] attempt 1/2 failed: Failed to connect to CDP at http://127.0.0.1:9867 within 30000ms: browserType.connectOverCDP: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9867
23:22:21  Terminate orphan process: pid (8996) (rstudio)
23:22:21  Terminate orphan process: pid (8372) (rsession-utf8)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

Once RStudio stops being reachable over CDP partway through a shard, nothing
detects that every subsequent test is failing for the same reason. The
per-launch retry is correctly bounded at 2 attempts, but there is no
shard-level circuit breaker for "N consecutive launches have failed, stop
trying." The heartbeat watchdog was written for this class of problem and does
work -- it caught a genuinely silent hang in the same batch of runs, reporting
`run-with-heartbeat: no output for 300s -- treating the run as hung and
terminating it` -- but it cannot see this shape, because the retry loop's own
logging keeps its idle timer alive. The result is a shard that occupies a
Windows runner for two hours, produces no test signal at all, and blocks other
queued runs in the same concurrency group.

Noted as an open question rather than a diagnosis: it isn't clear why the port
stops accepting connections. Seven launches on port 9867 succeed and then none
do, while RStudio processes continue to spawn without binding it. That could be
RStudio failing to open its remote-debugging port on a later relaunch, or the
harness's between-launch cleanup (`Cleaning up any RStudio on port 9867...`)
leaving state that prevents rebinding -- the longer 18-second gap on the failing
launch may be a clue. Nothing in the logs distinguishes those, so this report
doesn't assume either, and the request below is only about how the harness
responds.

### Describe the behavior you expected

A shard would ideally give up after a small bounded number of consecutive launch
failures and fail red within a few minutes, so that an environment problem
doesn't cost two hours of a Windows runner, surfaces a clear reason in the
report, and doesn't hold the concurrency group against newer runs.

title: macOS file monitor: bursts of dropped-event warnings and repeated full-project rescans
description:
On macOS, sessions monitoring a large project (e.g. this repository) sporadically log bursts of:

```
WARNING File monitor events were dropped; rescanning /path/to/project; LOGGED FROM: ... MacFileMonitor.cpp:402
```

Each warning corresponds to an FSEvents delivery carrying `kFSEventStreamEventFlagUserDropped` / `kFSEventStreamEventFlagKernelDropped`, i.e. fseventsd's per-client queue overflowed before rsession drained it. The monitor recovers with a full recursive rescan of the project root.

Two mechanisms make this bursty and expensive:

1. The session-side ignore filter (`.git/`, `node_modules/`, gitignored dirs, etc.) is applied client-side, *after* delivery. Every event under the root still transits fseventsd's queue, so heavy churn (builds, git operations, `npm ci`) can overflow it on volume alone.
2. The recovery rescan runs inline in the FSEvents callback. On a large tree it blocks the run loop long enough for the queue to overflow again, so the next delivery also carries the dropped flag and triggers another full rescan -- one overload episode amplifies into several back-to-back rescans.

Proposed fixes:

- Use `FSEventStreamSetExclusionPaths` to suppress events for always-ignored high-churn directories (`.git`, `.Rproj.user`, `node_modules`, ...) at the fseventsd level, reducing queue pressure at the source.
- Debounce the dropped-event recovery rescan: rescan at most once per interval, and coalesce drops arriving inside the interval into a single deferred trailing rescan.
- Raise the FSEvents stream latency (currently 1s) for more temporal coalescing in fseventsd; `kFSEventStreamCreateFlagNoDefer` keeps isolated changes delivered immediately.

title: snippet popup help throws when the completion's snippet is missing for the active mode
description:
Surfaced by the e2e client-exception fixture during the `render quarto document` test on a windows shard of PR #18417's CI run ([job](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30597217542/job/91056404631)):

```
(TypeError) : Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'content')
  at $getSnippetContents (rstudio-0.js)
  at $showPopupHelp (rstudio-0.js)
  at run_84 (rstudio-0.js)   <- deferred/timer callback
```

## Analysis

`SnippetHelper.getSnippetContents` assumes the lookup always succeeds:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/2ed3623506/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/snippets/SnippetHelper.java#L332-L335

but `getSnippetImpl` explicitly returns `null` when the snippet name is not found for the active mode, and `getActiveMode()` is cursor-position dependent. The crashing caller is the completion popup's help timer (`CompletionManagerBase.showPopupHelp` -> `displaySnippetHelp(snippets_.getSnippetContents(completion.name))`): a snippet-type completion is selected, the help timer fires a beat later, and by then the active mode at the cursor no longer offers that snippet -- easiest to hit in a multi-mode Quarto/R Markdown document (markdown/YAML/chunk mode boundaries), which matches the test that tripped it. The result is an uncaught client exception (the "Error" dialog in production).

## Suggested fix

Null-guard the lookup: have `getSnippetContents` return `null` (or empty) when `getSnippetImpl` misses, and have `displaySnippetHelp` / the popup-help path skip rendering snippet help in that case. Low-risk; the popup help is best-effort UI.

title: e2e: shards die with 300s output silence (heartbeat exit 124) in the projects test region
description:
Two shards of the same CI run (30472858712, on PR #18390) were killed by the heartbeat watchdog with the identical signature -- 300 seconds of total output silence -- in the same test neighborhood (the `tests/projects/` serial region), on two different platforms and modes:

## windows / e2e-desktop-windows (4) ([job](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30472858712/job/90647709099))

```
17:25:44  ok 132 [desktop-windows] > tests\projects\project_editor_theme.test.ts:199:7 > ... project without EditorTheme keeps global theme (20.2s)
17:30:44  ##[error]run-with-heartbeat: no output for 300s -- treating the run as hung and terminating it.
```

The hang began inside (or entering) the file's third test, `project_editor_theme.test.ts:255` "project EditorTheme is not applied when project appearance settings are ignored". That test passed on linux-server the same day in ~31s.

## linux-server / e2e-server-ubuntu (2) ([job](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30472858712/job/90647709164))

```
17:28:29  ok 255 [server-linux] > tests/projects/project_editor_theme.test.ts:255:7 > ... (passed)
17:28:48  ok 256 [server-linux] > tests/projects/project_trust_dialog.test.ts:329:7 > No trust dialog when no project is open @server_only @serial (12.3s)
17:29:00  Project created at: /tmp/workdir_45692ac203bb/trust_test_project
17:34:00  ##[error]run-with-heartbeat: no output for 300s -- treating the run as hung and terminating it.
17:34:30  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 124.
```

The `Project created at:` line is `project_trust_dialog.test.ts:364`, inside "Trust dialog appears and \"Don't Trust\" enables restricted mode" (`:358`) -- so `createProjectViaUI` and `getWorkingDir` succeeded, and the wedge is somewhere in the subsequent `writeRprofile` / `restartRExpectingDialog` stretch, before any of the bounded dialog-visibility probes.

## Why this is a runner-level wedge, not a slow test

The suite's per-test timeout is 120s (`playwright.config.ts`). A hang inside a test body produces a Playwright timeout failure -- output -- at 120s, and the run continues. 300s of *zero* output means the worker process wedged hard enough that the reporter emitted nothing: neither shard ever printed a test-timeout failure for the test it died in.

## Notes

- The two hangs are in *different tests* (`project_editor_theme.test.ts:255` on Windows desktop; `project_trust_dialog.test.ts:358` on Linux server). The trust-dialog suite is `@server_only`, so the Windows hang cannot involve that file at all. What they share is the `tests/projects/` serial region, project create/open/restart traffic, and the total-silence failure mode.
- Unrelated to #18390's change on that run: Windows passes a real `PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER` path and Linux Server never sets the variable (its log shows the harness-default library, fully populated, at 17:00).
- The watchdog kill (exit 124) takes the entire remaining shard with it, so a single wedge costs ~35 minutes and every not-yet-run test on the shard.
- Both jobs uploaded their artifacts after the kill, so blob reports/traces from the killed shards should be available on the run for triage.

### Problem Statement

Certification requires a combination of operating systems and versions of R. Individual E2E workflows can be manually dispatched with any version of R. However, the workflow that triggers all environments on command always uses the latest version of R.

This can be tested by dispatching the new workflow against a handful of environments with different R versions specified, then checking that each one actually installed and ran the R version it was asked for rather than always grabbing the latest. No new test framework is needed beyond that -- this is about wiring versions through, not new product behavior.

title: Plots pane not activated when a plot is drawn during a busy R turn
description:
## Summary

When R draws a plot and the same turn stays busy afterwards, the Plots pane is not brought to the front. Two manifestations:

- The `plots-pane-activation.test.ts` e2e guard for #18037 fails consistently on Windows CI (6/6 attempts across two branches on 2026-08-13, e.g. runs [31749798004](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31749798004) and [31727193758](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31727193758)), and flakes on Linux: the assistant draws the plot via `executeCode`, but the pane stays behind Files.
- AI-free repro on any platform: run `plot(1:10); Sys.sleep(2)` in the console with the Files tab selected. The pane is not activated (a bare `plot(1:10)` activates fine).

## Mechanism

`session::http_methods`' polled-event handler runs `module_context::onBackgroundProcessing(false)` every ~50ms while R is executing. `SessionPlots::onBackgroundProcessing` consumes any graphics-device change older than 50ms via `detectChanges(isIdle)` -- with `activatePlots=false` when not idle (by design, to render plot animations incrementally without activating mid-turn).

Consuming the change clears `display().hasChanges()`. So when the turn ends and the REPL change source fires (`SessionConsoleInput`, or `executeCodeImpl`'s `ChangeSourceREPL` from #18052), `detectChanges(true)` sees no changes and does nothing. The activation is lost, not deferred.

Direct evidence from the failing Windows run's Playwright trace: the client received `plots_state_changed` with `plotCount: 1, activatePlots: false` during the assistant turn, and no `activatePlots: true` event ever followed.

The assistant path hits this reliably on Windows because `executeCodeImpl`'s post-plot work (output serialization, boundary hook, JSON-RPC response to the assistant backend) comfortably exceeds the two 50ms gates on a slow CI runner; macOS/Linux usually finish inside the window, which is why the e2e test passes there and only flakes occasionally on Linux.

## Proposed fix

In `SessionPlots`, when busy-time background processing consumes a device change without activation during a console turn or an interactive agent execution (`console_input::executing() || module_context::isAgentExecuting()`), record a pending activation; when the REPL change source fires at end of turn, honor it by re-emitting the plots state with activation requested (still self-gated on `plotCount > 0`). This preserves incremental animation rendering while restoring the end-of-turn activation contract.

title: rsession spins at 100% CPU in an error-logging feedback loop when its original stderr becomes unwritable
description:
### Observed behavior

A (dev-config) rsession was found pinned at ~93% CPU for hours, with the session log rotating continuously. The log was an endless stream of:

```
ERROR system error 5 (Input/output error); OCCURRED AT ... src/cpp/core/system/PosixOutputCapture.cpp:101
```

with entries only microseconds apart. `sample` showed one thread (`standardStreamCaptureThread`) spending nearly all its time in `logError()`, and the main thread burning additional CPU regex-annotating the captured output in `ClientEventQueue::annotateOutput`.

### Diagnosis

`core::system::secureStreamOutput` / output capture redirects the session's stdout/stderr into a pipe, and keeps a `dup()` of the original stderr so output is still echoed to the launching terminal. In `standardStreamCaptureThread` (`PosixOutputCapture.cpp`), the echo path handles write failures like this:

- `EPIPE` / `EBADF`: set a "skip further writes" flag and log once;
- `EAGAIN` / `EINTR`: ignore (transient);
- anything else: `LOG_ERROR` on **every** failed write, and keep trying.

When the terminal (pty) that launched the session goes away, writes to the saved stderr descriptor fail with `EIO` -- which falls into the last bucket. On its own that would merely be noisy, but when a stderr log destination is active (e.g. `log-stderr=1` in the dev config, or stderr logging via logging.conf), each logged error is written to fd 2, which is the *redirected* capture pipe. The capture thread then reads its own error message, tries to echo it to the dead pty, fails with `EIO` again, logs again -- a self-sustaining feedback loop that spins at full speed forever:

1. capture thread reads data from the stderr capture pipe;
2. echo `write()` to the saved (dead) stderr fd fails with `EIO`;
3. `LOG_ERROR` writes the error to all log destinations, including stderr;
4. that write lands in the capture pipe; goto 1.

### Root cause of the EIO

The launching terminal's pty went away while the session kept running (closed terminal tab/window hosting the dev server; the same applies to any parent whose stderr becomes unwritable). On macOS, once the pty master is closed, writes to the slave side fail with `EIO`. `lsof` on the stuck process showed no file descriptors 0-2 at all, consistent with a revoked tty. The bug is not the `EIO` itself -- terminals legitimately die before long-lived sessions -- but that output capture turns this normal event into an infinite loop.

### Proposed fix

Treat any non-transient write error (not just `EPIPE`/`EBADF`) as terminal for the echo: set the skip-write flag and log the error once.

title: windows output capture can log unboundedly when the console echo write fails
description:
Follow-up from the review of #18399, which fixed the Posix instance of this bug (#18398).

`src/cpp/core/system/Win32OutputCapture.cpp` has the same unbounded-logging shape in `standardStreamCaptureThread`, in two places:

- A failed `WriteFile` to the saved `CONOUT$` handle calls `LOG_ERROR` on **every** failure, with no "skip further writes" flag at all (the echo block around lines 62-75). With a stderr log destination active, each logged error is written to the redirected stderr pipe, read back by the stderr capture thread, echoed to the console handle, fails again, and logs again -- the same self-sustaining full-CPU loop fixed for Posix in #18399.
- A `ReadFile` failure is logged inside `while (true)` with no break or backoff (lines 78-83), so a persistent read error would also log unboundedly.

Reachability is lower than on Posix, which is why this was split out rather than fixed in #18399: in Desktop mode there is no console, so `CreateFile("CONOUT$")` fails once at startup and the original-handle argument stays `nullptr` (the caller initializes it that way), disabling the echo path entirely. The exposure is a Windows session with a console attached and `log-stderr=1` -- the only caller passes `options().logStderr()` as `forwardOutputToOriginalDescriptors` -- where the console handle later becomes unwritable.

The fix would mirror #18399: on a persistent echo-write failure, stop echoing and log the error once, and bound the `ReadFile` error logging as well.

title: Posit AI credential gate treats an expired access token as not signed in
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Server and Desktop (the gate runs before either is launched)
    RStudio Version : 2026.08.0-daily+173 (observed during verification of #18348)
    OS Version      : macOS 26.6
    R Version       : 4.6.1
    Assistant       : not captured

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Signed in to Posit AI locally, with `POSIT_EMAIL` and `POSIT_PASSWORD` unset so `auth.setup` takes the copy-the-local-store path. From `e2e/rstudio/`:

1. Confirm the local token store is present and its access token has not yet expired.

        node -e "const d=require(require('os').homedir()+'/.posit/ai/auth/data.json'); const t=d['auth:positai:oauth'].oauthAuth.tokenData.expiresAt; console.log(t, new Date(t) > new Date() ? 'valid' : 'EXPIRED')"

    - Prints a timestamp and `valid`.
2. Run any Posit AI gated test.

        npx playwright test --project=server tests/panes/posit-assistant-chat/open-chat-pane.test.ts

    - The setup copies the store and the test runs.
3. Wait until the access token's expiry passes without using Posit AI in the meantime. The lifetime observed here is one hour.
4. Re-run the same command.
    - The setup reports `[auth-setup] not signed in to Posit AI locally and no credentials set; Posit AI tests will skip`, and every Posit AI test skips.
    - With `PW_AI_AUTH_STRICT=1` the run fails outright: `PW_AI_AUTH_STRICT is set but Posit AI was not provisioned: not signed in to Posit AI locally and POSIT_EMAIL/POSIT_PASSWORD are unset`.
5. Open the IDE and use Posit AI once, so the client refreshes the token, then run the command a third time.
    - The setup copies the store again and the tests run.

### Describe the problem in detail

`isStoreFileAuthenticated` (`e2e/rstudio/utils/auth.ts:94-100`) treats an expired access token as "not signed in":

```
export function isStoreFileAuthenticated(file: string): boolean {
  const data = readAuthStore(file);
  const entry = data?.[AUTH_STORAGE_KEY];
  if (!isAuthEntry(entry)) return false;
  const expiresAt = new Date(entry.oauthAuth.tokenData.expiresAt);
  return !Number.isNaN(expiresAt.getTime()) && expiresAt.getTime() > Date.now();
}
```

The store also carries a `refreshToken`, and the Posit AI client refreshes transparently, so a developer whose access token lapsed an hour ago is still signed in as far as the IDE is concerned. The harness disagrees, and whether Posit AI tests run ends up depending on how recently the assistant was last used rather than on whether credentials exist.

The Copilot gate in the same file defines "signed in" differently. `isCopilotStoreAuthenticated` (`:192`) counts rows in `oauth_tokens` and never looks at expiry, and its comment states the intent plainly: "Mirrors what 'signed in' means for the on-disk store: the agent persists a token row on sign-in and deletes it on sign-out... this checks the store, not the entitlement." By that standard the Posit AI expiry test is the odd one out, and it carries no comment explaining why it is there.

Two consequences. Locally, Posit AI tests skip for a reason that reads as user error ("not signed in to Posit AI locally") when the developer is signed in. In CI with `PW_AI_AUTH_STRICT=1` and the copy path in use, a run fails or passes depending on the age of the token in the seeded store, which is not a property the suite otherwise depends on.

Observed here while verifying #18348: two runs twenty minutes apart, no change in configuration, gave "not signed in" and then a successful copy, purely because the token refreshed in between. Unrelated to the changes on that branch -- this function predates it and is untouched by it.

### Describe the behavior you expected

The two providers would ideally agree on what "signed in" means, checking that a credential is present on disk rather than that it is usable at this instant. For Posit AI that would mean accepting a store whose access token has expired when a `refreshToken` is present, and leaving the refresh to the client, the way the Copilot gate already leaves entitlement to the server.

If the expiry check is deliberate -- for instance if a copied store with a lapsed access token cannot refresh inside the sandbox -- then it would help to say so in a comment, and to give the skip reason wording that distinguishes "your token needs refreshing" from "you are not signed in".

title: Image-based checkmarks ignore Windows contrast themes
description: Follow-up to #18493. ### System details RStudio Edition : Desktop or Server RStudio Version : all current releases up to 2026.08.0 OS Version : Windows-11 R Version : any ### Describe the problem in detail #18493 covered the `` and `` controls, which RStudio restyles in CSS. Those are fixed by handing them back to native rendering when a contrast theme is active. RStudio draws several other check states as `` elements instead, and those are not covered. `ImageResource2x.getSafeHtml()` emits a literal `` (`src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/core/client/resources/ImageResource2x.java:101`), and CSS forced colors mode does not recolor image content. So these keep their authored colors regardless of the active contrast theme. Two distinct problems: **1. Menu checkmarks fail contrast outright.** `menuCheck_2x.png` averages `#172a36` over its opaque pixels. Against the `Canvas` of a black contrast theme that is **1.42:1** — far below the 3:1 minimum for non-text contrast. It is effectively unreadable. There is already an inverted asset (`menuCheckInverted_2x.png`, 20.96:1 against black), but it is selected from RStudio's *own* editor theme, not from the OS contrast theme: ```java // src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/core/client/command/AppCommand.java:479-489 if (RStudioThemes.isEditorDark()) { return isChecked ? new ImageResource2x(ThemeResources.INSTANCE.menuCheckInverted2x()) : null; } else { return isChecked ? new ImageResource2x(ThemeResources.INSTANCE.menuCheck2x()) : null; } ``` So with a light RStudio theme plus a black contrast theme -- the default combination when a user switches contrast on -- the dark asset is chosen and painted on a black background. Call sites: - `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/core/client/command/AppCommand.java:482,487` - `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/core/client/widget/CheckableMenuItem.java:85` - `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/rsconnect/ui/DeploymentMenuItem.java:95` **2. Cell-table tri-state checkboxes ignore the contrast palette.** `TriStateCheckboxCell.render()` picks one of three images (`src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/core/client/cellview/TriStateCheckboxCell.java:118-130`): ```java if (value == null) img = new ImageResource2x(RES.checkboxIndeterminate2x()); else if (value) img = new ImageResource2x(RES.checkboxOn2x()); else img = new ImageResource2x(RES.checkboxOff2x()); ``` These bake in their own light box and blue check, so unlike the menu checkmarks they stay *legible*. But they ignore the contrast theme entirely: a light box with a blue check sits in an otherwise black table, reading as a pasted-on sticker rather than a themed control. Affects the Packages pane, the Git/SVN changelist, and the unsaved-changes dialog. ### Reproduce - start RStudio with a light editor theme - Left Alt+Left Shift+Print Screen to enable contrast themes, choosing one with a black background - open any menu with a checkable item (e.g. **View** > **Panes**) -- the checkmark is not readable - open the **Packages** pane -- the checkbox images keep their light/blue palette ### Expected Both should follow the active contrast theme's foreground colors, as the native checkboxes now do. ### Notes on fixing There is no CSS-only fix here, which is why this was split out. `forced-color-adjust` does not recolor image content, and the `appearance: auto` approach used for #18493 does not apply to an ``. Options: - Render the glyph as a masked element instead of an `` -- `mask-image` plus a `background-color` the UA will force to `CanvasText`. Requires changing the Java that emits the markup, not just CSS. - Keep the `` and swap to the inverted asset when a contrast theme is active, driven by a `forced-colors` media query match rather than by `RStudioThemes.isEditorDark()`. Simpler, but only covers the black-background contrast themes -- Desert has a tan `Canvas` where the inverted asset would then fail. The first option is the one that generalizes to any contrast theme. Note for whoever picks this up: a bare `@media (forced-colors: active)` block in a `CssResource` stylesheet is **silently dropped**. GWT's legacy CSS parser is a CSS2 parser that accepts media types only; it logs a warning and the build still succeeds. See the comment added above the `@supports` block in `themeStyles.css` by the #18493 fix for the workaround.

title: e2e: scheduled rotation tests a stale daily because /rstudio/latest/index.json lags the branch rollover
description:
## Summary

The scheduled e2e rotation runs the tests from `main` against a daily build from the
`rel-yellow-yarrow` (2026.08) branch. Any test that asserts behavior added to `main`
after the 2026.08 branch cut fails on every platform, because the binary under test
does not contain the code.

This is not a test defect and not flake. The tests are correct and the product is
correct. Only the pairing is wrong.

## Symptom

Scheduled runs [31303035336](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31303035336)
(2026-08-09) and [31371013310](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31371013310)
(2026-08-10) failed the same tests on Ubuntu 24, Rocky 9, Rocky 10, Ubuntu 26,
macOS 14, macOS 15, macOS 26, and Windows Server 2025:

- `tests/panes/layout/panes.test.ts` -- 8 of the 9 tests added by #18454
- `tests/panes/editor/cpp_chunk_indent.test.ts` -- the test added by #18470

A representative failure:

```
panes/layout/panes.test.ts:760 › Restoring a zoomed pane from its header button ends the zoom (#18444)

Error: zoom bookkeeping should be cleared after escaping the zoom
Expected: false
Received: true
```

That is exactly the pre-#18454 behavior. The pane header button restored the vertical
split through `DualWindowLayoutPanel` but left `PaneManager.maximizedTab_` set.
`hookPaneMaximize` (`src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/ui/PaneManager.java:1344`)
is the code that routes the gesture through `restoreLayout()`, and it is absent from
the build under test.

The failure set confirms the diagnosis. #18454 added 9 tests, 8 fail, and the only
one that passes -- `'The pane header button still maximizes when nothing is zoomed'`
-- is the one that asserts behavior which predates the fix.

## Root cause

The rotation installs the build named by `https://dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/latest/index.json`.
That JSON object is stale. The HTML page at the same path is not:

| URL | `last-modified` | Serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/rstudio/latest/` (page) | Mon, 10 Aug 2026 19:36 GMT | Autumn Hawkbit, `2026.09.0-daily+11` |
| `/rstudio/latest/index.json` | **Sat, 08 Aug 2026 05:33 GMT** | Yellow Yarrow, `2026.08.0-daily+186` |
| `/rstudio/autumn-hawkbit/index.json` | Mon, 10 Aug 2026 18:32 GMT | Autumn Hawkbit, `2026.09.0-daily+11` |

So the `latest` alias rolled over to `main` for browsers but not for the JSON manifest
that CI consumes. The per-branch manifest is current and correct.

Commit check:

```
build installed by the rotation:  2026.08.0-daily+186  -> 0731c0d19d / a249c8fa0c (rel-yellow-yarrow)
build the page advertises:        2026.09.0-daily+11   -> 2f648f3a0d (main)

8b3b385e55 (#18454, pane zoom)         NOT in a249c8fa0c   IS in 2f648f3a0d
7ed4e560a0 (#18470, cpp chunk indent)  NOT in a249c8fa0c   IS in 2f648f3a0d
```

Reproduce:

```bash
curl -sSI https://dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/latest/index.json | grep -i last-modified
curl -fsSL https://dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/latest/index.json          | jq -r '.branch, .version'
curl -fsSL https://dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/autumn-hawkbit/index.json  | jq -r '.branch, .version'
```

## Why PR runs are unaffected

`os-test-e2e-rstudio-pr.yml` already guards against this. Its `decide()` function
requires the daily's commit to contain the PR's merge base, and falls back to a source
build when it does not. #18454 and #18470 both touched `src/`, so both built from
source and went green. The guard fails closed, which is why the problem only shows up
in the rotation.

`os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml` has no equivalent check. It installs whatever
`latest/index.json` names and runs `main`'s tests against it.

## Blast radius

Nine workflows read the stale manifest:

```
.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-linux.yml
.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-autocomplete-scheduled-windows-server-2025.yml
.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-14-arm64.yml
.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-15-x86_64.yml
.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-26-arm64.yml
.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025.yml
.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-pr.yml
.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml
.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-server-os-ubuntu-24.yml
```

The Windows one uses PowerShell (`Invoke-RestMethod`); the rest use `curl` + `jq`.

## Potential fixes

### 1. Resolve the manifest per branch (recommended)

Derive the manifest path from `version/RELEASE`, which is already in the workspace by
the time the installer is resolved. Lowercase it and replace the space with a hyphen:
`Autumn Hawkbit` -> `autumn-hawkbit`, `Yellow Yarrow` -> `yellow-yarrow`. Both paths
exist and both are current.

```bash
BRANCH_SLUG=$(tr 'A-Z ' 'a-z-' < version/RELEASE)
MANIFEST_URL="https://dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/${BRANCH_SLUG}/index.json"
if ! MANIFEST=$(curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 "$MANIFEST_URL"); then
  echo "::error::No daily manifest for branch '$BRANCH_SLUG' at $MANIFEST_URL."
  exit 1
fi
```

This stops depending on the `latest` alias, so a stale alias cannot mis-pair the build
again. It also pairs a release-branch PR with that branch's daily, and it removes the
needless source builds the PR workflow does today whenever `latest` lags.

Cost: nine files, one of them PowerShell. Worth factoring the resolution into a single
composite action in the same change.

### 2. Add the merge-base staleness guard to the rotation

Port `decide()` from `os-test-e2e-rstudio-pr.yml` into
`os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml`, so a daily that does not contain `main`'s HEAD
triggers a source build.

Correct, and it makes the rotation self-defending against any future skew. But while
the manifest is stale it would build every engine from source -- more than ten of
them -- which is a large cost for a rotation whose stated purpose is to test the
shipped daily.

Best used together with option 1, as a backstop rather than the primary fix.

### 3. Fix the publisher

`/rstudio/latest/index.json` should be regenerated whenever `/rstudio/latest/` is.
This needs whoever owns the dailies site, so it is not fixable in this repo. Even
after it is fixed, option 1 is still worth doing: a consumer that names its own branch
cannot be mis-pointed by an alias.

### Not recommended: skip or version-gate the tests

Adding `test.skip` or a version guard to the affected specs would turn a build-pairing
problem into permanently disabled coverage, and would hide the next occurrence.

## Suggested order

1. Report the stale `index.json` to the dailies owners (option 3).
2. Land option 1 so CI stops depending on `latest`.
3. Land option 2 as a backstop.

title: Editor breakpoints in S7 methods ignored
description: ### System details RStudio Edition : Desktop RStudio Version : 2025.09.0+387 OS Version : macOS Tahoe 26.0, aarch64, darwin20 R Version : R version 4.5.1 (2025-06-13) ``` version R version 4.5.1 (2025-06-13) os macOS Tahoe 26.0 system aarch64, darwin20 ui RStudio language (EN) collate en_US.UTF-8 ctype en_US.UTF-8 tz Europe/Berlin date 2025-09-27 rstudio 2025.09.0+387 Cucumberleaf Sunflower (desktop) pandoc 2.9.2 @ /usr/local/bin/pandoc quarto 1.7.33 @ /usr/local/bin/quarto ``` ### Steps to reproduce the problem - Save the below code lines in a script outside of an R package project - Set editor breakpoint in S7 method - Save and source the file - Run the lines inside the `if (FALSE)` block. It's in the if block to avoid auto run of the code when the file is sourced. ```r S7::method(mean, S7::new_class("s7mean")) <- function(x, ...){ print("This is my S7 method") } if (FALSE){ x <- 1:4 mean(x) class(x) <- "s7mean" mean(x) } ``` ### Describe the problem in detail #### Before Sourcing Here is how the IDE displays the breakpoint inside the S7 method before sourcing. This looks fine, it tells me to source the file. #### After Sourcing Here is the IDE after I clicked "source". The breakpoint is gone and it's unclear whether it is set or not. Additionally I see the warning ``` Breakpoints can only be set inside the body of a function. ``` which suggests that RStudio doesn't recognize the S7 method as function. Running the code inside the if block results in ```r x <- 1:4 mean(x) #> [1] 2.5 class(x) <- "s7mean" mean(x) #> [1] "This is my S7 method" ``` So the breakpoint wasn't set and the only way for me to solve this is to use `browser()`. ### Describe the behavior you expected I am looking to set editor breakpoints inside S7 methods. - [x] I have read the guide for [submitting good bug reports](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Writing-Good-Bug-Reports). - [x] I have installed the latest version of RStudio, and confirmed that the issue still persists. - [x] If I am reporting an RStudio crash, I have included a [diagnostics report](https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/articles/200321257-Running-a-Diagnostics-Report). - [x] I have done my best to include a minimal, self-contained set of instructions for consistently reproducing the issue.

title: E2E harness logs into RStudio Server twice per external run and can trip the sign-in throttle
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Server
    RStudio Version : 2026.08.0-daily+173
    OS Version      : Fedora 44 via Google Chrome on macOS 26
    R Version       : 4.6.1

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Using the Playwright e2e suite (`e2e/rstudio/`) against a real, persistent
RStudio Server account reached by URL (`PW_RSTUDIO_SERVER_URL`), e.g. a
dedicated test VM:

1. Run any server-mode Playwright test against the external server
   (`npm run test:server` with `PW_RSTUDIO_SERVER_URL` set, or an
   equivalent CI run).
    - The suite's setup project first logs into the account to provision AI
      credentials (`tests/auth.setup.ts` -> "provision external server
      credentials", which calls into `utils/remote-provision.ts`).
    - Moments later, the test's own fixture logs into the same account
      again (`fixtures/server.fixture.ts`, `signInToServer`), to run the
      test itself.
2. If the two logins land within `auth-sign-in-throttle-seconds` (default
   5, `src/cpp/server/server-options.json`) of each other, the second
   sign-in is rejected.
    - The client sees a generic "Temporary server error, please try again"
      page. This message alone doesn't distinguish a throttle rejection
      from a decrypt failure--both render as the same `kErrorServer` code.
    - The server's own log shows the real cause: "Too many attempts within
      5 seconds for '<user>'" (`isUserSignInThrottled`,
      `src/cpp/server/auth/ServerAuthHandler.cpp:1214-1240`).
    - After roughly 30-60 seconds the throttle window passes and a retry
      succeeds.
3. Separately, if two independent Playwright invocations happen to run
   against the same account at overlapping times, a related symptom
   appears: an already-connected browser gets an "R Session Disconnected...
   because another browser connected" dialog, since RStudio Server allows
   only one active browser connection per rsession.

### Describe the problem in detail

The harness always performs two separate logins per external-server run
against the same account, seconds apart: one to provision AI credentials,
one for the actual test session. This works most of the time, but races the
account's own login throttle and its one-connection-per-session limit.
It's shown up both as an outright login failure (the throttle) and, when
two runs overlap, as a live session getting kicked.

CI's own linux-server engine performs the identical two-login sequence
(against an rserver instance it spins up itself, also reached by URL) but
hasn't been observed to hit the throttle. Why CI doesn't reproduce this
despite the same code path isn't understood yet.

### Describe the behavior you expected

The harness shouldn't need two separate logins to the same account in
quick succession, or if it does, shouldn't race the server's own
throttle and connection limits.

### Possible approaches

1. Add a short sleep (roughly 6 seconds, comfortably past the 5-second
   throttle window) at the end of `closeExternalSession()` in
   `utils/remote-provision.ts`, after credentials are pushed and before the
   browser closes. Cheapest option, a few lines. Costs a few seconds on
   every external-server run. Doesn't help if two separate Playwright
   invocations hit the account at the same time.
2. Add an equivalent short sleep in `fixtures/server.fixture.ts`, right
   before `signInToServer()`, gated on `isExternalServerRun()`. Same cost
   and same limitation as option 1--two workers or two separate runs
   starting close together would still collide with each other.
3. Remove the double login altogether--have provisioning hand its
   already-authenticated session over to the fixture, or otherwise share
   one login for both purposes, instead of logging in twice. More involved
   than the other two, but the only option that removes the race instead of
   spacing it out.

Also worth a look: on a dedicated test VM (not a shared or production
server), setting `auth-sign-in-throttle-seconds=0` in `rserver.conf` and
restarting the service sidesteps the issue for that one machine. That's a
config change to a specific server, not a fix to the harness, so it
wouldn't help CI's ephemeral servers or anyone else's VM--but there's
precedent for this kind of test-only config override in this repo: CI's own
runners carry a systemd drop-in enabling `--automation-agent`, explicitly
commented as "ephemeral, do NOT enable in production."

description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop and Server
    RStudio Version : dev (main), present since 2026.04.0
    OS Version      : any
    R Version       : any (version-independent)

### Steps to reproduce the problem

With the S7 package installed:

1. Create a new R script with this content:

```r
library(S7)

s7class <- new_class("s7class")
s7generic <- new_generic("s7generic", "x")

method(s7generic, s7class) <- function(x, ...) {
  message("inside the method")
  42
}

obj <- s7class()
```

2. Save the file, then click in the editor gutter next to the `message("inside the method")` line to set a breakpoint. A red dot appears.
3. Source the file with Ctrl-Shift-S. The dot stays solid, suggesting an active breakpoint.
4. In the Console, run `s7generic(obj)`.

The method body runs to completion and the debugger never stops. No error or warning is shown.

This is the sibling of #18526, but for methods registered on *S7 generics* (`new_generic()`) rather than S7 methods for S3 generics (e.g. `mean`), and unlike #18526 it reproduces on every R version, including current ones. The original S7 breakpoint support in #16490 / PR #16742 wired up this dispatch path (`.rs.setBreakpointImpl`'s `S7_generic` branch), but its automated test only covers the S3-generic path, so this was never caught.

### Root cause

`.rs.setBreakpointImpl` correctly locates the method in the generic's methods environment and calls `.rs.setFunctionBreakpoints`, but the `trace()` call inside fails:

```
Error in !is.null(prototype) && is.na(match(name, .BasicClasses)) :
  'length = 3' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
```

The stored method has class `c("S7_method", "function", "S7_object")`, and the methods package cannot derive a trace class from a length-3 class vector (`.TraceWithMethods` / `.makeTracedFunction`). The error is swallowed by the `tryCatch` in `.rs.setBreakpoint`, so the breakpoint is silently dropped -- the same silent-failure mode as #18526.

Stripping the class from the stored method before tracing (and restoring it when the breakpoint is cleared) makes the standard trace machinery work: S7 dispatch calls the traced function, the breakpoint fires, and `untrace()` plus class restoration returns the method to its original state.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Setting a breakpoint inside a method registered on an S7 generic stops execution when the generic dispatches to it, the same way breakpoints in S7 methods for S3 generics do after #18526.

title: Posit Assistant: chat backend permanently reports "update is in progress" after an R session restart
description:
### Symptom

After an R session restart, starting the Posit Assistant chat backend can fail indefinitely with:

> A Posit Assistant update is in progress. Please try again in a moment.

even though no update is running. Retrying never helps; the chat pane just never becomes ready. The same underlying condition also produces the "R Session Error" / "previous R session terminated abnormally" dialog after the restart.

Observed on the e2e server shard in [run 31839732347](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31839732347/job/94897988955?pr=18568) (`chat-user-skills.test.ts` beforeAll failure), but the mechanism is a product bug any server user can hit by restarting R while the assistant is active.

### Root cause

`installLock()` in `SessionChat.cpp` names this session's in-use lock file (`pai/locks/sessions/<ownerId>.lock`) with `module_context::activeSession().id()`. That id is **stable across R session restarts**, so the replacement rsession process uses the *same lock file name* as its predecessor.

`ChatInstallLock.hpp` documents the actual requirement: "ownerId: unique per rsession process."

Normally the predecessor exits and releases the lock before the replacement starts the backend. But when the predecessor process outlives the restart (the restart-with-live-agent wedge family, see #18394), it keeps holding and heartbeating the link-based lock, so it is never stale. The replacement then can never acquire "its own" lock:

- `chat_start_backend` fails with `system error 37 (No locks available)` on `pai/locks/sessions/<session-id>.lock`, which `acquireInUseForStart()` classifies as retryable contention and reports as "A Posit Assistant update is in progress".
- The same leaked process holds the project source-database lock, so the replacement's `attachToSourceDatabase()` fails and logs "The previous R session terminated abnormally", raising the modal "R Session Error" dialog.

In the CI run above, the leaked predecessor (pid 9716) was still alive and logging assistant-agent output 13 minutes after its replacement started; three successive replacement rsessions (pids 9722, 10030, 10143) all failed `chat_start_backend` on the same lock file over a 2+ minute span.

### Fix

Make the InstallLock ownerId unique per process, as the header already requires -- e.g. `<session-id>-<uuid>` (keeping the session id prefix for attributability). Concurrent in-use holders are already a supported steady state (one lock file per owner), so a replacement coexisting briefly with its leaked predecessor is safe: mutation (update/uninstall) still correctly refuses while either holder lives, and leftover files from dead processes are stale-cleaned by the next mutator.

The leaked-rsession wedge itself is tracked separately (#18394 family); this issue covers the lock collision that turns a transient leak into a permanent assistant outage.

title: Backport #18515 to Yellow Yarrow 2026.08.1
description:
Backport #18515 to Yellow Yarrow 2026.08.1.

Fixed in Autumn Hawkbit by #18519 (`9e0e8e998bbb489a997bf35e400389509381758a`), which restores
the `install(DIRECTORY)` rule in `src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt` that collects the 32-bit
sub-build's output (`<build>/src/cpp/session/x86`) into the staged app tree, plus the
`file(MAKE_DIRECTORY)` call that keeps non-multiarch builds working.

Yellow Yarrow is affected: `src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt` on `rel-yellow-yarrow` has no rule
installing the session `x86` directory -- it was deleted with the winpty block in 04db3f557da
(#17814). Multiarch Windows Desktop builds there build, install and code-sign the 32-bit
session, but `resources/app/bin/x86` ships without `rsession.exe` or `rsession.dll`, so with a
32-bit R the desktop falls back to the 64-bit session and cannot load a 32-bit `R.dll`.

Verification needs a multiarch Windows package build
(`make-package.bat clean electron multiarch`): confirm the 32-bit session binaries are present
in `resources/app/bin/x86` after install, and that a session against a 32-bit R starts.

Ordering note: #18557 (backport of #18512) adds the x86 `rsession.dll` to the Windows sign
list. The two are independent, but this issue is what makes those signed x86 binaries actually
reach the installer.

**Note: This issue is to record the need to backport the linked issue only. Please add comments or discussion relating to the original issue onto it directly.**

title: Backport #18512 to Yellow Yarrow 2026.08.1
