title: Split up scheduled weekend E2E runs grouped by architecture
description:
### Problem Statement

A bunch of new E2E environments in GitHub Actions workflows were created since the initial schedule was created. The schedule was modified here and there, but with the inclusion of a bunch of Linux environments as part of #18410, we now have 21 environments. For a full weekend run, 21 in one run is undesirable.

### Proposed Behaviour

Create two schedules, one for all x86 environments and a second for all ARM. These will be staggered, at 8:00 and 14:00 UTC.

### Testing

This can be tested by pulling the engine-picking logic out of the workflow and running it against every trigger (weekday, both Sunday runs, Friday, manual dispatch), checking that the two Sunday runs together cover all 21 engines with nothing missing or duplicated, and that the weekday schedule doesn't change. actionlint should also pass on the updated file. No new automated test is needed since this is scheduling logic, not something that changes how RStudio behaves.

title: Harden Playwright renameConversation helper to assert the rename took effect
Windows: rsession.dll is not code-signed
description:
## Problem

The Windows Desktop build ships `rsession.dll` unsigned. It is the only shipped session
binary that DigiCert signing skips.

The `Sign Executables` stage in `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows` signs seven binaries:

```
package\win32\build\src\cpp\session\rsession-utf8.exe
package\win32\build\src\cpp\session\rsession.exe
package\win32\build\src\cpp\session\x86\rsession.exe
package\win32\build\src\cpp\session\consoleio\consoleio.exe
package\win32\build\src\cpp\session\postback\rpostback.exe
package\win32\build\src\cpp\diagnostics\diagnostics.exe
src\node\desktop-build-AMD64\out\RStudio-win32-x64\rstudio.exe
```

`rsession.dll` is not in that list, but it is installed into the same directory as the
launcher stubs (`src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt`, `install(TARGETS rsession-shared ...)`)
and so ends up in the installer. Multiarch builds produce two copies, one per
architecture:

- `package\win32\build\src\cpp\session\rsession.dll` (x64)
- `package\win32\build\src\cpp\session\x86\rsession.dll` (x86, `RSTUDIO_INSTALL_BIN` is
  `x86` for `RSTUDIO_SESSION_WIN32`)

## How this happened

#18070 (`cc8959d7dd`, 2026-06-25) moved the bulk of the session code out of
`rsession.exe` and `rsession-utf8.exe`, which each statically linked their own copy, into
a single shared library. The two executables became thin launcher stubs that forward to
`rsessionMain()` in the DLL. The signing list in `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows` was not
updated to match, so code that was previously covered by the signatures on the two
executables is now in an unsigned module.

## Impact

The signed `rsession.exe` / `rsession-utf8.exe` stubs load an unsigned DLL that contains
essentially all of the session implementation. Policies that verify loaded modules rather
than just the launching image -- WDAC, AppLocker publisher rules, and some EDR
configurations -- can block or flag it, and the signature coverage of a shipped install no
longer matches what it was before #18070.

## Fix

Add both DLL paths to `%EXECUTABLES%` in the `Sign Executables` stage of
`jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows`. Signing runs before the `Package` stage, so the signed DLLs
get picked up by the installer with no further reordering.

Note that only `rsession.dll` is covered here; other DLLs in the shipped tree, including
those from the Electron distribution, were not audited.

title: Windows: 32-bit (multiarch) session binaries are missing from the installer
description:
## Problem

Multiarch Windows Desktop builds build, install and code-sign the 32-bit session, then
drop it before packaging. In the shipped installer, `resources/app/bin/x86` contains only
the x86 VC runtime DLLs installed by `src/node/desktop/CMakeLists.txt:320` -- no
`rsession.exe`, and (since #18070) no `rsession.dll`.

Evidence from a local multiarch package build:

- `package\win32\build\src\cpp\session\x86\` -- `rsession.exe`, `rsession.dll`
- `<CPack staging>\resources\app\bin\x86\` -- 9 VC runtime DLLs, no session binaries
  (same in both the `NSIS` and `ZIP` staging trees)

## How this happened

`04db3f557da` (#17814, 2026-06-02, "Migrate the Windows terminal backend from winpty to
ConPTY") deleted the whole `if(WIN32)` block under `# install winpty on windows` in
`src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt`. Four of the six install rules in that block were
winpty's; the other two were not. The rule that collected the 32-bit session went with it
(`v2026.05.1+225:src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt:856-860`):

```cmake
      # install 32 bit binaries
      file(MAKE_DIRECTORY  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/x86")
      install(DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/x86"
              USE_SOURCE_PERMISSIONS
              DESTINATION  ${RSTUDIO_INSTALL_BIN})
```

`git log -S'install 32 bit binaries' -- src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt` returns exactly two
commits: `e505193f677` (2019) added the rule, `04db3f557da` removed it.

## Mechanism

The 32-bit sub-build has always installed into the 64-bit *build* tree; the 64-bit build
then had an install rule that scooped that directory into the staged app tree at package
time.

- `package/win32/make-package.bat:242-247` runs the 32-bit sub-build after the 64-bit
  build, via `make-install-win32.bat "%BUILD_DIR%\src\cpp\session"`.
- `package/win32/make-install-win32.bat:55-66` configures `build32` with that path as
  `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX` and `RSTUDIO_TARGET=SessionWin32`. `RSTUDIO_ELECTRON` is false for
  that target, so `RSTUDIO_INSTALL_BIN` is plain `x86` (`cmake/globals.cmake:521-525`),
  giving `build/src/cpp/session/x86/`.
- In the 64-bit Electron build, `RSTUDIO_INSTALL_BIN` is `resources/app/bin`
  (`cmake/globals.cmake:512-517`) and the session project's `CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR` is
  `build/src/cpp/session`, so the deleted rule copied that directory to
  `resources/app/bin/x86`. `install(DIRECTORY)` without a trailing slash installs the
  directory itself, hence the `/x86` suffix. CPack re-runs install rules at packaging
  time -- after the sub-build -- so the directory was populated by then.

Nothing replaced the rule, and no other rule in the tree collects that directory.

## Impact

`src/node/desktop/src/main/session-launcher.ts:654-663` is the only consumer:

```ts
      const arch = getenv('R_ARCH');
      if (arch === 'i386') {
        const x86SessionPath = this.sessionPath.getParent().completeChildPath('x86/rsession.exe');
        if (x86SessionPath.existsSync()) {
          this.sessionPath = x86SessionPath;
          ...
        } else {
          logger().logWarning('R is 32-bit, but no 32-bit rsession.exe was found');
        }
      }
```

`R_ARCH` comes from `.Platform$r_arch`, queried out of R itself
(`src/node/desktop/src/main/detect-r.ts:75`), so this is auto-detected, not gated on a
preference -- `platform.windows.useDefault32BitR` and the Choose R dialog only select which
R. With a 32-bit R, the lookup fails, a warning is logged, and the launcher falls through
to the 64-bit `rsession.exe`, which cannot load a 32-bit `R.dll`; the user should get the
generic "R session had a fatal error" dialog with nothing naming the real cause. That last
step is inferred from the code path and has not been reproduced against a built installer.

Affected releases (verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; #18070 split the session
into `rsession.dll` plus launcher stubs from 2026.07 onward):

| Release | Missing payload |
| --- | --- |
| `v2026.05.1+225` and earlier | -- (working) |
| `v2026.06.0+242` | `rsession.exe` |
| `v2026.07.0+139`, `v2026.07.1+147`, current `main` | `rsession.exe` + `rsession.dll` |

Two related things are dead while this is broken: `src/cpp/session/SessionOptions.cpp:123-128`,
which strips a trailing `x86` component from the resource path for the 32-bit session; and
the `x86\rsession.exe` entry in the `Sign Executables` stage of `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows`
(plus `x86\rsession.dll` once #18512 lands), which signs files that never ship.

## Fix

Restore the collection rule in `src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt`, at roughly line 911 --
immediately before the `# install libclang` block -- inside the existing
`if(NOT RSTUDIO_SESSION_WIN32 AND NOT RSESSION_ALTERNATE_BUILD)` guard opened at line 739:

```cmake
   # collect the 32-bit session binaries produced by the multiarch sub-build, which
   # package/win32/make-install-win32.bat installs into <build>/src/cpp/session/x86
   if(WIN32)
      file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/x86")
      install(DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/x86"
              USE_SOURCE_PERMISSIONS
              DESTINATION "${RSTUDIO_INSTALL_BIN}")
   endif()
```

Keep the comment tying the rule to `make-install-win32.bat`: the rule was lost precisely
because it sat under a `# install winpty on windows` comment with nothing indicating it
was unrelated to winpty.

`file(MAKE_DIRECTORY)` is load-bearing, not vestigial. `install(DIRECTORY)` errors on a
missing source directory, so without it every non-multiarch Windows build fails at install
-- and `MULTIARCH` defaults to 1 only on Jenkins (`package/win32/make-package.bat:43-48`),
so local builds are the common case.

Prefer this over repointing the sub-build's install prefix at the staged app tree. That
tree is CPack-owned and only exists during packaging, and signing runs against the build
tree between the sub-build and CPack (`jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows`), so the payload has to
be collected at package time for signed binaries to ship.

Verification for the fix:

- multiarch package build (`make-package.bat clean electron multiarch`): `rsession.exe` and
  `rsession.dll` present in `<staging>\resources\app\bin\x86`
- non-multiarch build: still configures and installs cleanly, with an empty `x86` directory
- ideally, a smoke test with a 32-bit R selected, confirming the session starts

Needs a `NEWS.md` entry under `### Fixed` (the regression shipped in 2026.06.0, so it has
reached official-release users).

title: Pin panmirror to a named branch and drop the GitHub API cache-bust from the Dockerfiles
description:
## Problem

Every Jenkins builder Dockerfile carries a GitHub API cache-bust ahead of the panmirror install:

```dockerfile
# panmirror check for changes
ADD https://api.github.com/repos/quarto-dev/quarto/git/refs/heads/main panmirror.version.json
# ADD https://api.github.com/repos/quarto-dev/quarto/git/refs/heads/release/rstudio-autumn-hawkbit panmirror.version.json
```

Two problems with it:

1. **It gets rate-limited, which fails image builds.** Unauthenticated `api.github.com` allows 60 requests/hour per IP. There are 7 of these `ADD`s in rstudio and 8 in rstudio-pro, each hit on every image build, all from shared CI egress. When the limit is hit the `ADD` fails and the build dies.
2. **The branch name is encoded in ~15 places.** Each release cycle it is toggled by hand: unpinned to `main` at the start, pinned to a release branch as release approaches. Per repo that means 7-8 Dockerfiles (active `ADD` plus commented-out variant) plus two clone lines, two checkout lines, and two "keep this in sync" comments across the two install scripts.

panmirror changes rarely, so tracking `main` and re-detecting every upstream commit is more machinery than the situation needs.

## Why the ADD exists today

Worth understanding before changing anything, so it doesn't get restored later.

panmirror is baked into the builder image, and the build consumes the baked copy rather than cloning at build time. `src/gwt/build.xml:281-284` resolves `panmirror.dir` with `set-if-exists`, trying `/opt/rstudio-tools/src/gwt/lib/quarto/apps/panmirror` first; Ant properties are write-once, so on a builder the image copy wins. The `ADD` is what forces the image to re-bake when the tracked branch tip moves. Nothing reads `panmirror.version.json` — it is only a Docker cache key.

## Proposed change

Always fetch panmirror from an explicitly named branch of the quarto repo, and drop the `ADD` entirely.

- At the start of a release cycle, create a branch in `quarto-dev/quarto` off `main`, e.g. `release/rstudio-autumn-hawkbit`, and set the install scripts to use it.
- To update panmirror mid-cycle, create a **new** branch with the fixes, e.g. `release/rstudio-autumn-hawkbit-01`, and point the scripts at it.

Changing the branch name in a script is itself the cache-bust: in every Linux Dockerfile `COPY dependencies/common/` precedes `RUN ... install-common` (e.g. `Dockerfile.jammy:129` then `:136`), and on Windows the `COPY dependencies/common` and `COPY dependencies/windows` lines precede `RUN install-dependencies.cmd`. Editing a copied script invalidates that layer and forces the re-clone. This is the same mechanism the pinned Quarto version already relies on.

Switching an existing clone to a new branch already works: `dependencies/common/install-panmirror:46-54` does `git fetch` -> `git reset --hard` -> `git clean -dfx` -> `git checkout <branch>` -> `git pull`, and `clone-panmirror-repo.cmd:23-29` mirrors it. No new logic is needed there.

### The rule this depends on

**A branch that the scripts reference must be treated as immutable.** With the `ADD` gone, nothing detects the branch tip moving. If commits are pushed to an already-referenced branch, builder images cached before the push keep the old panmirror while freshly built ones get the new code, and the divergence is silent. That is why mid-cycle changes get a new suffixed branch instead of a push to the existing one. This rule should be stated in the script comment that replaces the current "keep in sync" note.

## Files to change

**rstudio**

- `dependencies/common/install-panmirror` — add a `PANMIRROR_BRANCH="release/rstudio-autumn-hawkbit"` variable near the top; use it in the clone (`:38`) and the checkout (`:49`); delete the commented-out branch variants at `:39` and `:50`; replace the "IMPORTANT: When changing which branch this pulls from below, also update the Dockerfiles..." comment at `:32-33` with a note describing the branch-per-cycle convention and the immutability rule.
- `dependencies/windows/install-panmirror/clone-panmirror-repo.cmd` — same treatment: `set PANMIRROR_BRANCH=release/rstudio-autumn-hawkbit`, use it in the clone (`:15`) and checkout (`:24`), delete the commented variants at `:16` and `:25`, replace the sync comment at `:11-12`.
- Remove the three-line panmirror block (comment, active `ADD`, commented `ADD`) from each of: `Dockerfile.bionic:107-109`, `Dockerfile.focal:113-115`, `Dockerfile.jammy:131-133`, `Dockerfile.opensuse15:96-98`, `Dockerfile.rhel8:100-102`, `Dockerfile.rhel9:103-105`, `Dockerfile.windows:144-146` (all under `docker/jenkins/`).

**rstudio-pro** (the two scripts are identical across repos and arrive via the upstream merge, so only the Dockerfiles need touching here)

- Remove the same block from `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.{bionic,focal,jammy,opensuse15,rhel8,rhel9,windows}` and from `Dockerfile.rhel10`, which has no rstudio counterpart and will not be covered by the merge.

## Implementation notes

- **Do not put the branch name in a new shared file** without also updating `.dockerignore`. The rstudio `.dockerignore` is deny-all-then-allowlist and only admits `dependencies/common/install-*`, `dependencies/common/lockfiles`, and `dependencies/common/patch-node*`. A new file there would be silently excluded from the build context — not copied into the image, and not busting the cache. rstudio-pro has `!dependencies`, so it would work there and fail only in rstudio. Keeping the value inside the two existing install scripts avoids this entirely; both are already in the build context.
- **Fail loudly if the branch does not exist.** `git clone --branch` and `git checkout` both fail under `set -e`, but the raw git error is not obvious. A short explicit check with a message naming the missing branch and the convention will save someone a confused half hour. Do not fall back to `main` — that would silently ship the wrong panmirror.
- Local and macOS developer builds are unaffected: with no `/opt/rstudio-tools` present, `set-if-exists` falls through to `./lib/quarto/apps/panmirror` in the checkout.
- No `NEWS.md` entry — build tooling only.
- Leave the pinned-Quarto handling alone; it is unrelated and already fetches from the `rstudio-buildtools` mirror.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `api.github.com` reference remains in `docker/jenkins/` in either repo.
- `grep -rn 'quarto-dev/quarto' dependencies/` shows the branch named exactly once per script, via the variable.
- A Linux builder image and the Windows builder image both build, and `/opt/rstudio-tools/src/gwt/lib/quarto` (resp. `c:/rstudio-tools/...`) is on the expected branch afterwards — confirm with `git -C <path> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`.
- Changing `PANMIRROR_BRANCH` and rebuilding re-clones panmirror rather than reusing the cached layer.
- The release-cycle convention (create branch off `main`; new suffixed branch for mid-cycle fixes; never push to a referenced branch) is written down in both scripts.

title: Branch and pin panmirror to 2026.09 release branch near end of development
description:
Follow-up to #18411 (the 2026.09 unpin).

Near the end of `2026.09 (Autumn Hawkbit)` development, we need to re-pin panmirror (Visual Editor) to a dedicated release branch so that late-cycle changes on quarto-dev/quarto `main` don't destabilize the release. This re-applies the equivalent of #18163 (which pinned to `release/rstudio-yellow-yarrow`), but targeting the 2026.09 release branch (`release/rstudio-autumn-hawkbit`).

The unpin for 2026.09 (#18485) already staged the commented-out release-branch lines, so the work here is mostly:

1. Create the `release/rstudio-autumn-hawkbit` branch in the `quarto-dev/quarto` repo.
2. In the 9 build files, uncomment the release-branch lines and comment out the `main` lines (the inverse of the unpin change):
   - `dependencies/common/install-panmirror`
   - `dependencies/windows/install-panmirror/clone-panmirror-repo.cmd`
   - `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.bionic`
   - `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.focal`
   - `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.jammy`
   - `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.opensuse15`
   - `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.rhel8`
   - `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.rhel9`
   - `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.windows`

When `main` is reopened for `2026.10` development, we'll need to revert this pin again (resume pulling from `main`) -- open another follow-up issue at that time. That unpin should also repoint the now-inactive placeholder lines at the 2026.10 release branch (`release/rstudio-unknown-flower`, once the flower name for 2026.10 is assigned).

title: Server-mode Playwright fixture writes session state into the sandbox seed directory
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Server (in-tree rserver-dev spawned by the Playwright fixture)
    RStudio Version : 2026.07.999-dev+999 (local dev build from 2026-07-27)
    OS Version      : macOS 26.6
    R Version       : 4.6.1

The fixture code is current main. The binary is an older local dev build, which
is incidental here: the problem is in the TypeScript fixture rather than in
anything the session does, and the reproduction does not depend on the binary's
version.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Running the Playwright e2e suite in Server mode against the spawned in-tree `rserver-dev` (that is, with `PW_RSTUDIO_SERVER_URL` unset), from `e2e/rstudio/`:

1. Run the sandbox layout tests.

        npm run test:server-dev -- tests/sandbox.test.ts

    - The test "Server R workdir uses workdir_ prefix; no config trees written locally" fails on `expect(dataHomeEntries.length).toBe(0)`, receiving 21.
2. Open the preserved sandbox directory printed at the end of the run and list `data-home`.
    - It holds rsession state written during the run: `sessions`, `client-state`, `history_database`, `log`, `monitored`, `notebooks`, `persistent-state`, `sources`, and others.

### Describe the problem in detail

The sandbox-level `data-home` is a seed source rather than a session data home. `fixtures/sandbox-setup.ts` creates it and copies the Posit Assistant build into `data-home/pai` when `PW_SEED_PAI` is set. The Desktop fixture says so directly at `fixtures/desktop.fixture.ts:33-37` and never uses it as `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME`: each Desktop launch gets its own data home under a `config_*` root, with `data-home/pai` symlinked in.

The Server fixture instead points `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` straight at that seed directory (`fixtures/server.fixture.ts:30` and `:185`), so every spawned server session writes its state into it.

Two consequences beyond the failing assertion. The seed directory accumulates session state from every server run. And because the path is shared rather than per worker, parallel server workers write to one data home, so they lack the isolation the Desktop fixture provides.

This appears to date from the fixture change rather than the test. The assertion arrived 2026-05-17 in 0c10ad1a64 (#17631), when the Server fixture did not set `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME`. Two days later 2877a98d4b (#17691) added it pointing at the sandbox `data-home`, and the test was not updated. Both are still on main, so the test has been failing in Server mode since then. Server mode is exercised less often than Desktop, which is likely why it went unnoticed.

One coupling worth knowing about before changing this. Server mode never calls `seedPaiIntoDataHome` -- that function is private to `desktop.fixture.ts` (declared at `:315`, referenced only at `:268` and `:423`). Server sessions currently find the seeded Posit Assistant at `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME/pai` only because they are pointed at the directory that contains it. Giving the Server fixture its own data home would drop that seeding unless the symlink step is added at the same time.

### Describe the behavior you expected

The spawned server's `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` would ideally be a per-worker directory, leaving the sandbox-level `data-home` untouched as the seed source, the way the Desktop fixture already works. The `serverRoot` temporary directory the fixture creates for `config-home` looks like a natural place for it.

title: Linux E2E branch dispatches time out building from source on cold caches (build_timeout_minutes: 90)
description:
### What happens

Dispatching `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-linux.yml` on a topic branch with `build_from_source: true` (the default) gets the build job cancelled at the engine's `build_timeout_minutes` when the caches are cold. Observed while validating #18378 on `fedora-43-x86_64` (limit: 90 minutes):

- Attempt 1 ([run 30497728838](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30497728838)): `rstudio-tools` and GWT caches missed (evicted by the 10 GB Actions cache LRU), sccache S3 effectively empty for this engine (4 hits / 699 requests). Dependency install took 12 minutes; the build step was cancelled 78 minutes in, roughly 90% through the C++ compile.
- Attempt 2 ([run 30502793933](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30502793933), dispatched from a temporary branch with the timeout raised to 180): completed in ~46 minutes -- 11 minutes of (still cold) dependency install plus a 35-minute build riding the sccache objects attempt 1 had banked in S3 (686 hits / 769 requests).

Extrapolating, a fully cold one-shot Fedora source build needs roughly 120 minutes on the `ubuntu-latest` container runners.

### Why branch runs are cold

- The `rstudio-tools` / R-libs / GWT cache *saves* are deliberately gated to `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` (each branch copy would be pure pressure on the 10 GB quota), so a branch dispatch can never warm them for its own retry, and the main-scoped copies are frequently evicted.
- sccache's S3 backend is not main-gated, but engines whose scheduled runs test daily installers (`build_from_source: false`) never populate it, so the first from-source dispatch on such an engine starts from nothing. It does bank progress across attempts, which is why retrying eventually converges.

### Suggested fix

Raise `build_timeout_minutes` for the engines still at 90 (both fedoras, debian-13, the ubuntus) toward the 150 that `rocky-9-x86_64` and `rocky-10-arm64` already use; 150 fits the observed ~120-minute cold Fedora build with margin. The timeout only bounds runaway jobs -- a successful warm build finishes in well under an hour, so the cost of a higher ceiling is only paid by runs that would otherwise die at 90 and waste the whole spend.

Context: the 180-minute validation bump was made on a throwaway branch (workflow_dispatch reads the engine config from the dispatched ref) and deleted after; nothing is committed. See also the note on rstudio/rstudio#18396.

title: Linux builds fail when keytar's prebuilt binary is unavailable: libsecret-1-dev is missing from the dependency scripts
description:
Linux builds have no working fallback when `keytar`'s prebuilt native binary cannot be downloaded, so an unavailable GitHub release asset fails the whole build.

### What happens

`src/gwt/build.xml:309-315` (the `panmirror` target, reached from `gwtc` at `:350`) runs `yarn install` in `src/gwt/lib/quarto`. That workspace pulls in `keytar@7.9.0`, whose install script is:

```
prebuild-install || npm run build
```

`prebuild-install` downloads a prebuilt native binary from GitHub release assets. When that download fails, yarn falls back to `npm run build` -> `node-gyp rebuild`, which needs the `libsecret-1` development headers:

```
error .../src/gwt/lib/quarto/node_modules/keytar: Command failed.
Command: prebuild-install || npm run build
  > keytar@7.9.0 build
  > node-gyp rebuild

  Package libsecret-1 was not found in the pkg-config search path.
  Perhaps you should add the directory containing `libsecret-1.pc'
  to the PKG_CONFIG_PATH environment variable
  Package 'libsecret-1', required by 'virtual:world', not found
  gyp: Call to 'pkg-config --cflags libsecret-1' returned exit status 1 while in binding.gyp
```

`libsecret` appears nowhere in this repository -- `dependencies/linux/install-dependencies-noble:30-74` and the equivalent package lists in `install-dependencies-jammy`, `-focal`, `-resolute`, `-bionic`, and `-yum` do not include `libsecret-1-dev` (or `libsecret-devel`). The source-build fallback therefore cannot succeed on a stock build machine; the build depends entirely on the prebuilt download.

The `<retry retrycount="3">` around `yarn install` does not help here. Once `prebuild-install` fails, every retry hits the same missing headers, so all three attempts fail identically and the build stops.

### Observed occurrence

`linux-desktop / Build (ubuntu-24-x86_64)` in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31640451121/job/94261800776 (PR #18535).

This was a transient GitHub release-asset outage rather than anything in that PR: GitHub release downloads were returning 503 during the same window (reproduced for unrelated assets), another PR's `linux-desktop / Build` failed at the same time with `socket hang up` while packaging Electron, and the keytar asset downloads normally again now. The point of this issue is not the outage -- it is that a brief blip in GitHub release-asset availability deterministically fails every Linux build, with no local recovery path.

### Suggested fix

Add `libsecret-1-dev` to the Debian/Ubuntu package lists in `dependencies/linux/` (and `libsecret-devel` to the yum/zypper equivalents), so the `node-gyp` fallback can actually build keytar from source when the prebuilt binary is unreachable. This also helps developers doing Linux builds behind restrictive networks.

This is a build-infrastructure gap only; it does not change shipped behaviour.

title: e2e: Re-enable the Server-mode tests skipped in PR #17939
description:
PR #17939 brought RStudio Server (Ubuntu 24) under the E2E Playwright
automation lifecycle. To land the suite green, several tests that fail on
Server were tagged `@desktop_only` (each marked with a `TODO(aza)` comment)
because the failures look test-side rather than product-side. This issue
tracks re-enabling them on Server. It replaces the per-test follow-up TODOs;
each `TODO(aza)` comment can be updated to reference this issue.

The skips fall into three groups by suspected cause.

### Group 1 -- post-restart console output unreadable on Server

- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/misc/session_restart.test.ts` (guards #14636)
- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/console/r_session_restart.test.ts`
- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/console/package_installation.test.ts`

After an R session restart on Server, the post-restart console fills with
escape-sequence glyphs (long runs of `ה`/`X`) instead of the marker the
helper prints via `afterRestart`'s `cat()`, so the console text match never
succeeds. All three suites share `ConsolePaneActions.restartSession()` and
read the restart result off console text.

Note for `session_restart.test.ts`: it guards #14636 (variables defined
before a restart survive into the after-restart command). The skip comment
attributes the failure to `save_workspace=never`, but that preference is set
on Desktop too (where the test passes), so it is likely not the cause. When
re-enabling, confirm workspace survival through a sentinel file
(`file.exists`) or the automation bridge rather than scraping console text,
so the harness fix also rules out a genuine Server-side regression.

### Group 2 -- GWT null dereference during preview consent

- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/sql_preview_security.test.ts`
- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/r2d3_preview_security.test.ts` (already
  `test.fixme` on Server)

The preview consent and render flow raises an uncaught client exception
(`Cannot read properties of null`, obfuscated symbol `WXc` on Linux Server
and `VXc` on Windows CI). This looks like a `src/gwt/` product issue rather
than a test issue; decoding the stack needs a build with `-DGWT_STYLE=PRETTY`.
For consistency, `sql_preview_security.test.ts` would ideally use the same
`test.fixme(... mode === 'server')` treatment as `r2d3_preview_security.test.ts`
so it stays visible in reports and re-enables automatically once the GWT bug
is fixed.

### Group 3 -- other Server-specific UI timing

- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/debugger/debugger.test.ts` -- clicking a call
  frame to switch the Environment context.
- `e2e/rstudio/tests/preferences/global_prefs_panels.test.ts` -- the Python
  interpreter selector modal does not open within the timeout on Server.
- `e2e/rstudio/tests/projects/project_id.test.ts` -- the second
  `restartSessionWithSentinel` (after clearing `project_user_data_directory`)
  times out waiting for `window.rstudio.ready`. Server logs show the session
  restarts cleanly (event stream up ~2s, `client_init` 1-3s), so this is the
  bridge readiness signal not re-arming across a Server restart, not a slow or
  failed session -- distinct from Group 1's console-text problem. Intermittent;
  the first restart in the same test passes, and Desktop passes.

### Done when

- Each test above runs on Server or carries a `test.fixme` tied to a tracked
  product issue, with no bare `TODO(aza)` markers remaining.
- The #14636 guard confirms workspace survival without relying on console text.

See PR #17939.

title: e2e runs intermittently hang at project-switch cycling; watchdog kill leaves no diagnostics
description:
### Summary

E2E CI runs intermittently hang partway through the `tests/projects/` serial chain (`project_editor_theme.test.ts` -> `project_trust_dialog.test.ts`) until the `run-with-heartbeat` watchdog declares the run hung (`no output for 300s`) and terminates it (exit 124). Because the SIGKILL lands mid-teardown, the run produces **no diagnostics at all**: the blob report is never written, `test-results/` contains only an `error-context.md`, no trace exists (`trace: 'off'`), and the per-test log/console attachments never run.

11 job hangs between 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-11, across **three platforms**, all at the same test region. The affected test files have not changed since 2026-06-09.

### Occurrences

| date (UTC) | run | job | hang point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-08-11 23:40 | [31547344591](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31547344591) (PR #18521) | linux-server e2e (2) | trust test 2, after project create |
| 2026-08-11 23:36 | [31547120281](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31547120281) (PR #18520) | linux-server e2e (2) | after project_editor_theme:255 |
| 2026-08-11 19:34 | [31528533302](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31528533302) | linux-server e2e (2) | after project_editor_theme:255 |
| 2026-08-11 17:06 | [31515906367](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31515906367) | linux-server e2e (2) | trust test 2, after project create |
| 2026-08-11 06:50 | [31466565329](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31466565329) | linux-server e2e (2) | trust test 2, after project create |
| 2026-08-07 22:14 | [31223110969](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31223110969) | linux-server e2e (2) | trust test 2, after project create |
| 2026-08-05 20:03 | [31042248386](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31042248386) | linux-server e2e (2) | trust test 2, after project create |
| 2026-08-04 16:03 | [30927290169](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30927290169) | windows desktop e2e (4) | after project_editor_theme:255 |
| 2026-08-03 18:49 | [30843028345](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30843028345) | windows desktop e2e (4) | after project_editor_theme:90 |
| 2026-07-31 02:57 | [30600331378](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30600331378) | linux-server e2e (2) | after project_editor_theme:255 |
| 2026-07-31 02:57 | (same run) | linux-desktop E2E | after project_editor_theme:255 |

### Analysis

From run 31547344591 (analyzed in detail):

- The test hung immediately after a successful project switch (the new session answered `getwd()`, then everything stopped). `error-context.md` shows both `Test timeout of 120000ms exceeded` **and** `Tearing down "perTestReset" exceeded the test timeout of 120000ms` -- the teardown's first step is a bare `page.evaluate` (`drainClientExceptions`), so the page's JS context was permanently unavailable, not just a slow assertion.
- `page.evaluate` is the one Playwright operation with **no timeout** (`actionTimeout: 10000` bounds clicks/presses; all `waitForFunction` calls pass explicit timeouts). An evaluate blocks forever only when the frame has no usable JS context: a navigation that never commits, or a frozen renderer.
- On the server occurrences, `rserver.log`'s mtime freezes at exactly the hang start and the rsession goes silent in the journal -- the entire client/server conversation stops at once.
- The kill is guaranteed to destroy diagnostics: the legitimately-silent teardown chain after a wedged page is up to 120s (test) + 120s (perTestReset teardown) + 120s (worker fixture teardown) = 360s, which exceeds the 300s heartbeat idle window, so the watchdog always fires mid-teardown. The SIGINT-then-SIGKILL grace (30s) cannot flush the blob report because the wedged worker never winds down.

Why it clusters on these tests: this stretch performs the most session starts per minute in the whole suite (`project_editor_theme` does ~6 project switches; `project_trust_dialog` has 22 restart/switch calls). Any per-session-startup hang probability concentrates here; the tests themselves look innocent.

### Root-cause hypothesis (product side)

A session that silently dies or wedges mid-startup during a project switch leaves the browser stuck on a page transition that never completes, producing exactly this signature on both server and desktop. That matches the masked background-thread startup-crash class addressed by #18517 / #18520 (e.g. the `detectParentTermination` environ race). All 11 hangs predate the #18520 merge (2026-08-11 23:39 UTC). If hangs recur on branches containing #18520, this hypothesis is wrong and the investigation reopens.

### Mitigation plan (harness side, this issue)

Regardless of root cause, this failure class must stop taking out whole shards with zero diagnostics:

- [ ] Bound the page-touching work in `perTestReset` setup/teardown (and session shutdown) with explicit deadlines so a wedged page becomes a fast, descriptive test failure instead of an unbounded hang. Playwright then restarts the worker (fresh browser + RStudio session) and the rest of the shard survives, with the blob report intact.
- [ ] On detecting a wedged page, capture protocol-level diagnostics that do not require the JS context: `page.url()` (distinguishes a never-committing navigation from a frozen renderer), a CDP screenshot, and rsession/rserver log tails.
- [ ] Keep the worst-case silent stretch comfortably under the heartbeat idle window so the watchdog only fires for genuinely dead runners.

title: Remaining routes that re-lay-out panes without clearing zoom state
description:
Follow-up to #18444. That issue fixed the routes the forum reporter actually hit; a
code review of the fix turned up four more instances of the same family, all
pre-existing and deliberately left out of that PR to keep it reviewable.

The shared root cause is unchanged: `PaneManager`'s zoom bookkeeping
(`maximizedWindow_` / `maximizedTab_`, and the column-zoom widths
`widgetSizePriorToZoom_` / `leftWidgetSizePriorToZoom_` / `sidebarSizePriorToZoom_`)
is only cleared by `restoreLayout()`, so anything else that re-lays-out the panes
leaves it live. While it is live, the `WindowEnsureVisibleEvent` handler re-zooms
whichever pane raises itself next.

### 1. `showSidebar`'s zoom guard covers pane zoom but not column zoom

`PaneManager.showSidebar` now ends an active *pane* zoom when sidebar visibility
changes, but checks only `maximizedWindow_ != null`. `endZoomIfActive`
(`PaneManager.java:749-751`) documents that there are three trackers:

    maximizedWindow_ != null || maximizedTab_ != null || getZoomedColumn() != null

Column zoom (`zoomColumn`, reachable from View > Panes > Zoom Left/Right Column and
Zoom Sidebar) is untouched by the guard.

Reproduction, two clicks:

1. View > Panes > Zoom Sidebar. This sets `right_` and every left column to 1px.
2. Click the sidebar header's close button (`setSidebarPref(false)` -> `showSidebar(false)`).

The guard does not fire. `MainSplitPanel.removeSidebarWidget` (line 470) only removes
the sidebar and calls `forceLayout()` -- it has no redistribution counterpart to
`setSidebarWidget`'s. `center_` absorbs the freed width and the right column stays at
1px, so Environment / Plots / Help are gone. Because the width is 1px rather than 0,
`getZoomedColumn()` returns null, so no zoom command is check-marked either: the menu
reports a normal layout while a whole column is invisible. The only recovery is
View > Panes > Show All Panes, which the user has no reason to try.

Quieter damage in the same shape: `widgetSizePriorToZoom_` survives the sidebar
toggle, and `fullyMaximizeWindow` only records the pre-zoom width when
`widgetSizePriorToZoom_ < 0`, so the *next* zoom restores a width measured before the
sidebar existed.

Widening the guard to `endZoomIfActive`'s full condition would close this without
loosening the "don't clobber custom widths" constraint that method documents.

### 2. `isAnimating_` is dead, so `toggleWindowZoom` has no re-entrancy guard

`PaneManager.java:1292` reads `isAnimating_` and `PaneManager.java:3085` declares it
`= false`. Nothing in the tree ever assigns it, so `toggleWindowZoom`'s
`if (isAnimating_) return;` can never fire.

Either remove the field and the guard, or make it real. There is a genuine hazard it
looks like it should cover: `restoreLayout()` -> `restorePaneStateToDefault()` fires
window state changes -> `transitionToState` -> `onBeforeShow()`, and a tab that calls
`bringToFront()` from `onBeforeShow` re-enters the `WindowEnsureVisibleEvent` handler
while `maximizedWindow_` is still set (it is cleared on `restoreSavedLayout`'s last
line), which would call `fullyMaximizeWindow` mid-restore. Clearing the bookkeeping
before firing the state changes may be the cheaper fix than a flag.

### 3. `EnsureHeightEvent.MAXIMIZED` bypasses the frame's maximize action

#18444 funnelled the frame-level maximize gestures through `WindowFrame.maximize()` so
an owner can intercept them in one place. `LogicalWindow.onEnsureHeight`
(`LogicalWindow.java:138-149`) converts `EnsureHeightEvent.MAXIMIZED` into a
`WindowStateChangeEvent(MAXIMIZE)` fired at the `LogicalWindow`, bypassing the frame
entirely. Producers include `ToolbarPane.maximize()`, reached from
`ViewerPresenter` and `Source`.

So e.g. an `EnsureHeightEvent.NORMAL` arriving while the Source pane is zoomed
undraws the zoom without clearing `maximizedWindow_`. `MinimizedWindowFrame`'s own
maximize button is the same shape, though it is not reachable while a zoom is drawn
(the zoomed pane's sibling is HIDE, not MINIMIZE).

### 4. Adding a source column while a pane is zoomed

`createAndDisplaySourceColumn` -> `MainSplitPanel.addLeftWidget` (line 327) ->
`clearForRefresh()` + `initialize(...)`, which re-applies persisted or default column
widths. That undraws the zoom while `maximizedWindow_` stays set.

### 5. `zoomColumn` switching from a tracked pane zoom to a different column

**Manually reproduced.** This is the one to fix first.

The #18444 fix made `zoomColumn`'s un-zoom branch delegate to `restoreLayout()` when a
pane zoom is tracked. That guard sits inside the
`StringUtil.equals(currentZoomedColumn, columnId)` branch, i.e. toggling the *same*
column off. Asking for a *different* column falls through to the per-column branches,
which never clear the pane-zoom bookkeeping.

Steps (default layout, sidebar visible with Chat in it):

1. View > Panes > Zoom Chat. `zoomTab` -> `fullyMaximizeWindow` sets
   `maximizedWindow_` to the sidebar window and `maximizedTab_` to `Chat`.
2. View > Panes > Zoom Left Column (Zoom Right Column behaves the same).
3. View > Panes now shows **two checkmarks at once**: *Zoom Chat* and *Zoom Left
   Column*. They come from independent sources -- `manageLayoutCommands` reads
   `maximizedTab_`, `manageZoomColumnCommands` reads `getZoomedColumn()` -- and cannot
   both be legitimately live.
4. Run `plot(1:10)`. The right column takes over the whole window and everything else
   collapses: `WindowEnsureVisibleEvent` sees `maximizedWindow_` still pointing at the
   sidebar, which is not Plots' window, and calls `fullyMaximizeWindow` on TabSet2.
   This is the original #18444 symptom.

Steps 3 and 4 were confirmed by hand. Worth noting that in the bad state the sidebar
sits at 0 width, so nothing on screen suggests Chat is still tracked as zoomed.

Read off the code but not confirmed by hand: invoking the same column zoom a second
time should hit the new guard and self-heal, and Show All Panes should recover, because
`zoomColumn` only records pre-zoom widths when they are `< 0` so the pre-pane-zoom
widths survive. If both hold, the dangerous window is just between the column switch
and the next such action.

A guard at the top of `zoomColumn` covering any tracked pane zoom -- not only the
toggle-off branch -- would close this. Ordering needs care:
`invalidateSavedLayoutState` resets `widgetSizePriorToZoom_` to -1, which `zoomColumn`
then reads.

### Notes

Items 1-4 were found by reviewing the #18444 fix rather than from user reports, so
severity is unknown for 2-4; item 1 is a concrete two-click reproduction that hides a
pane column with no indication in the UI. Item 5 was predicted from the same review and
then reproduced by hand, and is the highest priority of the five: it reaches the
original #18444 symptom through a route that fix does not cover.

title: Localhost proxy (/p/, /p6/) does not restrict "localhost" resolution to the requested address family
description:
## Description

rserver's localhost-proxying paths (`/p/<port>` for IPv4, `/p6/<port>` for IPv6) connect to the target application via the hostname `localhost`, but nothing previously restricted DNS resolution of that hostname to the address family the request's `/p/` vs `/p6/` prefix actually indicated.

If the resolver returns both an A and an AAAA record for `localhost` (common on hosts with `::1 localhost` in `/etc/hosts`), an `/p/` (IPv4-intended) request could non-deterministically connect over IPv6, or a `/p6/` request over IPv4, depending on whichever family the resolver happened to try/return first.

This is the open-source (rserver-side, non-Launcher) side of a fix originally made in rstudio-pro for its Launcher-mode `SessionProxy` hop (rstudio-pro#12142), which has the same underlying issue when routing through a separately-hosted session.

## Fix

Restrict the resolution of `localhost` to the correct address family before connecting, rather than relying on whichever family the resolver returns first:

- `TcpIpAsyncConnector::connect()` gains an optional address-family parameter, restricting `resolver_.async_resolve()` accordingly when set.
- `TcpIpAsyncClient`/`TcpIpAsyncClientSsl` gain a protected `setIpFamily()` setter.
- `LocalhostAsyncClient`/`LocalhostAsyncClientSsl` gain a public `setIpv6()` convenience setter.
- `ServerSessionProxy.cpp`'s `proxyLocalhostRequest()` now calls `setIpv6()` on the `LocalhostAsyncClient` it constructs, matching the request's `/p/` vs `/p6/` prefix.

Unit test coverage using real loopback listeners was added in `SocketOwnershipTests.cpp`.

title: mathjax inline preview popup leaks escape preview handlers
description:
### Symptom

After an inline math preview popup has been shown and dismissed, every subsequent Escape keydown in the IDE raises an uncaught client exception:

```
(TypeError) : Cannot read properties of null (reading 'real')
```

thrown from a `NativePreviewHandler` lambda. The leaked handler also calls `nativePreviewEvent.cancel()` before throwing, so it cancels the Escape preview event app-wide.

### Root cause

`MathJax.renderPopup()` calls `popup_.show()` twice per render: once offscreen before typesetting, and once more in the async typeset-complete callback ([`MathJax.java:543-560`](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/main/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/common/mathjax/MathJax.java#L543-L560)).

`MiniPopupPanel.show()` unconditionally calls `addEscHandler()` ([`MiniPopupPanel.java:86-90`](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/main/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/core/client/widget/MiniPopupPanel.java#L86-L90)), so the second `show()` overwrites `escapeHandler_` and the first registration leaks -- it stays registered for the lifetime of the app, and nothing ever removes it.

Once the popup is dismissed (`removeEscHandler()` nulls the field), each Escape keydown fires the leaked lambda, which does `escapeHandler_.removeHandler()` on a null field. In compiled output this surfaces as the `reading 'real'` TypeError because GWT inlines `LegacyHandlerWrapper.removeHandler()` (whose delegate field is named `real`).

Every show/hide render cycle of the popup leaks one more handler, so N leaked handlers produce N TypeErrors per Escape press (aggregated into one `UmbrellaException`).

### Impact

- Uncaught JS exceptions accumulate on every Escape press after any inline math preview has been shown.
- In the e2e suite this makes unrelated tests fail: any test that presses Escape after `math_preview.test.ts` has run in the same worker gets the drained client exceptions attributed to it. In the `pr-18467` all-platforms run, `multiselect_basic.test.ts :: typing lands at every cursor` failed attempt 0 on all four platforms for exactly this reason (and passed on retry, where the fresh worker never showed a math popup): https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18467/31132726266-1/all-platforms/index.html

### Suggested fix

Make `MiniPopupPanel.show()` idempotent with respect to the escape handler -- e.g. call `removeEscHandler()` before `addEscHandler()`, or skip registration when `escapeHandler_` is already non-null.

title: edits can leave stale syntax highlighting below the edited line in Markdown and YAML documents
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.08.0-daily (long-standing)
    OS Version      : all
    R Version       : all

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Enable rainbow fenced divs (Tools > Global Options > R Markdown).
2. Open a plain Markdown (`.md`) document containing many fenced divs, tall enough to scroll -- e.g. 40 copies of:

   ```markdown
   ::: {#block}
   text
   :::
   ```

3. At the very top of the document, insert a new (unclosed) opening fence, e.g. `::: {#outer}`.
4. Scroll down.

### Describe the problem in detail

Every fenced div in the document is now nested one level deeper, so all fences should shift to the next rainbow color. Only the first couple of rows update; the rest of the document keeps the old colors indefinitely (confirmed by inspecting the background tokenizer's caches: after the edit, 79 of 81 fence rows in a 160-row document still held stale tokens).

The Ace background tokenizer re-tokenizes the row following an edited row only when the edited row's *end state* changes. Tokenizer *contexts* (an rstudio-ace extension used for rainbow parentheses and fenced divs, YAML multiline-string indents, and chunk fence widths) also flow into following rows, but context changes do not propagate invalidation -- so an edit that changes only context data leaves every following row's cached tokens stale.

In R, R Markdown, and Quarto documents this is masked by an unrelated mechanism: modes with a code-model scope tree rebuild the scope tree after every edit, and that path (`TokenIterator.tokenizeUpToRow`) force-retokenizes every row from the edit point to the end of the document. Modes without a scope tree -- plain Markdown, YAML -- have no such rebuild, and show the stale highlighting. The same applies to YAML multiline strings: re-indenting a `|` block-scalar opener does not re-highlight the lines below it.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Rows below an edit are re-highlighted whenever the edit affects them, whether the dependency is carried by the tokenizer state or by the tokenizer context.

title: Windows: ConPTY teardown throws from a destructor at process exit, aborting rsession
description:
### Summary

On Windows, `ConPty::teardownLocked()` can throw `std::system_error` out of a
destructor during process shutdown, which calls `std::terminate()` and aborts
the process. In a Debug build this surfaces as a modal
"Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime Library / Debug Error! ... abort() has been called"
dialog; in a Release build rsession simply terminates with abort during exit.

### Root cause

`ConPty::teardownLocked()` (`src/cpp/core/system/Win32ConPty.cpp`) closes the
pseudoconsole on a short-lived `std::thread`. It is reached from `~ConPty`.
rsession always exits through R's `exit()`, so any terminal still registered
with the process-wide `ProcessSupervisor` is torn down from that singleton's
`atexit` destructor -- i.e. inside `LdrShutdownProcess`, where `CreateThread`
fails with `STATUS_PROCESS_IS_TERMINATING`. `std::thread`'s constructor then
throws, the exception escapes the destructor chain, and `std::terminate()` runs.

Stack (symbolized from a live hung process):

```
R_CleanUp -> exit() -> LdrShutdownProcess -> _execute_onexit_table
  -> atexit dtor for module_context::processSupervisor::instance
  -> ~ProcessSupervisor -> ~AsyncChildProcess -> ~ChildProcess
  -> ~ConPty -> ConPty::stop() -> ConPty::teardownLocked()
  -> std::thread::_Start -> std::_Throw_Cpp_error -> terminate -> abort
```

### Reproduction

Reliable on a Debug Windows build:

```
build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests.bat --scope r --filter terminal
```

The tests pass, then the process hangs on the abort dialog instead of exiting.
`test-terminal.R` leaves a ConPTY-backed child in the supervisor, because the
`--run-script` exit path (R's own `R_CleanUp`, driven by `RReadScript`
returning EOF) bypasses `win32Quit` and so never runs the session cleanup that
terminates child processes. The full `--scope r` run does the same, which is
how this was found.

### User impact

`terminateAllChildren()` (`SessionMain.cpp`) waits at most 1 second for the
supervisor's children, then logs a warning and proceeds. Children that have not
been reaped stay in the supervisor's vector and are destroyed at static
destruction, so quitting with a terminal that does not exit within that second
reaches the same throw. Present since the winpty -> ConPTY migration (#17814),
which shipped in 2026.06.0.

### Related, not covered here

On Windows the `Rstart` struct is never given a `CleanUp` hook
(`REmbeddedWin32.cpp`), so `RScriptCleanUp` does not run and `--run-script`
never terminates its child processes. That is why a live ConPTY survives to
static destruction in the first place.

title: e2e: consolidate R package provisioning across runner workflows
description:
## Background

Getting the e2e suite's R packages installed where the session can see them is currently spread across several runner-specific mechanisms:

- The package list itself is single-sourced (`e2e/rstudio/required-packages.txt`) and the installer is one shared action (`os-e2e-deps`), but every workflow must hand-wire a **pair** of settings that only work together: `install-required-packages` on the action, and `PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER` pointing globalSetup at the same library the action populated. Configuring one without the other silently degrades to a thinner library plus test-time CRAN installs -- the failure class behind both #18390 (env var set but effectively empty on Linux) and the desktop-windows CRAN-outage hangs diagnosed in the [pr-18449 all-platforms run](https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18449/31218669330-1/all-platforms/index.html) (env var set but flag missing; fixed by PR #18487).
- The Linux Server workflow has a third mechanism: a hand-curated package list seeded into a root-owned system library, with a caveat comment warning that uninstall-test subjects must never be added to it.
- Repo selection exists twice: PPM in the action's bash, cran.r-project.org in `r-libs-setup.ts` for non-Linux.

## Plan

1. **Make `os-e2e-deps` own the whole contract.** Default `install-required-packages` to `"true"` and have the action export `PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER` (pointing at its `r-libs-user` input) to `GITHUB_ENV` itself, skipping the export when the caller already defines the variable or opts out of the install. The action already exports `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` the same way. Callers then can't half-configure the pairing, and the per-workflow env/flag wiring (Windows x2, macOS x3, the Linux test-step expression) gets deleted.
2. **Server: provision the per-run test user's library instead of the system library.** After `os-e2e-deps` populates the workspace `R-libs` tree, copy it into the test user's default user library (`~/R/%p-library/%v`) and `chown` it. R picks that path up with no env plumbing (nothing has to survive rserver's per-session environment rebuild, #18348), sessions get every package read-write, and uninstall-flow tests work on anything. The root-owned system-library seed and its separate curated list are then retired. Notes: the DBI uninstall test (`s4_unloaded_package`) is `@desktop_only` so it never ran on server anyway; `fortunes` (the `missing_packages_banner` subject) stays absent from every manifest; `readr` is genuinely used (`import_dataset.test.ts`) and moves into `required-packages.txt`; `tidyverse` is referenced by no test and is dropped.
3. **Keep what encodes real differences**: the macOS `cache-scope` keys (ABI boundaries) and the Linux per-engine `preinstall_r_packages` escape hatch (passing an empty value still opts out).

## Out of scope

`packageRepo()` in `r-libs-setup.ts` and the per-test `ensurePackageInstalled` self-heal path still point at cran.r-project.org; with the library pre-populated everywhere these reduce to presence checks, so repointing them at PPM can be considered separately.

title: e2e: sandbox layout test races Chromium's delayed Local State write
description:
### Symptom

`sandbox.test.ts :: Desktop launch populates electron-userdata and creates data-home/user-home` failed hard (both attempts) on desktop-linux in the `pr-18467` all-platforms run:

```
config_KEJMdm: expected electron-userdata/Local State to exist
Timeout 5000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
```

https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18467/31132726266-1/all-platforms/index.html

The failing dir was not the spec's own config root (that one passed) -- it was a leftover sibling from an earlier Desktop spawn in the same run. `config-home/rstudio-prefs.json` and `electron-userdata/` both existed in it; `Local State` never appeared.

### Root cause

The test polls (5s) for `electron-userdata/Local State` in *every* `config_*` dir of the shared per-run sandbox. Two facts make that assertion racy for sibling dirs:

- Chromium writes `Local State` through a delayed committer, roughly 10s after launch. This is observable in the same report: the healthy config root in the retry attempt needed ~3s of polling, which lands at ~10s after process start.
- `shutdownRStudio` SIGTERMs the process group, so an Electron instance that exits young may never flush the pending write.

Any Desktop instance that lives less than ~10 seconds can therefore leave a config dir that permanently lacks `Local State`. Candidates in a full-suite run include the multi-instance specs (`pane_location_persistence`, `s4_unloaded_package`, `uninstall-posit-ai`) and the sandbox-setup probe. Because the stale dir persists for the entire run, retries can never pass -- one bad dir turns this test into a guaranteed failure for the rest of the run.

### Analysis

Checking all sibling dirs was deliberate (#17953) to catch Desktop spawns that died mid-launch. But `Local State` cannot distinguish "died mid-launch" from "healthy instance that exited before Chromium's first commit", so the assertion is over-strict on siblings.

### Suggested fix

Keep the `Local State` poll only for the current spec's own config root (whose instance is guaranteed to be alive), and assert `config-home/rstudio-prefs.json` -- written synchronously at startup by RStudio itself -- as the init marker for sibling dirs.

title: macOS: Copilot language server fails to start in ad-hoc signed package builds
description:
### Symptom

In an ad-hoc signed macOS package build (a local `make install` / package build without Posit's signing credentials), selecting **GitHub Copilot** as the "Use code assistant" never connects. The assistant pane spins, eventually times out, and shows "The assistant is not currently running." with **Sign In** / **Refresh** / **Diagnostics** buttons. Diagnostics spins on "Generating diagnostics report" and then closes with no report.

The same version installed from a daily build works and shows the user as signed in to Copilot.

### Cause

The Copilot language server cannot load its own native modules, so it exits immediately. From `~/.local/share/rstudio/log/rsession-$USER.log`:

```
ERROR /Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/Resources/app/copilot-language-server-js/main.js:1
Error: dlopen(/Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/Resources/app/copilot-language-server-js/compiled/darwin/arm64/watcher.node, 0x0001):
  tried: '.../compiled/darwin/arm64/watcher.node' (code signature in <...> '.../watcher.node' not valid
  for use in process: mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs)
  ...
  code: 'ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED'
WARNING [onExit]: Agent process exited with status 1.
```

`package/osx/scripts/codesign-package.sh` signs every file in the bundle with `--options runtime` (hardened runtime) and `package/osx/entitlements/default.plist`, which grants only `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` and `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`. The hardened runtime enforces library validation, and ad-hoc signatures carry no Team ID, so the bundled `node` is refused every `*.node` module in the package.

`rsession` and `Contents/MacOS/RStudio` are already re-signed with `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` from their respective `*-adhoc.plist` files. The bundled `node` binaries under `Contents/Resources/app/bin/node*/bin/node` were never given the same treatment.

Reproduced directly with the shipped binary:

```
$ /Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/Resources/app/bin/node-arm64/bin/node \
    -e "require('.../copilot-language-server-js/compiled/darwin/arm64/watcher.node')"
Error: dlopen(...) ... ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED
```

Re-signing a copy of that same `node` with `disable-library-validation` added makes the module load.

### Scope

Ad-hoc builds only. Signed and notarized builds sign every binary in the package with Posit's Developer ID, so `node` and the `*.node` modules share one Team ID and library validation passes — which is why daily builds are unaffected. No released-build user encounters this.

### Affected files

- `package/osx/scripts/codesign-package.sh`
- `package/osx/entitlements/default.plist`

title: Stale pane-zoom state re-zooms any pane that raises itself, breaking the four-pane layout
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.07.1+147
    OS Version      : not specified by reporter
    R Version       : not specified by reporter

Reported layout: standard four-pane layout (Source upper left, Environment upper
right, Console lower left, Files lower right), with Posit Assistant assigned to
the left sidebar and the sidebar hidden.

Original report: https://forum.posit.co/t/rstudio-keeps-forgetting-pane-layout/216975

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Not yet reproduced from a clean state; the trigger that starts it is still open
(see "What is unconfirmed" below). Once a session is in the bad state, the
reported sequence is reliable:

1. Do anything that makes a pane raise itself -- update R packages, render a
   Quarto document, run a `?help` command.
2. That pane takes over the entire window: its column expands to the full panel
   width and its sibling quadrant disappears.
3. Click the pane header's maximize/minimize button. The vertical split in that
   column comes back, but the other column stays collapsed -- e.g. the two
   right-hand panes never return.
4. Re-opening Tools > Global Options... > Pane Layout shows the correct
   configuration and does not restore the layout.
5. Toggling the sidebar open and closed sometimes restores four visible columns,
   but leaves quadrants in the wrong maximize/minimize state, and the next
   pane-raising action breaks the layout again.

### Describe the problem in detail

`PaneManager` tracks pane zoom in `maximizedWindow_` / `maximizedTab_`. While
`maximizedWindow_` is non-null, any pane that raises itself is forcibly zoomed:

```java
// PaneManager.java:492-517  (WindowEnsureVisibleEvent handler)
if (maximizedWindow_ != null && !maximizedWindow_.equals(window))
{
   ...
   fullyMaximizeWindow(window, lastSelectedTab_);   // steals the zoom
   return;
}
```

Every `ensureVisible()` in the IDE reaches this handler by way of
`WindowFrame.onEnsureVisible` (`WindowFrame.java:401-417`), so updating packages
raises Packages, `?foo` raises Help, rendering raises the Render/console pane,
and so on. `fullyMaximizeWindow` (`PaneManager.java:1318`) puts the target pane
in `EXCLUSIVE` (hiding its sibling quadrant) and animates the other columns to
width 0.

So the visible symptoms all follow from one condition: **`maximizedWindow_` is
stale** -- the zoom bookkeeping says "zoomed" while the layout looks normal.
Nothing that visually undoes a zoom clears those fields. Only `restoreLayout()`
-> `invalidateSavedLayoutState()` (`PaneManager.java:1614`) does, and that is
reached only from End Zoom ("Show All Panes") or a zoom toggle. Each of these
changes the visible layout while leaving the bookkeeping live:

- the pane header maximize/minimize button drives `DualWindowLayoutPanel`'s state
  machine directly (vertical only); `PaneManager` never hears about it. With the
  pane in `EXCLUSIVE`, the button maps to `NORMAL` via `LogicalWindow.java:114`,
  which is why the vertical split returns but the collapsed column does not;
- toggling the sidebar goes through `MainSplitPanel.setSidebarWidget` /
  `removeSidebarWidget`, which reset the other columns to default widths
  (`MainSplitPanel.java:415-467`);
- a window resize re-applies `widgetPercentages_` captured before the zoom
  (`MainSplitPanel.java:622-657`);
- the `panes` pref handler (`PaneManager.java:410-480`) rebuilds tab panels and
  never touches zoom state, which is why revisiting Pane Layout does not help.

**Why it survives a restart.** Both halves of a zoom are project-persistent
client state, restored verbatim with no sanity guard:

- `TabZoom` -> `<proj>/.Rproj.user/<id>/pcs/workbench-pane.pper`, replayed 200 ms
  after startup by calling `fullyMaximizeWindow` again
  (`PaneManager.java:143-167`);
- `topwindowstate` (`EXCLUSIVE` / `HIDE` / `MAXIMIZE`) ->
  `pcs/windowlayoutstate.pper` (`DualWindowLayoutPanel.java:320-332`).

Meanwhile `MainSplitPanel` deliberately refuses to restore zoomed *column
widths* (`isZoomedColumnState`, added for #16688 --
`MainSplitPanel.java:162-170`). A session that ends while zoomed therefore
reopens with default column widths but live zoom bookkeeping: a guaranteed
desync, where the layout looks correct until the first pane-raising action.

This is the same fragility that #17832 worked around on the test side ("break
the zoom cascade") by adding `PaneManager.endZoomIfActive` for
`resetForNextTest`. The product has no equivalent recovery.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Raising a pane (package update, render, help lookup) should activate that pane
within the existing layout and never zoom it. Ending a zoom by any route -- pane
header button, sidebar toggle, window resize, Pane Layout changes -- should leave
the zoom bookkeeping and the visible layout in agreement, and a restart should
not resurrect a zoom whose column widths were intentionally not restored.

### Diagnostic / workaround

`View > Panes` is a live readout of the tracked state
(`manageLayoutCommands`, `PaneManager.java:2761-2767`): if a "Zoom <pane>" item
is check-marked while the layout looks normal, the stale zoom is present.

- Workaround: `View > Panes > Show All Panes` (`Ctrl+Shift+0`;
  `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+0` on Windows desktop) is the only route that clears
  `maximizedWindow_` / `maximizedTab_`.
- If it returns on every launch: with RStudio closed, delete
  `workbench-pane.pper` and `windowlayoutstate.pper` from
  `<project>/.Rproj.user/<id>/pcs/` (or `~/.local/share/rstudio/pcs/` outside a
  project).

### What is unconfirmed

The cascade above is read off the code and matches the report step for step, but
which event first set `maximizedWindow_` in this user's session is not
established. Candidates: an explicit zoom that was escaped with the pane header
button; the startup replay of a persisted `TabZoom`; or a zoom whose widths were
subsequently overwritten by a window resize. The `View > Panes` checkmark is the
cheapest way to confirm the state is stale in a live session.

### Suggested fix direction

1. Do not replay `TabZoom` / `EXCLUSIVE` quadrant state at startup when the
   column widths were not restored -- make the `isZoomedColumnState` guard in
   `MainSplitPanel` and the `TabZoom` restore in `PaneManager` agree.
2. Clear the zoom bookkeeping whenever something else re-lays-out the columns
   (sidebar show/hide, pane-header state changes, pane config changes), rather
   than only in `restoreLayout()`.

title: R raw strings corrupt editor row states, breaking header folding in R Markdown
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.08.0-daily (long-standing; since R raw string support)
    OS Version      : all
    R Version       : all

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Open a new R Markdown document:

   ````markdown
   ```{r}
   x <- r"(hello)"
   ```

   # Header one

   content one

   # Header two

   content two
   ````

2. Click the fold gutter arrow on `# Header one`.

### Describe the problem in detail

The fold for `# Header one` swallows `# Header two` and everything after it, extending to the end of the document. Without the raw string, the fold correctly stops before the next header.

The raw-string rules in `r_highlight_rules.js` store the entry state and expected exit suffix in the Ace tokenizer stack (`stack[0..2]`) but never remove them when the raw string closes (compare the sh-mode heredoc rules, which `stack.splice(-3)` on exit). Since the tokenizer returns the stack as the row state whenever it is non-empty, every row after the first raw string -- to the end of the document -- carries an array state such as `["#tmp", "start", "r-start", "r-rawstring", ")\""]` instead of the string `"start"`.

`rmarkdown_folding.js` compares row states with strict `!==` when searching for the next header, which never matches two array instances, so the fold-range search runs off the end of the document. The array states also defeat the strict-equality state caching in `r_code_model.js` (every scope-tree pass re-tokenizes everything below the raw string).

### Describe the behavior you expected

Row states below a closed raw string are plain strings, and header folds stop before the next header of the same depth.

title: pressing Enter in an Rcpp chunk of an R Markdown document throws and skips auto-indent
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.08.0-daily (regressed in 2024.12; commit eafc5faf44)
    OS Version      : all
    R Version       : all

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Open a new R Markdown (or Quarto) document containing a completed chunk followed by an Rcpp chunk, e.g.:

   ````markdown
   ```{r}
   1 + 1
   ```

   ```{Rcpp}
   int add(int x) {
   ```
   ````

2. Place the cursor at the end of `int add(int x) {` and press Enter.

### Describe the problem in detail

The new line receives no auto-indent, and an uncaught exception is raised (visible in the devtools console):

    TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'width')
        at onMatch
        at getLineTokens
        at $tokenizeUpToRow
        at getNextLineIndent
        at insert

`TokenUtils.$tokenizeUpToRow` (used by `CppCodeModel` for C++ chunk indentation) calls `getLineTokens(line, state, row)` without threading a tokenizer context, so every `onMatch` handler receives a fresh empty object. The chunk-end rule installed by `Utils.embedRules` dereferences `context.chunk.width` unguarded, so the exception fires as soon as tokenization crosses any completed chunk fence above the cursor. Broken since commit eafc5faf44 (September 2024), which introduced context-based chunk tracking.

The same unguarded context reads exist in the quarto (`#|`), YAML multiline string, and Sweave `\Sexpr{}` rules.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Pressing Enter inside a C++ chunk indents the new line, without raising an exception.

title: E2E sandbox AI credentials do not reach an RStudio Server session
description:
This concerns the Playwright E2E suite (`e2e/rstudio`) and how AI provider
credentials (Posit AI and GitHub Copilot) are provisioned for tests.

### Describe the problem

The `auth.setup` project provisions AI credentials into a per-run sandbox home
(`$PW_SANDBOX/user-home`), and the credential gate reads that sandbox. This
works in Desktop mode, where the IDE reads the sandbox home. In Server mode it
does not: `rserver` builds each rsession's environment from scratch and takes
the session's `HOME` from the system password database (`getpwnam` -> `pw_dir`),
i.e. the logged-in OS user's real home directory, not the sandbox. So the
credentials written to the sandbox never reach a server rsession, and the AI
features behave as signed-out even though setup reported success.

This affects both providers and pre-dates the Copilot work (it shipped with the
Posit AI credential provisioning in #17680). PR #18342 only surfaces it: the
setup now prints a warning in Server mode that the sandbox credentials will not
reach the session.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

On a machine where the logged-in user's real home directory is not signed in to
the provider:
1. Run a Copilot feature test in server-dev mode:
   ```
   npm run test:server-dev -- tests/panes/editor/code_suggestions.test.ts -g "GitHub Copilot"
   ```
   - The `auth.setup` project signs in and writes the store to the sandbox, and
     the setup test passes.
2. The credential gate reads the sandbox, finds it authenticated, and does not
   skip, so the feature test runs.
3. The feature fails: Copilot ghost text times out, and Posit Assistant chat
   loads but the response comes back empty (or a sign-in overlay blocks it),
   because the rsession read the real home, which has no credentials.

If the logged-in user's real home directory is itself already signed in to the
provider, the tests pass, but only because the rsession reads that pre-existing
local sign-in, not the credentials the setup provisioned into the sandbox. A
green result in that case does not mean the provisioning reached the session.
Confirmed live on an external RStudio Server (Fedora VM) and via
`test:server-dev` on macOS.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Sandbox-provisioned AI credentials should reach the server rsession so the
feature tests exercise real credentials.

### What addressing it would involve

Getting sandbox-provisioned credentials to a server rsession, e.g. writing them
into the location the rsession's real `HOME` resolves to, running the rsession
under a user whose home is the sandbox, or forwarding the credential dirs the
way `RSTUDIO_CONFIG_HOME`/XDG vars are already forwarded. Likely its own effort,
and it must cover both providers.

See issue #18306. Related: PRs #17680 and #18342.

title: Change edit suggestion diff previews from character- to word-level
description:
### Problem Statement
When using `rstudioapi::showEditSuggestion()`, the inline preview highlighting can be fragmented and difficult to read. Changes that are semantically a single word replacement, such as renaming a variable, are often shown as multiple small interleaved character-level highlights rather than cleanly marking the old and new word.

This may also apply to Copilot and Posit AI next-edit suggestions, which appear to use the same preview rendering.

### Proposed Behaviour
Word-level highlighting would be easier to read in most cases.

As far as I can see, the current implementation uses `JsDiff.diffChars` to compute the diff segments. Switching to `JsDiff.diffWords` or `JsDiff.diffWordsWithSpace` (available in the same bundled library) would produce word-level highlights. The way whitespace is handled may need special attention, possibly a combination of `JsDiff.diffWordsWithSpace` and still using `JsDiff.diffChars` on tokens that are fully whitespace would be best?

title: publish windows debug symbols to rstudio-debug-symbols
description:
### Current state

Linux builds publish debug symbols to `s3://rstudio-debug-symbols`: `add_stripped_executable()` (cmake/globals.cmake) splits debug info into `.debug` files via objcopy, and the "Upload Debug Symbols" stage in `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.linux` collects and uploads them per-version via `package/linux/scripts/upload-debug-symbols`. The `debuginfo` script shipped with the product downloads them back for symbolication.

Windows builds never got the equivalent. Official Windows packages build as `RelWithDebInfo` (`package/win32/make-package.bat`), so the linker produces PDBs for all of our binaries in the build tree, but:

- nothing collects or uploads them -- `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows` only uploads the installer `.exe` and `.zip` to `s3://rstudio-ide-build`;
- the only PDB install rule (rsession targets, `src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt`) is gated on `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL Debug`, so release packages do not include PDBs either.

As a result, a crash dump from a released Windows build cannot be symbolicated without rebuilding that exact version locally.

### Proposed work

- Add a `package/win32` script that collects the linker PDBs for shipped binaries (rsession.exe, rsession-utf8.exe, the shared session DLL, the x86 session, consoleio.exe, rpostback.exe, diagnostics.exe) from the build tree into a per-version archive following the bucket's naming convention (`<version>/<product>-windows-<arch>`, zip rather than tar.xz since these are consumed on Windows).
- Add an "Upload Debug Symbols" stage to `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows` that uploads the archive to `s3://rstudio-debug-symbols`, alongside the existing installer upload.

### Possible follow-ups (not in scope)

- Document how to load the published PDBs in WinDbg / Visual Studio.
- Backfill symbols for currently-supported released versions (see `package/linux/scripts/prepare-symbol-backfill` for the Linux equivalent).
- macOS dSYMs are likewise not uploaded today; that is a separate piece of work.
