title: file monitor may miss a change arriving shortly after a large burst of changes (macOS)
description:
### Problem

On macOS, a single file change that lands within ~1-2 seconds after a large burst of file changes (thousands of files modified at once) may not be delivered to the client by the file monitor for 30+ seconds -- possibly never; a manual refresh recovers. Both the project file monitor (Git pane) and the Files-pane listing monitor miss the same event, so the cause is upstream of both consumers.

### Evidence

Found while verifying #18257 / #18259 with an instrumented Playwright run that captured all `get_events` response bodies (rsession dev build, macOS, FSEvents backend):

1. Create a git project; seed and commit 3000 files under `src/`.
2. Modify all 3000 files at once (external writes). All 3000 `file_changed` events are delivered and the changelist populates in ~1.2s.
3. ~1.2s after the burst, create a new untracked file `extra.R` at the project root. **No `get_events` payload ever mentions `extra.R` over the following 30s**, and neither the Git pane nor the Files pane shows it. `git status` on disk sees it immediately.
4. A manual `vcsRefresh` picks the file up instantly (so full-status RPC is fine; only event delivery is affected).
5. A `.gitignore` edit ~35s after the burst IS delivered normally -- the monitor recovers.

The same probe passes when the new file is created ~13s after the burst (observed on a slower client build where the probe timing shifted), so the gap is a timing window shortly after a burst, not a permanently wedged monitor.

### Notes

- FSEvents stream is created with latency 1s and `kFSEventStreamCreateFlagNoDefer` (`src/cpp/core/system/file_monitor/MacFileMonitor.cpp`), so this is not normal coalescing latency.
- The recursive-watch callback handles `MustScanSubDirs`; `kFSEventStreamEventFlagKernelDropped` / `UserDropped` are only checked in the non-recursive path, which may or may not be related.
- One hypothesis worth checking: post-burst work on the session main thread (e.g. code-search indexing of the changed files) starving file-monitor callback dispatch; the recovery after tens of seconds is consistent with that, but this needs proper instrumentation.

Not a regression from #18259 (the backend never emitted the event; that change is client-side only), but the faster client makes the window easier to hit.

title: IDE unresponsive after thousands of git-tracked files change at once
description:
### Problem

When a large number of git-tracked files change at once (e.g. moving/committing ~5000 files), the IDE UI grinds to a halt for a minute or more, with progress spinners across multiple panes.

### Analysis

The file monitor delivers the changes as a single batch, and the backend computes git status once per batch (good). But from there:

1. The backend fans the batch out into **one `file_changed` client event per file** (`enqueFileChangedEvents`, `src/cpp/session/SessionModuleContext.cpp`), so ~5000 individual events are streamed to the client.
2. On the client, `VcsState.onFileChange` handles **each** event by linearly scanning the entire status list to find the matching path, then firing a `VcsRefreshEvent` -- so N events cost O(N^2) scans and emit up to N refresh events (`VcsState.java`).
3. Each `VcsRefreshEvent` causes `GitChangelistTablePresenter` to call `ChangelistTable.setItems()`, which sets the page size to the full item count, clears the backing list, re-adds every row, and re-sorts -- a full rebuild of a 5000-row CellTable on the UI thread, once per event (`ChangelistTable.java`).

The net effect is O(N^2) DOM work on the single GWT UI thread, which starves every other pane's rendering and progress indicators.

The Files pane already solved this same problem for itself: `FilesList` debounces its redraw with a 100ms timer. The VCS changelist path has no equivalent debounce or coalescing.

### Proposed fix

In `VcsState`, coalesce incoming file-change events: buffer them, apply them to the status list in a single pass (map lookup instead of a linear scan per event), and fire a single debounced `VcsRefreshEvent` per burst. This collapses ~5000 changelist table rebuilds into one or two.

Possible follow-ups (not required for the main fix):

- Batch the backend `file_changed` fan-out into a single client event carrying an array.
- Paginate or virtualize the changelist table for very large changelists.

### Workaround

Unchecking Tools -> Global Options -> Git/SVN -> "Enable automatic refresh of Git status" (`vcs_autorefresh`) avoids the per-file decoration/refresh path.

title: Files pane: follow Windows .lnk shortcuts and show a link indicator
description:
### Problem

On Windows, the Files pane treats `.lnk` shortcuts as opaque files:

- Clicking a shortcut to a **folder** shows an error instead of navigating into the folder.
- Clicking a shortcut to a **file** opens the `.lnk` file's binary contents in the editor instead of the document it points to.
- Nothing distinguishes a shortcut row from a regular file.

Earlier reports of this: #7327 and #8514. This had been fixed in the Qt version of RStudio but broke again when we switched to Electron.

### Proposal

Bring Windows shortcuts to parity with the recently added macOS Finder alias support (#18158) and the link indicator (#9924):

- Resolve `.lnk` shortcuts during Files pane listings: clicking a shortcut to a folder navigates to that folder; clicking (or using Open on) a shortcut to a file opens the target file. File open dialogs and target-based file-type icons follow the target as well.
- Show the link indicator badge on shortcut rows (as symbolic links and Finder aliases get), labeled "Shortcut", with a `name -> target` tooltip.
- Broken shortcuts (target deleted) and shortcuts without a file-system target (e.g. Control Panel applets) keep the badge but otherwise behave as plain files.
- Resolution must not hit the disk, network, or show UI during listings (no `IShellLink::Resolve`); network targets are never probed, so a disconnected share cannot stall the session.

### System details

    RStudio Edition : server
    RStudio Version : latest, likely many prior
    OS Version      : all

### Steps to reproduce the problem

No identified code paths are currently impacted by this, hypothetical improvement only.

Two fields are not copied/moved from Request to Request when it is `assign()`ed:
* `rootPath_`
* `handlerPrefix_`

Lack of copying these fields doesn't cause bugs as discussed below, but the intent is for all fields to be copied/transferred, and esp. in the case of `handlerPrefix_` there's potential for surprise future misbehavior.

### Why this doesn't cause tangible bugs today

**rootPath_**
since rootPath_ is only ever set once at request creation (from server config) and never mutated per-request, omitting it from assign is likely benign in practice — a copied/moved Request would just fall back to reading X-RStudio-Root-Path from headers (which is copied via Message::assign) rather than the stored default. It's really only a latent bug if some code path calls setRootPath() on a Request after creation and before it gets assigned into another Request.

**handlerPrefix_**
Currently there's no caller of handlerPrefix() (basically the getter for handlerPrefix_) anywhere in this repo — not in core, session, or server. It's set on every request but never consumed on the open-source side.

title: Data Viewer: mouse-wheel scrolling over the table body gets stuck on Windows
description:
### Description

On Windows, after `View(iris)` (or any data frame), vertical scrolling with a mouse wheel gets "stuck" at various points in the dataset when the pointer is over the table body. Scrolling works normally when the pointer is over the row names (the pinned/frozen pane).

### Cause

The data viewer grid is virtualized: as the user scrolls, the rendered row window is replaced and the top spacer row is resized. `#gridViewport` does not opt out of browser scroll anchoring, so Chromium adjusts `scrollTop` to compensate for the content shift above the anchor node, undoing the user's wheel scroll.

This is most visible on Windows because discrete mouse-wheel ticks are driven through Chromium's smooth-scroll animation, leaving a window between ticks where the spacer resize happens and anchoring snaps the position back. Scrolling over the row names works because the pinned pane mirrors its scroll position onto the viewport programmatically on every scroll event, overriding the anchoring adjustment.

The virtualized summary sidebar received the equivalent fix (`overflow-anchor: none`) in #17977, but the grid viewport and pinned pane did not.

### Fix

Add `overflow-anchor: none` to `#gridViewport` and `#pinnedPane` in `DataViewer.css`.

title: rpcs can fail with "unable to connect to service" for 30s+ after session suspend
description:
### Symptom

After a session suspend (observed with a forced `suspendSession`, but any suspend that races an incoming request should qualify), RPCs sent to the session can fail with

```
Error: jsonrpc error 1 (Unable to connect to service)
```

for 30 seconds or more, even though nothing is wrong with the session itself -- the very next RPC after the failures relaunches the session and succeeds within a couple of seconds. In the IDE this surfaces as the error above printed in the console when the user types during the window; in CI it surfaced as the `session_suspend.test.ts` e2e failure on PR #18203 (run 29273786621-1, server-linux).

### Root cause

rserver already buffers proxied RPCs across a session restart: `proxyRpcRequest` attaches `sessionRetryProfile` (`ServerSessionProxy.cpp`), which retries the session connection every 25ms for up to `rsession-proxy-max-wait-secs` (default 30s) and, on the **first** failed attempt, relaunches the session via `launchSessionRecovery`.

The failure mode is a stuck state in that recovery path:

1. The first post-suspend RPC's `launchSession` races the still-exiting suspended session and the launched process dies (or never becomes connectable), but the launch is recorded in `pendingLaunches_`.
2. `SessionManager::launchSession` returns early ("launch already pending") for any pending entry younger than **one minute** (`ServerSessionManager.cpp`, `launchSession`), and `launchSessionRecovery` only launches when `firstAttempt` is true -- so neither the remaining 30s of that RPC's polling nor any subsequently arriving RPC re-attempts the launch. Every request buffered in this window burns its full 30s and fails with `errc::ConnectionError` (mapped to "jsonrpc error 1").
3. The stale entry is only cleared when a failing RPC's `handleRpcError` calls `removePendingLaunch` (`ServerSessionProxy.cpp`) -- which is why the *next* RPC after the 30s failures relaunches successfully.

Timeline evidence from the failing e2e trace: two console inputs submitted at 18:46:01 and 18:46:03 both returned the JSON-RPC ConnectionError envelope ~30s later; a third input at 18:46:33 (immediately after the first error handler cleared the pending launch) relaunched the session and succeeded.

### Proposed fix

Make the buffered-RPC recovery self-healing instead of one-shot:

- Re-attempt `launchSession` from the retry loop rather than only on the first attempt, letting the `pendingLaunches_` bookkeeping dedupe concurrent launches.
- Treat a pending launch as stale once its launched process is known to be dead (local launches can observe child exit), rather than relying on the fixed one-minute age check.

The e2e-side false-pass that let a test wedge on this window was fixed separately in #18207.

title: `install.packages()` hook with URL and `repos = NULL` emits tar errors/warnings
description:
### System details

RStudio Edition: Desktop
RStudio Version: 2026.01.0+392.pro5 (reproducible in all later releases; NOT reproducible in 2025.09.2+418.pro4 and earlier)
OS Version: macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon)
R Version: 4.6.1 (`brew install --cask r-app`)

### Steps to reproduce the problem

In the RStudio console, install a source package directly from a URL and set `repos = NULL`:

```r
install.packages("https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/RECA_1.7.1.tar.gz", repos = NULL)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

The package installs successfully, but after `* DONE (RECA)`, tar errors are printed to the console along with three warnings:

```text
* DONE (RECA)
tar: https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/RECA_1.7.1.tar.gz: m: No such file or directory
tar: https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/RECA_1.7.1.tar.gz: m: No such file or directory
Warning messages:
1: In system(cmd, intern = TRUE) :
  running command '/usr/bin/tar -tf 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/RECA_1.7.1.tar.gz'' had status 1
2: In min(n) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
3: In untar(packagePath, files = descPath, exdir = tmpdir) :
  '/usr/bin/tar -xf 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/RECA_1.7.1.tar.gz' -C '/var/.../T//RtmpXhnehM/description-...'' returned error code 1
```

The cause appears to be the package source recording feature added to the `install.packages()` hook in `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionPackages.R`.

When `repos = NULL`, the install is treated as "local", and after the install the hook calls `.rs.readPackageDescription(pkgs)` with the user's original `pkgs` argument. When `pkgs` is a URL rather than a local file path, `.rs.readPackageDescriptionFromArchive()` calls `untar(<URL>, list = TRUE)` and then `untar(<URL>, files = descPath, exdir = tmpdir)`, passing the URL to the system tar as if it were a local archive path. This produces the output above:

- Warning 1 comes from the `untar(list = TRUE)` call shelling out to `/usr/bin/tar -tf <URL>`.
- Warning 2 comes from `descPath <- descPaths[n == min(n)]` operating on the empty listing.
- Warning 3 comes from the extraction attempt, and the subsequent `read.dcf()` error is silently caught by the hook's `tryCatch()`, so no source is recorded.

This issue is not reproducible with `utils::install.packages()` called directly or in terminal R, on the same R/macOS setup.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Installing a source package from a URL with `repos = NULL` completes without tar errors or warnings, as it does in terminal R and in RStudio <= 2025.09.2. If the post-install source recording cannot handle a URL input, it should skip quietly rather than surface tar errors and warnings for a successful install.

title: Update build pipeline to Visual Studio 2026 (remove VS 2026 CI stopgaps from #17850)
description:
#17850 patched the toolchain so Windows Desktop e2e CI can build on the `windows-2025` GitHub runner after it migrated from Visual Studio 2022 to Visual Studio 2026 (see [actions/runner-images#14017](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14017)). Those changes are deliberately stopgaps to unblock CI; the regular/production build pipeline should be updated to VS 2026 properly.

**Stopgaps landed in #17850 that should be revisited:**

- **Boost / SOCI prebuilts (`src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`):** the runner reports `MSVC_TOOLSET_VERSION=145` (VS 2026), but only `msvc143` prebuilts exist on S3. CMake currently falls back to the `msvc143` directory and relies on MSVC 14.x binary compatibility. We should publish proper `msvc145` Boost and SOCI prebuilts and drop the fallback (or keep it only as a safety net).
- **`find_package(Boost)` bypass:** CMake 4.x removed `FindBoost.cmake` (CMP0167), so the Windows path now wires up `Boost_INCLUDE_DIRS` directly. Confirm this is the desired long-term approach (vs. Boost's own config package).
- **install-soci.R generator:** the workflow passes `CMAKE_GENERATOR=Visual Studio 18 2026`. The default generator in the script should be updated once VS 2026 is the standard toolchain.
- **node-gyp v12 (`src/node/desktop/package.json` override + workflow step):** npm's bundled node-gyp (v11) only recognizes VS 2017-2022. The `@electron/node-gyp -> node-gyp@^12` override and the bundled-node-gyp replacement step exist to support VS 2026's native rebuild.

**To close:**
- Update the production build dependencies (Boost/SOCI prebuilts) to target the VS 2026 toolset.
- Update the build scripts/generators to VS 2026 and remove or simplify the CI workarounds above.
- Confirm Jenkins build agents are on a supported toolchain.

Tracking follow-up to #17850.

title: Posit Assistant test-manifest banner intermittently missing at startup (client_init clears startup events)
description:
## Summary

With the `posit_assistant_test_manifest` user preference (or the `--posit-assistant-test-manifest` session option) enabled, RStudio is supposed to show a warning bar at startup reading:

> Posit Assistant is using the pre-release (test) manifest. Do not use for production work.

The banner appears **intermittently**. On some starts it is missing even though the preference is clearly in effect (other test-manifest behavior confirms it). Quitting and restarting usually makes it reappear.

This is a genuine startup race: the banner is delivered as a startup client event, and that event can be silently discarded by the `client_init` handler when startup requests are processed in an unlucky order.

## Root cause

**1. The banner is enqueued from deferred init.** `chat::onDeferredInit` (`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp:4032`) calls `showTestManifestWarning()` (`SessionChat.cpp:4021`), which does `enqueClientEvent(kShowWarningBar)`.

**2. Deferred init runs lazily, coupled to the "session initialized" flag.** `onDeferredInit` is fired by `rDeferredInit` -> `completeDeferredSessionInit` (`src/cpp/r/session/RInit.cpp`), which only runs when `ensureDeserialized()` (`RInit.cpp:399`) is invoked. That happens inside `ensureSessionInitialized()` (`src/cpp/session/SessionInit.cpp:45-69`), in this order:

```cpp
s_sessionInitialized = true;                 // line 64
rstudio::r::session::ensureDeserialized();   // line 69 -> onDeferredInit -> enqueues the banner
```

So **whichever request first calls `ensureSessionInitialized()` both flips the flag and enqueues the banner.**

**3. `client_init` clears the pending event queue if it thinks it is a "re-join."** `handleClientInit` (`src/cpp/session/SessionClientInit.cpp:207-228`):

```cpp
bool resumed = suspend::sessionResumed();
bool isSessionInitialized = init::isSessionInitialized();   // line 208
if (isSessionInitialized)
   resumed = true;                                          // "re-join"
bool clearEvents = resumed;
clientEventService().setClientId(clientId, clearEvents);    // clears pending events
```

`setClientId(..., true)` calls `clientEventQueue().clear()` (`src/cpp/session/SessionClientEventService.cpp:141-142`), wiping every pending client event.

## Why it is intermittent

It comes down to **which request first calls `ensureSessionInitialized()`** in the R main thread's `waitForMethod` loop (`src/cpp/session/SessionHttpMethods.cpp:500-600`):

- **Good ordering (banner shows):** `client_init` is the first request to trigger it. It reads `isSessionInitialized() == false` at `SessionClientInit.cpp:208` -> `clearEvents == false` -> nothing is cleared. Then at the end of the handler (`SessionClientInit.cpp:736`) it calls `ensureSessionInitialized()`, which enqueues the banner. The banner survives and is delivered on the client's first `get_events`.

- **Bad ordering (banner missing):** Some other request reaches `handleConnection` -> `ensureSessionInitialized()` first (`SessionHttpMethods.cpp:660`/`666`), or a second/reload `client_init` occurs (e.g. the language/dialog-cookie reload at `src/gwt/.../application/Application.java:1107-1111`). That flips the flag and enqueues the banner. The subsequent `client_init` now reads `isSessionInitialized() == true` -> treats itself as a re-join -> `clearEvents == true` -> `clientEventQueue().clear()` wipes the just-enqueued banner. The final `ensureSessionInitialized()` at line 736 is a no-op, so the banner is never re-enqueued.

The clearing logic was designed with this class of event in mind: the comment at `SessionClientInit.cpp:216-218` explicitly says it drops "events queued up by R during startup (e.g. printing of the banner)." The **R startup banner is subject to the same race**; the Posit Assistant warning just made it visible.

"Quit and restart usually fixes it" is consistent: a restart re-runs boot with different timing, usually landing in the good ordering.

## The actual defect

`SessionClientInit.cpp:213` uses `isSessionInitialized()` as a proxy for "a client already connected." But that flag can flip true before/during the very first `client_init` (because it is set lazily by the first request that triggers `ensureSessionInitialized()`), misclassifying the first client as a re-join and clearing its startup events.

## Confirming diagnostic

Every `client_init` logs its classification at `SessionClientInit.cpp:210`:

```
Begin /rpc/client_init for client: <id>: initialized: 0 resumed: 0
```

With session protocol debug logging enabled, a "no banner" start should show a `client_init` with `initialized: 1` (preceded by another request's log), while a working start shows `initialized: 0`.

## Possible fix directions

1. **Fix re-join detection (broadest).** Track whether a `client_init` has actually completed before, and use that (plus `sessionResumed()`) instead of `isSessionInitialized()` to decide `clearEvents`. Precisely fixes the misclassification for the first client and also fixes the general R-banner startup-event race. Touches core startup, so needs care/testing.
2. **Decouple the banner (feature-scoped).** Deliver the test-manifest warning independent of the fragile startup queue (e.g. include it in `sessionInfo` on `client_init`, or re-fire it from `onClientInit`). Low blast radius; does not address the general startup-event race.

## Affected files (reference)

- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp` (banner enqueue: `onDeferredInit`, `showTestManifestWarning`)
- `src/cpp/session/SessionInit.cpp` (`ensureSessionInitialized` sets flag then runs deferred init)
- `src/cpp/session/SessionClientInit.cpp` (re-join detection + event-queue clear)
- `src/cpp/session/SessionClientEventService.cpp` (`setClientId` clears the queue)
- `src/cpp/session/SessionHttpMethods.cpp` (`waitForMethod` / `handleConnection` call `ensureSessionInitialized`)

title: Per-user install of RStudio on Windows doesn't uninstall cleanly
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2023.12.0+369 (likely a problem with any version we've ever released)
    OS Version      : Windows-11
    R Version       : Any

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Install RStudio Desktop on Windows, per-user. The setup wizard doesn't provide this option, but it can be forced, e.g. https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8598#issuecomment-1883610096. Customers have reported that this also happens on their domain-connected PCs, likely due to a group policy (though I haven't hunted down the exact group policy).

A per-user install won't ask for elevation (i.e. no UAC prompt).

- The program bits are installed to `%localappdata%\Programs\RStudio`
- The start menu entry is at `%appdata%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\RStudio`
- The add/remove data is in the registry under `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\RStudio`

Now uninstall via Add/Remove programs.

### Describe the problem in detail

First, you get prompted to elevate (UAC), which shouldn't be necessary. If you do that and proceed, the program bits are removed, but the start menu entry and the add/remove data is not removed.

So now there is a broken add/remove entry for RStudio, and a broken Start Menu entry. Only way to recover is to manually delete these.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Uninstalling a per-user install shouldn't require UAC, and it should fully clean up after itself.

title: Update maximum tested R version (RSTUDIO_R_VERSION_MAXIMUM) to 4.6.1
description:
### Summary

The maximum tested R version in `cmake/globals.cmake` is stale. It is currently set to `4.6.0`:

```cmake
set(RSTUDIO_R_VERSION_MAXIMUM "4.6.0")
set(RSTUDIO_R_MAJOR_VERSION_MAXIMUM 4)
set(RSTUDIO_R_MINOR_VERSION_MAXIMUM 6)
set(RSTUDIO_R_PATCH_VERSION_MAXIMUM 0)
```

R 4.6.1 was released on 2026-06-24 and is now the latest R 4.6.x. This constant should be bumped to `4.6.1`.

### Background

This value is a "tested with" ceiling, not a hard version gate. It does not block RStudio from starting, and R 4.6.1 on its own works fine in RStudio. The constant is consumed in only two places:

- `src/cpp/session/SessionMain.cpp` (~line 604): logs a warning ("...newer than the maximum version of R tested with this version of RStudio...") when the running R exceeds the maximum. Log-only; no user-facing effect.
- `src/node/desktop/src/main/gwt-callback.ts`, `addRVersionTooNewError()` (~line 1187): adds a note to the desktop launch-error page ("The version of R you are using (R x.y.z) is newer than the maximum version of R supported by this version of RStudio...").

Importantly, the desktop message is only produced when the launch-error page requests the `launch_failed` diagnostic, which happens only when the rsession process fails to launch for some other reason. In that situation the note is prepended to the actual launch-failure message. With the maximum stuck at `4.6.0`, any user running R 4.6.1 (or newer) who hits an unrelated startup failure will see this note appended to their error page, which is misleading since the R version is not the cause.

### Proposed change

Bump the maximum to the current released R version (4.6.1) in `cmake/globals.cmake`. This should be revisited each time a newer R is released.

title: Add rserver --setup-db
description:
## Problem

Before Workbench can start against PostgreSQL, an admin must manually create the database, a service user, and the right grants. That includes the PostgreSQL 15+ `GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public` step. It's easy to miss, and skipping it fails silently at first start with a permission error that looks like a product bug. The docs now show the exact SQL (see the PostgreSQL configuration page), but running it is still a manual step.

## Proposal

Add a `--setup-db` flag to `rserver`, plus a `rstudio-server setup-db` wrapper. `--check-config`/`rstudio-server check-config` already work this way: same flag, two entry points. Running `setup-db`:

1. Gets the PostgreSQL host, port, and master username via an interactive prompt. The master password can come from `--master-password-file <path>` (reads the first line of the file, for admins injecting secrets via a mounted file such as a Kubernetes Secret volume), the `RSERVER_SETUP_DB_MASTER_PASSWORD` environment variable, or a masked prompt, in that order of precedence. It's never accepted as a plain CLI argument.
2. Prompts for the database/user name. Default is `rstudio-os` for this repo, `rstudio` when built as part of Workbench.
3. Connects as the master user and runs, one statement at a time so each step can be reported individually:
   ```sql
   CREATE DATABASE "<db>";
   CREATE USER "<user>" WITH PASSWORD '<generated>';
   GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE "<db>" TO "<user>";
   -- connected to <db>:
   GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO "<user>";
   ```
4. Is idempotent. If the database or user already exists, that step is reported as informational, not a failure, so it's safe to re-run.
5. Generates a strong service-user password. By default it writes the resulting connection string straight into `database.conf`, created with `0600` permissions, and never prints the password. Two opt-in flags change that: `--print-only` skips the config write and writes the same fields to a standalone `0600` credentials file instead; `--show-password` prints the generated password to stdout, clearly marked as sensitive, for admins who want it inline, for example to pipe into their own secrets tooling, rather than read from a file. The two can be combined.
6. Prints a reminder that Workbench needs to be restarted to pick up the change. It won't guess how: these run under systemd, containers, or whatever process manager the admin already uses.

## Why this repo

`database.conf`, `DatabaseConstants.hpp`, and the database-initialization path in `ServerMain.cpp` live and function here. None of it is Pro-exclusive plumbing. So the flag and its core create-db/user/grant logic belong here, the same way `--check-config`'s base implementation did. A follow-up in rstudio-pro will add audit-database setup on top, through the same overlay extension point `--check-config` already uses for downstream builds.

## Acceptance criteria

- `rserver --setup-db` and `rstudio-server setup-db` both work and produce identical behavior.
- Re-running against an already-set-up database reports informational, not failing, output.
- The master password can be supplied via file, environment variable, or prompt. The generated password is never shown unless `--show-password` is explicitly passed.
- Default database/user name is correct both standalone and when built as part of Workbench.

Part of ITGP-39 (C-06).

title: visual editor activation can hang indefinitely on the loading spinner
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Open Source
    RStudio Version : dev (observed on main and recent PR branches, 2026-07-02)
    OS Version      : Ubuntu 24.04 (GitHub Actions), desktop and server e2e projects

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Intermittent; observed in CI in the `quarto.test.ts` e2e test ("render quarto document"): create a `.qmd`, type YAML + a couple of paragraphs and an R chunk in source mode, then toggle to visual mode. Occasionally the editor shows the panmirror loading spinner and never mounts (`.ProseMirror` never appears) -- the e2e helper's 90s wait expires. A retry of the same test passes in ~15s.

Examples (same signature on unrelated branches, so not caused by those changes):

- [Run 28614679201](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/28614679201), `linux-desktop / e2e-desktop-ubuntu (1)` -- flaky (failed first attempt)
- [Run 28608398057](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/28608398057), `linux-desktop / e2e-desktop-ubuntu (1)` -- same
- Run 28614679201, `linux-server / e2e-server-ubuntu (1)` -- same signature in the server project

### Analysis so far

From the Playwright trace of the failing attempt in run 28614679201 (artifact `test-results-linux-desktop-1`, `panes-editor-quarto-Quarto-render-quarto-document-desktop-linux/trace.zip`):

- The visual-mode toggle click registered: the toggle shows pressed and the source pane shows the panmirror loading spinner for the full 90s (screenshot in the artifact).
- The network trace shows `pandoc_get_capabilities` and `pandoc_list_extensions` were issued and completed successfully, but the init never proceeded to the bibliography/zotero RPCs or `pandoc_markdown_to_ast`. No RPC was left pending and none returned an error status.
- The rsession logs for that spec's data home contain nothing in the failure window -- no server-side errors.
- No uncaught client exception was recorded (the e2e fixture fails a test outright when `window.rstudio.errors` is non-empty, and it did not).

So this looks like a silent client-side stall in visual editor activation -- a promise between the pandoc capabilities/extensions queries and the initial `setMarkdown` conversion that never resolves. Distinct from the toggle-timing race fixed in #18038 (activation *starts* here, then stalls).

Next step is probably a `-style PRETTY` e2e run to catch the stall point, or instrumentation around editor creation between the capabilities query and `setMarkdown`.

title: Run Selection as Background Job does nothing from detached source window on Windows
description:
### System details

* RStudio IDE: 2026.01.1 Build 403
* OS: Windows
* R version: (fill in)
* Mode: Desktop

### Description

When using a detached (popped-out) source window, the **Run Selection as Background Job** command silently fails. The same command works as expected when the file is open in the main source pane.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open an `.R` script.
2. Detach the script into its own source window (**Move to New Window**).
3. Select one or more lines of valid R code.
4. Invoke **Code → Run Selection as Background Job** (or the equivalent command).
5. Observe the result.

### Expected behavior

A background job is created that executes the selected code, just as it does when the script is open in the main RStudio window.

### Actual behavior

Nothing happens:

* No background job is created.
* No error message is displayed.
* No warning or notification appears.
* The command simply has no visible effect.

### Additional information

* The issue appears to be specific to detached source windows.
* Running the same selected code from the main RStudio source pane works correctly.
* Because there is no error message, it's difficult to determine whether the command is unsupported in detached windows or whether this is an IDE bug.

title: Missing-package banner may not reappear when "Detect missing R packages" is toggled back on
description:
After dismissing the editor's missing-packages banner with "Don't show for this file" and then re-enabling it via the **Toggle Detect Missing Packages** command (command palette), the banner sometimes fails to reappear even though the document still references uninstalled packages.

This is a client-side race in `TextEditingTargetWidget.toggleDetectMissingPackages`:

```java
docUpdateSentinel_.setProperty(DISABLE_DEPENDENCY_DISCOVERY, "0");
target_.getPackageDependencyHelper().discoverPackageDependencies();
```

`DocUpdateSentinel.setProperty` only applies the new value to the local property bag in the `modify_document_properties` RPC's `onResponseReceived`. The `discover_package_dependencies` RPC is issued concurrently, and its response handler (`TextEditingTargetWidget.showRequiredPackagesMissingWarning`) reads the local property and silently returns if it still says `"1"`. If the discovery response arrives before the property-modification response — realistic over rserver-proxied HTTP — the banner is never shown and nothing retries.

This is also the cause of intermittent failures of the e2e test `missing_packages_banner.test.ts` ("dismisses per-file and re-appears when toggleDetectMissingPackages is flipped back on") on server-linux CI.

The fix is to re-run discovery only after the property write has completed and been applied locally.

title: Visual editor breaks for the rest of the session when a document is closed while its markdown conversion is in flight
description:
### Symptom

Closing a visual-mode document (e.g. a freshly created Quarto document) while its markdown conversion is still in flight throws an uncaught client exception:

```
java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: -1, Size: 1
  at DocTabLayoutPanel.getTabWidget
  at SourcePane.setDirty (SourcePane.java:185)
  at SourceColumn.lambda (SourceColumn.java:562)   // dirtyState ValueChangeHandler
  ...
  at VisualMode.withSwitchConfirmation continuation (VisualMode.java:590 -> markDirty)
```

Worse than the exception itself: `VisualMode.setMarkdownQueue_` is a **static** `PreemptiveTaskQueue` shared by all editors. The exception fires inside the async `setMarkdown` continuation, before the task's `done` command runs, so the queue's `processing_` flag never clears (its try/catch only covers synchronous exceptions). From that point on, every `setMarkdown` task from any editor queues behind the dead task and never executes -- the visual editor hangs at the progress spinner for all subsequently opened documents until the IDE is reloaded.

### Root cause

`SourceColumn.addTab` registers four handlers on the `EditingTarget` (name, dirtyState, ensureVisible, close) whose lambdas capture the tab `Widget`. Their `HandlerRegistration`s are discarded, and `closeTabIndex` never detaches them, so they outlive the tab. When the visual editor's `withSwitchConfirmation` continuation calls `markDirty()` after the tab was closed (the new-Quarto-doc template is not in pandoc canonical form, so `markDirty` runs on every fresh visual-mode open), the stale dirtyState handler calls `display_.setDirty(widget, ...)` with a widget no longer in the panel; `getWidgetIndex` returns -1 and `getTabWidget(-1)` throws.

### Reproduction

1. File > New File > Quarto Document (visual editor enabled, the default), accept the wizard.
2. Close the tab (don't save) quickly, before the visual editor finishes its pandoc round-trip.
3. Open another Quarto/R Markdown document in visual mode: it never finishes loading.

Deterministically reproduced by the e2e tests in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/create_file_types.test.ts` (Quarto document, Quarto presentation, R Markdown), which create a doc and immediately reset the source pane. The exception previously went unreported because it fired inside a native promise continuation; #18137 made those surface to the uncaught-exception handler, which is why these tests now fail (flaky on all platforms, consistently on server-linux).

### Fix

Retain the `HandlerRegistration`s created in `SourceColumn.addTab` and detach them when the tab is removed in `closeTabIndex`, so a dismissed/moved editing target can no longer drive the column's display with a stale widget.

title: IndexOutOfBoundsException in SourcePane.setDirty when creating Quarto / R Markdown documents
description:
### Description

Creating a new Quarto document, Quarto presentation, or R Markdown document can raise an uncaught client exception:

```
IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: -1, Size: 1
```

thrown from `DocTabLayoutPanel.getTabWidget()`, via `SourcePane.setDirty()` (`SourcePane.java:185`). The dirty-state `ValueChangeHandler` registered in `SourceColumn.java:561` captures the tab's `Widget` and calls `display_.setDirty(widget, ...)`; the exception fires when that widget is not present in the tab panel (`getWidgetIndex()` returns -1). The triggering stack runs through the visual editor's switch-confirmation continuation (`VisualMode.withSwitchConfirmation`, `VisualMode.java:590`) -> `markDirty` -> dirty-state `ValueChangeEvent` -- i.e. the document is marked dirty at a moment when the captured widget is not (or not yet / no longer) in the panel. When this happens, the tab's dirty indicator is silently dropped.

The exception itself likely predates its visibility: #18137 (`0efacc4153d`, "report exceptions thrown from native promise continuations") made exceptions thrown inside native promise continuations reach the uncaught-exception handler, where previously they were swallowed.

### Impact on CI

The e2e Playwright fixture fails any test that raises an uncaught client exception, so since #18137 merged this destabilizes the `create_file_types.test.ts` document-creation tests on every PR -- flaky (passes on retry) on desktop-linux/macos/windows, and reliably failing on server-linux. Example reports from unrelated PRs with identical signatures:

- https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18144/28716085451-1/all-platforms/index.html
- https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18142/28696836300-1/all-platforms/index.html

### Reproduction

Run the e2e suite against a recent main build:

```
npx playwright test tests/panes/editor/create_file_types.test.ts
```

The `create Quarto document via newQuartoDoc`, `create Quarto presentation via newQuartoPres`, and `create R Markdown document via newRMarkdownDoc` tests fail intermittently (most reliably on server-linux) with the exception above.

### Suggested direction

Find why the captured widget is absent from the tab panel when the visual-mode `markDirty` fires (stale handler after tab close/move, or handler firing before tab insertion) and fix the root cause; failing that, `SourcePane.setDirty()` should tolerate a widget that is not in the panel rather than throwing.

title: Object Explorer emits "Setting class(x) to \"environment\"" warnings for S4 objects wrapping environments
description:
### Description

Opening an object in the Object Explorer (e.g. via `View()`) emits warnings when the object contains S4 objects that wrap environments — for example, reference class (R5) instances, or instances of S4 classes defined with `contains = "environment"`:

```
Warning messages:
1: In class(object) <- "environment" :
  Setting class(x) to "environment" sets attribute to NULL; result will no longer be an S4 object
```

One warning is emitted per such object described by the explorer.

### Reproduction

```r
Gen <- setRefClass("MyRC", fields = list(x = "numeric"))
obj <- list(a = Gen$new(x = 1), b = Gen$new(x = 2))
View(obj)
# expand the list in the Object Explorer; warnings appear in the console
```

### Cause

`.rs.explorer.objectDesc()` in `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionObjectExplorer.R` describes environments by temporarily assigning `class(object) <- "environment"`, printing, and restoring the previous class. For S4 objects wrapping environments, `typeof(x)` is `"S4"` rather than `"environment"`, so the assignment emits the warning above and then errors; the error is swallowed by a surrounding `tryCatch()`, but the warning escapes to the console, and no description is produced. Additionally, because environments have reference semantics, the temporary class assignment mutates the user's actual object rather than a copy.

title: concurrent local e2e runs kill each other via shared CDP port cleanup
description:
### Problem

The desktop e2e fixture computes each worker's CDP port as `9231 + workerIndex` and, at worker startup, frees the port with:

```ts
execSync(`lsof -ti :${CDP_PORT} | xargs kill -9 2>/dev/null`, { stdio: 'ignore' });
```

(`e2e/rstudio/fixtures/desktop.fixture.ts`, ~line 357)

Two consequences when a second `npm run test:desktop` starts from another checkout/worktree on the same machine:

1. Both runs land on the same port band, so the newcomer's cleanup kills the first run's RStudio instance.
2. Worse, `lsof -ti :port` matches **both ends** of a TCP connection, so it also SIGKILLs the first run's Playwright *worker process* (its CDP client socket has the port as remote port). The victim run reports a test failing at 0ms with `worker process exited unexpectedly (code=null, signal=SIGKILL)`, and the replacement worker's own cleanup then cascades into `Target page, context or browser has been closed` on the next test.

Observed while verifying #18133: two runs from different worktrees repeatedly killed each other's workers on unrelated, fully-local tests; the same specs passed 11/11 once isolated with `PW_CDP_PORT=9351`.

### Possible fixes

- Narrow the kill to the listener only: `lsof -ti :${CDP_PORT} -sTCP:LISTEN` -- kills a leftover RStudio from a prior interrupted run (the stated intent of the comment above the cleanup) without touching another run's connected client processes.
- Derive the port band per checkout (e.g. hash of the repo root path) so concurrent runs from different worktrees don't collide at all.
- Probe for a free port instead of assuming the band (the desktop rsession launcher already does this via `findFreePort` after #18013-era work).

The first option is the minimal safe change; the second/third remove the collision entirely.

### Workaround

Set a private band per run: `PW_CDP_PORT=93xx npm run test:desktop -- <spec>`.

title: windows e2e dependency cache can clobber tracked install scripts
description:
### Problem

The Windows e2e build workflow caches `dependencies/common` and `dependencies/windows` wholesale ("Restore rstudio-tools deps" in `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025.yml`). Those directories contain both the downloaded/extracted dependencies (the thing we want to cache) and the *tracked install scripts themselves*. When a PR modifies the install scripts, the exact cache key misses and the `restore-keys` prefix restores a stale cache from main -- whose extraction overwrites the PR's checked-out scripts with main's copies.

The effect is that any PR changing a dependency version silently builds with the *old* scripts. The Boost 1.91 upgrade (#18128) hit this: the build step logged `-- boost 1.90.0 is already installed.` from main's `install-dependencies.cmd` and then failed CMake configure because the Boost 1.91 directories didn't exist.

### Mitigation in place

#18128 adds a `git checkout -- dependencies/common dependencies/windows` step immediately after the cache restore, so tracked files always reflect the PR while the cached (untracked) downloads remain. This works but has to be remembered in every workflow that caches repo-internal paths.

### Proper fixes to consider

1. **Cache only untracked paths**: list the actual download/extract directories in the cache `path` instead of the parent directories, so tracked files never enter the cache. Low effort; the path list needs maintenance as dependencies change (a missed path only costs a re-download).
2. **Move Windows dependencies out of the repo tree**: the macOS/Linux workflows are immune because posix dependencies install into `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT` (e.g. `/opt/rstudio-tools`), outside the checkout. Migrating Windows to an out-of-tree root (e.g. `C:\rstudio-tools`) would eliminate this class of bug and align the platforms, but touches `install-dependencies.cmd`, `RSTUDIO_WINDOWS_DEPENDENCIES_DIR` in `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`, `make-package.bat`, and developer setup docs.

Not an `actions/cache` bug: overwriting on restore is documented, intended behavior; the issue is caching paths that contain tracked sources.

title: provide AWS credentials for uploading build dependencies from GitHub Actions
description:
#18123 adds a `workflow_dispatch` workflow (`os-build-dependencies-windows.yml`) that builds the Windows Boost / SOCI prebuilts consumed by `install-dependencies.cmd`. The workflow can upload the resulting archives directly to the `rstudio-buildtools` S3 bucket, but no AWS credentials are currently available to GitHub Actions in this repository, so the upload step is gated behind an `upload` input that defaults to off.

**What's needed**

- An IAM role assumable via GitHub's OIDC provider (`token.actions.githubusercontent.com`), with its trust policy restricted to this repository (ideally to the `os-build-dependencies-windows.yml` workflow on `main`).
- Permissions: `s3:PutObject` and `s3:PutObjectAcl` on `arn:aws:s3:::rstudio-buildtools/*` (uploads use `--acl public-read`, matching the existing `dependencies/tools/upload-*.sh` scripts).
- The role ARN stored as an Actions secret named `AWS_BUILDTOOLS_UPLOAD_ROLE_ARN` on this repository (the workflow already declares `permissions: id-token: write` and uses `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials`).

**Alternatives considered**

- The repo's existing Actions secrets (`CONNECT_API_KEY`, `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`) are not AWS credentials; the 1Password service account was deliberately scoped to e2e secrets and shouldn't be widened.
- Jenkins has AWS access via `withAWS(role: 'build' / 'ide-build')`, but those roles are assumed from the Jenkins agents' instance profiles and cannot be exported to GitHub Actions. The Jenkins Windows agents are also VS 2022 only, so they cannot produce the msvc145 prebuilts this workflow exists to build (#17986).

**Interim**

Until the role exists, run the workflow with `upload: false` and push the artifacts manually with developer SSO credentials via `dependencies/tools/upload-windows-dependencies.sh` (added in #18123).

Related: #17986.

title: license-manager in Workbench 2026.05.0 is linked against OpenSSL 1.1 on RHEL 9
description:
From https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/11569


🧾 Issue: license-manager in Workbench 2026.05.0 is linked against OpenSSL 1.1 on RHEL 9

Environment:
OS: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 (Plow)
OpenSSL: 3.2.2
Workbench versions tested:
2026.04.0 (working)
2026.05.0+218.pro1 (broken)

🐛 Problem description

After upgrading from Posit Workbench 2026.04.0 to 2026.05.0+218.pro1, the following command fails:

`rstudio-server license-manager status`

with:

```log
error while loading shared libraries: libssl.so.1.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

🔍 Analysis

On RHEL 9, only OpenSSL 3 is available:

openssl version
OpenSSL 3.2.2 4 Jun 2024 (Library: OpenSSL 3.2.2 4 Jun 2024)

No OpenSSL 1.1 compatibility libraries are installed or available in the system repositories.

✔️ Working version (2026.04.0)

`ldd /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/license-manager | grep ssl`

Output:

```
libssl.so.3 => /lib64/libssl.so.3 (0x00007fa0ddbe2000)
```

This version works correctly on RHEL 9 and links only against OpenSSL 3.

❌ Broken version (2026.05.0+218.pro1)

`ldd /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/license-manager | grep ssl`

Output:

```
libssl.so.1.1 => not found
libssl.so.3 => /lib64/libssl.so.3 (0x00007fa5daa3f000)
```

Additionally, `readelf` confirms the binary dependency:

```
NEEDED Shared library: [libssl.so.1.1]
NEEDED Shared library: [libcrypto.so.1.1]
```

📌 Impact

license-manager is unusable on RHEL 9 systems
The rest of Workbench appears to link correctly against OpenSSL 3
This suggests a packaging inconsistency in 2026.05.0 where license-manager is still built against OpenSSL 1.1

🧪 Summary

RHEL 9 does not provide OpenSSL 1.1
2026.04.0 works correctly (OpenSSL 3 only)
2026.05.0+218.pro1 introduces a regression where license-manager depends on OpenSSL 1.1

🙏 Request

Could you please confirm whether this is a packaging issue in 2026.05.0 and provide a corrected build of license-manager linked against OpenSSL 3 for RHEL 9?

title: SQL chunk option lines (`--|`) sent to DB server, breaking MySQL/MariaDB interactive execution
description:
### System details

    RStudio Version : 2026.06.0+242
    OS Version      : macOS 26.5.1
    R Version       : 4.6.0 (2026-04-24)

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Connect to a MySQL or MariaDB server from R:
2. Add a `sql` chunk using the Quarto/knitr cell-option syntax for the connection:
3. Run the chunk interactively (green "Run Current Chunk" arrow).

````qmd
---
format: html
---

```{r}
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(), dbname = "...", host = "...", user = "...", password = "...")
```

```{sql}
--| connection: con
SELECT 1;
```
````

### Describe the problem in detail

RStudio sends the chunk-option comment line `--| connection: con` to the database server as part of the SQL statement. MySQL/MariaDB require at least one whitespace (or control) character after `--` for it to be treated as a comment (https://mariadb.com/docs/server/reference/sql-statements/comment-syntax). Because `--|` has no trailing space, the server parses it as SQL and errors:

```txt
Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near '--| connection: con
SELECT 1' at line 1 [1064]
Failed to execute SQL chunk
```

This is invisible with SQLite/Postgres because they treat `--|` as a comment regardless of the following character.
Working around it with `-- |` (adding a space) satisfies the server but then RStudio no longer recognises the option marker and fails with:

```txt
The 'connection' option (DBI connection) is required for sql chunks.
```

So there is no syntax that works interactively on MariaDB/MySQL.
MariaDB/MySQL do accept `#` as a comment symbol (which has no trailing-space requirement), but Quarto registers only `--` as the SQL comment symbol, so options are always emitted as `--|`; `#|` is not an option.

Discovered in: https://github.com/orgs/quarto-dev/discussions/14636

### Describe the behavior you expected

RStudio should strip cell-option lines (`--|` / `#|`) from the chunk body before sending the SQL to the database server, the same way rendering (knitr) does.
The option line is metadata, not SQL, and should never reach the server.
This keeps interactive execution working across all DBI backends regardless of their comment-syntax rules.

(cc. @juliasilge @cscheid)

- [x] Installed the latest version of RStudio and confirmed the problem persists.
- [x] Provided minimal, reproducible steps.

title: Tech debt: collapse duplicated browser-active cache between RSession.cpp and SessionEnvironment.cpp
description:
## Background

Both `src/cpp/r/session/RSession.cpp` and `src/cpp/session/modules/environment/SessionEnvironment.cpp` keep a file-local `s_browserActive` boolean. RSession's copy is the authoritative source — it's set/cleared from `RReadConsole` based on the prompt regex. SessionEnvironment's copy is a derived cache, only ever updated inside `onConsolePrompt` / `onBeforeExecute` via `s_browserActive = r::session::isBrowseActive();`.

This duplication is a desync class — the two copies *can* diverge, and when they do, the symptoms are silent: bad inputs to `getFunctionContext` and the change-detection conditions in `onConsolePrompt`, missed `kContextDepthChanged` events, and confusing `.rs.isBrowserActive()` query results during debug introspection.

#17487 fixed two specific manifestations of this fragility (top-level breakpoints and multi-line input at the Browse prompt), but didn't tackle the underlying duplication. It's left as a follow-up because it's a larger, separate refactor.

## Proposal

Remove `SessionEnvironment.cpp`'s `s_browserActive` entirely and have all readers (notably `rs_isBrowserActive` and the change-detection / early-return logic in `onConsolePrompt`) call `r::session::isBrowseActive()` directly each time. RSession's copy is already authoritative and updated synchronously from the R callback path, so a direct read can't go stale.

## Acceptance

- `s_browserActive` no longer declared in `SessionEnvironment.cpp`.
- `rs_isBrowserActive()` returns `r::session::isBrowseActive()`.
- Conditions in `onConsolePrompt` and `onBeforeExecute` consult `r::session::isBrowseActive()` instead of a local cache.
- Existing debugger BRAT tests still pass; ideally extend coverage with a stepping-through-multi-line-paste case.

## Out of scope

- Reworking the change-detection conditions in `onConsolePrompt` to be transition-based rather than equality-based (separate, larger discussion).
- Adding a heartbeat / sequence-number reconciliation between server and client for kContextDepthChanged.

Context: forked from PR #17487 review thread.

title: Auto-downloaded Air should not go in `~/.local/lib`
description:
On my Mac, the auto downloaded Air binary goes in `~/.local/lib/air/0.10.0/bin/air`.

This location seems a bit odd to me for two reasons:
- It seems like a bit of an arbitrary location, idk of any other software that uses this
- It isn't obviously owned by RStudio

---

Air's own installer scripts follow the XDG Base Directory Specification for all platforms https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir/latest/. I find this cheatsheet easier to consume https://gist.github.com/roalcantara/107ba66dfa3b9d023ac9329e639bc58c.

We default to `$XDG_BIN_HOME` with a fallback of `$HOME/.local/bin`, so that's why Air's binary ends up in `$HOME/.local/bin/air`. This is also what ruff, ty, and a number of other executables use.

(We should probably put it somewhere else on Windows, but there isn't an obvious place for executables there, and our installer generator doesn't let us change it per platform https://github.com/axodotdev/cargo-dist/issues/288)

I don't think RStudio should put it here, but I'm just showing that the choice of this location wasn't arbitrary and there are some standards for this.

---

I _think_ it would make the most sense for RStudio to use the persistent application "data" locations:

- macOS / Linux: `$XDG_DATA_HOME` with a fallback of `$HOME/.local/share`
- Windows: `~\AppData\Local\`

The Windows location comes from the [Known Folder API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/knownfolderid) and is meant to be a user writable location. It's the location that lines up for `data_local_dir` in the table at the bottom of the readme for this crate, which manages all of this stuff for you on the rust side https://crates.io/crates/dirs.

Within those folders, I think the full paths look like:
- macOS / Linux: `$HOME/.local/share/rstudio/air/0.10.0/air`
- Windows: `~\AppData\Local\rstudio\air\0.10.0\air.exe`

While researching this, I happened to note that RStudio already uses `$HOME/.local/share/rstudio` on my Mac, so I think it would be very natural to add to that! It looks like this is the infrastructure for that, and it already uses the right location on Windows too!

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/38c21eddf8396e73484503207c851c80177d08b1/src/cpp/core/include/core/system/Xdg.hpp#L59-L64

title: Enable GSS support to allow named CSS constants in .ui.xml files
description:
## Summary

RStudio's GWT frontend should enable GSS (GWT Style Sheets) support so that `.ui.xml` files can use `@def` to define named CSS constants. This would reduce duplication of hardcoded color values scattered across many files, and improve maintainability of the styling layer.

## Background

RStudio uses GWT 2.12.2, which fully supports GSS. The codebase already uses some GSS-specific directives (`@eval`, `@external`, `@url`, `@sprite`) — for example, `@eval` is used in ~16 `.ui.xml` files to reference dynamic theme colors from `ThemeColors` and `ThemeFonts` Java classes. However, the `@def` directive (named CSS constants) does not work because GSS mode is not explicitly enabled.

## Motivation

There are approximately 101 `.ui.xml` files with inline `<ui:style>` blocks. Many of these contain hardcoded color values that are repeated across files:

- **Border colors**: `#c0c0c0`, `#909090`, `#BBB`, `#a0a0a0` — repeated 10+ times
- **Text colors**: `#404040`, `#aaa`, `#555` — repeated 8+ times
- **Background colors**: `#f0f0f0`, `#e0e0e0`, `#FFF` — repeated 6+ times

These values are not centralized, making it difficult to maintain consistency or make broad styling changes.

## Proposed Change

1. **Enable GSS** by adding the appropriate configuration property in the `.gwt.xml` module file:

   ```xml
   <set-configuration-property name="CssResource.enableGss" value="true" />
   ```

2. **Validate** that existing `@eval`, `@external`, `@url`, and `@sprite` directives still compile and function correctly with GSS enabled.

3. **Introduce `@def` constants** for commonly repeated values — either locally within individual `.ui.xml` files or via shared style resources — to replace hardcoded color literals.

## Considerations

- Enabling GSS may surface compile errors in existing CSS if any syntax is incompatible with the GSS parser. A thorough build + test pass is needed.
- RStudio uses a custom fork of GWT (`rstudio/gwt`), so any upstream GSS quirks should be verified against that fork.
- The `@eval` directive is already working (suggesting partial GSS support may already be active); enabling GSS formally would unlock `@def` and `@defmixin`.
- This is a good candidate for incremental adoption: enable GSS first, fix any breakage, then introduce `@def` constants file-by-file.

title: Spare pandoc "grid tables" from being automatically reformatted when switching to "Visual" editing mode
description:
Somehow related to #8159, but not the same.

Let's consider the following sample Rmd document:

```
---
title: "Tables in visual editor"
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: 80
---

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------+---------------+
| **Variable**                                                                        | **Description**    | Values        |
+:====================================================================================+:===================+===============+
| variable_name                                                                       | Certain variable   | -   True      |
|                                                                                     | I'm giving         |               |
|                                                                                     | information about  | -   False     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------+---------------+
| other_variable_with_extremely_long_name_that_is_wrapped_in_two_lines_automatically  | Additional         | -   More      |
|                                                                                     | variable with      |               |
|                                                                                     | extremely long and | -   bullet    |
|                                                                                     | detailed           |               |
|                                                                                     | information that   | -   points    |
|                                                                                     | requires extra     |               |
|                                                                                     | column width       |               |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------+---------------+

```

Here you can see how I have a table that:

* Is formatted as a "grid table" by the visual editor automatically, due to the use of bullet points in one column.
* Needs a very wide column, due to a value that needs to be written "as is", without text wrapping inside the cell.

When I have this case, and I turn on the visual editor mode, this reformats the whole table in order to apply the 80-charecter-width line wrapping to the whole table, resulting in:

```
+-------------------------------------------------+-------------+-------------+
| **Variable**                                    | **De        | Values      |
|                                                 | scription** |             |
+:================================================+:============+=============+
| variable_name                                   | Certain     | -   True    |
|                                                 | variable    |             |
|                                                 | I'm giving  | -   False   |
|                                                 | information |             |
|                                                 | about       |             |
+-------------------------------------------------+-------------+-------------+
| other_variable_with_extremely_long_             | Additional  | -   More    |
| name_that_is_wrapped_in_two_lines_automatically | variable    |             |
|                                                 | with        | -   bullet  |
|                                                 | extremely   |             |
|                                                 | long and    | -   points  |
|                                                 | detailed    |             |
|                                                 | information |             |
|                                                 | that        |             |
|                                                 | requires    |             |
|                                                 | extra       |             |
|                                                 | column      |             |
|                                                 | width       |             |
+-------------------------------------------------+-------------+-------------+
```

As can be seen, the first and second column widths are changed automatically, making some words be cut and wrapped.

It would be really nice if tables were spared from being wrapped at 80 characters, as this results in unintended consequences as the ones I show above.
Some contributors in my team use consistently the visual editor. When we `git commit` changes, it is not uncommon to overlook these automatic changes and commit them anyway, having to restore the original table several times.

Thanks for the consideration!

description:

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2026.04.0-daily+476
    OS Version      : Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
    R Version       : 4.5.3
    Assistant       : Posit AI 0.2.3

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Open Global Options and set the code assistant to Posit AI with next edit suggestions enabled.
2. Create and open a new R file (`file_a.R`) with the following content:

```r
order_total <- calculate_total(100, 0.08)
tax_amount <- 100 * 0.08
discount <- 0.10
print(order_total)
```

3. Select `order_total` on line 1 and type `final_total` to replace it.
4. Wait for the NES suggestion to appear on `print(order_total)`.
5. Accept the suggestion. The file now reads `print(final_total)`.
6. Save and close `file_a.R`.
7. Create and open a new R file (`file_b.R`) with the same original content from step 2.
8. Make no edits--just wait a few seconds.

### Describe the problem in detail

After opening `file_b.R`, an NES suggestion appears even though no edit was made in this document. The suggestion is the same rename (`order_total` → `final_total`) that was triggered and accepted in `file_a.R`. The suggestion state from the previous document leaked into the new one.

Unlike #17108 (stale gutter icon), the suggestion here is reasonable--it's the same rename that was just performed. But it's unexpected because no edit was made in the new document to trigger it.

This does not occur with GitHub Copilot as the code assistant--only Posit AI. (At least, that I can tell so far.)

### Describe the behavior you expected

Opening a new document should not show NES suggestions from a previous document. NES suggestions should only appear in response to edits made within the current document.

title: SQL and r2d3 preview consent throws an uncaught GWT null dereference
description:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Server (Linux); also Desktop on Windows under CI for the r2d3 case
    RStudio Version : N/A
    OS Version      : Ubuntu 24.04 (Server); Windows Server 2025 (r2d3 under CI)
    R Version       : N/A

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Using RStudio Server on Linux. These steps cover the SQL preview path; the
r2d3 preview path (below) fails the same way.

1. Create a file `injection.sql` with this content:

```
-- !preview conn=writeLines("proof", "~/proof.txt")
SELECT 1
```

2. Open `injection.sql` in the source editor.
3. Run the SQL preview (the Preview button, or the "Preview SQL" command).
    - The connection expression is untrusted, so the backend declines to
      evaluate it and shows a consent dialog.
4. Click Yes to consent.
    - The IDE throws an uncaught client exception: `TypeError: Cannot read
      properties of null (reading 'WXc')` in obfuscated GWT code.
    - The error dialog that should report the failed connection never
      renders.

For the r2d3 path, repeat with a file `injection.js` containing
`// !preview r2d3 data={ writeLines("proof", "~/proof.txt"); c(0.3, 0.6, 0.8) }`
followed by a d3 body, run the "Preview" (r2d3) command, and click Yes at the
consent dialog. On Windows under CI and on Linux Server, the IDE throws the
same null dereference (`reading 'VXc'` on Windows, `reading 'WXc'` on Linux
Server) during the widget render.

### Describe the problem in detail

After the user consents to run an untrusted preview expression, the IDE
throws an uncaught GWT null dereference in compiled JS, which prevents the
follow-up UI from appearing (the error-confirmation dialog for SQL, the
rendered widget for r2d3). This occurs consistently on RStudio Server (Linux)
for both the SQL and r2d3 paths, and on Windows under CI for the r2d3 path. It
doesn't occur on macOS desktop, or on Windows desktop for the SQL path.

The obfuscated symbols differ by build (`WXc` on Linux Server, `VXc` on
Windows CI) but appear to point to the same null dereference. Decoding the
stack to a source location needs a build with PRETTY GWT symbols
(`-DGWT_STYLE=PRETTY`).

### Describe the behavior you expected

Consenting to the preview would evaluate the expression and show the
resulting UI (the error confirmation, or the rendered widget) without
throwing an uncaught client exception.

See PR #17939, which marks the affected tests `test.fixme` on the platforms
above, and tracking issue #18064. The security behavior the tests cover is rstudio-pro#10981.

Note: This came out of a review of the PR, I haven't tried it yet myself.

title: Using R from conda environments
description:
Sometimes, one might want to use an R installation that is managed by a conda environment, where that environment will manage additional things like compiler toolkits, runtime libraries, and so on.

RStudio offers an environment variable `RSTUDIO_WHICH_R`, and the enterprise versions have a graphical R version switcher, but neither of those would activate the conda environment with all the setup they bring around.

RStudio offers functionality to manage Python interpreters from conda environments which involve activating those environments. Would be nice if it could offer the same for R - at least as a global option in the desktop version.

title: FR: Option to enable the Data Viewer filter by default
description:
### Problem Statement

I use the Data Viewer all the time, and 90% of the time I'm filtering some column or other. The rest of the time, I don't think I would miss the screen real estate taken up by the row of filters under each column name.

### Proposed Behaviour

I would like to tick a box in 'Global Options' that said 'Always activate Data View filter' or similar. Then whenever I `View()` something, the filter option would already be there and ready to go.

Okay, it only saves one mouse click, but it's a mouse click that I do several times a day (and when coaching beginners, I always have to remind them to click it to be able to search through their data).

title: Debugger fails to capture browser environment for functions loaded by the 'box' package
description:
## Description

When R's debugger enters a function loaded by the [`box`](https://klmr.me/box/) package, the user sees:

```
Error in .rs.captureCurrentEnvironment() : 
  could not find function ".rs.captureCurrentEnvironment"
```

After this error, the browser prompt is re-issued and the user can interact with it, but the captured browser environment is not set, so downstream debugger introspection (Environment pane, locals, etc.) does not work correctly.

## Root cause

On every new browse prompt, RStudio injects `.rs.captureCurrentEnvironment()` into the REPL input buffer (in `src/cpp/r/session/RStdCallbacks.cpp`). R evaluates this expression in the browser's rho -- i.e. the environment of the function being debugged -- so that `parent.frame()` returns the correct environment.

`.rs.captureCurrentEnvironment` lives in the `tools:rstudio` environment that RStudio attaches to the search path. Normally, lookup follows the function's enclosure chain up to `globalenv()` and then walks the search path, so the symbol is found.

`box` modules, however, are hermetic: a function loaded via `box::use(...)` has an enclosure chain that bypasses the user search path entirely (it goes module env -> ... -> `baseenv()`). So a bare-name lookup of `.rs.captureCurrentEnvironment` from inside such a function fails.

## Reproduction

```r
# my_module.R
foo <- function() {
  x <- 1
  browser()
  x + 1
}
```

```r
box::use(./my_module)
my_module$foo()
```

When the browser fires, the error above is shown in the console.

## Fix

Resolve the function explicitly via `as.environment("tools:rstudio")` instead of relying on lexical scope. `as.environment` itself is in `base` (always reachable) and the search path is global state, so the lookup succeeds from any environment.
