title: Trust the operating system certificate store for AI assistant connections
description:
### Problem Statement

The GitHub Copilot agent and the Posit Assistant / chat backend are Node.js processes, so their network requests go through Node's TLS stack, not curl/OpenSSL. The environment variables R users normally reach for (`CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, etc.) have no effect on them.

In a corporate environment with a TLS-inspecting proxy, the agent needs the proxy's root CA to connect. Right now the only ways to provide it are the server options `copilot-ssl-certificates-file` / `posit-assistant-ssl-certificates-file` in `rsession.conf`, or setting `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to a PEM file by hand in `~/.Renviron`.

Both are awkward on RStudio Desktop on Windows. `rsession.conf` isn't used on Desktop, so that's out. And corporate CAs usually live in the Windows Certificate Store rather than as a PEM file, so `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` means exporting the cert and tracking an absolute path. The result is that a machine which already trusts the proxy CA everywhere else still can't get Copilot or the Assistant to connect, and the workaround is obscure and undocumented for Desktop.

### Proposed Behaviour

Add an opt-in preference, `assistant_use_system_ca`, as a checkbox under Tools > Global Options > Assistant ("Use the system certificate store"). When it's on, RStudio enables Node's `--use-system-ca` for the assistant agent, so it trusts the OS certificate store (Windows Certificate Store, macOS Keychain) in addition to Node's built-in CAs. For enterprise users on Windows that's close to zero config: if the machine already trusts the proxy CA, ticking one box makes the agent trust it too.

A few things that make this workable:

- RStudio already bundles Node 22.22.2, and `--use-system-ca` landed in Node 22.15.0 ([release notes](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v23.8.0), backported to 22.x), so the runtime already supports it.
- The flag is additive. It supplements `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` / `copilot-ssl-certificates-file` rather than replacing them, so existing setups keep working.
- It can be enabled either as a CLI argument to `node` or via `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca`. The `NODE_OPTIONS` route works on Node 22.17.0+ (confirmed by a Node maintainer in [nodejs/node#58346](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/58346); it errors out on older lines like 20.19.x), and since RStudio bundles 22.22.2 either approach is fine. Setting `NODE_OPTIONS` has the nice property of also covering the helper-script launch paths without any extra plumbing.

Rough sketch: add the boolean to `user-prefs-schema.json` (default `false`) and regenerate accessors, then, when it's enabled, set (or append to) `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca` in the agent environment where the agents and chat backend are launched in `SessionAssistant.cpp::startAgent` and `SessionChat.cpp` (this is where `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is set today). Add the checkbox in `AssistantPreferencesPane.java` with a restart requirement, and document it in `docs/user/rstudio/ide/guide/tools/copilot.qmd` as the recommended way to handle custom CAs on Desktop/Windows.

title: RStudio works extremely slow when opening a project on a network drive
description:
There are several bug reports related to this RStudio being slow with network drives on Windows but most of them focus on some specific aspects of the underlying problem. The underlying problem is that RStudio works extremely slow when opening a project that is located on a network drive (Windows). The Ctrl-. combination is useless. Simply opening a file can take ages. For quick fixes, I tend to open VSCode (or sometimes even IDEA) in the meantime, fix the problem and then return to RStudio to evaluate the code, which is quicker than waiting for RStudio to finish whatever it is doing.

Access to network drives is slower than access to local hard drives. Is it possible that useless accesses to the drive (e.g. to pull file information) are causing this problem? No other software behaves that badly.

This problem has pertained for several versions of RStudio, which is why I do not attach any session info. It would be useless. I'm pretty sure this problem has nothing to do with the version of R or the packages being loading.

I'm aware this isn't the best bug report. It would be nice though if somebody took notice this problem exists.

title: Desktop: failed set_user_state during bootstrap leaves an unrecoverable grey screen
description:
## Summary

On RStudio Desktop, if the `set_user_state` RPC fails during workbench bootstrap, startup silently dead-ends and the user is left with an unrecoverable grey window (title bar and menu bar present, empty grey content). There is no retry, error dialog, or recovery; the session stays grey indefinitely until killed.

Observed once on a fresh install, first launch; a subsequent launch started normally. The failure is timing-dependent (a transient connection blip during bootstrap), so it is intermittent.

## Environment

- RStudio 2026.06.0+240 (Blue Plumbago), Desktop
- Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
- Electron 41.7.2

## Symptoms

1. Main window shows the title bar and menu bar, but the content area is blank grey. Waiting several minutes does not change it.
2. DevTools console shows a single error:
   - `Unable to establish connection with R session when executing 'set_user_state'`
   - `Failed to load resource: net::ERR_CONNECTION_FAILED  :<port>/rpc/set_user_state`
3. Killing the process via Task Manager and relaunching starts normally with no delay.

## Root cause

The workbench bootstrap chains the IDE-building call behind two server RPCs, and only continues on success:

`Application.java:271-287`
```java
// refresh prefs incase they were loaded without sessionInfo (this happens exclusively
// in desktop mode ...). ... in desktop mode that returns an incomplete set until the
// pref refresh has run.
userState_.get().writeState(boolArg ->          // fires set_user_state
{
   userPrefs_.get().writeUserPrefs(boolArg1 ->   // fires set_user_prefs
   {
      ...
      initializeWorkbench();                       // only runs if BOTH succeed
   });
});
```

`UserState.writeState`'s error handler does not invoke the completion continuation:

`UserState.java:82-91`
```java
if (onCompleted != null)
   onCompleted.execute(true);   // success path continues the chain
...
public void onError(ServerError error)
{
   Debug.logError(error);       // failure path logs and stops; onCompleted never called
}
```

So when `set_user_state` fails at the TCP level (`ERR_CONNECTION_FAILED`):

- `onError` logs and returns. The continuation lambda (which runs `writeUserPrefs(... initializeWorkbench())`) never executes.
- `initializeWorkbench()` never runs, so the IDE is never built or painted -> permanent grey screen, no retry, no error UI.
- `writeUserPrefs()` never runs, so the user pref layers stay in the incomplete "loaded without sessionInfo" state that the comment at `Application.java:272-275` describes.

### Secondary effect: the only entry in the rsession log

Because the bootstrap RPCs failed at the TCP layer, those requests never reached rsession, so nothing about them appears in the rsession log. The only logged errors come later, when the user attempted to close/quit the grey window. Quitting routes through `DesktopHooks.quitR()` (`DesktopHooks.java:204`) -> `quitSession` command -> `ApplicationQuit.onQuitSession()` -> `prepareForQuit()` (`ApplicationQuit.java:544-549`), which lazily instantiates the Source pane for the first time. `SourceColumnManager`'s state init reads a global pref:

`SourceColumnManager.java:341-350`
```java
new JSObjectStateValue("source-column-manager", "column-info", ...)
{
   protected void onInit(JsObject value)
   {
      if (!userPrefs_.allowSourceColumns().getGlobalValue())   // index-based global read
```

`getGlobalValue` walks the pref layers by index and dereferences each layer; with the layers still incomplete, `layers_.get(i)` is `undefined`:

`Prefs.java:159-169`
```java
public T getGlobalValue()
{
   for (int i = userLayer(); i >= 0; i--)
   {
      if (layers_.get(i).getValues().hasKey(name_))   // layers_.get(i) is undefined
```

`PrefLayer.getValues()` is `return this.values;` (`PrefLayer.java:31-32`), so an undefined layer produces `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'values')`. (Note the contrast with the project-aware `getValue()` at `Prefs.java:145-156`, which iterates with `JsUtil.asReverseIterable` and skips missing layers, so it does not throw.)

The rsession log shows exactly this, repeated for each close attempt:
```
ERROR CLIENT EXCEPTION: (TypeError): Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'values');
  Prefs.java#159::getGlobalValue
  SourceColumnManager.java#348::onInit
  ... JSObjectStateValue ctor / GIN get SourceColumnManager -> get Source ...
  ApplicationQuit.java#122::prepareForQuit
  ApplicationQuit.java#545::onQuitSession
  DesktopHooks.java#204::quitR
```
spanning ~15:17:59 to ~15:18:09 (four attempts), followed at ~15:19:22 by:
```
ERROR system error 5 (Access is denied); ... ChildProcess::terminate ... Win32ChildProcess.cpp:334
```
which is rsession failing to terminate a child while being force-killed by Task Manager (a consequence of the manual kill, not a cause).

So the grey screen and the `getGlobalValue` TypeError share one root cause: the failed `set_user_state` aborted bootstrap, leaving both an un-built workbench and incomplete pref layers.

## Not yet determined: the trigger

Why `set_user_state` got `ERR_CONNECTION_FAILED` during bootstrap is not established. The GWT host page is served `no-cache` (`GwtFileHandler.cpp:163`) and the app clearly loaded, so rsession's listener was up at page-load time and then briefly unreachable for that RPC -- suggestive of a transient listener loss or reload/relaunch race during startup. Confirming this needs the desktop/Electron main-process log and a DEBUG-level rsession log, which were not captured in this occurrence (default log level).

The connection trigger is worth separate investigation, but it is secondary: a transient failure of one bootstrap RPC should not leave the user with an unrecoverable grey screen regardless of the cause.

## Suggested remediation (for discussion, not yet implemented)

- Make bootstrap resilient to a failed `set_user_state` / `set_user_prefs`: have `writeState`'s `onError` either retry or invoke the continuation / route to the existing connection-error/reload UI, instead of silently stopping.
- Defense-in-depth: guard the index-based accessors in `Prefs.java` (`getGlobalValue`, `getProjectValue`, `setGlobalValue`) against a not-yet-populated `layers_`, returning the default when a layer is absent.

## Related

- #17733 (gray-screen on automation startup from an incomplete pref set) and the Global Options TypeError addressed in #17994 are the same family (reading prefs before layers are fully populated), but in different code paths; this bootstrap dead-end path is not covered by those fixes.

title: Add a setting to keep data viewer scrollbars always visible
description:
Spun off from a comment on #17563 by @ldecicco-USGS.

### Describe the feature

The data viewer scrollbars are now auto-hiding (they appear only on hover/interaction and fade out quickly). Some users would prefer the option to keep them always visible. The request is for a setting that forces the data viewer scrollbars to always be shown.

### Motivation

When the scrollbars auto-hide, it isn't obvious how to scroll left/right. The available workarounds aren't discoverable:

- Arrow keys are slow.
- Scrolling the wheel briefly reveals the bars long enough to grab them.
- The middle mouse button can be used to scroll horizontally, but this is undiscoverable (the commenter only found out by reading #17563).

An "always show scrollbars" setting would address the discoverability problem directly, and there's a secondary question of how to surface the middle-mouse horizontal-scroll capability.

Originally reported on Windows 11 (RStudio 2026.05.0+162).

title: Different theming options for section headers of different levels
description:
It is currently possible to style section headers in an RStudio theme, but all header levels receive the same styling:

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/assets/3200601/7896d018-7258-4bf9-9666-8bbcb8bc733f)

It would be great if different levels could be given different classes so that they can be styled separately (in this case, I'd give lower-level headers dimmer background colours to help with scanning the script).

Thanks!

title: SHA256 mismatch for RStudio Desktop 2026.05.1+225 Ubuntu 22 (jammy) amd64
description:
### System details

RStudio Edition : Desktop
RStudio Version : 2026.05.1+225
OS             : Ubuntu 22.04 (jammy) amd64

### Steps to reproduce

1. Download the release build:
   wget https://download1.rstudio.org/electron/jammy/amd64/rstudio-2026.05.1-225-amd64.deb

   Or equivalently from S3 (both URLs serve the identical file):
   wget https://s3.amazonaws.com/rstudio-ide-build/electron/jammy/amd64/rstudio-2026.05.1-225-amd64.deb

2. Verify:
   sha256sum rstudio-2026.05.1-225-amd64.deb

### Describe the problem

The SHA256 recorded on the dailies page (for both jammy and noble, which
point to the same file) does not match the actual file served:

- Expected (dailies.rstudio.com): d4c8e870bab69ebd644e90581edf6ac39a132766e6d6a53f6394c9ccb8dc5fd3
- Actual (file on disk):          dd4dca49a8d980c28ab61b125d4aa5037a101d664252779f63a381e2367c95fe

References:
- https://dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/golden-wattle/electron/jammy-amd64/2026-05-1-225/
- https://dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/golden-wattle/electron/noble-amd64/2026-05-1-225/

The build is dated June 3, 2026, commit 89e0c7da7b7b806fc5701ecb567f993716d8cfdc.
This appears to be a recurring issue (see also #13709), suggesting the binary
is silently replaced on S3 after the dailies checksum is recorded, without
updating the metadata.

### Expected behavior

The SHA256 on the dailies detail page should match the file actually served
at the download URL, so users can verify integrity.

- [x] I have done my best to include a minimal, self-contained set of instructions for consistently reproducing the issue.
